title: Feature Flag Verification Test (rich-ui compile-time toggle)
description:
## Test: rich-ui Feature Flag Toggle

Verify that the rich-ui feature can be completely disabled at compile time without breaking any functionality.

### Why This Matters

1. Users may want minimal dependencies
2. Embedded/constrained environments may not support terminals
3. Provides fallback if rich_rust causes issues
4. Ensures clean separation between core functionality and UI

### Test Implementation

```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/test_feature_flag.sh
set -euo pipefail

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
pass() { log "✓ PASS: $*"; }
fail() { log "✗ FAIL: $*"; exit 1; }

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 1: Build WITHOUT rich-ui feature
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log "TEST 1: Build without rich-ui feature"

cargo build -p rch --no-default-features --release --target-dir target/no-rich 2>&1 || {
    fail "Failed to build without rich-ui feature"
}

NO_RICH="./target/no-rich/release/rch"
if [[ \! -x "$NO_RICH" ]]; then
    fail "Binary not created"
fi
pass "Build without rich-ui succeeded"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 2: Build WITH rich-ui feature  
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log "TEST 2: Build with rich-ui feature"

cargo build -p rch --features rich-ui --release --target-dir target/with-rich 2>&1 || {
    fail "Failed to build with rich-ui feature"
}

WITH_RICH="./target/with-rich/release/rch"
pass "Build with rich-ui succeeded"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 3: Binary size comparison
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log "TEST 3: Binary size comparison"

SIZE_NO_RICH=$(stat -f%z "$NO_RICH" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$NO_RICH")
SIZE_WITH_RICH=$(stat -f%z "$WITH_RICH" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$WITH_RICH")

DIFF=$((SIZE_WITH_RICH - SIZE_NO_RICH))
PERCENT=$(echo "scale=1; $DIFF * 100 / $SIZE_NO_RICH" | bc)

log "Binary sizes: no-rich=${SIZE_NO_RICH} with-rich=${SIZE_WITH_RICH} diff=+${DIFF} (+${PERCENT}%)"

# Warn if rich-ui adds more than 50% size
if (( DIFF > SIZE_NO_RICH / 2 )); then
    log "WARNING: rich-ui adds significant binary size (+${PERCENT}%)"
fi
pass "Binary size measured"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 4: Core functionality works WITHOUT rich-ui
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log "TEST 4: Core functionality without rich-ui"

# Hook classification must work
echo '{"tool":"Bash","input":{"command":"echo test"}}' | "$NO_RICH" hook --stdin > /tmp/hook_no_rich.json 2>&1 || {
    fail "Hook failed without rich-ui"
}

if \! jq -e . /tmp/hook_no_rich.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "Hook output not valid JSON without rich-ui"
fi
pass "Hook works without rich-ui"

# Status command must work
"$NO_RICH" status > /tmp/status_no_rich.txt 2>&1 || true
pass "Status command runs without rich-ui"

# Workers list must work
"$NO_RICH" workers list > /tmp/workers_no_rich.txt 2>&1 || true
pass "Workers list runs without rich-ui"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 5: Outputs are functionally equivalent
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log "TEST 5: Functional equivalence"

# Hook output should be identical
echo '{"tool":"Bash","input":{"command":"echo test"}}' | "$WITH_RICH" hook --stdin > /tmp/hook_with_rich.json 2>&1

if \! diff /tmp/hook_no_rich.json /tmp/hook_with_rich.json; then
    fail "Hook output differs between builds\!"
fi
pass "Hook output identical"

# --json output should be identical
"$NO_RICH" status --json > /tmp/status_no_rich.json 2>&1 || true
"$WITH_RICH" status --json > /tmp/status_with_rich.json 2>&1 || true

if [[ -s /tmp/status_no_rich.json ]] && [[ -s /tmp/status_with_rich.json ]]; then
    if \! diff /tmp/status_no_rich.json /tmp/status_with_rich.json; then
        fail "--json output differs between builds\!"
    fi
    pass "--json output identical"
else
    log "SKIP: Status --json not available (daemon not running)"
fi

log ""
log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
log "ALL FEATURE FLAG TESTS PASSED"
log "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
```

### Cargo.toml Requirements

```toml
[features]
default = ["rich-ui"]
rich-ui = ["rich_rust"]

# Code should use cfg(feature = "rich-ui") guards
```

### Files

- CREATE: scripts/test_feature_flag.sh
- MODIFY: rch/Cargo.toml (ensure feature flag properly defined)
- VERIFY: All #[cfg(feature = "rich-ui")] guards work correctly
close_reason: Merged into bd-2ga8 (feature-flag output gating tests).

title: Harness-agnostic build interception for dispatcher boxes (rch shim + dispatcher role) — stop codex/direct cargo building locally on orchestrators
description:
## Problem (root-caused live on trj 2026-07-23)

rch only auto-intercepts builds via PER-HARNESS hooks: `rch agents install-hook`
covers Claude Code (settings.json PreToolUse) and Gemini CLI. **codex has no hook
API**, and neither do plain shells, scripts, or CI. So codex/direct `cargo build`
invocations run LOCALLY on orchestrator boxes — defeating rch's entire purpose. On
trj this produced 38->127 local rustc and made the box "nearly unusable."

Two deeper design gaps make it worse:

1. **The cargo-wrapper contract exists but no wrapper ships.** rch sets
   `RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1` when it re-execs cargo on local fallback
   (`rch/src/hook.rs:524` `local_fallback_command`), i.e. rch was DESIGNED to sit
   behind a cargo wrapper. But rch installs none. Result: the wrapper is hand-rolled
   inconsistently per box (csd has a project-scoped bash wrapper; trj/ts2/css got an
   ad-hoc sh wrapper 2026-07-23; most boxes have nothing).

2. **Policy is per-invocation and fail-open.** `general.force_remote` is fail-OPEN
   (placement.rs: `force_remote_is_fail_open`) — when the fleet is busy it runs the
   build LOCALLY (with the bypass set, so no loop), repopulating rustc on the very
   box we are trying to keep clean. The only way to get "never local" is to hand-set
   `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1` on every call. There is no box-level "dispatcher" role.

types.rs already carries a comment about builds that "silently ran on the
orchestrator" — the failure mode is known, just unaddressed.

## Fix (staged; see child beads)

- **P1 `rch shim`** — ship+install a canonical, versioned cargo wrapper (harness-
  agnostic; covers codex/scripts/CI). Replaces every hand-rolled wrapper.
- **P2 box role** — `general.role = dispatcher|worker|hybrid`; dispatcher defaults to
  fail-closed+queue (no local rustc) without per-call env.
- **P3 loud detection** — `rch status`/`doctor` alarms when a dispatcher runs local
  builds (kills the silent-fallback failure mode, mirrors the fleet-degraded alarm).
- **P4** absolute-path invocation catch (PATH shim misses `.rustup/.../bin/cargo`).
- **P5** durability: shim dir acfs won't clobber + watchdog re-assert + install.sh.

## Acceptance

On a `dispatcher` box, ANY agent (codex included) running `cargo build/test/check`
offloads to the fleet or queues — zero local rustc — with one `rch shim install`, no
hand-rolled scripts, and a loud alarm if that ever stops holding.

title: Idea: Transfer size estimator + skip heuristics
description:
## Background
Some projects are too large to benefit from remote execution due to transfer overhead. A size estimator prevents wasting time and bandwidth.

## Goals
- Estimate upload/download size and expected transfer time before offloading.
- Skip remote execution if estimated transfer exceeds a configurable threshold.
- Provide transparent reasoning in verbose logs.

## Design / Approach
- Use rsync dry-run (`--stats --dry-run`) to estimate bytes/files for upload.
- Combine with configured bandwidth estimate or measured link latency to derive transfer time.
- Add config: max_transfer_mb, max_transfer_time_ms.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Implement dry-run estimator with mock support.
- Add config settings and documentation.
- Integrate gating into hook (after classification, before worker selection).

## Tests
- Unit: parse rsync --stats output.
- Integration: estimator returns expected values for fixtures.
- E2E: remote skipped when transfer exceeds threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Remote offload is skipped for excessively large transfers.
- Estimator adds minimal latency (<5ms average for small projects).

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-g6vh.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- rsync dry-run unavailable: skip estimator and proceed (fail-open).
- Cache estimator result briefly to avoid repeated overhead.
- Include .rchignore + config excludes in estimate.

## E2E Outline
- Small fixture below threshold -> remote allowed.
- Large fixture above threshold -> local allowed.
- Verbose output includes estimated bytes + time.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rch/src/transfer.rs: parse rsync --stats output and bytes calculation.
- rch/src/hook.rs: estimator failure falls back to normal flow (fail-open).

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-g6vh.sh: small vs large fixture; verify skip threshold behavior.
- Logs include estimated bytes + transfer time.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by bd-3hho (Transfer Optimization). Size estimator merged with bandwidth control.

title: GH#27 P4: queue jobs on active-project exclusion (daemon)

title: Add short flags for common CLI options
description:
# Add Short Flags for Common Options

## Problem
Frequently-used flags have no short forms, requiring extra typing:

| Long Flag | Current Short | Proposed Short |
|-----------|--------------|----------------|
| --json | (none) | -j |
| --format | (none) | -f |
| --workers | (none) | -w |
| --jobs | (none) | -J |
| --all | (none) | -a |
| --force | -f | (keep) |
| --yes | -y | (keep) |
| --verbose | -v | (keep) |
| --quiet | -q | (keep) |

## Conflict Analysis
- -f is currently used by --force on rch cancel
- Solution: --format can use -F instead, or context-specific

## Implementation
In main.rs, update clap attributes:

```rust
/// Output as JSON for machine parsing
#[arg(long, short = 'j', global = true)]
json: bool,

/// Machine output format: json or toon
#[arg(long, short = 'F', global = true, value_name = "format")]
format: Option<String>,
```

## Testing
- Verify short flags work as expected
- Verify no conflicts between subcommands
- Update shell completions

Create Test Runner Script (scripts/run_true_e2e.sh)
description:
## Purpose
Create a comprehensive test runner script that executes all true e2e tests with proper logging, reporting, and CI integration.

## Why This Matters
- Manual test execution is error-prone
- CI systems need standardized entry point
- Developers need easy local testing
- Reports needed for tracking regressions

## Script: scripts/run_true_e2e.sh

### Basic Usage
```bash
# Run all true e2e tests
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh

# Run specific test category
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --filter cargo

# Run with verbose logging
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --verbose

# Skip if no workers (CI mode)
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --ci
```

### Script Features

#### 1. Pre-flight Checks
- Verify daemon is running (or start it)
- Verify at least one worker is reachable
- Verify required tools (rsync, ssh, etc.)
- Check Rust toolchain versions match

#### 2. Test Execution
- Run tests with cargo test --features true-e2e
- Capture all output (stdout, stderr, timing)
- Handle test timeouts gracefully
- Support parallel test execution

#### 3. Logging Integration
- Set RCH_E2E_LOG_DIR to timestamped directory
- Collect all test logs
- Generate summary log

#### 4. Report Generation
- JUnit XML for CI systems
- HTML report with timing graphs
- Summary table (pass/fail/skip counts)
- Failure details with log excerpts

### Output Structure
```
test-results/
├── run_2024-01-19_120000/
│   ├── junit.xml           # CI-compatible report
│   ├── report.html         # Human-readable report
│   ├── summary.json        # Machine-readable summary
│   ├── logs/
│   │   ├── test_cargo_build.jsonl
│   │   ├── test_cargo_test.jsonl
│   │   └── ...
│   └── artifacts/
│       └── (any test artifacts)
```

### CI Integration
```yaml
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Run True E2E Tests
  run: ./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --ci --junit test-results/junit.xml
  env:
    RCH_E2E_WORKERS_CONFIG: ${{ secrets.WORKERS_CONFIG }}
    
- name: Upload Test Results
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: e2e-test-results
    path: test-results/
```

### Exit Codes
- 0: All tests passed
- 1: Some tests failed
- 2: Infrastructure error (no workers, daemon failed)
- 3: Configuration error

## Implementation

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"

# ... (full implementation in script)
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Script runs all true e2e tests
- [ ] Pre-flight checks prevent confusing failures
- [ ] JUnit XML is valid and parseable
- [ ] HTML report is clear and useful
- [ ] CI mode skips gracefully when no workers
- [ ] Exit codes are correct
- [ ] Documentation in script header

title: Replace TUI emoji icons with unicode symbols for terminal compatibility
description:
# Replace Emoji with Unicode Symbols

## Problem
In rch/src/tui/widgets.rs lines 249-253, circuit breaker state uses emoji:

```rust
let circuit_icon = match w.circuit {
    CircuitState::Closed => "",
    CircuitState::HalfOpen => " ⚡",
    CircuitState::Open => " 🔴",  // ← EMOJI
};
```

The 🔴 emoji renders as boxes/mojibake in:
- PuTTY and older Windows terminals
- xterm without font support
- screen/tmux sessions without UTF-8
- Many SSH clients
- CI/CD log viewers

## Solution
Replace emoji with unicode symbols that have broader support:

```rust
let circuit_icon = match w.circuit {
    CircuitState::Closed => "",       // Normal - no indicator needed
    CircuitState::HalfOpen => " ◐",   // Half-filled circle = testing
    CircuitState::Open => " ●",       // Filled circle = blocked
};
```

Use the existing color system to indicate state (red for open, yellow for half-open).

## Testing
1. Run `rch dashboard` in various terminals:
   - macOS Terminal.app
   - iTerm2
   - Linux xterm
   - Windows Terminal
   - PuTTY
2. Verify no boxes/replacement characters appear
3. Verify meaning is clear from color alone (for color users)
4. Verify meaning is clear from symbol alone (for colorblind users)

## Files to Modify
- rch/src/tui/widgets.rs (lines 249-253)

title: Test: SSH Command Execution & Output Capture
description:
## Purpose
Test SSH command execution on real workers - running commands, capturing output, handling errors, and managing long-running processes.

## MANDATORY Logging
This test MUST use TestLogger for all phases:

```json
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_ssh_echo","phase":"execute","msg":"SSH command execution","data":{"cmd":"echo hello","worker":"css"}}
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_ssh_echo","phase":"result","msg":"Command completed","data":{"exit_code":0,"stdout_bytes":6,"stderr_bytes":0,"duration_ms":45}}
{"ts":"...","level":"DEBUG","test":"test_ssh_echo","phase":"output","msg":"Command output","data":{"stdout":"hello\\n","stderr":""}}
```

## Test Cases

### Basic Command Execution
1. Simple command:
   - Run: `echo 'hello world'`
   - Verify: stdout contains 'hello world'
   - Verify: exit code 0
   - Log: command, output, exit code

2. Command with exit code:
   - Run: `exit 42`
   - Verify: exit code 42 captured
   - Log: expected vs actual exit code

3. stderr output:
   - Run: `echo 'error' >&2`
   - Verify: stderr captured separately
   - Log: stderr content

### Environment & Working Directory
4. Working directory:
   - Run: `pwd` in specific directory
   - Verify: correct directory
   - Log: expected vs actual cwd

5. Environment variables:
   - Run: `echo $MY_VAR` with MY_VAR=test
   - Verify: env var passed correctly
   - Log: env vars set

### Long-Running & Complex Commands
6. Long output:
   - Run command producing >1MB output
   - Verify: all output captured
   - Log: total bytes, truncation status

7. Long-running command:
   - Run: `sleep 10` with timeout
   - Verify: timeout triggers correctly
   - Log: timeout value, actual duration

8. Binary output:
   - Run: `cat /bin/ls | head -c 1000`
   - Verify: binary data preserved
   - Log: binary bytes count

### Error Handling
9. Command not found:
   - Run: `nonexistent_command`
   - Verify: error captured, non-zero exit
   - Log: error type, exit code

10. Signal handling:
    - Kill long-running command
    - Verify: signal exit code (128+N)
    - Log: signal number, exit code

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All commands execute on real worker
- [ ] Output (stdout/stderr) correctly captured
- [ ] Exit codes correctly propagated
- [ ] Environment and cwd work correctly
- [ ] Timeouts and signals handled
- [ ] ALL phases logged with structured JSON

title: EPIC: Progress Indicators and User Feedback
description:
# Progress Indicators and User Feedback

## Overview
RCH has good progress indicator infrastructure but doesn't use it consistently across all long-running operations. This creates uncertainty about whether operations are progressing or hung.

## Current State

### Strong Points
- Spinner and TransferProgress types exist in rch-common/src/ui/progress/
- Automatic TTY/JSON mode detection
- Unicode/ASCII fallback support

### Missing Progress Indicators
These operations provide no progress feedback:

1. **rch workers benchmark** - Runs speed tests on workers with no indication of progress
2. **rch self-test** - Compiles test project with no feedback during compilation
3. **rch workers sync-toolchain** - Runs rustup on workers, can take minutes with no feedback
4. **rch fleet deploy** - Deploys to multiple workers but shows no per-worker progress

### Missing Multi-Progress
When deploying to 5 workers simultaneously, users see nothing until all complete. Should show:
```
Deploying to fleet (3/5 complete)
  css ████████████████ 100% ✓
  csd ████████░░░░░░░░  50%
  cse ████░░░░░░░░░░░░  25%
  csf ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% (connecting)
  csg ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% (queued)
```

## Key Files
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/spinner.rs - Spinner implementation
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/transfer.rs - TransferProgress
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/compile.rs - CompilationProgress
- rch/src/commands.rs - Command implementations needing progress

## Success Criteria
- All operations >2s show progress indication
- Parallel operations show nested/grouped progress
- Progress works in both TTY and non-TTY modes
- Progress can be disabled with --quiet

title: Idea: Per-command priority hint for worker selection
description:
## Background
When many agents run concurrently, some commands are more urgent than others. A simple priority hint improves responsiveness for critical tasks.

## Goals
- Allow users/agents to tag a command with priority (low/normal/high).
- Feed priority into selection scoring and queue ordering.
- Maintain fairness; avoid starvation.

## Design / Approach
- Use env var `RCH_PRIORITY=low|normal|high` or CLI flag in `rch compile`.
- Extend SelectionRequest with priority field; adjust selection weights or queue priority.
- Log priority decisions in daemon events.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Extend protocol types and daemon selection logic.
- Add CLI/env plumbing in hook and compile command.
- Add documentation and examples.

## Tests
- Unit: priority parsing + default.
- Integration: high priority selects from faster workers when available.
- E2E: priority logged and visible in status output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Priority hint affects selection without breaking fairness.
- Default behavior unchanged when priority not set.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-mvsl.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- Invalid priority -> default to normal with warning.
- Prevent starvation (priority affects selection, not infinite queueing).
- Priority visible in status/diagnostics.

## E2E Outline
- RCH_PRIORITY=high prefers fastest worker.
- RCH_PRIORITY=low avoids fastest when others available.
- Logs show priority value used.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rch-common/src/types.rs: priority parsing + default.
- rchd/src/selection.rs: priority influence on scoring.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-mvsl.sh: RCH_PRIORITY=high prefers fastest worker.

title: E2E Test: Compilation Offload Scenarios
description:
Add end-to-end tests for compilation offload pipeline.

## Scenarios to Test
1. **Basic Cargo Build**
   - Simple 'cargo build' offloads correctly
   - Artifacts returned to local machine
   - Exit code preserved

2. **Cargo Test**
   - Test output captured correctly
   - Failed tests return correct exit code (101)
   - --nocapture flag works

3. **Large Project Transfer**
   - rsync + zstd compression verified
   - Excluded directories (.git, target) not transferred
   - Incremental transfer efficiency

4. **Bun Typecheck**
   - TypeScript project offloads
   - Type errors returned correctly
   - node_modules excluded

5. **Build Failures**
   - Compiler error output preserved
   - Color codes passed through
   - Error locations accurate

6. **Concurrent Builds**
   - Multiple simultaneous builds
   - No artifact corruption
   - Worker slot management correct

## Logging Format
```
[E2E] TEST START: cargo_build_simple
[E2E]   Project: fixtures/simple-rust
[E2E]   Worker: test-worker-1
[E2E]   Transfer: 1.2MB compressed (45% ratio)
[E2E]   Build time: 12.3s
[E2E]   Artifacts: target/debug/simple (1.8MB)
[E2E] TEST PASS: cargo_build_simple (15.7s)
```

## Fixtures Required
- fixtures/simple-rust/ - Minimal Cargo project
- fixtures/large-rust/ - Multi-crate workspace
- fixtures/bun-project/ - TypeScript project

title: rch#23: durable remediation — installer linux fallback + clean-checkout CI guard
description: GitHub issue #23: v1.0.43 uninstallable on linux-x86_64. Part 2 (/dp absolute path deps in workspace Cargo.toml) was fixed by commit 8d6e3fe (switched to crates.io). Remaining durable work: (a) installer must fall back musl->gnu so install succeeds whenever either linux-x86_64 asset exists (v1.0.43 shipped only -gnu); (b) CI still clones /dp in every job, so it never proves the clean-checkout path the issue asks for — remove that vestigial provisioning + add a fast manifest guard rejecting /dp path deps. Republishing v1.0.43 assets is an outward-facing op left to the maintainer; the installer fallback makes it unnecessary.
close_reason: rch#23 durable remediation complete. All 3 children closed: .1 installer musl->gnu fallback (proven live vs v1.0.43: musl 404 -> gnu 200 -> checksum via SHA256SUMS verifies), .2 removed 22 vestigial /dp CI steps so every job is a clean-checkout build, .3 added scripts/check_no_dp_path_deps.sh manifest guard wired into ci.yml (catches the exact regression, proven vs pre-fix manifest). Combined with commit 8d6e3fe (Part 2: manifest now uses crates.io), this covers the durable asks in the issue. NOT done here (outward-facing, maintainer-owned): republishing v1.0.43's -musl asset — the installer fallback makes that unnecessary since v1.0.43 ships -gnu, which now installs.

title: Installer: linux-x86_64 prebuilt fallback (musl -> gnu)
description: install.sh maps linux-x86_64 to a single RELEASE_TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl and tries exactly one versioned asset (download_binaries ~L698). If that 404s (v1.0.43 shipped only -gnu) the -gnu asset is never tried before falling through to the source build. Fix: linux-x86_64 carries an ordered candidate list (musl preferred, gnu fallback); loop over candidates in the versioned-download step, pick the first that resolves. Verify: bash -n, shellcheck, simulated curl loop vs real v1.0.43 (musl 404 / gnu 200).
close_reason: Implemented in install.sh: detect_platform now builds an ordered RELEASE_TARGETS candidate list (linux-x86_64 = musl preferred, gnu fallback; other platforms single-entry), and download_binaries loops over candidates in the versioned-download step, using the first asset that resolves. Removed the now-dead singular RELEASE_TARGET var (kept shellcheck clean for the notify-acfs 'Shellcheck installer' CI job). Proven end-to-end against the real v1.0.43 release: musl 404 -> falls back -> gnu 200 resolves a 9948288-byte tarball containing rch/rchd/rch-wkr; per-asset .sha256 is 404 so it uses SHA256SUMS, and extract_checksum_from_manifest returns 56ff7002...e42586 matching the gnu asset -> checksum verify PASSES. Validation: bash -n OK, shellcheck clean (default severity = CI parity), detect_platform emits (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) on linux-x86_64. This fixes the 'uninstallable on linux-x86_64' half of rch#23 without needing to republish v1.0.43 assets.

title: CI: remove vestigial /dp provisioning so every job is a clean-checkout build
description: Now that workspace Cargo.toml uses crates.io deps (8d6e3fe), the 'Clone local path dependencies' steps (mkdir /dp + git clone rich_rust/toon_rust/frankentui) across ci.yml jobs, e2e.yml, test-release.yml, release.yml are dead AND defeat the clean-checkout ask: while /dp is provisioned a regression to /dp path deps would still pass CI. Remove them (and the now-noop sed in test-release.yml) so all jobs resolve from the registry.
close_reason: Removed all 22 vestigial /dp 'Clone local path dependencies' steps across ci.yml (11), release.yml (7), test-release.yml (3), e2e.yml (1) via 3 file-scoped subagents. Independently verified: git diff --numstat shows 0 insertions per file (no surviving line altered — pure step deletions); all 4 parse as valid YAML via python yaml.safe_load with job sets unchanged (ci=13, release=9, e2e=3, test-release=2); grep -rn /dp over .github/workflows returns nothing; manifests remain /dp-free. Net effect: every CI/release job now resolves ftui*/tru/rich_rust purely from crates.io, so each job IS a genuine clean-checkout build — the durable proof issue #23 requested. Spot-checked check/build-release jobs: checkout->rust-toolchain->rust-cache->cargo flows cleanly with no orphaned blank lines. (actionlint unavailable here due to snap /data sandboxing; yaml.safe_load is the same validator the repo's own test_dependabot_automerge_workflow.sh uses.)

title: CI: add fast manifest guard rejecting /dp absolute-path deps
description: Add a fast dependency-free guard (in the manifest_sync job, no /dp step) that greps all Cargo.toml for absolute path='/dp/...' deps and fails crisply. Turns the exact #23 regression into an instant legible CI failure instead of an opaque cargo resolution error.
close_reason: Added scripts/check_no_dp_path_deps.sh (set -euo pipefail, shellcheck-clean, bash -n OK) and wired it into ci.yml manifest_sync as step 'Guard manifests against absolute-path (/dp) deps (rch#23)'. It scans all git-tracked Cargo.toml for absolute-path deps (path = "/...", regex path[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*[quote]/) covering [dependencies]/[workspace.dependencies]/[patch.*]/[build-dependencies], and on a hit prints RCH-GATE-DP-PATH file:line + a crates.io remediation example, exit 1. Proven: PASS on current tree (17 manifests, 0 hits); the identical regex against the pre-fix manifest (git show 8d6e3fe~1:Cargo.toml) flags all 11 /dp deps — i.e. it would have failed CI on the exact #23 regression instead of surfacing an opaque cargo manifest-resolution error. ci.yml stays valid YAML (13 jobs; guard step confirmed present in manifest_sync).

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] cache_gc mtime walk follows symlinks, can prune an ACTIVE build tree
description: rch/src/cache_gc.rs:283-294 (tree_size_and_newest_mtime) and :165,181 (enumerate_staging_trees) use is_dir()/entry.metadata() which FOLLOW symlinks. The in-flight guard keeps a tree iff its newest descendant mtime is recent; following a symlink into an unrelated quiescent directory makes the computed newest-mtime reflect the symlink target, not this build activity. A staging tree containing a symlink (rsynced repo with a target-> link, vendored dep) whose target is old can be judged idle and remove_dir_all-pruned WHILE a build is live — the active-dir hazard the design claims to prevent. remove_dir_all targets the real tree path (no out-of-root escape) so this is loss-of-active-build → MEDIUM. FIX: use entry.file_type()/symlink_metadata in the walk; do not descend symlinked dirs; skip symlinked entries at enumeration.
close_reason: enumerate_staging_trees uses DirEntry::file_type (no-follow) + tree walk never descends symlinks. Commit 7ed0bf0. Symlink test passes; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] workers: legacy_status maps RecoveredPendingCanary→Degraded, will bypass canary gate once wired
description: rchd/src/workers.rs:243-251 — legacy_status() maps EligibilityState::RecoveredPendingCanary → WorkerStatus::Degraded. The live scheduler healthy_workers() (:1068-1078) treats Degraded as SCHEDULABLE, but is_schedulable() (:260-266) deliberately EXCLUDES RecoveredPendingCanary ("canary-pending is not normal scheduling"). LATENT: the two-axis lifecycle is currently scaffold (#![allow(dead_code)], no production call sites — confirmed). But the moment anyone bridges the lifecycle into the legacy status field via legacy_status(), a canary-pending worker becomes eligible for normal builds, violating the one-canary-build-first invariant. FIX (when wiring): route scheduling through is_schedulable()/is_canary_pending(), or map RecoveredPendingCanary→Unreachable in the legacy collapse so it stays excluded.
close_reason: Committed (rchd/src/workers.rs). WorkerLifecycle::legacy_status() now maps RecoveredPendingCanary -> WorkerStatus::Unreachable (was Degraded). Degraded is schedulable in the legacy scheduler while is_schedulable() excludes RecoveredPendingCanary, so the old mapping would have let a canary-pending worker take normal builds once anyone bridged the lifecycle into the legacy status field — violating one-canary-first. Both quarantine states (TemporaryBypass + RecoveredPendingCanary) now collapse to Unreachable (excluded); module doc + legacy_status test assertion updated to expect Unreachable. PROOF: cargo check -p rchd passes (via rch); the lifecycle assertions are pure unit checks. Did NOT run the flaky daemon-lifecycle E2E suite (operator-flagged hang, no bounded socket-wait); see follow-up bead for adding a bounded deadline to it.

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] fleet canary deploy with auto_promote=false reports Success while most of fleet undeployed
description: rch/src/fleet/executor.rs:219 — remaining workers (canary_count..worker_count) are deployed ONLY when auto_promote is true; otherwise never deployed and never counted. Function still returns FleetResult::Success { deployed, skipped, failed } at :309 with counts covering only the canary subset and NO pending indicator. A 100-worker fleet at 5% canary without auto_promote returns Success{deployed:5} while 95 workers still run the OLD binary; an operator/JSON consumer reading Success concludes the rollout finished. WHY WRONG: misrepresents fleet state, silent partial rollout. FIX: distinct variant (CanaryPending { promoted, remaining }) or explicit pending count in Success, surfaced by human/JSON renderers.
close_reason: Committed 965ec23 (rch/src/fleet/executor.rs + mod.rs). Added FleetResult::CanaryPending { promoted, remaining, skipped, failed }. execute()'s Canary arm: when canary succeeds but auto_promote=false and workers remain, it now records the pending count (worker_count - canary_count) and returns CanaryPending instead of the misleading Success{deployed:canary_subset}. Human renderer (fleet/mod.rs) prints an explicit 'fleet NOT fully rolled out — N still on previous version' warning + promotion hint; JSON consumers get status:'CanaryPending' via the serde tag (was reading Success => 'rollout finished'). PROOF (failure-class: silent partial rollout): 2 unit tests — canary_pending serializes distinctly from a same-deployed-count Success (status!=Success, carries promoted/remaining) + round-trips. cargo test -p rch --bins fleet_result_canary => 5 passed; clippy -p rch --bins --tests -D warnings clean; fmt clean (via rch). NOTE: the end-to-end execute() canary path uses real SSH with no mock-injection at that layer, so coverage is the serialization + renderer surface (which is exactly the JSON/operator misreport the defect described); a full mock-SSH execute() canary E2E would belong with the fleet E2E harness.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] doctor transitions_count increments on diagnostic-only changes (mislabeled metric)
description: rch/src/doctor.rs:1621-1624 — `any_change = diff.has_changes() || verdict_changed` increments state.transitions_count, but the exit summary + JSON (:1734/:1745 transitions/transitions_total) label it as transitions. A sweep where the reliability VERDICT is unchanged but a diagnostic message text changed bumps the transition count. Webhooks correctly fire on verdict_changed (not any_change) so no paging impact — purely a reporting/metric-naming inaccuracy that can mislead CI gates keying on transitions_total. FIX: gate the counter on verdict_changed, or rename the field to change_events.
close_reason: transitions_count gated on verdict_changed; any_change still drives --transitions-only. Commit 490c466. clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] flaky test: benchmarks::disk::test_benchmark_stability variance assertion fails under machine load
description: rch-telemetry/src/benchmarks/disk.rs:931 asserts `variance < 1.0` (i.e. <100% run-to-run variance) for the disk benchmark score. Observed 115.97% variance → FAILED on a loaded/shared machine during cargo test -p rch-telemetry --lib (score run2=6544 vs an earlier run). This is a non-deterministic, environment-sensitive assertion: disk benchmark scores legitimately vary far more than 100% under concurrent IO (other builds/agents on the box). WHY WRONG: a perf-variance threshold in a unit test makes the whole crate suite fail intermittently based on host load, unrelated to code correctness. FIX: gate the stability assertion behind a serial/ignored attribute or an env opt-in (e.g. #[ignore] by default, run only on a quiesced bench host), or relax/remove the hard variance bound and instead log the variance. Found incidentally during review-mode telemetry testing.
close_reason: Variance bound gated behind RCH_BENCH_STRICT; always sanity-checks finite/non-negative scores. Commit a39e1d0. Test passes; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] fleet backup interpolates unquoted worker-reported version into cp/sha256sum/rm
description: rch/src/fleet/executor.rs:1191-1192 build remote_backup_path and the cp command by interpolating the worker-reported version (parsed from rch-wkr --version, split_whitespace().nth(1), :1135) UNQUOTED into the backup filename + cp/sha256sum/rm (also rollback.rs:567,588,624,712,756,811 via backup.remote_path). Unlike the deploy finalize (shell_escape_path_with_home) this binary-derived component is unescaped: a version token with a shell glob or command-substitution makes cp word-split/glob, the backup SILENTLY fails or writes to the wrong path, and backup failure is non-fatal (Ok(None)) so deploy proceeds with NO rollback point. FIX: route backup path through shell_escape_path_with_home and/or reject version tokens with chars outside [A-Za-z0-9._+-].
close_reason: Worker-reported version validated (is_safe_version_token) at the source; unsafe versions skip backup, securing fleet+rollback shell commands. Commit f0b95f9. Tests pass; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] hook fails CLOSED if init_logging errors → blocks the user command (fail-open violation)
description: rch/src/main.rs:1753 init_logging(&log_config)? propagates Err into main() (1689-1704) which does std::process::exit(1). For a PreToolUse hook invocation (no subcommand) a non-zero exit is interpreted by Claude Code as DENY → the users Bash command is BLOCKED. The fail-open panic handler is not installed until :1832, AFTER init_logging. Concrete: RCH_LOG_FILE pointing at an unwritable/uncreatable dir → build_writer Err → init_logging Err → hook exits 1 → every Bash command the agent runs is blocked until the env var is fixed. The run_hook doc even names init_logging as the lone legitimate Err, but main does not honor fail-open for the hook branch. FIX: logging is best-effort diagnostics — degrade to no-logging on init failure (warn to stderr, continue) instead of ? -propagating; ideally also install the hook panic handler before parse/init so an early panic cant fail closed (separate LOW).
close_reason: Fixed in commit c4cd639: init_logging failure now degrades to no-logging (stderr warning) instead of ?-propagating to exit(1). Verified end-to-end: a hook invocation with an uncreatable RCH_LOG_FILE now exits 0 (fail-open allow) with a degradation warning, was exit 1 (deny/block) before.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] classifier make/ninja substring contains(clean/install) misclassifies real builds
description: rch-common/src/patterns.rs:1255 (make) and :1272 (ninja) reject via cmd.contains("clean")/contains("install")/contains("distclean") and contains("clean"). contains matches ANYWHERE, not the target token: "make CFLAGS=-Iinstall/include", "make build INSTALL_DIR=/x", "make TARGET=cleanup", and "ninja build/clean_obj.o" are real builds rejected as non-compilation (fail-open → run local, suboptimal not dangerous). FIX: tokenize args and match whole target tokens exactly (make clean|install|distclean|uninstall; ninja -t clean or a literal clean target token). MEDIUM (make/ninja secondary to cargo; failure is fail-open).
close_reason: make/ninja maintenance targets matched as whole tokens via positional_build_targets (skips flags/flag-values/VAR=value). Commit 8893d31. patterns tests pass (213); clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] telemetry: request_starts clear-on-full drops ALL in-flight request durations
description: rch-telemetry/src/metrics.rs:681-683 — record_request_start() does `if starts.len() >= MAX_TRACKED_REQUESTS { starts.clear(); }`. When 1024 started-but-not-ended requests accumulate, the ENTIRE map is wiped, so every prior request that later emits request.end (without an inline duration_seconds) finds no entry (record_request_end starts.remove returns None at :702) and silently records NO duration — a correctness/observability loss, not just a bounded leak. Also lines 678/700: a missing request_id defaults to the literal "default", so concurrent requests without an id collide on one key and overwrite each other. WHY WRONG: under load the request-duration histogram silently loses observations and conflates concurrent requests. FIX: evict the OLDEST entry (by RequestStart.start Instant) or use a bounded LRU/ring instead of clear(); and skip tracking (or use a unique synthetic key) when request_id is absent rather than colliding on "default".
close_reason: Fixed in commit c0f3ee4: record_request_start now evicts the single oldest in-flight entry instead of clear()-ing the whole map (preserving pending durations), and skips tracking id-less requests instead of colliding on a 'default' key. +3 regression tests; all 12 metrics tests green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] selection diagnostics ignore the admission gate (report Allow for a gate-Rejected worker)
description: rchd/src/selection.rs:1397 vs 1776-1821 — get_eligible_workers uses the AdmissionGate (when wired) and replaces the legacy pressure.state check, but build_selection_diagnostics only consults pressure.state == Critical (1397) and never calls the gate. So when a gate is configured, a worker the gate REJECTS is reported in diagnostics as Allow/eligible — misleading exactly the "why was nothing selected" output an operator relies on. Diagnostics-accuracy only (does not affect which worker runs). FIX: route the diagnostic decision through the same admission-gate verdict used in get_eligible_workers.
close_reason: build_selection_diagnostics now routes through the admission gate verdict (mirrors get_eligible_workers), so a gate-rejected worker is no longer reported Allow. Commit pending. clippy green; rchd selection tests pass.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] selection try_fallback returns an admin-Drained/Disabled worker (breaks fail-open + audit)
description: rchd/src/selection.rs:1006-1050 (try_fallback) resolves the last-success worker via pool.get() directly (bypassing healthy_workers()) and checks slots/circuit/success_rate but NEVER worker.status(). An operator-Disabled or Drained worker is returned as the affinity-fallback selection and audited as AffinityFallback. reserve_slots (workers.rs:515) re-checks status and refuses, so no bad build lands, BUT: the select→reserve retry loop in api.rs:2148/2244 does NOT add the worker to excluded_worker_ids on a reservation failure (only the active-build-race path at :2178 does), so try_fallback deterministically returns the SAME disabled worker each round → all attempts fail on it → request ends AllWorkersBusy instead of cleanly failing open to local. FIX: in try_fallback, reject the worker unless matches!(worker.status().await, Healthy | Degraded), mirroring healthy_workers().
close_reason: try_fallback rejects workers not Healthy|Degraded, mirroring main selection. Commit 72e0e72. try_fallback test passes; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] shell state machines honor backslash escapes inside single quotes (non-POSIX) → structure misjudgment
description: rch-common/src/patterns.rs — check_structure, split_and_chain, split_shell_commands, has_file_redirect all treat backslash as an escape even while inside single quotes. In POSIX/bash, backslash is LITERAL inside single quotes (the quote ends at the next single quote regardless of a preceding backslash). So a command that embeds a single-quoted backslash immediately before a closing quote followed by a control operator (e.g. && then a destructive command) parses in bash with the quote CLOSED and the operator EXPOSED, while this code keeps the quote open and misses the operator — classifying the structure differently than bash executes it. The classifier is fail-OPEN so the dangerous direction (a destructive compound looking like a clean single compile that gets sent remote) is constructible but narrow → LOW. FIX: in all four quote/escape state machines, do not honor backslash escapes while in_single is set (only inside double quotes / unquoted), matching POSIX.
close_reason: All 4 shell state machines treat backslash as literal inside single quotes (POSIX). Commit 67131b5. patterns tests pass incl. new regression; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] ssh classifier treats stale-mux-socket "No such file or directory" as non-retryable
description: rch-common/src/ssh_utils.rs:32 — is_retryable_transport_error_text fail-fast-rejects any message containing "no such file or directory". openssh surfaces stale-ControlMaster-socket errors like "mux_client_request_session: ... No such file or directory" / "ControlSocket ...: No such file or directory" on a transient socket-gone condition that a single reconnect would fix, but the broad substring forces them non-retryable. LOW because production uses fresh per-call connections (control_master=false) so the mux-socket case is rare today; matters once pooled/mux connections are used. FIX: scope the socket "No such file or directory" to retryable (or require "identity file"/"keyfile" co-occurrence for the auth-fatal case), and evaluate transport-retryable patterns before the fatal fall-through.
close_reason: Already fixed and tested (verified, not a regression). is_retryable_transport_error_text in rch-common/src/ssh_utils.rs no longer fail-fast-rejects a bare 'no such file or directory': it was removed from the fatal set (commit 7cd10f6 'expand SSH utility patterns'), the auth-fatal missing-key case is now gated on the 'identity file'/'keyfile' markers, and the stale-ControlMaster/mux patterns ('control socket'/'controlsocket'/'mux_client'/'multiplexing') are matched as transient-retryable. The bead's exact scenarios are proven by ssh_utils::tests::test_stale_control_socket_is_retryable_not_fatal (ControlSocket + mux_client 'No such file or directory' => retryable; 'Identity file ... No such file or directory' => still fatal) plus test_non_retryable_transport_error_text. All 8 ssh_utils tests green via rch exec offload. Took over a 9-day-stale pane-3 in_progress claim; no code change needed.

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] ssh SshPool reuses a pooled connection with no liveness check (returns dead master)
description: rch-common/src/ssh.rs:163-166 (is_connected = self.session.is_some()) feeding :630-652 (get_or_connect). get_or_connect decides reuse purely on is_connected(), which only checks a Session OBJECT exists, never that the underlying SSH ControlMaster is alive. A pooled connection whose master died (network blip, idle ControlPersist expiry, remote sshd killed it) is returned as "reusing existing connection"; the next execute() spawns over a dead master → broken-pipe/closed → hard build failure with no reconnect. LATENT: SshPool/get_or_connect have ZERO production call sites (every live path uses a fresh SshClient::new→connect→disconnect); confirmed. Bites when SshPool is wired into the build path. FIX: before returning a reused client, probe liveness (health_check or detect spawn failure); on failure drop the session and reconnect once; treat the first execute transport error as a reconnect-and-retry trigger.
close_reason: get_or_connect validates liveness on borrow (health_check probe) and reconnects via new SshClient::reconnect. Commit 2f74d98. ssh tests pass (102); workspace clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] ssh command-timeout leaks the remote process (caller skips disconnect on timeout)
description: rch-common/src/ssh.rs:431-444 / 566-597 — on execute() timeout the inner future owning the RemoteChild is dropped, but dropping an openssh RemoteChild does NOT kill the remote process while a ControlMaster is active. The build path remote_compilation.rs:559 does client.execute(&build_cmd).await? so on timeout the ? propagates and client.disconnect() at :560 is NEVER reached → the remote cargo build keeps running, burning worker CPU and holding cache/target locks until sshd reaps it. For production per-call sessions (control_master=false → ClosedAfterInitialConnection) the MASTER self-terminates so the leak is bounded, but the remote build process can linger. FIX: in execute/execute_streaming timeout arms explicitly kill/disconnect the remote child, or have callers disconnect() in a guard that always runs on the error path.
close_reason: Build/mkdir paths now always disconnect on the error path (capture-then-disconnect guard), so a timed-out remote build no longer leaks. Commit b0b48e3. Workspace clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][TEST] Golden-artifact + cross-contract metamorphic tests for admission/proof/exec/readiness surface
description: The new rch-common contracts (admit_preflight, admission_rejection, admission_recommendation, capability_probe eligibility, proof_policy, proof_handoff, classifier_drift, readiness, fleet_diff, exec_policy, exec_response, exec_misuse) have per-module unit tests but no consolidated GOLDEN-ARTIFACT suite nor cross-contract consistency checks. Add: (1) JSON golden files (committed) for each envelope serialization so a serde-token/shape regression is caught crate-wide (extend rch-common/tests/golden_schemas_e2e.rs); (2) metamorphic/consistency properties — every AdmissionRejectionCategory has exactly one recommend() NextAction and one RejectionClass and one incident_reason; every EligibilityVerdict reason maps to an AdmissionRejectionCategory; ExecResponse.invariant_holds() over a generated outcome matrix; readiness remote_ready ⇒ command_admissible>0 over a generated split matrix (proptest); (3) reason-code stability lint asserting no RCH-Innn renumber. Mock-free (golden artifacts + property tests).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 5e81885: tests/admission_goldens_e2e.rs — 5 committed json! goldens (AdmissionRejectionSummary/ProofHandoff/ExecResponse/ReadinessReport/AdmitPreflight) + cross-contract metamorphic invariants (category→action/class/reason totality, incident-reason round-trip, eligibility→vocabulary bridge, ExecResponse worker-iff-remote, proof-handoff totality, RCH-Innn stability) + proptest (readiness remote_ready⇒admissible, recommend_for_summary consistency). 13 tests green.

title: [REVIEW][TEST] Fuzz classify→capability/exec derivation (admit_preflight, exec_policy, exec_misuse) over arbitrary command strings
description: admit_preflight::preflight, exec_policy::decide_exec_policy/mutates_local_state, and exec_misuse::detect_exec_misuse parse arbitrary command strings (split_whitespace, env-prefix stripping, --target/+toolchain scanning). Add proptest/fuzz over arbitrary UTF-8 command strings + structured token sequences asserting: (1) none panic; (2) preflight base_recommendation is always definite (never ambiguous); (3) compound split round-trips (no token loss); (4) detect_exec_misuse never flags a --separated or multi-token argv, always flags a single whitespace string; (5) mutates_local_state is stable under benign flag/env-prefix permutations of a known mutating command. Mock-free pure-function fuzzing. Files: rch-common/src/{admit_preflight,exec_policy,exec_misuse}.rs.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 05fc44c: tests/classify_exec_fuzz.rs — proptest fuzz (1500 cases) over arbitrary+structured command strings for admit_preflight::preflight (total/definite/deterministic), exec_policy (total + mutating-never-remote invariant), exec_misuse (contract), + mutates-stability. Caught and fixed a real gap (mutates_local_state didn't skip +toolchain, hiding cargo +nightly fmt). 4 fuzz + 12 exec_policy unit tests green.

title: [REVIEW][TEST] Property/fuzz no-panic + metamorphic coverage for telemetry_freshness::assess()
description: The just-fixed mul_f64 panic (commit 106ddd2) shows assess() lacked adversarial-input coverage. Add proptest/fuzz over FreshnessInputs (arbitrary poll_interval, ssh_timeout, last_poll_duration, host_rtt incl. Duration::MAX, recent_timeout_count u32::MAX, concurrency_pressure incl. NaN/inf/out-of-range, age Some/None) asserting: (1) assess() never panics; (2) confidence is always finite and in [0,1]; (3) usable == matches!(verdict, Fresh|SlowObserver). Add metamorphic properties: larger age never yields a fresher verdict (monotonicity); higher concurrency_pressure never shrinks tolerated_age_ms; verdict is total (exactly one of Fresh/SlowObserver/Stale/Unknown). Mock-free, pure-function fuzzing. Files: rch-common/src/telemetry_freshness.rs.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 51f795d: proptest fuzz submodule (3 properties x 2048 cases) over arbitrary FreshnessInputs incl. NaN/inf pressure + extreme Durations — no-panic, confidence finite/in-range, usable mirrors verdict, plus metamorphic monotonicity (age) and pressure-widens-tolerance. The fuzz caught a real NaN-pressure panic in dominant_reason (Duration::from_secs_f64) which was fixed (sanitize non-finite pressure to 0.0). All 12 telemetry_freshness tests green; clippy clean.

title: [REVIEW][TEST] make webhook E2E deterministic + un-ignore (127.0.0.1:0 + bounded recv + watchdog)
description: Un-ignore the three rch/src/doctor_webhooks.rs webhook_e2e tests (signed HMAC, unsigned-omits-signature, bounded-retries-on-5xx) once the local-server round-trip is made deterministic and hang-proof. The scaffolding (TestSink: 127.0.0.1:0 ephemeral bind + mpsc recv_timeout instead of join + bounded accept deadline; deliver wrapped in tokio::time::timeout) already landed in commit 2362022 but the tests were observed to stall under cargo build-lock / runtime contention. TODO: (1) add a hard per-test watchdog (e.g. spawn a thread that aborts/panics after ~10s, or run the body under a single tokio::time::timeout that also covers the sync collect); (2) confirm reqwest opens a fresh connection per attempt (Connection: close is sent) so the retry count is exact and not keep-alive-coalesced; (3) verify the sink thread always terminates and never holds the process open; (4) run via timeout 60 cargo test -p rch --bin rch doctor_webhooks::tests::webhook_e2e (run LOCALLY — rch cannot host the localhost server) and confirm deterministic + <10s; then remove the #[ignore] attributes.
close_reason: Added Watchdog RAII backstop (abort >30s, cancelled on completion); removed 3 #[ignore]s. Verified deterministic: 5 local + 1 remote run, all pass <0.12s. clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][TEST] Mock-free real-service E2E for doctor webhook dispatch (local HTTP sink + structured JSONL)
description: doctor_webhooks.rs is unit-tested for render/HMAC but has no real-service E2E exercising the actual reqwest dispatch path. Add a mock-free E2E: spin a real local HTTP sink (tiny tokio/hyper or std listener bound to 127.0.0.1:0) that records method/headers/body to a JSONL log, point a DoctorWebhookEndpoint at it, and assert end-to-end: (1) GenericJson/Slack/PagerDuty bodies; (2) X-RCH-Signature present + HMAC verifies when signing_secret set; (3) endpoint SKIPPED (not delivered) when a configured secret/bearer/routing-key env is unset (ties to bd-review-webhook-unsigned-silent); (4) bounded retries + per-attempt timeout via a sink that 5xx/delays; (5) redirect NOT followed once Policy::none lands (ties to bd-review-webhook-redirect-leak). Structured JSONL assertions, no HTTP mocking library.
close_reason: Scaffolding landed (commit 2362022): mock-free real-service E2E — localhost TcpListener HTTP sink (127.0.0.1:0, bounded mpsc recv, no join) driving the real reqwest deliver, asserting POST/Content-Type, X-RCH-Signature HMAC over the exact body, unsigned-omits-header, and bounded retries on 5xx. The 3 tests are #[ignore]d pending a deterministic local-server fix (could stall under build-lock/runtime contention). Follow-up: bd-review-test-webhook-e2e-followup.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] unanchored toolchain prefix match (false positives) in worker_facts + capability_probe
description: rch-common/src/worker_facts.rs:169-174 has_toolchain() uses t.starts_with(name), and rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs assess_admissibility() uses `t.starts_with(needed)` for needs_toolchains. The prefix is not anchored to a separator, so has_toolchain("nightly") also matches a hypothetical "nightlyfoo", and needs_toolchains=["nightly-2025-11"] would match "nightly-2025-11-05" (intended) but also "nightly-2025-110" (unintended). Low severity given rustups well-formed channel names, but imprecise. FIX: anchor the match — `t == name || t.starts_with(&format!("{name}-"))` in both sites so a bare channel/pinned-date only matches itself or a "-"-suffixed host-triple form.
close_reason: has_toolchain + capability_probe needs_toolchains anchor prefix to '-' boundary. Commit eada5b2. rch-common tests pass (1877); clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] transfer: exit-0 partial-transfer indicators on upload only warn, never fail
description: rch/src/transfer.rs:1513-1535 — after a SUCCESSFUL (exit 0) rsync, stderr is scanned for partial transfer / connection unexpectedly closed / write error / read error / truncated file, and on a match it only warn!s, then returns Ok(SyncResult). rsync usually exits non-zero on these, but the code explicitly anticipates the exit-0-but-incomplete edge and then takes no protective action: the hook reports sync success, the remote source tree is incomplete, and the remote build compiles stale/partial sources returning a trusted-but-wrong result. The streaming path has NO equivalent check. FIX: on a partial-indicator match return Err(TransferError::SyncFailed{...}) (or treat as retryable); add the same scan to the streaming path combined stderr.
close_reason: All 4 transfer paths fail on exit-0 partial transfers via detect_partial_transfer (was warn-only on one path, absent on three). Commit 68ae309. Tests pass; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] transfer: streaming upload/retrieve paths have NO retry at all
description: rch/src/transfer.rs:1601-1608 (sync_to_remote_streaming) and :2239-2250 (retrieve_artifacts_streaming) call run_command_streaming directly, never through retry_with_backoff. They fetch effective_rsync_retry_config but use only its timeout; max_attempts/backoff are ignored. A single transient SSH/rsync drop on the streaming (agent-facing progress) path fails the whole transfer with ZERO retries. Combined with the just-fixed execute_rsync_with_retry CRITICAL (commit aa5fafb), the non-streaming path now retries but streaming still does not. FIX: wrap run_command_streaming in the retry loop (or a streaming-aware execute_rsync_with_retry variant) classifying the TransferError/stderr via is_retryable_transport_error; the on_line callback must tolerate re-invocation across attempts.
close_reason: Streaming upload/retrieve now retry transient transport drops via run_command_streaming_with_retry (classifies SyncFailed stderr). Commit e8bb500. 5 tests pass; workspace clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] doctor webhook client follows redirects, leaks X-RCH-Signature cross-host
description: rch/src/doctor_webhooks.rs:467-470 — reqwest::Client::builder() is built with no redirect policy, so it follows up to 10 redirects by default. reqwest strips Authorization on cross-origin redirects but does NOT strip the custom X-RCH-Signature header, so a 30x-redirecting (compromised/misconfigured) receiver receives a replayable signed payload on another host, inside one attempt timeout. Endpoint URLs are operator config (not untrusted), so SSRF risk is low. FIX: `.redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())` — a webhook should POST to the exact configured URL.
close_reason: Webhook client sets redirect Policy::none() so X-RCH-Signature can't leak cross-host. Commit d7abb6d. clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] doctor webhook silently sends UNSIGNED when signing_secret_env is configured-but-unset
description: rch/src/doctor_webhooks.rs:502 — `let signing_secret = endpoint.signing_secret_env.as_deref().and_then(read_env);`. If signing_secret_env is configured (Some) but the env var is unset/empty, and_then(read_env) yields None and the request is dispatched with NO X-RCH-Signature header. This is INCONSISTENT with render_request (:285-299) where routing_key_env and bearer_token_env raise RenderError::MissingEnv → endpoint skipped + journaled (doctor.webhook.skipped_misconfigured). WHY WRONG: an operator who configured HMAC signing gets a silent downgrade to unauthenticated delivery on a missing secret; a strict receiver 4xx-rejects (non-retryable → alert dropped) so paging silently fails, while a lax receiver accepts unsigned payloads. FIX: treat a configured-but-unset signing_secret_env as RenderError::MissingEnv (skip + journal) exactly like bearer/routing-key — resolve it in render_request, not via and_then.
close_reason: Fixed in commit b2806c4: signing_secret now resolved in render_request and raises RenderError::MissingEnv (skip+journal) when a configured signing_secret_env is unset, matching bearer/routing-key — no more silent downgrade to unsigned. +2 regression tests; all 17 doctor_webhooks tests green.

title: [REVIEW][LOW] rch-wkr cache eviction uses top-dir mtime only (TOCTOU vs a just-started build)
description: rch-wkr/src/cache.rs:121-136 — cleanup evicts a hash-dir based on hash_meta.modified() (top-dir mtime, line 112). A newly created cache dir mkdir-d but not yet written, OR one rsynced in with preserved old mtimes (rsync -t/--times), can be remove_dir_all-d by a concurrent cleanup while a build is about to use it. The orchestrator target-dir reaper (transfer.rs ~2325 / stale_target_reap) was explicitly hardened to check DESCENDANT mtimes to avoid exactly this; the worker cache path was not. With the default 168h window it is unlikely, but cleanup(max_age_hours) accepts small values. FIX: mirror the stale_target_reap predicate (check newest descendant mtime, not just top dir) before evicting, or take a per-hash lock / rename-then-delete.
close_reason: cleanup uses newest_descendant_mtime (dir+descendants, no symlink follow) instead of top-dir mtime. clippy green; cache tests pass incl. new helper test.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] rch-wkr output relay write-error drops trailing output but still reports build success
description: rch-wkr/src/executor.rs:433-446 / 457-470 — the stdout/stderr relay tasks, on a write_all/flush error to the workers own stdout (the SSH channel back to the client), log and break, abandoning the rest of the child pipe. execute() then awaits child.wait() and reports success/failure purely on the childs exit STATUS. So a build can be reported SUCCESS while its output was truncated mid-stream (the client only sees what was relayed before the write error) — result and output become inconsistent. Lower probability (needs a relay write error, e.g. SSH channel back-pressuring then closing) but explicitly swallowed. FIX: on a relay write error, treat the result as failed/unknown (or propagate the relay error) so the client knows output was incomplete rather than trusting exit status alone.
close_reason: Relay tasks report clean-drain; exit-0 with truncated output returns EXIT_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED (122) instead of false success. Commit b217703. Tests pass; clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][MEDIUM] rch-wkr prepare failure reports exit_code:1, indistinguishable from a real build exit 1
description: rch-wkr/src/executor.rs:395 — if the Bun/Node dependency prepare step (e.g. bun install) Fails/Times out, execute() returns CommandFailed { exit_code: 1 } WITHOUT running the user command. The client cannot distinguish "your bun test failed with exit 1" from "we never ran your command because remote dependency install failed", and the real test runner stdout/stderr is absent (only worker-side .rch_prepare_logs). FIX: use a distinct sentinel exit code for prepare failures and surface the install-log path to the client stderr, so the client reports "remote dependency install failed" instead of a misleading test failure.
close_reason: Prepare failure returns EXIT_PREPARE_FAILED (121) + clear stderr w/ install-log path instead of exit 1. Commit b217703. rch-wkr tests pass (182); clippy green.

title: [REVIEW][HIGH] classifier wrapper flag-eater drops value tokens (nice -n 10 cargo build → run local)
description: rch-common/src/patterns.rs:813-828 — normalize_command strips a wrapper (nice/taskset/ionice/time) then greedily eats leading dash-tokens as flags, only special-casing env -u VAR to consume a value. For value-taking wrapper flags the VALUE token is left as the command word: "nice -n 10 cargo build" → strips nice, eats -n, leaves "10 cargo build" → not a compilation → real cargo build silently runs LOCAL. Same for "taskset -c 0-3 cargo build", "ionice -c 2 cargo build", "timeout 60 cargo build". WHY WRONG: common cpu/io-nice wrappers around builds defeat offload. FIX: per-wrapper value-flag knowledge (nice -n N, ionice -c/-n N, taskset -c LIST, chrt) consuming the value like the env -u case; for timeout-style skip the single non-flag value token; add regression cases. NOTE: sibling global-flag bug cargo --offline build already FIXED in commit 743fcbe — this is the wrapper-side analogue.
close_reason: Committed bc1a07a (rch-common/src/patterns.rs). normalize_command now consumes value-taking wrapper flags' value token (wrapper_flag_takes_value: nice -n, ionice -c/-n/-p, taskset -c/-p, chrt -p, timeout -s/-k, env -u) instead of leaving it as the command word, and added timeout/chrt as wrappers with a guarded positional skip (looks_like_duration_or_priority => leading digit) for the bare duration/priority token. So 'nice -n 10 cargo build' / 'taskset -c 0-3 cargo build' / 'ionice -c 2 cargo build' / 'timeout 60 cargo build' / 'chrt -r 10 cargo build' now normalize to 'cargo build' and offload (were silently running LOCAL). Malformed 'timeout cargo build' keeps the command (non-digit positional not skipped). Attached/=-joined forms (-n10, --adjustment=10) unaffected. PROOF (failure class: offload defeated by cpu/io-nice wrappers): 3 unit tests — wrapper_value_flags_consume_their_value_token (all forms => 'cargo build'), positional_wrapper_does_not_eat_a_non_numeric_command, wrapped_cargo_build_is_still_classified_as_compilation (+ wrapped non-build still passes through); cargo test -p rch-common --lib tests_normalize_whitespace => 5 passed (via rch). fmt clean. CLIPPY NOTE: 'clippy -p rch-common --tests -D warnings' currently fails ONLY on an unrelated bool_comparison (needs_cargo == false) in another agent's uncommitted admit_preflight.rs:342 — not in this diff; patterns.rs itself is clippy-clean (this commit touches only patterns.rs).

title: Test: gcc/g++/clang Remote Compilation
description:
## Purpose

## MANDATORY Logging

{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_basic","phase":"execute","msg":"Remote compilation","data":{"cmd":"gcc -o hello main.c","exit_code":0,"worker":"css","duration_ms":234}}
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_basic","phase":"verify","msg":"Binary verification","data":{"path":"hello","exists":true,"runs":true,"output":"Hello, World!"}}

## Test Cases

## Acceptance Criteria

close_reason: Merged into bd-v9pq (True E2E C/C++ Compiler Tests).

title: Epic: Eliminate All Fleet Module Stubs for 1.0.0 Release
description:
# Epic: Eliminate All Fleet Module Stubs for 1.0.0 Release

## Background & Motivation

RCH 1.0.0 is being positioned as a production-ready release. During a deep code review, we discovered **three critical stubs** in the fleet module that return fake/hardcoded data instead of performing real operations. These stubs violate our core principle of NO TECH DEBT and make the following commands unreliable:

- `rch fleet preflight` - Returns hardcoded "all OK" without checking anything
- `rch fleet status` - Returns fake worker statuses without SSH
- `rch fleet rollback` - Simulates rollback with sleep() instead of restoring binaries

## Why This Matters

1. **User Trust**: Users running `rch fleet preflight` expect REAL checks. Reporting false positives erodes trust.
2. **Operational Safety**: Rollback is a critical recovery mechanism. A fake rollback that reports success while doing nothing is DANGEROUS.
3. **1.0.0 Quality Bar**: We cannot ship 1.0.0 with fake functionality. Every command must do what it claims.

## Scope

Replace all stub implementations with world-class, production-grade code that:
- Performs real SSH connections to workers
- Collects real metrics (disk space, tool versions, health)
- Handles errors gracefully with proper diagnostics
- Includes comprehensive tests (unit, integration, E2E)
- Follows RCH patterns (fail-open, structured errors, retry logic)

## Architecture Overview

All three functions need SSH access to workers. We should:
1. Reuse existing SSH infrastructure from `rch-common/src/ssh.rs`
2. Reuse retry logic from `rch/src/transfer.rs`
3. Follow the pattern established in `executor.rs` which was already fixed

## Files to Modify

- `rch/src/fleet/preflight.rs` - Main implementation
- `rch/src/fleet/rollback.rs` - Rollback implementation
- Possibly extract shared SSH utilities if patterns emerge

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All three functions perform real operations
- [ ] No hardcoded/fake return values
- [ ] Comprehensive error handling with RCH error codes
- [ ] Unit tests for all code paths
- [ ] E2E tests with real workers (or mock SSH)
- [ ] `cargo clippy` passes with no warnings
- [ ] Documentation updated

## Dependencies

This epic has no external blockers. It unblocks the 1.0.0 release.

title: Create Comprehensive E2E Test Scripts for Fleet Operations
description:
## Task
Create comprehensive end-to-end test scripts that verify all fleet operations work correctly
with real SSH connections and detailed logging.

## Background
User explicitly requested: "comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed 
logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation."

## E2E Test Script Requirements

### 1. Main Test Script: scripts/e2e_fleet_test.sh
\`\`\`bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# E2E Fleet Operations Test Suite
# Tests: preflight, fleet status, deployment, rollback
# 
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/e2e_fleet_test.sh              # Run with real workers from workers.toml
#   ./scripts/e2e_fleet_test.sh --localhost  # Run against localhost only
#   RCH_MOCK_SSH=1 ./scripts/e2e_fleet_test.sh  # Run with mock SSH

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "\${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "\$SCRIPT_DIR")"
LOG_FILE="\$PROJECT_ROOT/e2e_test_\$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log"

# Logging functions with timestamps and levels
log_info()  { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [INFO]  \$*" | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE"; }
log_warn()  { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [WARN]  \$*" | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE" >&2; }
log_error() { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [ERROR] \$*" | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE" >&2; }
log_debug() { [[ "\${DEBUG:-}" == "1" ]] && echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [DEBUG] \$*" | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE"; }

# Test result tracking
TESTS_PASSED=0
TESTS_FAILED=0
TESTS_SKIPPED=0

run_test() {
    local name="\$1"
    shift
    log_info "=== Running test: \$name ==="
    if "\$@" 2>&1 | tee -a "\$LOG_FILE"; then
        log_info "✓ PASSED: \$name"
        ((TESTS_PASSED++))
    else
        log_error "✗ FAILED: \$name"
        ((TESTS_FAILED++))
    fi
}

# Test: Preflight checks
test_preflight() {
    log_info "Testing rch fleet preflight..."
    local output
    output=\$(RCH_JSON=1 rch fleet preflight --all 2>&1)
    
    # Verify JSON output structure
    echo "\$output" | jq -e '.data.results' > /dev/null || {
        log_error "Invalid preflight JSON output"
        return 1
    }
    
    # Check for actual SSH connectivity (not hardcoded true)
    local ssh_tested
    ssh_tested=\$(echo "\$output" | jq -r '.data.results[0].ssh_ok')
    log_debug "SSH connectivity result: \$ssh_tested"
    
    # Verify disk space is realistic (not hardcoded 10000)
    local disk_mb
    disk_mb=\$(echo "\$output" | jq -r '.data.results[0].disk_space_mb')
    if [[ "\$disk_mb" == "10000" ]]; then
        log_warn "Disk space appears to be hardcoded (10000 MB)"
    fi
    
    log_info "Preflight output saved to log"
    return 0
}

# Test: Fleet status
test_fleet_status() {
    log_info "Testing rch fleet status..."
    local output
    output=\$(RCH_JSON=1 rch fleet status 2>&1)
    
    echo "\$output" | jq -e '.data.workers' > /dev/null || {
        log_error "Invalid fleet status JSON output"
        return 1
    }
    
    # Verify workers were actually queried (not all hardcoded reachable=true)
    local reachable_count
    reachable_count=\$(echo "\$output" | jq '[.data.workers[] | select(.reachable == true)] | length')
    log_debug "Reachable workers: \$reachable_count"
    
    return 0
}

# Test: Rollback (dry run)
test_rollback_dry_run() {
    log_info "Testing rch fleet rollback --dry-run..."
    local output
    output=\$(RCH_JSON=1 rch fleet rollback --dry-run --all 2>&1) || true
    
    # Even if no backups, should get structured response
    echo "\$output" | jq -e '.success' > /dev/null || {
        log_error "Invalid rollback dry-run JSON output"
        return 1
    }
    
    return 0
}

# Main
main() {
    log_info "Starting E2E Fleet Test Suite"
    log_info "Log file: \$LOG_FILE"
    log_info "RCH version: \$(rch --version)"
    
    run_test "preflight" test_preflight
    run_test "fleet_status" test_fleet_status
    run_test "rollback_dry_run" test_rollback_dry_run
    
    log_info "=== Test Summary ==="
    log_info "Passed:  \$TESTS_PASSED"
    log_info "Failed:  \$TESTS_FAILED"
    log_info "Skipped: \$TESTS_SKIPPED"
    
    [[ \$TESTS_FAILED -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
}

title: rch local staging GC: prune stale /tmp/rch-sync trees to bound disk usage
description: rch accumulates per-project sync trees under /tmp/rch-sync with no garbage collection. Must never delete the sync tree of an in-flight build. This directly prevents disk-full conditions during multi-agent swarms.

title: RCH session-history remediation program from complete history analysis
description:
# RCH session-history remediation program

This umbrella tracks the product work extracted from `COMPREHENSIVE_ISSUES_AND_PROBLEMS_WITH_RCH_BASED_ON_COMPLETE_SESSION_HISTORY_ANALYSIS.md`, AGENTS.md, README.md, and a fresh code-architecture pass over the workspace. The goal is to make the repeated cross-machine RCH failures recoverable, diagnosable, and proof-safe without future agents needing the source report.

RCH is the remote compilation substrate for multi-agent development. The session history shows that individual workers will fail: disk fills, SSH times out, VMI/Contabo hosts pause, toolchains drift, and worker binaries can be wrong for the host. The deeper product bug is that transient failures shrink or confuse the effective worker pool, silently fall back to local compilation, and leave agents uncertain whether proof actually ran remotely.

This program treats the fleet as desired state plus live eligibility. Transient failure should create auditable temporary bypass, scheduled diagnostics, canary rejoin, and admission explanations. Permanent disable remains an explicit admin action. Proof builds must fail closed or queue durable proof intents. Status and doctor surfaces must distinguish daemon availability, generic health, command-admissible workers, queue state, artifact retrieval, and incident history.

Done means the P0/P1/P2 child epics have self-contained implementation beads, tests, and dependency links; `br dep cycles` remains empty; and future agents can start from Beads alone.

title: P0: Temporary bypass and auto-rejoin worker lifecycle
description:
# Temporary bypass and auto-rejoin

The history shows agents responding to transient worker illness by draining, disabling, or editing `workers.toml`. That avoids the immediate failure but leaves the fleet smaller after the worker recovers. Current code confirms the risk: `WorkerStatus` has `Healthy`, `Degraded`, `Unreachable`, `Draining`, `Drained`, and `Disabled`; health updates deliberately preserve draining/drained/disabled states; reservation refuses them. That is correct for admin intent, but wrong as the default response to SSH failure, disk pressure, missing toolchain, stale telemetry, or circuit breaker churn.

This epic adds an automatic transient lifecycle separate from permanent admin disable. A worker can be temporarily bypassed with a reason, TTL/backoff, diagnostic history, and canary requirements, then automatically rejoin after consecutive successful checks. Admin-disabled workers must never auto-rejoin.

Acceptance criteria: status surfaces show bypass reasons and next probe; bypassed workers continue to be probed without taking builds; recovered workers pass exact-path `rch-wkr`, runtime/toolchain, disk/inode, load, telemetry, and canary checks; `workers.toml` is never mutated for transient illness; tests cover state transitions and rejoin safety.

title: Mount-aware build root and cargo-home selection
description: Implement mount-aware target and cargo-home root policy. Before admission, RCH should check free bytes and inodes on `/`, `/tmp`, configured cargo home, configured target root, and RCH sync root, then avoid RAM-backed or tiny `/tmp` roots when disk-backed build roots exist. The policy must explain chosen roots and reject workers where required roots are unsafe. Tests should model tmpfs pressure, disk-backed fallback, inode exhaustion, and worker-specific overrides.
close_reason: Committed 42e76cf (rchd/src/build_root_policy.rs + main.rs mod). Implemented the mount-aware build-root/cargo-home selection POLICY: evaluate_build_roots is a pure function over per-root MountStats (free bytes/inodes + FsKind, supplied by worker telemetry/facts — daemon does not statvfs worker mounts locally, matching the existing telemetry-driven disk model). Rejects roots under free-bytes/inode thresholds (InsufficientBytes/InsufficientInodes; u64::MAX inodes = not-reported), avoids tmpfs when a disk-backed safe root exists (RamBackedAvoided, overrides exempt), ranks override>disk>unknown>tmpfs then by free bytes, returns ChosenRoot+rationale, every RejectedRoot reason, a safe flag, and explanation (all Serialize for status). PROOF (matrix row ocv9i.11.1, failure classes 'critical pressure'/'disk full'): UNIT TESTS — 10 covering the bead's required scenarios: tmpfs pressure (disk preferred), disk-backed fallback (tmpfs only when no disk), inode exhaustion, insufficient bytes, worker override chosen over bigger disk, override-on-tmpfs kept (not RAM-avoided), missing-inode-counts unconstrained, max-free tie-break, empty-pool unsafe, status serialization; 'cargo test -p rchd --bins build_root_policy' => 10 passed (via rch); clippy -p rchd --bins --tests -D warnings clean; fmt clean. GOLDEN/SCHEMA: decision is Serialize with serde snake_case (status-surface ready); no golden file yet (status wiring is follow-on). INTEGRATION/E2E: N/A here — admission wiring + live mount-stat gather are explicit follow-ons (beads 6.x admission, 12.1 worker facts); module is allow(dead_code) scaffolding (workers.rs pattern) until then.
