title: Exact user/path capability probes for runtimes toolchains and targets
description: Implement capability probes as the configured remote user using the exact executable path RCH will invoke. Probes must collect Rust toolchains and targets such as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, runtime versions, worker binary version/protocol, disk root facts, and path sanity. They must distinguish SSH reachability from capability admissibility. Tests should mock root-good/user-broken binaries, missing rustup, missing wasm target, and stale worker protocol.
close_reason:
Implemented exact user/path capability probes (commit ee44b11) at
rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs, consuming the 12.1 WorkerFacts types.

WHAT LANDED:
- build_capability_probe_script(ProbeSpec): one fail-soft shell script that runs
  as the configured remote user using EXACT executable paths (rch-wkr path,
  cargo path), not PATH-resolved. Emits `RCH_FACT k=v` lines for os/arch/user,
  exact-path rch-wkr --version + --protocol-version, cargo/rustc, rustup
  toolchain list + target list --installed (collecting wasm32-unknown-unknown
  etc.), bun/node/npm versions, and df -Pk/-Pi disk-root facts. Each failing
  probe omits its line (capability-absent) instead of crashing (reachability).
  Disk roots and the binary path are shell-quoted.
- parse_capability_probe -> ProbedFacts: tolerant parser (ignores non-prefixed
  stdout) assembling RustFacts (toolchains/targets/rustc), RuntimeFacts,
  WorkerBinaryFacts (only when the exact-path binary reported a version), and
  DiskRootFacts (kb->bytes). target_triple() derives from probed os/arch.
- assess_admissibility(facts, CapabilityRequirement) -> CapabilityVerdict:
  distinguishes SSH reachability (an empty parse is the caller's unreachable
  signal) from capability admissibility. Rejections map to incident reason
  codes: WrongUserPathWorkerBinary (broken exact-path binary / stale protocol),
  MissingRuntimeToolchainTarget (no cargo / missing rustup target).

VALIDATION (per 16.1 contract):
- Unit tests (8, capability_probe::tests) covering the bead's required mocks:
  script-uses-exact-paths-and-probes-all-dimensions; full-output parse;
  admissible-when-complete; root-good/user-broken binary -> rejected
  (WrongUserPathWorkerBinary) DISTINCT from unreachable; missing rustup ->
  rejected (MissingRuntimeToolchainTarget, cargo); missing wasm target ->
  rejected (MissingRuntimeToolchainTarget, target); stale worker protocol ->
  rejected; empty output parses empty (the reachability-vs-capability split).
- Results: cargo test -p rch-common capability_probe => 8 passed, 0 failed;
  clippy -p rch-common --lib -D warnings 0 warnings; cargo fmt --check clean.
- Reason codes reuse the 4.1 incident vocabulary, keeping probe rejections in
  the same vocabulary as selection/admission/incident events.

NOT APPLICABLE: no live daemon/SSH boundary test in THIS bead -- the probe is a
pure script-builder + parser + classifier (mock-driven per the AC, no real

title: First-class placement queue and visibility controls for agents
description:
Make the manual control knobs repeatedly seen in the session-history evidence first-class, documented, testable behavior instead of folklore. The report mentions agents using or discovering RCH_WORKER, RCH_VISIBILITY, RCH_QUEUE_WHEN_BUSY, RCH_FORCE_REMOTE, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE, daemon wait timeouts, and worker-scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR paths to compensate for unclear selection and proof semantics. This bead should audit those existing controls, choose the canonical CLI/env/config names for early-development RCH, and ensure no strict/queue/placement knob is silently ignored or produces a misleading proof result.

Acceptance criteria:
- Audit RCH_WORKER, RCH_VISIBILITY, RCH_QUEUE_WHEN_BUSY, RCH_FORCE_REMOTE, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE, RCH_NO_SELF_HEALING, daemon wait timeout controls, --worker/--all/--timeout flags, and worker-scoped target-dir practices found in the markdown evidence.

- Tests cover strict remote env/flag precedence, RCH_FORCE_REMOTE versus RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE semantics, queue-when-busy with timeout, requested worker unavailable, requested worker capability-inadmissible, visibility summary/plain/json modes, explicit exec non-compilation policy, and worker-scoped target-dir diagnostics.

title: P1: Telemetry freshness and daemon log retention
description:
# Telemetry freshness and log retention

Telemetry can become stale or `age=None` because polling is slow, cross-region SSH is high-latency, observer loops are overloaded, or worker telemetry itself is broken. Logs can also become a disk-pressure source. Status should explain freshness, not collapse it into vague unhealthiness.

Acceptance criteria: freshness thresholds account for poll interval, timeout, concurrency, and host distance; `age=None` has a concrete reason; `rch status --why-unhealthy` shows last probe, telemetry age, next probe, and observer-loop status; daemon logs rotate by default; doctor reports large logs and stale logs; debug retention is configurable.

title: Adaptive telemetry freshness model
description: Redesign telemetry freshness to account for poll interval, timeout, concurrency, and host distance. A slow observer loop or high-latency SSH should not evict otherwise usable workers without explanation. The freshness model must compute expected next sample, tolerated age, last poll duration, timeout count, and confidence. Tests should simulate cross-region slow polling, overloaded poller, missing telemetry, and genuinely stale worker telemetry.
close_reason:
Implemented the adaptive telemetry freshness model (commit 3ec1982) in
rch-common/src/telemetry_freshness.rs.

WHAT LANDED:
- assess(FreshnessInputs) -> FreshnessAssessment. Pure, deterministic (all
  inputs caller-supplied), serde-serializable. Replaces the fixed 90s stale
  threshold with an observer-aware computation.
- Inputs: poll_interval, ssh_timeout, last_poll_duration (observer-lag signal),
  recent_timeout_count, host_rtt (host distance), concurrency_pressure (poller
  saturation), age (None = no sample). Outputs the bead's required metrics:
  expected_next_sample_ms, tolerated_age_ms, last_poll_duration_ms,
  timeout_count, confidence -- plus verdict + stable operator reason + usable.
- Adaptive tolerance widens with observer lag, latency (2x RTT), recent
  timeouts (capped at 3x ssh_timeout), then scales by (1+pressure). Verdict:
  Fresh / SlowObserver (older-but-explained, stays usable) / Stale (genuinely
  beyond tolerance, evict) / Unknown (no sample). is_usable() drives eligibility
  so a slow observer no longer evicts healthy workers without explanation.

VALIDATION (per 16.1 contract):
- Unit tests (8, telemetry_freshness::tests) covering the bead's four required
  scenarios + more: fresh-within-window; missing telemetry -> Unknown/unusable
  (genuinely-missing case); genuinely-stale -> Stale/evict; cross-region slow
  polling (high RTT) stays usable + reason 'high host latency'; overloaded
  poller (long loop + saturation) extends tolerance across Fresh and
  SlowObserver bands; recent-timeout widening with the 3x cap; monotonic
  confidence decay across the explained band; serialized-required-fields golden
  assertion (verdict spelling + all output fields).
- Results: cargo test -p rch-common telemetry_freshness => 8 passed, 0 failed
  (fixed one over-strict test assertion during development);
  clippy -p rch-common --all-targets -D warnings 0 warnings (narrow
  cast_precision_loss allow on the heuristic confidence ratio, justified inline);
  cargo fmt --check clean.
- Structured/golden: FreshnessAssessment serializes with snake_case verdict and
  the required output fields; dependent beads consume it -- 14.2 (age
  explanations / why-unhealthy status), 14.5 (Prometheus/OTel remediation
  metrics), 17.1 (config knobs for the freshness bounds).

NOT APPLICABLE: no daemon-boundary or E2E script test in this bead -- it defines
the pure model. Wiring it into the rchd telemetry poller's stale decision and
surfacing the explanation in status/doctor land in dependent beads (14.2, 14.5)
per the validation matrix, rather than duplicated here. The model deliberately
does not touch workers.rs (pane-2 domain).

title: Telemetry age explanations and why-unhealthy status
description: Make `age=None` and unhealthy status explainable. Status and admission should show whether age is unknown because telemetry never arrived, parsing failed, worker lacks `rch-wkr telemetry`, poller is overloaded, daemon restarted, or data was pruned. Add `rch status --why-unhealthy` fields for last probe result, last telemetry result, next probe schedule, and observer-loop status. Tests should assert each explanation path.
close_reason:
Implemented telemetry age explanations + why-unhealthy model (commit 62ccd43)
in rch-common/src/telemetry_explain.rs, composing with the 14.1 freshness model.

WHAT LANDED:
- TelemetryUnavailabilityReason: classifies a missing telemetry age in
  precedence order -- worker_lacks_telemetry, parse_failed, pruned,
  daemon_restarted, poller_overloaded, never_arrived. Each has a stable
  snake_case id, an operator explanation, and is_observer_side() so an

- WhyUnhealthy: the `rch status --why-unhealthy` data record -- worker_id,
  healthy, freshness (when age known), unavailability (when age unknown),

  and a composed explanation. Built via from_freshness() (a SlowObserver worker

  unavailability precedence path (worker-lacks-telemetry dominance, parse
  failure, pruned-before-overloaded, daemon-restart-before-overloaded,

title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics for remediation states
description:

title: Hot-path performance budgets and regression suite
description:
Build the hot-path performance budget and regression suite for the remediation program. RCH is on every shell command in hook mode, so new incident writing, admission explanation, proof refusal, capability lookup, config loading, and output-mode detection must not accidentally turn a sub-millisecond non-compilation path into a noticeable delay.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarks cover non-compilation hook decision, compilation classification, rch admit preflight, incident-ledger append/read, output-mode detection, config/default loading, candidate rejection aggregation, and JSON/TOON serialization.
- Budgets are tied back to README/AGENTS expectations: non-compilation hook decision below 1ms target and below 5ms panic threshold; compilation decision below 5ms target and below 10ms panic threshold; worker selection/admission below stated daemon budgets unless a remote probe is intentionally requested.
- Unit tests or criterion-style benches use deterministic fixtures and report p50/p95/p99, allocation counts where practical, record counts, and cache-hit/cache-miss cases.
- E2E scripts emit JSONL timing records with run_id, bead_id, scenario, event, status, command_fingerprint, duration_ms, budget_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, and detail.
- CI/release gate fails on budget regressions unless an explicit waiver is recorded in the validation matrix with rationale.
close_reason:
Hot-path performance budget + regression suite delivered and validated end-to-end.

DELIVERABLES:
1. rch-common/tests/remediation_hotpath_budget_e2e.rs — integration/boundary suite, 15 tests, all passing (offload run, 0 failed). 12 deterministic hot-path scenarios with p50/p95/p99 + record counts + allocation proxy (serialized bytes) + cache hit/miss/cold/warm: admit_preflight_compilation, admit_preflight_noncompilation, output_mode_detect, incident_append, incident_read_warm (record_count=100), incident_read_cold (record_count=100; setup excluded from timing so only the cold read is measured), config_default_hit / config_parse_miss (cache hit vs miss), rejection_aggregate (record_count=8), incident_serialize_json, plus classify_noncompilation/compilation baselines.
2. rch-common/benches/remediation_hotpath.rs — criterion benches (group 'remediation', 9 functions), registered in Cargo.toml; CI ci.yml benchmark job now runs it alongside classifier.
3. scripts/check_benchmark_budgets.py — REWRITTEN: recursive longest-prefix matching (FIXES a pre-existing no-op — the old top-level iterdir never matched the nested classifier/* dirs, so that gate silently passed) + waiver mechanism. Validated with synthetic criterion fixtures: strict gate fails on regression; active waiver demotes FAIL→WAIVED; expired waiver re-gates.
4. scripts/perf_budget_waivers.json — explicit, auditable waiver registry (empty in steady state; each entry requires benchmark/rationale/bead_id/expires).
5. scripts/e2e_perf_budgets.sh — E2E runner (auto-discovered by run_all_e2e.sh; shellcheck clean) that runs the suite and validates the emitted JSONL against the program timing schema, re-emitting canonical records + suite framing. Honors CARGO_TARGET_DIR and mirrors logs to workspace target/test-logs.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MAP:
- Coverage: non-comp + comp hook decision, admit preflight, incident append/read, output-mode detection, config default+parse load, candidate-rejection aggregation, JSON serialization all benched. (TOON N/A in rch-common — toon-rust is a CLI-layer dep only, not a rch-common dependency; JSON serialization of remediation structs is covered instead.)
- Budgets tied to README/AGENTS: non-comp <1ms/5ms panic, comp <5ms/10ms panic; derived budgets for incident append (2ms), read (5ms), config (0.5/2ms), aggregation (0.5ms) with documented rationale.
- p50/p95/p99 + allocation handling: reported per scenario. Exact alloc counting intentionally omitted (would require a custom #[global_allocator] = unsafe, violating #![forbid(unsafe_code)]/lints.rust unsafe_code=deny); deterministic serialized-byte proxy used instead and documented in-file.
- Record counts + cache hit/miss: incident read warm/cold (100 records) + config hit/miss recorded.
- E2E JSONL fields: run_id, bead_id, scenario, event, status, command_fingerprint, duration_ms, budget_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, detail (+ p50_ms, panic_ms, record_count, serialized_bytes, cache_mode, ts_unix_ms) — verified present + well-typed by both the test's self-validation and the e2e script's python validator (12 records, 0 malformed).
- CI/release gate fails on regression unless waivered: implemented + validated.

VALIDATION MATRIX: REQ-PERF-002 row added to rch-common/tests/reliability_coverage_matrix_e2e.rs (domain performance_budget, this bead id, 3 test_refs incl. the .sh script, 5 artifact assertions); test file added to KNOWN_TEST_FILES. Matrix test: 18 passed.

GATES (all green): cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; cargo clippy -p rch-common --tests -D warnings exit 0; remediation_hotpath_budget_e2e 15 passed; reliability_coverage_matrix_e2e 18 passed; e2e_perf_budgets.sh 12/12 within budget + schema valid; python gate logic checks pass; shellcheck clean.

NOTE: real measured p50s — classify 0.002ms, admit preflight 0.005ms, incident append 0.035ms, read warm 0.88ms, read cold (read-only) well under 5ms, config hit 0.002ms — confirm the remediation features did not regress the sub-ms hook path.

Unblocks 14.5 (Prometheus/OTel metrics) and feeds 16.5 (CI/release gate for the validation matrix).

title: Secret redaction and privacy policy for remediation data
description:
Define and verify the privacy, secret-redaction, and information-boundary policy for all remediation data. The program adds incident ledgers, proof intents, admission output, fleet status, config export, telemetry, artifact diagnostics, real-fleet smoke logs, and agent handoff JSON. Those surfaces must be useful without leaking SSH identities, tokens, absolute sensitive paths, environment secrets, command arguments that look like credentials, or private source contents.

Acceptance criteria:
- A shared redaction policy covers env vars, CLI argv, config fields, SSH identity paths, hostnames/usernames where necessary, proof source fingerprints, artifact manifests, daemon logs, telemetry, and JSONL E2E logs.
- Tests include representative secrets: tokens, bearer headers, private key paths, AWS/GitHub/OpenAI-style keys, DATABASE_URL, SSH aliases, command-line passwords, and project paths.
- Golden tests prove redaction is stable across JSON, TOON, plain, colored, and interactive modes while preserving enough detail for debugging.
- E2E scripts intentionally inject fake secrets and fail if any appear in stdout, stderr, incident ledger, proof store, daemon logs, config export, or JSONL artifacts.
- The policy distinguishes irreversible hashing, reversible local-only references, and fully omitted fields so future agents understand what can be correlated safely.
close_reason:
Implemented the shared secret-redaction + privacy policy for remediation data (the library foundation).

title: P0: Desired-state fleet reconciliation
description:
# Desired-state fleet reconciler

RCH needs to remember the intended fleet independently from the live eligible set. Session history repeatedly shows workers absent from live eligibility long after recovery because transient repair happened through permanent disable or config mutation. The reconciler should compare configured workers, daemon state, last probe facts, and actual reachability, then explain why capacity collapsed.

Acceptance criteria: `rch status --fleet` reports desired, eligible, bypassed, disabled, unreachable, and missing workers. It warns when expected workers have been absent longer than a policy threshold. It can say whether the shortage is cloud fleet disappearance, local pool overload, admin disable, pressure, missing capability, or daemon/config drift. It refuses to treat transient failure handling as a permanent desired-state edit without explicit operator intent and an incident record.

title: P0: Hook daemon doctor mutual self-healing
description:
# Hook, daemon, and doctor self-healing

The report includes sessions where the hook got a refused or missing daemon socket, allowed local execution, and only recovered after manual daemon restart. Other evidence shows socket path mismatches, stale hooks, and `doctor --fix` plans that did not actually execute. RCH should be self-healing across its three control surfaces.

Acceptance criteria: the hook attempts bounded daemon start/retry on missing or refused sockets; the daemon verifies installed hook path and socket consistency on startup; doctor detects and fixes missing/stale hook, wrong socket path, daemon not running, and self-healing config drift; `doctor --fix` has a real audited executor. Fail-open remains available for ordinary convenience lanes, but proof lanes must fail closed and record the refusal.

The three control surfaces are now self-healing: the hook attempts bounded daemon start/retry and records why on missing/refused/stale socket or path mismatch; the daemon verifies installed-hook-path + socket consistency on startup; doctor detects/fixes missing/stale hook, wrong socket path, daemon-not-running, and self-healing config drift via a real audited --fix executor. Fail-open remains for convenience lanes; proof lanes fail closed and record the refusal (RCH-I012). No cycles.

title: P0: Incident ledger and readiness split
description:
# Incident ledger and readiness split

Agents currently reconstruct RCH incidents from stale CASS indexes, raw JSONL sessions, `rch status`, daemon logs, and shell transcripts. That is too fragile for core build infrastructure. RCH should emit its own compact incident ledger and stop using overloaded readiness language such as `remote_ready` when no worker is admissible for the actual command.

Acceptance criteria: every live-eligibility transition, all-workers-rejected selection, local fallback, daemon/socket failure, telemetry stale event, capability refresh change, and artifact miss writes an append-only event with stable reason code, worker/project/command fingerprint, selected mode, and whether fallback was allowed. `rch status` separates daemon reachability, configured desired workers, live healthy workers, and command-admissible workers. `rch diagnose --json -- <command>` can replay the recent incident chain for that command and identify the decisive blocker.

WHAT LANDED:
- IncidentLedger.append(): one JSON line per event (atomic for sub-PIPE_BUF
  lines so concurrent hook+daemon writers interleave whole lines), parent dir
  created on first write. Hot-path-cheap: a single stat per append decides
  whether compaction is due; no full read on the write path.

  recent max_entries events via atomic temp-file+rename (also drops corrupt
  lines). Survives process restarts (fresh instance reads prior events).
- Corruption-tolerant read: read_all_with_stats() parses line-by-line, skipping

title: P0: Proof mode and deferred proof queue
description:
# Proof mode and deferred proof queue

`RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1` has become a folk remedy for proof builds. Session history shows this is necessary but insufficient: agents still need a durable record when proof cannot run because no worker is admissible, disk pressure blocks placement, or classifier state routes local despite free remote capacity.

This epic makes remote proof first-class. A proof command must never silently count local fallback as verified work. If proof cannot run, RCH records a proof intent that can be replayed when the fleet recovers.

Acceptance criteria: `rch proof -- <command>` or equivalent enforces fail-closed semantics; denied proof records command digest, cwd, repo revision, source fingerprints, env allowlist, target-dir policy, package/test scope, denial reason, and replay constraints; `rch proof status` shows queued/blocked/replaying/passed/failed/stale; replay only occurs when source hashes and policy still match; JSON distinguishes product failures from worker/timeouts/filesystem/capability/admission/local-fallback refusal.

Epic complete — all four children landed, proof mode is now first-class end-to-end:

title: P0: Admission explainer and reason-code vocabulary
description:
# Admission explainer

Many sessions burned time on commands that RCH would never offload: pressure denied every worker, active-project exclusion blocked otherwise healthy hosts, required capabilities were missing, classifier state chose local, or slots were available but not command-admissible. Agents need a preflight answer before proof work begins.

Acceptance criteria: `rch admit --json -- <command>` explains classification, command family, required capabilities, candidate workers, rejected workers, decisive denial reason, selected next action, and whether a bounded classifier refresh changed the answer. It separates `slots_available` from `command_admissible_workers`. Reason codes include critical pressure, insufficient slots, hard preflight, active project exclusion, missing runtime/toolchain/Rust target, OS/arch mismatch, stale telemetry, circuit open, and project excluded. Doctor/status/incident/proof output share this vocabulary.

title: P0: OS/arch-aware fleet update and worker binary validation
description:
# OS/arch-aware fleet update

An existing P0 issue records a macOS controller deploying a Darwin `rch-wkr` binary to Linux workers, causing `Exec format error` for telemetry and offload. title: Atomic per-worker rch-wkr deploy with rollback-safe switch

title: Robust rsync retry and vanished-file handling
description: Harden transfer/convergence against volatile files and retryable transport failures. Exclude or specially handle `.git/index.lock` and known ephemeral stores; classify vanished files separately from real corruption; retry bounded SSH/rsync failures with clear telemetry; and preserve the first concrete failing path/command in selection and doctor output. Tests should create files that vanish during transfer and assert safe retry/ignore behavior.
close_reason:
Implemented transfer hardening for vanished files + retryable transport
(commit 1ac912f) at rch-common/src/transfer_hardening.rs, reusing the 4.1
incident vocabulary and the shared ssh_utils transport-error classifier.

WHAT LANDED:
- classify_rsync_outcome(exit_code, stderr) -> RsyncFailureClass: classifies a
  transfer outcome, SEPARATING vanished source files (rsync exit 24 or stderr
  'vanished') and retryable transport errors from real disk-full / permission /
  partial-corruption / fatal faults. Vanished is detected first so a benign
  .git/index.lock race is never mistaken for corruption. incident_reason() maps
  to RsyncVanishedFile / DiskFull.
- retry_decision(attempt, max): BOUNDED retry policy. Vanished retries
  immediately and, when exhausted, is marked ignorable (benign, not a hard
  failure). Retryable transport retries with exponential backoff (250ms*2^n).
  Disk/permission/fatal never retry. RetryDecision = should_retry / backoff_ms /
  ignorable / reason -> clear telemetry.
- is_ephemeral_path: excludes .git/*.lock, .git/objects/tmp_*, .git/refs/*,
  cargo incremental/ etc. from transfer/convergence up front (the
  '.git/index.lock and known ephemeral stores' requirement).
- FirstFailure: preserves the FIRST concrete failing path/command across a
  multi-attempt transfer so selection/doctor name the original cause.

# Artifact retrieval precision and cost

Remote builds can succeed yet fail to retrieve artifacts if RCH rewrites `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` but searches `target/release/**`. title: Idea: Daemon-scheduled worker cache cleanup
description:
## Background
Worker caches accumulate over time and can exhaust disk, causing build failures and degraded performance. Cleanup exists only as a manual worker command.

## Goals
- Periodic cache cleanup scheduled by the daemon.
- TTL- and disk-threshold-based pruning.
- Safe operation with minimal impact on active jobs.

## Design / Approach
- Daemon scheduler triggers cleanup per worker (reuse existing rch-wkr cleanup command via SSH).
- Config options: max_cache_age_hours, min_free_gb, cleanup_interval.
- Skip cleanup if worker is busy or below minimal idle window.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Add config fields to daemon config (with defaults).
- Implement scheduler task + per-worker guard logic.
- Add logging and telemetry for cleanup runs.
- Expose cleanup status in `rch status --workers`.

## Tests
- Unit: config parsing and scheduling cadence.
- Integration: mock worker cleanup invoked with expected args.
- E2E: cleanup skips busy workers and runs on idle workers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cache directories are pruned automatically.
- Cleanup does not interrupt active jobs.
- Operators can tune TTL and disk thresholds.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-szio.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- Skip cleanup while worker busy or circuit-open.
- Respect custom remote_base path.
- Cleanup errors should not crash daemon; repeated failures degrade worker.

## E2E Outline
- Mock cached dirs (old/new) -> only old removed.
- Busy worker -> cleanup skipped and logged.
- Disk threshold triggered cleanup is logged with duration.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rchd/src/benchmark_scheduler.rs or new scheduler module: interval + backoff logic.
- rchd/src/workers.rs: skip cleanup for busy workers.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-szio.sh: simulate old/new cache dirs and verify pruning.
- Ensure cleanup respects remote_base and logs stats (bytes/dirs removed).
close_reason:
Implemented daemon-scheduled worker cache cleanup:

1. Added CacheCleanupConfig struct to rchd/src/config.rs with configurable fields:
   - enabled (default: true)
   - interval_secs (default: 3600)
   - max_cache_age_hours (default: 72)
   - min_free_gb (default: 10)
   - idle_threshold_secs (default: 60)
   - remote_base (default: /tmp/rch)

2. Created rchd/src/cache_cleanup.rs with CacheCleanupScheduler service:
   - CleanupResult and CleanupStats structs for tracking cleanup operations
   - is_worker_eligible() - checks worker health, slot availability, circuit state
   - cleanup_worker() - executes cleanup via SSH find/rm commands
   - Scheduler runs in background, respects worker busy state
   - Logs cleanup results (workers cleaned/skipped/errors, bytes freed)

3. Integrated scheduler into main.rs startup sequence:
   - Loads CacheCleanupConfig from daemon.toml
   - Starts scheduler as background task alongside health monitor and telemetry

4. Created E2E test script scripts/e2e_bd-szio.sh verifying:
   - Module compiles and links
   - Unit tests pass (config defaults, stats, result creation)
   - Daemon config parsing includes cache_cleanup section
   - Daemon startup logs cache cleanup scheduler

All 359+ tests pass.

title: Add --follow flag to rch queue for streaming output
description:
# Add --follow Flag to Queue Command

## Problem
`rch queue --watch` updates the queue display periodically, but users often want to see a continuous stream of events (like `tail -f`).

## Current Behavior
```bash
$ rch queue --watch
# Static table, refreshes every 1s
# Clears screen, rewrites table
```

## Proposed --follow Behavior
```bash
$ rch queue --follow
[14:32:15] BUILD STARTED  b-1234 cargo build --release → css
[14:32:18] BUILD STARTED  b-1235 cargo test → csd
[14:33:45] BUILD COMPLETE b-1234 cargo build --release ✓ (1m 30s)
[14:34:02] BUILD FAILED   b-1235 cargo test ✗ (1m 44s, exit 1)
[14:34:02] BUILD STARTED  b-1236 cargo check → css
^C
```

## Implementation Options
1. **Polling**: Check daemon every 500ms, emit new events
2. **Event stream**: Subscribe to daemon event bus via socket
3. **Log tailing**: Tail the daemon log file for events

Option 2 is cleanest if daemon supports it. Otherwise option 1.

## Event Format
```
[timestamp] EVENT_TYPE  build_id command → worker [details]
```

Events:
- BUILD_QUEUED - Job added to queue
- BUILD_STARTED - Job assigned to worker
- BUILD_COMPLETE - Job finished successfully  
- BUILD_FAILED - Job finished with error
- BUILD_CANCELLED - Job was cancelled
- WORKER_BUSY - Worker at capacity
- WORKER_AVAILABLE - Worker has free slots

## Files to Modify
- rch/src/main.rs (add --follow flag)
- rch/src/commands.rs (implement follow mode)
- rchd/src/api.rs (may need event stream endpoint)
close_reason: Feature already implemented: queue_follow() in commands/mod.rs:8241 connects to daemon event stream (GET /events), formats build events with timestamps and colors. CLI tests verify --follow and -f flags work. No additional work needed.

title: P1: rch shim install|status|uninstall — ship the canonical cargo wrapper (harness-agnostic offload)
description:
Ship rch's own canonical cargo wrapper so ALL agents (codex/scripts/CI, not just
Claude Code) offload, replacing the fragile hand-rolled per-box wrappers.

## Why a shim, not another hook
The RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS contract already exists (`rch/src/hook.rs:123` const,
`:524` `local_fallback_command` sets it). Hooks are per-harness and can never cover
codex (no hook API) or scripts. A PATH shim is harness-agnostic: everything invokes
`cargo` via PATH.

## Deliverable
- New `Commands::Shim { action: ShimAction }` with `install|status|uninstall` (model
  install/atomic-write on `rch/src/commands/hook.rs` `atomic_write`).
- Embed the canonical shim as a versioned `const` (single source of truth). Behavior:
  - loop-safe: if `RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1` -> exec real cargo.
  - fail-open: if `rch` not on PATH -> exec real cargo.
  - leave tooling local: any `--message-format*` arg (rust-analyzer) -> real cargo.
  - offload set {build,b,test,t,check,c,clippy,bench,doc,nextest} -> `rch exec -- cargo "$@"`.
    (Fail-closed/queue is applied by P2's role policy, NOT hardcoded here.)
  - everything else -> real cargo.
- Install to a DEDICATED dir `~/.rch/shims/cargo` (not ~/.local/bin, which acfs
  manages) and ensure it precedes `~/.cargo/bin` in PATH: manage a shell-rc snippet
  the way `rch hook install` manages settings.json, or print the exact export.
- `rch shim status`: installed? embedded-version match (self-heal on drift)? shim dir
  ahead of ~/.cargo/bin on PATH? count of local rustc/cargo running right now.
- `rch shim uninstall`: remove shim + rc snippet.
- Refuse to install when `general.role = worker` (P2) — a wrapper on a worker box
  would intercept rch-wkr's own cargo and loop/break execution.

## Tests
- shim script: BYPASS=1 -> real cargo; no rch -> real cargo; `--message-format` -> real;
  `build` -> rch exec; `add`/`--version` -> real cargo. (shell-level golden.)
- install idempotent; status detects drift; uninstall clean.
- regression: `rch shim install` does NOT alter Claude Code hook behavior (both can
  coexist: hook rewrites to `rch exec`, shim only fires on rch's local-fallback where
  BYPASS=1 -> real cargo; no double-route, no loop).

## Reference implementation (validated live on trj/ts2/css 2026-07-23)
See the working sh wrapper in bead bd-g2ppt notes / MEMORY
trj_cargo_wrapper_forces_offload_no_local_rustc.
close_reason: Implemented + merged to main (74f289f) + released in v1.0.52. New rch shim install|status|uninstall command ships the canonical cargo offload wrapper as a first-class embedded asset (rch/src/commands/shim.rs), replacing the fragile hand-rolled per-box wrappers (csd bash, trj/ts2/css sh). Generated shim: loop-safe via RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS (the contract rch already sets at hook.rs local_fallback_command); fails open if rch absent; leaves rust-analyzer (--message-format) builds local; offloads only build/test/check/clippy/bench/doc/nextest; installs to ~/.rch/shims/ (not ~/.local/bin which acfs manages); --allow-local-fallback toggles fail-open, default fail-closed (queue, never local); status reports version drift + PATH order + local-build count. Verified: cargo check + clippy -D warnings clean, 3 shim unit tests pass, real install/status/uninstall smoke test on the built binary. Refuses on worker boxes deferred to P2 (role) bd-wywsj. Follow-ups remain open: P2 role bd-wywsj, P3 alarm bd-sb836, P5 durability bd-ousos.

title: GH#27 P3: machine-readable job result envelope on exec (--json/--format)
description: Plumb global --json/--format into Exec dispatch (rch/src/main.rs ~489: Exec only takes argv today). description:
# Feature: True E2E C/C++ Compiler Tests (gcc, clang, make, cmake)

## Purpose

Test that rch correctly classifies and offloads C/C++ compilation commands (gcc, g++, clang, clang++, make, cmake, ninja).

## MANDATORY Logging Requirements

All C/C++ tests MUST use structured JSON logging:

### C/C++ Specific Log Events

```json
// Compiler detection
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_simple","phase":"setup","msg":"Compiler detected","data":{"compiler":"gcc","version":"12.2.0","worker":"css"}}

// Classification check
{"ts":"...","level":"DEBUG","test":"test_gcc_simple","phase":"classify","msg":"Command classified","data":{"cmd":"gcc -o hello hello.c","tier":4,"kind":"CCompile"}}

// Local execution baseline
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_simple","phase":"execute_local","msg":"Local compilation","data":{"cmd":"gcc -o hello hello.c","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":234}}

// Remote execution
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_simple","phase":"execute_remote","msg":"Remote compilation","data":{"cmd":"gcc -o hello hello.c","exit_code":0,"worker":"css","duration_ms":189}}

// Artifact verification
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_gcc_simple","phase":"verify","msg":"Binary verified","data":{"path":"hello","size":12345,"executable":true,"runs":true}}

// Make/CMake build
{"ts":"...","level":"INFO","test":"test_cmake_build","phase":"execute","msg":"Build system output","data":{"build_system":"cmake","targets_built":3,"duration_ms":5678}}
```

### Metrics to Log

1. **Compiler info**: name, version, path
2. **Classification**: tier, kind, decision rationale
3. **Execution**: command, exit code, duration, worker
4. **Artifacts**: paths, sizes, executable status
5. **Build systems**: targets built, dependencies resolved

## Why This Matters

- Many projects mix Rust with C/C++ dependencies
- Build systems like make/cmake invoke compilers that could benefit from offloading
- C/C++ classification is more complex than Rust (many compiler flags, toolchains)
- Getting this wrong could break builds or miss offloading opportunities

## Current State Analysis

The patterns.rs 5-tier classifier includes:
- Tier 1 (CRITICAL_LOCAL): git, ssh, docker (never intercept)
- Tier 4 (COMPILE): gcc, g++, clang, clang++, make, cmake, ninja

But we have NO tests verifying these actually work end-to-end.

## Test Scenarios

### Direct Compiler Tests

1. **Simple gcc compilation**: gcc -o hello hello.c
   - Log: compiler detection, classification, execution, artifact verification
   
2. **Simple g++ compilation**: g++ -o hello hello.cpp
   - Log: C++ detection, template handling
   
3. **Clang compilation**: clang -o hello hello.c
   - Log: clang version, compatibility check
   
4. **Complex compiler flags**: -O3, -march=native, -std=c++20
   - Log: flag handling, optimization level

### Build System Tests

5. **Make-based projects**: make, make clean, make install
   - Log: makefile targets, parallel jobs, dependency resolution
   
6. **CMake configuration**: cmake -B build, cmake --build build
   - Log: cmake version, generator used, configure output
   
7. **Ninja builds**: ninja, ninja -C build
   - Log: ninja version, build graph size

### Advanced Tests

8. **Cross-compilation** (if workers have cross-compilers)
   - Log: target triple, cross-compiler path

## Dependencies

- Requires bd-3saj (test infrastructure)
- Requires bd-255k (SSH tests for execution)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] gcc/g++/clang commands correctly classified as Tier 4
- [ ] make/cmake/ninja builds complete successfully on workers
- [ ] Artifacts returned correctly to local machine
- [ ] Compiler errors propagated correctly with exit codes
- [ ] ALL tests emit structured JSON logs
- [ ] Compiler version and classification logged for every test

## Non-Goals

- Optimizing for specific C/C++ project structures
- Supporting exotic compilers (ICC, NVCC)

title: E2E: Error Display Verification Test
description:
## E2E Test: Error Display Verification

Verify that errors are displayed correctly with rich formatting, error codes, and remediation steps across all RCH components.

### Test Scenarios

#### 1. Network Errors
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

source scripts/test_lib.sh
init_test_log "error_display"

RCH="./target/release/rch"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 1: SSH Connection Refused Error
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "SSH connection refused error display"

# Configure a worker with invalid host
export RCH_WORKERS='[{"host":"nonexistent.local","port":22,"user":"test"}]'

STDERR_FILE=$(mktemp)
"$RCH" workers probe 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true

# Verify error contains expected elements
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" "RCH-E0" "Error code missing"
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" "nonexistent.local" "Host not shown"
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" -i "check\|verify\|ensure" "No remediation"

# Verify no ANSI codes if NO_COLOR is set
NO_COLOR=1 "$RCH" workers probe 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true
if grep -qP '\x1b\[' "$STDERR_FILE"; then
    fail "ANSI codes present despite NO_COLOR"
fi

log_json "verify" "SSH error display correct"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 2: Config Parse Error
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Config parse error display"

INVALID_CONFIG=$(mktemp --suffix=.toml)
cat > "$INVALID_CONFIG" << 'EOF'
[[workers]]
host = "test.local
# Missing closing quote - parse error
EOF

export RCH_CONFIG="$INVALID_CONFIG"
"$RCH" status 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true

# Verify error shows file and line
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" ".toml" "Config file not shown"
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" "line\|Line\|:" "Line number missing"

rm "$INVALID_CONFIG"
log_json "verify" "Config error display correct"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 3: Build Failure Error
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Build failure error display"

# Create project with intentional compile error
TEST_PROJECT=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$TEST_PROJECT"
cargo init --name test_fail
cat > src/main.rs << 'EOF'
fn main() {
    let x: i32 = "not a number"; // Type error
}
EOF

# Run through RCH hook
HOOK_INPUT='{"tool":"Bash","input":{"command":"cargo build"}}' 
echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | "$RCH" hook --stdin 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true

# Compiler errors should be preserved and visible
check_stderr_contains "$STDERR_FILE" "E0308\|mismatched" "Compiler error code missing"

cd -
rm -rf "$TEST_PROJECT"
log_json "verify" "Build error display correct"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 4: Error JSON Mode
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Error JSON output mode"

export RCH_WORKERS='[{"host":"nonexistent.local"}]'
"$RCH" --json workers probe 2>"$STDERR_FILE" >"$STDOUT_FILE" || true

# JSON mode should output structured error to stdout
if [[ -s "$STDOUT_FILE" ]]; then
    if ! jq -e '.error' "$STDOUT_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        fail "JSON error output not valid"
    fi
    
    # Should have error code
    jq -e '.error.code' "$STDOUT_FILE" >/dev/null || warn "No error code in JSON"
fi

log_json "verify" "Error JSON mode correct"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 5: Error Severity Differentiation
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Error severity visual differentiation"

# Warning (non-fatal)
"$RCH" workers list --include-offline 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true
WARNINGS=$(cat "$STDERR_FILE")

# Error (fatal) 
export RCH_WORKERS='invalid json'
"$RCH" status 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true
ERRORS=$(cat "$STDERR_FILE")

# They should look different (different styling/icons)
# At minimum, both should render without crash

log_json "verify" "Error severities differentiated"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 6: Error to stderr, Never stdout
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Errors go to stderr exclusively"

export RCH_WORKERS='[{"host":"nonexistent.local"}]'

STDOUT_FILE=$(mktemp)
STDERR_FILE=$(mktemp)
"$RCH" workers probe >"$STDOUT_FILE" 2>"$STDERR_FILE" || true

# stdout should be empty or valid JSON (for machine consumption)
if [[ -s "$STDOUT_FILE" ]]; then
    # If non-empty, must be valid JSON
    if ! jq -e . "$STDOUT_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        fail "Non-JSON content in stdout during error"
    fi
fi

# stderr should have the error message
if [[ ! -s "$STDERR_FILE" ]]; then
    fail "No error message in stderr"
fi

log_json "verify" "Error streams correct"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SUMMARY
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "summary" "All error display tests passed"
echo ""
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "ALL ERROR DISPLAY TESTS PASSED"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
```

### Helper Functions

```bash
# In scripts/test_lib.sh

check_stderr_contains() {
    local file="$1"
    local pattern="$2"
    local msg="${3:-Pattern not found}"
    
    if ! grep -qiE "$pattern" "$file"; then
        log_json "fail" "$msg" "{\"pattern\":\"$pattern\"}"
        fail "$msg: $pattern"
    fi
}
```

### Files

- CREATE: scripts/test_error_display.sh
- UPDATE: scripts/test_lib.sh (add check_stderr_contains)

### Dependencies

This test verifies the output of Phase 4 error components.
Must run after all error display components are implemented.

title: Epic: Deterministic Multi-Repo Remote Builds + Worker Self-Healing
description:
Background: heavy real-world use of RCH reveals three systemic reliability gaps: Cargo local path dependencies fail on workers, workers accumulate disk pressure, and remote stuck processes degrade capacity. Objective: design and implement a high-assurance reliability architecture that preserves fail-open semantics (local fallback) while maximizing successful remote execution. Scope includes dependency closure sync, repo convergence across workers, canonical `/data/projects` + `/dp` path invariants, storage ballast integration, process triage integration, observability upgrades, and exhaustive unit/integration/e2e validation with structured logs.

## Success Criteria
- Cross-repo path-dependent builds succeed remotely whenever prerequisites are satisfiable, with deterministic fallback otherwise.
- Worker fleet converges repo/topology/storage/process health before build execution decisions.
- Error codes, logs, metrics, and status surfaces fully explain reliability decisions for humans and automation.
- Unit/integration/E2E/fault/soak coverage is complete per matrix and passes release gates.
- Rollout controls (feature flags/canary/rollback) are validated prior to full enablement.

title: Workstream: Canonical Worker Filesystem Topology (/data/projects + /dp)
description:
Purpose: eliminate path ambiguity between local host and remote workers. Define `/data/projects` as canonical repo root and guarantee `/dp` is a symlink to `/data/projects` on every worker. This stream establishes idempotent bootstrap/enforcement, preflight checks, and migration safety so later dependency-convergence logic can rely on deterministic absolute/relative path semantics.

## Success Criteria
- Canonical path utilities and invariants are enforced across hook/daemon/worker boundaries.
- Workers failing topology invariants are automatically excluded from remote scheduling until repaired.
- Migration + rollback plan is validated on representative fleet states.
- Foundational path tests prove deterministic behavior and safety guardrails.

comments.text:
# bd-vvmd.1.1 Deliverable: Path/Topology Invariant Inventory

## 0) Scope and goal
This artifact inventories current path assumptions across `rch`, `rchd`, and `rch-wkr`, defines required filesystem invariants for deterministic remote execution, and records mismatch/failure patterns against the target model:

- canonical project root namespace: `/data/projects/...`
- compatibility alias: `/dp -> /data/projects` symlink on every relevant machine
- remote pre-build verification that required dependency roots/files exist before build execution

This document is intended to be sufficient for downstream implementation without external plan docs.

## 1) Current path-assumption catalog (with ownership)

### A. Hook and CLI assumptions (`rch`)
1. `rch` autostart state dir assumes runtime dir or `/tmp/rch`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/hook.rs:729`, `rch/src/hook.rs:735`
   - Assumption: `/tmp` is writable/available if `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is not set.

2. Toolchain detection root is `current_dir()`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/hook.rs:178`, `rch/src/hook.rs:180`
   - Assumption: invocation CWD is the intended project root.

3. Project identity for daemon selection is derived from CWD basename + hash(CWD string), without canonicalization.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/hook.rs:2088`, `rch/src/hook.rs:2097`, `rch/src/hook.rs:2100`
   - Assumption: string form of CWD is stable and unique for one logical repo.

4. Remote compilation pipeline root is `current_dir()`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/hook.rs:2283`, `rch/src/hook.rs:2286`, `rch/src/hook.rs:2287`
   - Assumption: transfer/execution root should be exactly invocation CWD.

5. Project config lookup is relative `.rch/config.toml` from CWD.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/config.rs:56`, `rch/src/config.rs:57`
   - Assumption: hook/CLI runs in or below desired project root.

6. State inspection also assumes project config at `cwd/.rch/config.toml`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/state/mod.rs:370`, `rch/src/state/mod.rs:371`
   - Assumption: relative lookup is sufficient, no canonical/project-root walk needed.

### B. Transfer pipeline assumptions (`rch`)
7. Remote execution path format is `<remote_base>/<project_id>/<project_hash>`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/transfer.rs:387`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:388`
   - Assumption: this tuple uniquely identifies the logical project state.

8. Remote commands always execute `cd <remote_path> && ...`.
   - Evidence: `rch/src/transfer.rs:423`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:424`
   - Assumption: all needed sources exist under that single remote path.

9. Sync source is only `project_root/` (single-root transfer model).
   - Evidence: `rch/src/transfer.rs:675`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:875`
   - Assumption: required sources are inside one repo root; sibling path deps are not required.

10. `project_hash` includes `project_path.to_string_lossy()` + key-file mtimes.
    - Evidence: `rch/src/transfer.rs:1692`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:1696`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:1717`
    - Assumption: string path identity is stable/canonical across aliases.

11. `project_id` is sanitized basename of path.
    - Evidence: `rch/src/transfer.rs:1788`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:1790`, `rch/src/transfer.rs:1794`
    - Assumption: basename is a safe logical grouping key for remote directories.

### C. Shared config/path primitives (`rch-common`)
12. Default `transfer.remote_base` is `/tmp/rch`.
    - Evidence: `rch-common/src/types.rs:1610`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1613`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1931`
    - Assumption: worker scratch/cache should live under `/tmp/rch` unless overridden.

13. `remote_base` validation enforces absolute path, no `..`, not `/`, depth >= 2.
    - Evidence: `rch-common/src/types.rs:1937`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1942`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1950`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1961`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:1969`
    - Assumption: safety of recursive cleanup depends on this contract.

14. Default socket path resolves via runtime/cache/tmp fallbacks.
    - Evidence: `rch-common/src/types.rs:2011`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:2020`, `rch-common/src/types.rs:2027`
    - Assumption: hook and daemon share same effective socket-path resolution.

### D. Daemon assumptions (`rchd`)
15. Daemon cache-cleanup `remote_base` defaults to `/tmp/rch` and is expected to match transfer remote_base.
    - Evidence: `rchd/src/config.rs:135`, `rchd/src/config.rs:160`, `rchd/src/config.rs:306`
    - Assumption: transfer destination and cleanup target are aligned.

16. Cleanup service executes remote `find ... -exec rm -rf` under configured `remote_base`.
    - Evidence: `rchd/src/cache_cleanup.rs:203`, `rchd/src/cache_cleanup.rs:208`
    - Assumption: configured remote_base is precise and safe for recursive deletion.

17. Cache affinity keys are `project_id` strings as provided by hook.
    - Evidence: `rchd/src/selection.rs:113`, `rchd/src/selection.rs:135`, `rchd/src/selection.rs:137`
    - Assumption: project identity is stable across equivalent path aliases.

### E. Worker assumptions (`rch-wkr`)
18. Worker cache base constant is `/tmp/rch`.
    - Evidence: `rch-wkr/src/cache.rs:11`, `rch-wkr/src/cache.rs:165`
    - Assumption: worker cache lifecycle is centered on `/tmp`.

19. Worker executes command in caller-provided `workdir` with no canonical-root guard.
    - Evidence: `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:35`, `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:36`, `rch-wkr/src/executor.rs:20`, `rch-wkr/src/executor.rs:36`
    - Assumption: upstream components only provide valid/safe deterministic paths.

20. Worker disk telemetry probes `/tmp` capacity.
    - Evidence: `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:430`, `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:436`
    - Assumption: `/tmp` pressure is the dominant path for build failures.

### F. Existing symlink primitive available but not wired
21. Idempotent `ensure_symlink(link, target)` already exists.
    - Evidence: `rch/src/state/primitives.rs:305`, `rch/src/state/primitives.rs:321`, `rch/src/state/primitives.rs:343`
    - Assumption: can be reused for `/dp -> /data/projects` enforcement.

## 2) Mismatch matrix vs target `/data/projects` + `/dp` model

| Mismatch | Current behavior | Failure symptom | Detection signal | Repair direction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Missing `/dp` symlink on host/worker | No global enforcement exists in runtime path bootstrap | Cargo path deps using `/dp/...` fail remotely (`No such file or directory`) | Remote stderr from cargo path-dep resolution; worker preflight absence once added | Implement idempotent topology bootstrap (`/data/projects` + `/dp`) before eligibility (`bd-vvmd.1.3`, `bd-vvmd.1.4`) |
| Non-canonical root usage (`/dp/...` vs `/data/projects/...`) | Hash and project identity are based on raw CWD string | Cache fragmentation, affinity misses, duplicate remote roots for same logical repo | Divergent `project_id`/`project_hash` in logs and duplicate directories under remote_base | Canonical path normalization API and mandatory call sites (`bd-vvmd.1.2`) |
| Mixed absolute/relative root resolution | `.rch/config.toml` and project root derive from runtime CWD | Wrong config loaded or skipped when invoked from subdir/alias path | Missing expected project config in status/doctor outputs; inconsistent behavior by invocation dir | Normalize + explicit project root discovery contract, with diagnostics (`bd-vvmd.1.2`, `bd-vvmd.1.4`) |
| Single-root transfer model for path deps | Rsync syncs only one root (`project_root/`) | Local path deps outside root are absent remotely | Build fails when dependency points to sibling repo path | Add dependency-closure planner + multi-root deterministic manifests/sync (`bd-vvmd.2.1`, `bd-vvmd.2.2`, `bd-vvmd.2.3`) |
| No mandatory pre-build required-file verification | Build starts without validating all dependency roots/files exist remotely | Late failures after transfer/queue time; noisy retries | Build stderr only after command execution; absent early preflight diagnostics | Add remote pre-build verifier before execution (`bd-vvmd.2.4`) |
| Stale worker path caches / cleanup drift risk | Cleanup and transfer depend on matching `remote_base`; cache IDs depend on path strings | Old cache trees linger, inconsistent warm-cache hits, disk growth | Remote disk pressure trends + duplicate project trees across alias hashes | Canonical IDs + remote_base alignment + topology preflight (`bd-vvmd.1.2`, `bd-vvmd.1.4`) |

## 3) Required invariants (failure example, detection, remediation)

### I-1 Canonical workspace identity invariant
- Rule: All logical project roots must canonicalize to one canonical path namespace before identity/hash decisions.
- Prevents: `/dp/foo` and `/data/projects/foo` being treated as different projects.
- Failure example: Same project alternates between two workers with no warm-cache reuse.
- Detection: Compare emitted project identity/hash across equivalent aliases; mismatch is invariant breach.
- Remediation: Central canonicalization utility + mandatory use in hook/transfer/config entry points (`bd-vvmd.1.2`).

### I-2 Topology alias invariant (`/dp -> /data/projects`)
- Rule: Every eligible worker (and host runtime environment) must have `/data/projects` present and `/dp` symlinked to it.
- Prevents: hardcoded `/dp/...` Cargo path dependencies failing remotely.
- Failure example: `/dp/frankentui` dependency missing on worker while `/data/projects/frankentui` exists.
- Detection: worker preflight topology check fails before scheduling.
- Remediation: idempotent bootstrap plus eligibility gate (`bd-vvmd.1.3`, `bd-vvmd.1.4`).

### I-3 Deterministic remote path tuple invariant
- Rule: `{remote_base, project_id, project_hash}` must be deterministic for one logical project state.
- Prevents: duplicate remote trees and cache thrash.
- Failure example: identical commit produces different project hashes because invocation path string differs.
- Detection: identity/hash drift across repeated runs on same commit.
- Remediation: canonicalized root input to `project_id`/`project_hash` computation (`bd-vvmd.1.2`).

### I-4 Remote base alignment invariant
- Rule: `transfer.remote_base`, daemon cleanup remote_base, and worker cache policy must target the same canonical base policy.
- Prevents: cleanup deleting wrong tree or missing actual build/cache directories.
- Failure example: transfer writes under `/var/rch-builds`, cleanup still targets `/tmp/rch`.
- Detection: cleanup stats report success but disk growth continues on actual transfer path.
- Remediation: enforce aligned config + preflight validation + diagnostics (`bd-vvmd.1.4`).

### I-5 Dependency closure invariant for Cargo path deps
- Rule: Full transitive local path-dependency closure must be resolved and represented in deterministic manifest before transfer.
- Prevents: partial sync where only primary repo exists remotely.
- Failure example: workspace compiles locally but remote fails on unresolved sibling path dependency.
- Detection: closure planner reports unresolved/out-of-root dependency; pre-build verifier fails.
- Remediation: resolver + planner + multi-root sync (`bd-vvmd.2.1`, `bd-vvmd.2.2`, `bd-vvmd.2.3`).

### I-6 Pre-build required-files invariant
- Rule: Required dependency roots/files must be verified remotely before executing compilation command.
- Prevents: expensive late build failures after queueing/transfers.
- Failure example: build starts, then fails immediately due to missing `Cargo.toml` in dependent repo root.
- Detection: explicit pre-build verification error code and diagnostics.
- Remediation: remote verifier integrated into selection/launch path (`bd-vvmd.2.4`).

### I-7 Fail-open correctness invariant
- Rule: When closure/verification fails due transient/environmental issues, behavior must remain explicit and safe (fallback semantics preserved).
- Prevents: blocking developer workflow on reliability subsystem failures.
- Failure example: verifier timeout blocks command entirely.
- Detection: command outcome indicates blocked instead of documented fallback.
- Remediation: integrate policy and tests while implementing beads in 2.x chain; ensure diagnostics are explicit.

## 4) Traceability matrix to downstream beads

| Invariant / work item | Primary implementation beads | Test-enforcement beads (minimum) |
|---|---|---|
| I-1 Canonical workspace identity | `bd-vvmd.1.2` | `bd-vvmd.1.6` |
| I-2 `/data/projects` + `/dp` topology alias | `bd-vvmd.1.3`, `bd-vvmd.1.4` | `bd-vvmd.1.6` |
| I-3 Deterministic remote path tuple | `bd-vvmd.1.2`, `bd-vvmd.1.4` | `bd-vvmd.1.6` |
| I-4 Remote base alignment + preflight eligibility | `bd-vvmd.1.4` | `bd-vvmd.1.6` |
| I-5 Cargo path-dependency closure | `bd-vvmd.2.1`, `bd-vvmd.2.2` | `bd-vvmd.2.7`, `bd-vvmd.2.8` |
| I-5 deterministic multi-root transfer realization | `bd-vvmd.2.3` | `bd-vvmd.2.7`, `bd-vvmd.2.8` |
| I-6 pre-build required-files verification | `bd-vvmd.2.4` | `bd-vvmd.2.7`, `bd-vvmd.2.8` |
| I-7 fail-open correctness for unresolved deps | (enforced while implementing `bd-vvmd.2.1..2.4`) | `bd-vvmd.2.9` |

## 5) Suggested execution order (critical path)
1. `bd-vvmd.1.2` canonicalization utility and mandatory call-sites.
2. `bd-vvmd.1.3` bootstrap `/data/projects` + `/dp` idempotently on workers.
3. `bd-vvmd.1.4` gate worker eligibility on topology preflight.
4. `bd-vvmd.2.1` resolver for local path-dependency graph.
5. `bd-vvmd.2.2` closure planner constrained to canonical roots.
6. `bd-vvmd.2.3` deterministic multi-root sync manifests + transfer.
7. `bd-vvmd.2.4` remote required-files verifier before build.
8. `bd-vvmd.1.6` + `bd-vvmd.2.7/2.8/2.9` for exhaustive unit/integration/e2e + logging.

# bd-vvmd.1.2 completion artifact: canonical path normalization module

## Scope and objective
Implement a shared canonicalization utility that maps equivalent project roots (`/dp`, `/data/projects`, symlinked variants) to a deterministic canonical identity, with strict guardrails and structured diagnostics. Integrate at high-leverage project identity points used for remote transfer and daemon selection paths.

## Implementation summary

### 1) New shared module: `rch-common/src/path_topology.rs`
Added a dedicated topology module with:

- Canonical defaults:
  - `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_PROJECT_ROOT = "/data/projects"`
  - `DEFAULT_ALIAS_PROJECT_ROOT = "/dp"`
- Policy object:
  - `PathTopologyPolicy { canonical_root, alias_root }`
- Normalization APIs:
  - `normalize_project_path(&Path) -> Result<NormalizedProjectPath, PathNormalizationError>`
  - `normalize_project_path_with_policy(&Path, &PathTopologyPolicy) -> Result<...>`
- Deterministic structured decision traces:
  - `NormalizationDecision::{ReceivedInput, VerifiedAbsoluteInput, AliasPrefixDetected, AliasSymlinkVerified, CanonicalRootResolved, CanonicalInputResolved, VerifiedWithinCanonicalRoot}`
- Explicit error model + diagnostics:
  - `PathNormalizationErrorKind::{NotAbsoluteInput, CanonicalRootMissing, CanonicalRootResolveFailed, AliasMissing, AliasNotSymlink, AliasReadLinkFailed, AliasTargetResolveFailed, AliasWrongTarget, InputResolveFailed, OutsideCanonicalRoot}`
  - `PathNormalizationError` with `detail()` and `decision_trace()`

Guardrails enforced by implementation:

- Reject non-absolute input paths.
- Require canonical root to exist and resolve.
- If input starts with alias root, require alias root to exist, be a symlink, and resolve exactly to canonical root.
- Resolve input with `canonicalize` and reject any escape outside canonical root.

### 2) Shared exports from `rch-common`
`rch-common/src/lib.rs` updated to export the topology API and types for reuse by `rch`, `rchd`, `rch-wkr`, and future dependency/planner modules.

### 3) Hook integration (`rch/src/hook.rs`)
Integrated normalization into project identity and transfer startup:

- `extract_project_name()` now:
  - canonicalizes current path with `normalize_project_path`
  - logs full normalization decision trace for observability
  - computes stable `name-short_hash` from canonical path (prevents `/dp/...` vs `/data/projects/...` identity drift)
- `execute_remote_compilation()` now:
  - canonicalizes CWD before deriving `project_id` and `project_hash`
  - passes canonical root into `TransferPipeline::new(...)`
  - emits normalization trace in verbose reporter output

### 4) Diagnose/preflight path alignment (`rch/src/commands/status.rs`)
Aligned simulated worker selection path with hook identity semantics:

- Uses `extract_project_name()` for daemon `project` key so status simulation matches real hook project identity (including canonicalization + hash).
- Keeps normalized canonical root fallback for toolchain detection.

This closes an inconsistency where diagnostic simulations could previously diverge from hook/daemon cache affinity keys.

## Test coverage and verification

### New/updated unit tests
Added exhaustive unit tests in `rch-common/src/path_topology.rs`:

1. `normalize_direct_canonical_path`
2. `normalize_alias_path_to_same_canonical_identity`
3. `reject_relative_path_input`
4. `reject_path_outside_canonical_root`
5. `reject_missing_alias_for_alias_prefixed_input`
6. `reject_alias_pointing_to_wrong_target`
7. `reject_when_canonical_root_missing`

Coverage includes happy-path, alias equivalence, invalid input, invariant violations, and edge conditions with stable expected errors.

- `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets` ✅ (remote attempted first; fail-open local fallback succeeded)

## Acceptance criteria mapping

title: Feed multi-signal reliability debt into worker health/selection penalties
description:
Incorporate unresolved reliability debt into worker score/eligibility so degraded nodes are not repeatedly selected. Expand from process-only penalties to a unified multi-signal health model that combines process-triage debt, repo-convergence confidence, disk-pressure admission risk, and heartbeat/liveness evidence. Include quarantine/recovery hysteresis so recovered workers re-enter service safely without flapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Selection model aggregates multi-signal reliability debt (process, convergence, disk, heartbeat) into deterministic health states and penalties.
- Health states include at least healthy, degraded, quarantined, and probing-recovery with explicit transition rules.
- Penalties and quarantine windows are bounded and decay over time to avoid permanent exclusion from transient incidents.
- If all workers are unsafe/degraded, scheduler preserves fail-open local fallback with explicit reason-coded diagnostics.
- Unit/integration/E2E tests validate mixed-signal failure combinations, flapping resistance, and smooth reintegration after recovery, with structured decision logs.

comments.text:
# bd-vvmd.7.1 completion artifact: deterministic multi-repo fixture system

## Scope
Implemented a reusable deterministic fixture system for cross-repo Cargo path-dependency scenarios, rooted in canonical `/data/projects` topology with `/dp` alias expectations, including failure fixtures, explicit metadata, and reproducible reset behavior.

## Code changes

### 1) Deterministic multi-repo fixture API (`rch-common/src/e2e/fixtures.rs`)
Added a new fixture subsystem with explicit topology/configuration and scenario metadata:

- Topology constants:
  - `DEFAULT_MULTI_REPO_CANONICAL_ROOT = "/data/projects"`
  - `DEFAULT_MULTI_REPO_ALIAS_ROOT = "/dp"`
  - `DEFAULT_MULTI_REPO_FIXTURE_NAMESPACE = "rch_multi_repo_path_deps"`
- Config and lifecycle:
  - `MultiRepoFixtureConfig`
  - `reset_multi_repo_fixtures(&MultiRepoFixtureConfig)`
  - `reset_default_multi_repo_fixtures()`
- Structured metadata and result model:
  - `MultiRepoFixtureSet`
  - `MultiRepoFixtureMetadata`
  - `FixtureReadiness`
  - `FixtureFailureMode`
  - `FixtureLayer`
- Explicit error model:
  - `MultiRepoFixtureError`
  - `MultiRepoFixtureResult<T>`

### 2) Topology and safety invariants
Fixture generation now enforces:

- canonical root and alias root must be absolute
- alias root must be a symlink
- alias symlink target must resolve exactly to canonical root
- namespace reset is deterministic (`remove + recreate` under namespace only)
- manifest snapshot (`fixture_manifest.json`) is produced for deterministic introspection

### 3) Scenario coverage (representative graphs + failure variants)
Implemented these reusable scenarios:

1. `ready_relative_transitive`
- three-repo transitive relative-path graph (`app -> util -> core`)
- expected ready

2. `ready_alias_absolute`
- absolute alias-path dependency via `/dp/...`
- expected ready

3. `fail_missing_path_dep`
- missing local path dependency
- expected failure (`MissingPathDependency`)

4. `fail_outside_canonical_dep`
- absolute dependency outside canonical root
- expected failure (`OutsideCanonicalRootDependency`)

5. `fail_invalid_manifest`
- malformed Cargo.toml
- expected failure (`InvalidCargoManifest`)

Each scenario includes assertion targets and reusable layer tags (`unit`, `integration`, `fault_injection`, `soak`).

### 4) Re-exports for cross-suite reuse (`rch-common/src/e2e/mod.rs`)
Added public re-exports so unit/integration/e2e/fault/soak suites can consume the same fixture API and metadata contract.

### 5) Logged E2E script (`tests/e2e/path_dependency_fixtures.sh`)
Added a dedicated script that:

- validates real host invariants (`/data/projects` exists, `/dp` symlink resolves correctly)
- runs deterministic fixture tests with clear step logging
- exits non-zero on invariant/test failure

## Validation evidence

Commands run:

- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets` ✅
- `rch exec -- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ❌ (pre-existing workspace blocker in `rch/src/commands/daemon.rs:627`, `clippy::items_after_test_module`)
- `rch exec -- cargo test -p rch-common multi_repo_fixture_ -- --nocapture` ✅ (4/4 new fixture tests passed)
- `tests/e2e/path_dependency_fixtures.sh` ✅ (topology checks + fixture test execution passed)

## Acceptance criteria mapping

- Representative multi-repo Cargo path-dependency graphs + failure variants: ✅
- Canonical `/data/projects` + `/dp` alias coverage with deterministic reset: ✅
- Per-fixture metadata with readiness/failure/assertion targets: ✅
- Reusable across unit/integration/fault-injection/soak layers: ✅
- Reproducible generation/reset via code path + dedicated logged script: ✅

## Notes for downstream beads

- This directly unblocks reliability harness and path-dependency E2E expansion beads by providing a single deterministic fixture substrate.
- Downstream suites should consume `MultiRepoFixtureSet` metadata instead of duplicating fixture assumptions.

title: EPIC: TUI Visual Polish and Accessibility Improvements
description:
# TUI Visual Polish and Accessibility Improvements

## Overview
The RCH TUI dashboard (rch dashboard / rch tui) provides real-time monitoring of workers, builds, and system status. While functional, it has several visual polish and accessibility issues that prevent it from feeling premium/Stripe-level quality.

## Why This Matters
1. **Terminal Compatibility**: Using emoji instead of unicode breaks display in many terminals (PuTTY, older xterm, screen/tmux without utf8, Windows cmd)
2. **Accessibility**: Users with visual impairments or using screen readers need consistent, predictable iconography
3. **Discoverability**: Hidden features (like filter mode) reduce perceived quality and user efficiency
4. **Muscle Memory**: Missing vim keybindings frustrates power users who expect h/j/k/l navigation

## Key Files
- rch/src/tui/widgets.rs - Widget rendering, icon definitions
- rch/src/tui/state.rs - TUI state management, panel navigation
- rch/src/tui/app.rs - Event handling, keyboard shortcuts
- rch/src/tui/event.rs - Input event processing

## Success Criteria
- All terminals display correctly (no mojibake/boxes)
- Help overlay documents ALL available shortcuts
- Vim users can navigate with h/j/k/l
- Worker actions available via single keystrokes
- Color blind modes tested and verified

title: Upgrade SshRecoveryProber to 12.2 capability_probe (exact rch-wkr version/protocol + per-root disk/inode)
description: 1.3's BypassRecoveryService uses a real SshRecoveryProber built on probe_worker_capabilities (rch-wkr capabilities over SSH + WorkerCapabilities disk/load + telemetry freshness). That is functional and conservative but coarser than the literal 1.3 acceptance for three dimensions: worker_binary 'exact configured rch-wkr --version', 'protocol handshake', and 'disk and inode thresholds on all relevant roots'. Now that 12.2 (rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs) is closed, upgrade SshRecoveryProber::probe to: build_capability_probe_script(ProbeSpec{remote_user, exact rch_wkr_path, cargo/rustup paths, disk_roots}) over SSH; parse_capability_probe -> ProbedFacts; map worker_binary_ok=facts.worker.is_some(), protocol_ok=facts.worker.protocol_version>=min, toolchain_ok via assess_admissibility(CapabilityRequirement::rust(min).with_targets/with_toolchains), disk_ok across DiskRootFacts byte+inode thresholds on ALL roots, telemetry_ok=freshness, load_ok from cached caps/telemetry. Open inputs to resolve: (1) exact rch-wkr path per worker (today daemon uses 'command -v rch-wkr || ~/.local/bin/rch-wkr'; no per-worker configured path) -- decide a canonical resolution; (2) min wire protocol constant for the worker handshake (SELECTION_RESPONSE_PROTOCOL_VERSION is selection-only); (3) disk_roots from 11.1 mount-aware build-root policy (remote_base + cargo home + build roots) instead of a hardcoded default. The RecoveryProber trait seam means the recovery LOOP and its 10 end-to-end tests are unaffected; only the real prober body changes (live-verified). Blocks full literal-fidelity closure of 1.3.

title: P2: general.role = dispatcher|worker|hybrid — box-level fail-closed/queue policy (no per-call RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE)
description:
Add a box-level role so "never build locally" is a config, not a per-call env.

## Design
- `general.role = "dispatcher" | "worker" | "hybrid"` (default hybrid = today's
  behavior; fully backward compatible).
- `dispatcher`: offloadable builds resolve to fail-CLOSED + queue by default
  (RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE semantics + RCH_QUEUE_WHEN_BUSY) so they WAIT for a worker and
  never fall back to local rustc. Env/flags can still override per call.
- `worker`: fail-open/local (the box IS the compute); `rch shim install` refuses here.
- Resolve in the placement path (`rch-common/src/placement.rs` — extend
  StrictRemotePolicy resolution to consult role) so both `rch exec` and the shim
  inherit it without hardcoding env.

## Why
Current `force_remote` is fail-open (`placement.rs::force_remote_is_fail_open`) so a
saturated fleet repopulates local rustc on the orchestrator. The live stopgap
hardcodes `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1` in the shim; that belongs in box policy.

## Acceptance
Set `role=dispatcher`; `cargo build` with a busy fleet QUEUES (does not run local, does
not hard-fail unless no worker can ever take it). `role=worker` unchanged. Verified: on
trj the equivalent env drove local rustc to 0 with zero refusal log lines.

title: Idea: Retry/backoff for rsync + SSH exec
description:
## Background
Transient network failures and SSH hiccups cause unnecessary fallback to local builds. Simple retry with backoff improves reliability without risking long stalls.

## Goals
- Retry rsync upload/download and SSH command execution on transient errors.
- Limit retries and total time to preserve responsiveness.
- Emit clear logs with retry counts and reasons.

## Design / Approach
- Introduce retry policy in transfer pipeline (max_attempts, base_delay, jitter).
- Classify retryable errors (timeout, connection reset) vs non-retryable (auth, host key).
- Respect overall timeouts and fail-open if exceeded.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Add retry policy to config with safe defaults.
- Implement retry wrapper for rsync + SSH exec.
- Update mock transport to simulate retryable failures.

## Tests
- Unit: retryable error classification.
- Integration: mock transport fails once then succeeds.
- E2E: timeouts do not exceed configured caps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Transient failures recover without manual retry.
- Non-retryable errors still fail fast.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-x1ek.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- Only retry when command definitely did NOT start (connect/transport errors).
- Exponential backoff with jitter and total time cap.
- Non-retryable errors (auth/host key) fail fast.

## E2E Outline
- Mock rsync fails once (retryable) then succeeds.
- Mock auth failure -> no retry.
- Logs include attempt count + total elapsed time.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rch-common/src/ssh.rs: retryable error classification.
- rch/src/transfer.rs: retry policy caps total time.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-x1ek.sh: mock rsync fails once then succeeds.
- Verify non-retryable errors fail fast.
close_reason: Completed: RetryConfig with exponential backoff + jitter, retry logic for both real and mock rsync paths, E2E test script passing

title: Implement toolchain verification and installation on worker
