description:
# Worker Preflight Health Guards (Load Average + Disk Space)

## Merged Scope
This bead consolidates two related worker preflight check features:
- **Load Average Guard** (formerly bd-2hbf): Skip workers with high CPU load
- **Disk Space Guard** (formerly bd-1mij): Skip workers with low free disk

Both are preflight checks that improve worker selection quality by filtering out unhealthy workers before job assignment.

## Background
Even if slots are available, a worker may be unsuitable:
- High load average spikes hurt build times
- Low disk space can cause builds to fail or slow dramatically

Preflight guards prevent wasted transfers and improve overall compilation success rates.

## Goals
1. Skip workers whose load average exceeds a threshold (per-core normalized)
2. Skip workers whose free disk space is below minimum
3. Provide clear selection reasons (NoWorkersWithCapacity, NoWorkersWithDisk)
4. Fail-open: if all workers exceed thresholds, pick best available with warning

## Design / Approach

### Configuration
```toml
[selection]
max_load_per_core = 2.0    # Skip if load1 / cores > threshold
min_free_gb = 10.0         # Skip if free disk < threshold
```

### Telemetry Fields
Extend worker capabilities/telemetry:
- `load_avg_1`, `load_avg_5`, `load_avg_15` (from /proc/loadavg or uptime)
- `disk_free_gb`, `disk_total_gb` (from df or statfs)

### Selection Logic
1. Filter by slot availability
2. Filter by load-per-core threshold
3. Filter by disk space threshold
4. Sort by SpeedScore
5. If all filtered out, pick best available with warning

## Tasks / Subtasks
1. Extend telemetry payload to include load avg and disk metrics
2. Add fallback SSH probe (uptime, df) when telemetry unavailable
3. Add config fields with validation
4. Update selection logic with reason codes
5. Expose in `rch status` and `rch workers list` output
6. Add warnings when using degraded workers

## Tests

### Unit Tests
- `rchd/src/selection.rs`: load-per-core threshold logic, disk space filter
- `rchd/src/telemetry.rs`: load avg parsing, disk metric extraction
- Selection reason codes for each guard type

### Integration Tests
- Mock worker reports high load -> skipped
- Mock worker reports low disk -> skipped
- All workers degraded -> pick best with warning

### E2E Tests
Script: `scripts/e2e_preflight_guards.sh`

Scenarios:
- Mixed load -> skip high, select low
- Mixed disk -> skip low-disk, select adequate
- All high load -> select least-loaded with warning
- All low disk -> select most-available with warning
- Status output displays load and disk warnings

## Acceptance Criteria
- High-load workers are skipped automatically
- Low-disk workers are skipped automatically
- Selection reasons are visible and actionable
- Thresholds are configurable and documented
- Fail-open behavior preserves system usability

## Logging & E2E
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, duration_ms, result, error
- Phases: classify, select (with guard reasons), sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary

## Edge Cases & UX
- Missing telemetry -> allow worker but warn
- Use load-per-core to normalize across heterogeneous machines
- Support per-worker threshold overrides
- Selection reason includes specific guard signals

## Dependencies
- Depends on bd-155i (Worker capabilities report + mismatch warnings)

title: Add vim-style navigation keybindings to TUI
description:
# Add Vim-Style Navigation to TUI

## Problem
Power users expect vim keybindings (h/j/k/l) in TUI applications. RCH TUI only supports arrow keys, forcing users to move hands from home row.

## Current State
In rch/src/tui/app.rs, event handling maps:
- Up/Down arrows → select_up/select_down
- Left/Right → NOT MAPPED (could switch panels)
- Tab → next_panel

## Proposed Keybindings
```
Navigation:
  j / ↓     Move selection down
  k / ↑     Move selection up
  h / ←     Previous panel (same as Shift+Tab)
  l / →     Next panel (same as Tab)
  g g       Jump to first item
  G         Jump to last item
  
Panel-specific:
  H         Jump to first panel (Workers)
  L         Jump to last panel (Logs)
  1-4       Jump to panel by number
```

## Implementation
1. In event.rs, add KeyCode::Char('j'), etc. mappings
2. In state.rs, add jump_to_first/jump_to_last methods
3. In app.rs, wire up the new keybindings

## Help Text Update
Update the help overlay (render_help_overlay) to document:
- All vim keybindings
- Panel numbers
- Jump commands

## Testing
- Verify j/k work identically to arrows
- Verify h/l switch panels
- Verify g/G jumps work
- Verify no conflicts with existing bindings

## Files to Modify
- rch/src/tui/app.rs (event handling)
- rch/src/tui/state.rs (new methods)
- rch/src/tui/widgets.rs (help overlay text)
close_reason: Implemented vim-style navigation keybindings for TUI: h/l for prev/next panel, H/L for first/last panel, 1-4 for direct panel jump, g/G extended for list items, help overlay updated. 25 new tests, all 1714 pass.

use tracing_subscriber::{fmt, EnvFilter};

title: Meta Skill: Create v0.1.1 release tag
CRITICAL: Compile Command Hook Context Test
description:
## Test: rch compile in Hook Context

This test verifies that when an AI agent invokes `rch compile` (or any compilation command), the rich_rust integration does NOT interfere with the compilation output that the agent is parsing.

### Why This Is Critical

When Claude Code uses RCH, it:
1. Invokes `rch hook --stdin` with JSON describing the command
2. Expects JSON response with `allow`/`intercept` result
3. If intercepted, expects compilation stdout/stderr to pass through unchanged
4. Parses exit codes to determine success/failure

If rich output contaminates stdout, agents will fail to parse compilation results.

### Test Scenarios

#### Scenario 1: Hook Invocation (JSON Protocol)
```bash
# Test: Hook JSON response unchanged
INPUT='{"tool":"Bash","input":{"command":"cargo build"}}'
OUTPUT=$(echo "$INPUT" | rch hook --stdin)

# Verify: stdout is valid JSON
echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -e . || fail "Not valid JSON"

# Verify: No ANSI codes in JSON
echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -qP '\x1b\[' && fail "ANSI codes in JSON!"
```

#### Scenario 2: Compilation Output Passthrough
```bash
# Test: cargo build output unchanged
cd /tmp/test_project
OUTPUT=$(rch compile cargo build 2>&1)

# Verify: rustc output preserved
echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "Compiling" || echo "WARN: No Compiling output"

# Verify: Exit code preserved
rch compile cargo build
EXIT=$?
[[ $EXIT -eq 0 ]] || [[ $EXIT -eq 101 ]] || fail "Unexpected exit: $EXIT"
```

#### Scenario 3: Error Output Preserved
```bash
# Create invalid Rust file
echo "fn main() { invalid syntax" > /tmp/test_project/src/main.rs

# Compile and capture error
OUTPUT=$(rch compile cargo build 2>&1)

# Verify: rustc error preserved
echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "error" || fail "Error not preserved"

# The error message itself should be parseable by agents
# Rich formatting should be on stderr, not mixed with compiler output
```

### Test Implementation

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/test_compile_hook_context.sh
set -euo pipefail

source scripts/test_lib.sh
init_test_log "compile_hook_context"

RCH="./target/release/rch"
TEST_PROJECT="/tmp/rch_test_$$"

setup() {
    log_json "setup" "Creating test project"
    mkdir -p "$TEST_PROJECT/src"
    cat > "$TEST_PROJECT/Cargo.toml" << 'EOF'
[package]
name = "test_project"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
EOF
    echo 'fn main() { println!("Hello"); }' > "$TEST_PROJECT/src/main.rs"
}

cleanup() {
    rm -rf "$TEST_PROJECT"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

setup

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 1: Hook invocation JSON purity
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Hook JSON purity test"

export RCH_HOOK_MODE=1
cd "$TEST_PROJECT"

HOOK_INPUT='{"tool":"Bash","input":{"command":"cargo build"}}'
STDOUT_FILE="$(mktemp)"
STDERR_FILE="$(mktemp)"

echo "$HOOK_INPUT" | "$RCH" hook --stdin > "$STDOUT_FILE" 2> "$STDERR_FILE"

# Check stdout
if ! jq -e . "$STDOUT_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fail "stdout is not valid JSON"
fi

if grep -qP '\x1b\[' "$STDOUT_FILE"; then
    log_json "error" "ANSI codes found in stdout" "{\"content\":\"$(cat $STDOUT_FILE | head -c 500 | base64)\"}"
    fail "ANSI codes in hook stdout!"
fi

log_json "verify" "Hook stdout is clean JSON" '{"passed":true}'
unset RCH_HOOK_MODE

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 2: Compilation stdout/stderr separation
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Compilation output separation"

# Run compile with rich output potentially enabled
STDOUT_FILE="$(mktemp)"
STDERR_FILE="$(mktemp)"

"$RCH" compile cargo build --release > "$STDOUT_FILE" 2> "$STDERR_FILE" || true

# stdout should have compiler output (or be empty if intercepted)
# It should NOT have ANSI codes from RCH (compiler may add its own)
RCH_ANSI_PATTERN='\[rch\].*\x1b\['  # RCH-specific rich output pattern
if grep -qP "$RCH_ANSI_PATTERN" "$STDOUT_FILE"; then
    fail "RCH rich output leaked to stdout"
fi

log_json "verify" "stdout clean of RCH rich output" '{"passed":true}'

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 3: Exit code preservation
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Exit code preservation"

# Successful build
"$RCH" compile cargo build --release >/dev/null 2>&1
EXIT_SUCCESS=$?

# Failed build (introduce error)
echo 'fn main() { invalid' > "$TEST_PROJECT/src/main.rs"
"$RCH" compile cargo build --release >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
EXIT_FAIL=$?

# Restore
echo 'fn main() { println!("Hello"); }' > "$TEST_PROJECT/src/main.rs"

log_json "verify" "Exit codes" "{\"success\":$EXIT_SUCCESS,\"fail\":$EXIT_FAIL}"

if [[ $EXIT_SUCCESS -ne 0 ]] && [[ $EXIT_SUCCESS -ne 101 ]]; then
    log_json "warning" "Unexpected success exit code" "{\"exit\":$EXIT_SUCCESS}"
fi

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TEST 4: Error message preservation
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "test" "Error message preservation"

echo 'fn main() { let x: i32 = "string"; }' > "$TEST_PROJECT/src/main.rs"
ERROR_OUTPUT="$(\"\\" compile cargo build 2>&1 || true)"

# Should contain rustc error (type mismatch)
if ! echo "$ERROR_OUTPUT" | grep -q "mismatched types\|expected.*found"; then
    log_json "warning" "Error message may be modified" "{\"output_sample\":\"$(echo $ERROR_OUTPUT | head -c 200)\"}"
fi

log_json "verify" "Error messages preserved" '{"passed":true}'

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SUMMARY
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
log_json "summary" "All compile hook context tests passed" '{"total_tests":4}'
echo ""
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "ALL COMPILE HOOK CONTEXT TESTS PASSED"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
```

### Acceptance Criteria

1. [ ] Hook JSON response contains no ANSI codes
2. [ ] Compilation stdout has no RCH rich output leakage
3. [ ] Exit codes preserved through rich integration
4. [ ] Compiler error messages preserved and parseable
5. [ ] Test runs in CI

### Files

- CREATE: scripts/test_compile_hook_context.sh
- CREATE: rch/tests/compile_context.rs
close_reason: Merged into bd-2ga8 (Hook protocol integrity scenarios).

# Progress Indicators and User Feedback

## Overview
RCH has good progress indicator infrastructure but doesn't use it consistently across all long-running operations. This creates uncertainty about whether operations are progressing or hung.

## Current State

### Strong Points
- Spinner and TransferProgress types exist in rch-common/src/ui/progress/
- Automatic TTY/JSON mode detection
- Unicode/ASCII fallback support

### Missing Progress Indicators
These operations provide no progress feedback:

1. **rch workers benchmark** - Runs speed tests on workers with no indication of progress
2. **rch self-test** - Compiles test project with no feedback during compilation
3. **rch workers sync-toolchain** - Runs rustup on workers, can take minutes with no feedback
4. **rch fleet deploy** - Deploys to multiple workers but shows no per-worker progress

### Missing Multi-Progress
When deploying to 5 workers simultaneously, users see nothing until all complete. Should show:
```
Deploying to fleet (3/5 complete)
  css ████████████████ 100% ✓
  csd ████████░░░░░░░░  50%
  cse ████░░░░░░░░░░░░  25%
  csf ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% (connecting)
  csg ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% (queued)
```

## Key Files
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/spinner.rs - Spinner implementation
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/transfer.rs - TransferProgress
- rch-common/src/ui/progress/compile.rs - CompilationProgress
- rch/src/commands.rs - Command implementations needing progress

## Success Criteria
- All operations >2s show progress indication
- Parallel operations show nested/grouped progress
- Progress works in both TTY and non-TTY modes
- Progress can be disabled with --quiet

# bd-vvmd.1.2 completion artifact: canonical path normalization module

## Scope and objective
Implement a shared canonicalization utility that maps equivalent project roots (`/dp`, `/data/projects`, symlinked variants) to a deterministic canonical identity, with strict guardrails and structured diagnostics. Integrate at high-leverage project identity points used for remote transfer and daemon selection paths.

## Implementation summary

### 1) New shared module: `rch-common/src/path_topology.rs`
Added a dedicated topology module with:

- Canonical defaults:
  - `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_PROJECT_ROOT = "/data/projects"`
  - `DEFAULT_ALIAS_PROJECT_ROOT = "/dp"`
- Policy object:
  - `PathTopologyPolicy { canonical_root, alias_root }`
- Normalization APIs:
  - `normalize_project_path(&Path) -> Result<NormalizedProjectPath, PathNormalizationError>`
  - `normalize_project_path_with_policy(&Path, &PathTopologyPolicy) -> Result<...>`
- Deterministic structured decision traces:
  - `NormalizationDecision::{ReceivedInput, VerifiedAbsoluteInput, AliasPrefixDetected, AliasSymlinkVerified, CanonicalRootResolved, CanonicalInputResolved, VerifiedWithinCanonicalRoot}`
- Explicit error model + diagnostics:
  - `PathNormalizationErrorKind::{NotAbsoluteInput, CanonicalRootMissing, CanonicalRootResolveFailed, AliasMissing, AliasNotSymlink, AliasReadLinkFailed, AliasTargetResolveFailed, AliasWrongTarget, InputResolveFailed, OutsideCanonicalRoot}`
  - `PathNormalizationError` with `detail()` and `decision_trace()`

Guardrails enforced by implementation:

- Reject non-absolute input paths.
- Require canonical root to exist and resolve.
- If input starts with alias root, require alias root to exist, be a symlink, and resolve exactly to canonical root.
- Resolve input with `canonicalize` and reject any escape outside canonical root.

### 2) Shared exports from `rch-common`
`rch-common/src/lib.rs` updated to export the topology API and types for reuse by `rch`, `rchd`, `rch-wkr`, and future dependency/planner modules.

Integrated normalization into project identity and transfer startup:

title: Project Cache Affinity System (pinning + warm-cache + stable paths)
description:
# Project Cache Affinity System

## Merged Scope
This bead consolidates cache affinity features for improved build performance:
- **Affinity Pinning Window** (original bd-5a5k): Pin projects to successful workers
- **Warm-Cache Command**: Pre-sync sources without executing builds
- **Last-Success Fallback**: Fall back to last successful worker when selection fails
- **Stable Remote Paths** (merged from bd-2df5): Reuse remote paths when hash unchanged

All these features work together to maximize cache hit rates and minimize redundant transfers.

## Background
Cache affinity helps incremental builds, but several factors can reduce effectiveness:
- Selection can bounce between workers
- Remote paths may churn even for unchanged projects
- First build to a worker suffers cold-cache latency
- No fallback when preferred worker is unavailable

This unified system addresses all these issues holistically.

## Goals
1. Pin a project to the last successful worker for a configurable window (30-120 min)
2. Add `rch cache warm` command to pre-sync sources without executing builds
3. If selection yields no worker, fall back to last-successful worker if healthy
4. Reuse stable remote path for a project when its hash is unchanged
5. Keep isolation when hash changes (avoid mixing incompatible states)

## Design / Approach

### Affinity Pinning
- Store last-successful worker + timestamp in daemon history
- Selection checks pin window before normal strategy
- Config: `selection.affinity_pin_minutes`

### Last-Success Fallback
- If selection fails, attempt last-successful worker (health/slots/runtime OK)
- Config: `selection.enable_last_success_fallback`

### Warm-Cache Command
```bash
rch cache warm [--workers ...] [--project PATH]
```
- Reuses TransferPipeline sync_to_remote without execute step
- Records warm-cache events for affinity tracking

### Stable Remote Paths
- Maintain `project_id + hash` mapping
- Reuse existing remote dir if hash unchanged
- Add optional local cache metadata for speed
- Cleanup routines respect stable paths

### Remote Path Computation
```
/tmp/rch/{project_id}/{hash}/
```
- If hash unchanged and dir exists on worker → reuse
- If hash changed → new directory
- Per-worker stability (not cross-worker)

## Tasks / Subtasks
1. Add pin metadata + last-success mapping to build history
2. Implement selection override with safeguards (pin + fallback)
3. Implement warm-cache command path (sync-only)
4. Adjust remote path computation to check for existing directory
5. Add local cache metadata for path stability tracking
6. Update cleanup logic to avoid deleting active cache
7. Emit selection audit reasons (pinned, fallback, normal)

## Tests

### Unit Tests
- `rchd/src/selection.rs`: pin expiry logic, fallback logic
- `rch/src/transfer.rs`: remote path computation with hash reuse
- `rch/src/commands.rs`: warm-cache argument parsing
- Cleanup logic ignores active hash dirs

### Integration Tests
- Selection respects pin window and fallback
- Repeated build reuses remote dir

### E2E Tests
Script: `scripts/e2e_cache_affinity.sh`

Scenarios:
- Same hash builds reuse same remote dir
- Change key file -> new hash -> new remote dir
- Warm-cache improves subsequent build selection
- Fallback succeeds when preferred worker down
- Cleanup keeps newest dir

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pinning improves cache hit rates for repeated builds
- Warm-cache completes without running builds
- Fallback improves success rate without masking real errors
- Repeated builds with unchanged inputs reuse remote path
- Hash changes still isolate build state
- Behavior is transparent in logs/status

## Logging & E2E
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result
- Include selection reason (pinned/fallback/normal) in logs

## Edge Cases & UX
- Stability is per-worker; do not reuse across workers
- If remote dir existence check fails, fall back to normal path
- Old hash dirs eligible for cleanup to prevent bloat
- Unhealthy/insufficient-runtime workers not used for fallback

title: Epic: rich_rust Integration - Premium Terminal Output for RCH
description:
# Epic: rich_rust Integration - Premium Terminal Output for RCH

## Executive Summary

This epic encompasses the complete integration of the rich_rust library into RCH (Remote Compilation Helper) to provide beautiful, premium terminal output for human operators watching AI coding agents work. The integration must maintain **zero interference** with AI agents, which are the primary users of RCH.

## Background & Motivation

### The Problem
RCH currently outputs plain text for status, errors, and progress. While functional, this provides a poor experience for humans monitoring AI agents. When operators run 15+ agents simultaneously, they need at-a-glance visual feedback about:
- Which workers are healthy/degraded/offline
- What compilations are in progress
- Where errors occurred and how to fix them
- Transfer and benchmark progress

### The Solution
Integrate rich_rust (a Rust port of Python's Rich library) to provide:
- Styled text with markup syntax ([bold red]text[/])
- Tables with auto-sizing columns and Unicode borders
- Panels for framed content (errors, status)
- Progress bars for transfers and benchmarks
- Color-coded status indicators
- Automatic terminal capability detection and color downgrade

## The Cardinal Rule: Agent-First Architecture

**CRITICAL**: AI coding agents are the PRIMARY users of RCH. They interact through:
1. JSON hook protocol (stdin -> stdout)
2. Exit codes (0, 1, 101, 128+N)
3. Streamed compilation output

Rich formatting must NEVER interfere with these machine interfaces. The design principle is:
- **stderr for humans**: Rich output goes to stderr
- **stdout for machines**: Structured data stays pristine on stdout
- **Graceful degradation**: If rich_rust fails, fall back to plain text

## Output Classification

### NEVER Add Rich Formatting (Machine Output)
- Hook JSON responses (stdout)
- --json flag output (stdout)
- Compilation output passthrough (stdout)
- Test output streaming (stdout)
- Exit codes (process exit status)

### ADD Rich Formatting (Human Output)
- rch status commands (stderr)
- rch workers list/probe/benchmark (stderr)
- rchd startup banner and health (stderr)
- Error messages and warnings (stderr)
- Transfer and benchmark progress (stderr)

## Implementation Phases

1. **Phase 1: Foundation** - Infrastructure, modules, context detection
2. **Phase 2: CLI Commands** - Rich output for status/worker commands
3. **Phase 3: Daemon UI** - Startup banner, health displays
4. **Phase 4: Error Experience** - Beautiful error panels
5. **Phase 5: Progress & Feedback** - Progress bars, spinners
6. **Phase 6: Polish** - Theme refinement, docs, validation

## Success Criteria

1. All rch CLI commands have beautiful, informative output
2. AI agents function identically with rich output enabled/disabled
3. NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR environment variables are respected
4. Performance: Zero overhead on hook classification hot path
5. All existing tests pass
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE: rich_rust Integration - Premium Terminal Output for RCH. All 6 phases closed: Phase 1 (Foundation), Phase 2 (CLI Commands), Phase 3 (Daemon UI), Phase 4 (Error Experience), Phase 5 (Progress & Feedback), Phase 6 (Polish & Documentation). RCH now has beautiful, context-aware terminal output that works correctly with both humans and AI agents.

title: Fix compilation errors blocking build
description:
## Critical Build Errors

The rch crate fails to compile due to API mismatches:

### Issues Identified:
1. **commands.rs uses ctx.style() but OutputContext has theme()** - Multiple locations call `ctx.style()` but the method doesn't exist
2. **ui/progress.rs uses ctx.theme().supports_unicode()** - Calling theme() method that exists but the API usage pattern may be inconsistent

### Root Cause:
API changes in OutputContext/Theme not propagated to all consumers.

### Fix Required:
- Replace `ctx.style()` with `ctx.theme()` in commands.rs
- Or add a `style()` method to OutputContext as an alias for theme()

### Files Affected:
- rch/src/commands.rs
- rch/src/ui/progress.rs

title: True E2E Test Infrastructure & Harness
description:
# Feature: True E2E Test Infrastructure & Harness

## Purpose

Establish the foundational infrastructure needed to run true end-to-end tests against real workers. This includes test harness utilities, worker discovery, output comparison helpers, and CI/local run configuration.

## Why This Comes First

All other true e2e tests depend on this infrastructure. Without a proper harness that can:
1. Discover available workers
2. Skip gracefully when no workers available
3. Compare local vs remote output
4. Clean up test artifacts

...the individual tests would each need to reinvent this logic, leading to duplication and inconsistency.

## MANDATORY Logging Standards

All tests and utilities in this infrastructure MUST implement structured JSON logging:

### Log Format Specification

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-01-19T12:00:00.123Z",
  "level": "INFO|WARN|ERROR|DEBUG",
  "test": "test_cargo_build",
  "phase": "setup|sync|execute|validate|teardown",
  "worker": "css|local|null",
  "duration_ms": 1234,
  "msg": "Human-readable message",
  "data": { /* phase-specific structured data */ }
}
```

### Required Log Events

1. **Test Start**: test name, worker target, fixture paths
2. **Phase Transitions**: setup→sync→execute→validate→teardown with timing
3. **Command Execution**: full command, args, working directory
4. **Output Capture**: stdout/stderr size, truncation if any
5. **Comparison Results**: match/mismatch, diff summary if failed
6. **Test End**: pass/fail/skip, total duration, cleanup status

### Logger Interface

```rust
pub struct TestLogger {
    test_name: String,
    log_file: BufWriter<File>,
    start_time: Instant,
    current_phase: Option<String>,
}

impl TestLogger {
    pub fn new(test_name: &str) -> std::io::Result<Self>;
    pub fn phase(&mut self, name: &str);
    pub fn info(&mut self, msg: &str, data: serde_json::Value);
    pub fn warn(&mut self, msg: &str, data: serde_json::Value);
    pub fn error(&mut self, msg: &str, data: serde_json::Value);
    pub fn finish(self) -> TestResult;
}
```

### Log File Location

- Per-test logs: `target/true_e2e_logs/{test_name}_{timestamp}.jsonl`
- Combined log: `target/true_e2e_logs/combined_{run_id}.jsonl`
- Human-readable summary: `target/true_e2e_logs/summary_{run_id}.txt`

## Technical Requirements

### Test Harness (`tests/true_e2e/harness.rs`)

```rust
pub struct TrueE2EHarness {
    daemon_socket: PathBuf,
    available_workers: Vec<WorkerInfo>,
    test_project_root: PathBuf,
    logger: TestLogger,  // MANDATORY: every harness has a logger
}

impl TrueE2EHarness {
    /// Create harness with logger, skip test if no real workers available
    pub fn new_or_skip(test_name: &str) -> Result<Self, SkipReason>;
    
    /// Run command locally and capture output (logs execution details)
    pub fn run_local(&mut self, cmd: &str) -> CommandOutput;
    
    /// Run command via RCH hook and capture output (logs execution details)
    pub fn run_via_rch(&mut self, cmd: &str) -> CommandOutput;
    
    /// Compare outputs, logs diff details on mismatch
    pub fn assert_outputs_match(&mut self, local: &CommandOutput, remote: &CommandOutput);
}
```

### Output Comparison Strategy

Not all output will be byte-identical. We need configurable comparison that ignores:
- Absolute paths (replace with relative or placeholder)
- Timestamps in compilation output
- Worker hostnames in debug output
- Order of parallel compilation units

Comparison must log:
- What normalization was applied
- Original vs normalized content hashes
- Line-by-line diff for mismatches

### Skip Logic

Tests must skip gracefully when:
- No daemon running
- No workers configured
- All workers unreachable
- Required toolchain not on workers

Use `#[ignore]` attribute plus custom skip macro that logs why (with structured JSON).

### CI Configuration

Add Cargo feature `true-e2e` that:
- Gates the `tests/true_e2e/` module
- Defaults to OFF in CI (no workers there)
- Documents how to run locally with workers
- Sets log output directory via env var

## Files to Create

- `tests/true_e2e/mod.rs` - Module root
- `tests/true_e2e/harness.rs` - Test harness with integrated logger
- `tests/true_e2e/logging.rs` - Structured JSON logging infrastructure
- `tests/true_e2e/output.rs` - Output comparison utilities with diff logging
- `tests/true_e2e/fixtures/` - Test project templates

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Harness can discover real workers from daemon
- [ ] Harness skips cleanly when no workers available
- [ ] ALL harness operations emit structured JSON logs
- [ ] Output comparison handles path/timing differences
- [ ] Output comparison logs detailed diffs on mismatch
- [ ] At least one "hello world" test passes using harness
- [ ] Logs are written to target/true_e2e_logs/
- [ ] Documentation explains how to run true e2e tests and read logs

title: Idea: Per-project always/never remote override
description:
## Background
Some projects should never be offloaded (sensitive code), while others should always be offloaded (very large builds). A per-project override is simple and powerful.

## Goals
- Allow `.rch/config.toml` to force local-only or remote-only behavior.
- Surface the decision in diagnostics.

## Design / Approach
- Add config keys: general.force_local, general.force_remote.
- Hook checks overrides before classification gating.
- For force_remote, still respect safety gates (e.g., structural checks, toolchain missing).

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Extend config schema and validation.
- Integrate into hook decision flow.
- Update docs + examples.

## Tests
- Unit: override precedence rules.
- Integration: force_local bypasses remote even if classified.
- Integration: force_remote offloads when safe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Overrides work and are visible in output.
- No regression in safety/fail-open behavior.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-1vzb.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- force_remote still respects structural safety (pipes/redirects).
- force_local skips daemon selection to reduce latency.
- Conflicting force flags are lint errors.

## E2E Outline
- force_local -> local allowed with reason.
- force_remote -> remote attempted if safe.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rch/src/config.rs: force_local/force_remote validation + precedence.
- rch/src/hook.rs: override short-circuit and safety checks.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-1vzb.sh: force_local bypasses daemon; force_remote attempts offload.

title: WS3.2: Replace scalar RwLocks with atomics
description:
Convert hot-path scalar RwLock fields to atomics:

1. last_latency_ms: RwLock<Option<u64>> (line 27) → AtomicU64
   - CONFIRMED HOT PATH: accessed in selection.rs:1405 during worker scoring
   - Use 0 as None sentinel (latency of 0ms is not meaningful)
   - get: let v = self.last_latency_ms.load(Relaxed); if v == 0 { None } else { Some(v) }
   - set: self.last_latency_ms.store(ms.unwrap_or(0), Relaxed);

LOWER PRIORITY (not on selection hot path, but could still benefit):

2. disabled_at: RwLock<Option<i64>> (line 39) → AtomicI64
   - NOT in selection.rs hot path (only used in workers.rs enable/disable)
   - Still worth converting for consistency
   - Use 0 as None sentinel

NOTE: consecutive_failures and total_builds do NOT exist as direct fields on WorkerState. They are tracked inside CircuitStats. Do not try to extract them — the circuit RwLock stays.

Update all read/write sites. Remove .await from accessor calls that become non-async.

Files affected:
- rchd/src/workers.rs (struct def, accessors at lines ~282, 300, 337)
- rchd/src/selection.rs (line 1405 uses last_latency_ms)
close_reason: Replaced last_latency_ms (RwLock<Option<u64>> -> AtomicU64 with 0 sentinel) and disabled_at (RwLock<Option<i64>> -> AtomicI64 with 0 sentinel). Updated accessors to synchronous, removed .await from all callers in workers.rs, health.rs, selection.rs. network_score() now synchronous. All tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Create Test Runner Script (scripts/run_true_e2e.sh)
description:
## Purpose
Create a comprehensive test runner script that executes all true e2e tests with proper logging, reporting, and CI integration.

## Why This Matters
- Manual test execution is error-prone
- CI systems need standardized entry point
- Developers need easy local testing
- Reports needed for tracking regressions

## Script: scripts/run_true_e2e.sh

### Basic Usage
```bash
# Run all true e2e tests
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh

# Run specific test category
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --filter cargo

# Run with verbose logging
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --verbose

# Skip if no workers (CI mode)
./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --ci
```

### Script Features

#### 1. Pre-flight Checks
- Verify daemon is running (or start it)
- Verify at least one worker is reachable
- Verify required tools (rsync, ssh, etc.)
- Check Rust toolchain versions match

#### 2. Test Execution
- Run tests with cargo test --features true-e2e
- Capture all output (stdout, stderr, timing)
- Handle test timeouts gracefully
- Support parallel test execution

#### 3. Logging Integration
- Set RCH_E2E_LOG_DIR to timestamped directory
- Collect all test logs
- Generate summary log

#### 4. Report Generation
- JUnit XML for CI systems
- HTML report with timing graphs
- Summary table (pass/fail/skip counts)
- Failure details with log excerpts

### Output Structure
```
test-results/
├── run_2024-01-19_120000/
│   ├── junit.xml           # CI-compatible report
│   ├── report.html         # Human-readable report
│   ├── summary.json        # Machine-readable summary
│   ├── logs/
│   │   ├── test_cargo_build.jsonl
│   │   ├── test_cargo_test.jsonl
│   │   └── ...
│   └── artifacts/
│       └── (any test artifacts)
```

### CI Integration
```yaml
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Run True E2E Tests
  run: ./scripts/run_true_e2e.sh --ci --junit test-results/junit.xml
  env:
    RCH_E2E_WORKERS_CONFIG: ${{ secrets.WORKERS_CONFIG }}
    
- name: Upload Test Results
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: e2e-test-results
    path: test-results/
```

### Exit Codes
- 0: All tests passed
- 1: Some tests failed
- 2: Infrastructure error (no workers, daemon failed)
- 3: Configuration error

## Implementation

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"

# ... (full implementation in script)
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Script runs all true e2e tests
- [ ] Pre-flight checks prevent confusing failures
- [ ] JUnit XML is valid and parseable
- [ ] HTML report is clear and useful
- [ ] CI mode skips gracefully when no workers
- [ ] Exit codes are correct
- [ ] Documentation in script header

title: Add --verbose flag consistently to all CLI commands
description:
# Add --verbose Flag to All Commands

## Problem
The --verbose flag is defined globally in main.rs (line 107) but not all commands use it. Users expect `rch workers list --verbose` to show more details.

## Commands Missing --verbose Behavior

### rch workers list
Current: Shows basic worker info
With --verbose: Should additionally show:
- Last probe timestamp
- Circuit breaker state
- Speed score history
- Recent job count
- SSH connection status

### rch self-test
Current: Shows pass/fail only
With --verbose: Should show:
- Each test step as it runs
- Timing for each phase
- Worker selection reasoning
- Transfer size and speed
- Compilation output

### rch queue
Current: Shows active builds
With --verbose: Should show:
- Queue position and ETA
- Resource requirements
- Why each build is waiting
- Worker assignment reasoning

### rch status
Current: Summary only
With --verbose: Should show:
- All worker details
- Active job details
- Recent build stats
- Config source info

## Implementation Pattern
In each command handler, check `cli.verbose`:

```rust
pub async fn workers_list(verbose: bool, json: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let workers = get_workers().await?;
    
    if json {
        // JSON always includes all fields
        output_json(&workers)?;
    } else if verbose {
        // Verbose: extra columns, more rows
        print_workers_verbose(&workers)?;
    } else {
        // Normal: compact summary
        print_workers_compact(&workers)?;
    }
}
```

## Files to Modify
- rch/src/commands.rs (multiple command handlers)
- rch/src/main.rs (ensure verbose is passed to handlers)

## Testing
- Test each command with and without --verbose
- Verify JSON output is unaffected (always complete)
- Verify --quiet suppresses verbose output

title: Unify Error Code System to RCH-Exxx Format
description:
## Overview

Migrate all error codes to use the unified RCH-Exxx format from `rch-common/src/errors/catalog.rs`.

## Problem

Currently there are TWO incompatible error code systems:
1. `ErrorCode` enum in `rch-common/src/errors/catalog.rs` → `RCH-E001` format
2. `error_codes` module in `rch/src/commands.rs` → `WORKER_UNREACHABLE` format

This creates confusion for agents parsing JSON responses.

## Solution

1. DELETE the `error_codes` module in `rch/src/commands.rs` (no backwards compatibility needed per AGENTS.md)
2. Create `rch-common/src/api/error.rs` with `ApiError` type
3. Update `JsonError` to use `ErrorCode` enum and become `ApiError`
4. Add `LegacyErrorCode` enum for any string-to-ErrorCode mapping needed internally
5. Update ALL call sites in CLI and daemon

## Implementation Details

### ApiError Structure

```rust
pub struct ApiError {
    pub code: String,           // "RCH-E100"
    pub category: ErrorCategory, // network, config, worker, etc.
    pub message: String,
    pub details: Option<String>,
    pub remediation: Vec<String>,
    pub context: ErrorContext,   // worker_id, host, etc.
    pub retry_after_secs: Option<u64>,
}
```

### ErrorCode Mapping

| Legacy String | New ErrorCode | RCH Code |
|--------------|---------------|----------|
| WORKER_UNREACHABLE | SshConnectionFailed | RCH-E100 |
| WORKER_NOT_FOUND | ConfigInvalidWorker | RCH-E008 |
| CONFIG_INVALID | ConfigValidationError | RCH-E004 |
| CONFIG_NOT_FOUND | ConfigNotFound | RCH-E001 |
| DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING | InternalDaemonNotRunning | RCH-E502 |
| INTERNAL_ERROR | InternalStateError | RCH-E504 |

## Required Unit Tests

### Test File: `rch-common/src/api/tests.rs`

```rust
#[test]
fn api_error_from_code_populates_all_fields() {
    let err = ApiError::from_code(ErrorCode::ConfigNotFound);
    assert_eq!(err.code, "RCH-E001");
    assert_eq!(err.category, ErrorCategory::Config);
    assert!(!err.message.is_empty());
    assert!(!err.remediation.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn api_error_with_context_serializes_correctly() {
    let err = ApiError::from_code(ErrorCode::SshConnectionFailed)
        .with_context("worker_id", "builder-1")
        .with_context("host", "192.168.1.100");
    
    let json = serde_json::to_value(&err).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["context"]["worker_id"], "builder-1");
    assert_eq!(json["context"]["host"], "192.168.1.100");
}

#[test]
fn api_error_serialization_excludes_empty_optionals() {
    let err = ApiError::from_code(ErrorCode::ConfigNotFound);
    let json = serde_json::to_string(&err).unwrap();
    
    // Should not contain empty fields
    assert!(!json.contains("\"details\":null"));
    assert!(!json.contains("\"retry_after_secs\":null"));
}

#[test]
fn legacy_error_code_mapping_covers_all_known_codes() {
    let codes = [
        "WORKER_UNREACHABLE", "WORKER_NOT_FOUND", "CONFIG_INVALID",
        "CONFIG_NOT_FOUND", "DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING", "INTERNAL_ERROR"
    ];
    for code in codes {
        let parsed = LegacyErrorCode::from_str(code);
        assert!(parsed.is_some(), "Missing mapping for {}", code);
    }
}

#[test]
fn error_code_numbers_are_unique() {
    let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for code in ErrorCode::all() {
        let num = code.code_number();
        assert!(seen.insert(num), "Duplicate code number: {}", num);
    }
}
```

## Required E2E Test Script

### File: `scripts/e2e_api_error_codes.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# E2E Test: Verify all JSON error responses use RCH-Exxx format
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="/tmp/rch_e2e_error_codes_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log"

log() {
    local level="$1"; shift
    local msg="$*"
    local ts=$(date -Iseconds)
    echo "[$ts] [$level] $msg" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

log "INFO" "Starting API error code E2E tests"
log "INFO" "Log file: $LOG_FILE"

# Build release binaries
log "INFO" "Building release binaries..."
cargo build -p rch --release 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
RCH="./target/release/rch"

# Test 1: Invalid worker probe should return RCH-Exxx code
log "TEST" "Testing invalid worker probe error format"
OUTPUT=$($RCH workers probe nonexistent-worker --json 2>&1 || true)
log "DEBUG" "Output: $OUTPUT"

if echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -e '.error.code' | grep -q 'RCH-E'; then
    log "PASS" "Invalid worker probe returns RCH-Exxx error code"
else
    log "FAIL" "Expected RCH-Exxx format, got: $(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.error.code // .error // "no error"')"
    exit 1
fi

# Test 2: Error has required fields
log "TEST" "Testing error response structure"
REQUIRED_FIELDS=("code" "category" "message")
for field in "${REQUIRED_FIELDS[@]}"; do
    if echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -e ".error.$field" > /dev/null; then
        log "PASS" "Error has required field: $field"
    else
        log "FAIL" "Missing required field: $field"
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Test 3: Error category is valid
log "TEST" "Testing error category values"
CATEGORY=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.error.category')
VALID_CATEGORIES="config network worker build transfer internal"
if echo "$VALID_CATEGORIES" | grep -qw "$CATEGORY"; then
    log "PASS" "Error category '$CATEGORY' is valid"
else
    log "FAIL" "Invalid error category: $CATEGORY"
    exit 1
fi

# Test 4: Remediation steps present
log "TEST" "Testing remediation steps"
REMEDIATION_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.error.remediation | length // 0')
if [ "$REMEDIATION_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "PASS" "Error has $REMEDIATION_COUNT remediation steps"
else
    log "WARN" "No remediation steps (optional but recommended)"
fi

log "INFO" "All API error code tests passed"
log "INFO" "Full log: $LOG_FILE"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `error_codes` module DELETED from `rch/src/commands.rs` (NOT deprecated)
- [x] `ApiError` type created in `rch-common/src/api/error.rs`
- [x] `LegacyErrorCode` enum maps old string codes internally
- [x] All JSON error responses use `RCH-Exxx` format
- [ ] Unit tests cover all error code conversions (5+ tests)
- [ ] E2E script validates error format (`scripts/e2e_api_error_codes.sh`)

title: Implement Test Report Generation (JUnit/HTML/JSON)
description:
## Purpose
Implement test report generation that produces JUnit XML (for CI) and HTML (for humans) reports from test runs.

## Why This Matters
- GitHub Actions needs JUnit XML for test summaries
- Developers need HTML for visual debugging
- Historical data enables regression tracking
- Timing graphs help identify performance issues

## Report Formats

### 1. JUnit XML (junit.xml)
Standard format for CI systems:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<testsuites name="true_e2e" tests="25" failures="2" errors="0" skipped="3" time="145.32">
  <testsuite name="cargo_tests" tests="10" failures="1" time="45.12">
    <testcase name="test_cargo_build_simple" classname="true_e2e::cargo" time="5.23"/>
    <testcase name="test_cargo_build_release" classname="true_e2e::cargo" time="8.45">
      <failure message="Artifact hash mismatch">
Expected: abc123...
Actual: def456...
      </failure>
    </testcase>
    <testcase name="test_cargo_test_all_pass" classname="true_e2e::cargo" time="12.34">
      <skipped message="No workers available"/>
    </testcase>
  </testsuite>
</testsuites>
```

### 2. HTML Report (report.html)
Visual report with:
- Summary table (pass/fail/skip counts)
- Test list with expandable details
- Timing chart (bar graph of test durations)
- Failure details with log excerpts
- Worker utilization stats

### 3. JSON Summary (summary.json)
Machine-readable for dashboards:
```json
{
  "run_id": "2024-01-19_120000",
  "total_tests": 25,
  "passed": 20,
  "failed": 2,
  "skipped": 3,
  "total_duration_ms": 145320,
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "test_cargo_build_simple",
      "status": "pass",
      "duration_ms": 5230,
      "worker": "css",
      "phases": {
        "sync": 1200,
        "execute": 3800,
        "artifact": 230
      }
    }
  ],
  "workers_used": ["css", "gpu2"],
  "slowest_tests": [...],
  "flaky_tests": [...]
}
```

## Implementation

```rust
// tests/true_e2e/report.rs

pub struct TestReportGenerator {
    results: Vec<TestResult>,
    start_time: DateTime<Utc>,
}

impl TestReportGenerator {
    pub fn add_result(&mut self, result: TestResult);
    pub fn generate_junit_xml(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>;
    pub fn generate_html(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>;
    pub fn generate_summary_json(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>;
}

pub struct TestResult {
    pub name: String,
    pub status: TestStatus,
    pub duration: Duration,
    pub worker: Option<String>,
    pub phases: HashMap<String, Duration>,
    pub failure_message: Option<String>,
    pub log_file: PathBuf,
}
```

## HTML Template Features
- Responsive design (works on mobile)
- Dark mode support
- Collapsible sections
- Syntax highlighting for logs
- Copy-to-clipboard for commands

## Unit Tests
1. test_junit_xml_is_valid (parse with XML library)
2. test_html_contains_all_tests
3. test_timing_aggregation_correct
4. test_failure_details_included

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] JUnit XML validates against schema
- [ ] HTML renders correctly in browsers
- [ ] JSON is valid and complete
- [ ] Timing data is accurate
- [ ] Failure details are actionable
- [ ] Reports work with 0 tests (edge case)

title: Idea: Daemon hot-reload for config + workers
description:
## Background
Changing workers or config currently requires daemon restart, which disrupts ongoing sessions and adds friction. Hot-reload makes RCH feel always-on and operationally smooth.

## Goals
- Auto-detect changes to `workers.toml` and `config.toml` and apply without restart.
- Provide manual reload via SIGHUP / CLI `rch daemon reload`.
- Maintain fail-open behavior and avoid breaking active jobs.

## Design / Approach
- Add file watcher (polling/inotify) in rchd for workers/config paths.
- On change: validate new config, reconcile worker pool (add/update/remove), update selection config.
- Ensure no disruption: existing jobs continue; new jobs use updated config.
- Add CLI command to trigger reload (fallback if watchers unavailable).

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Extend daemon config loader to support reload + diff logging.
- Implement worker pool reconciliation (add new, update existing, mark removed as draining).
- Add `rch daemon reload` command and SIGHUP handler.
- Emit structured event logs for reload outcome.

## Tests
- Unit: config diff logic + invalid config rejection.
- Integration: modify workers.toml and confirm new worker appears in status without restart.
- Integration: removing worker marks it draining but does not kill active jobs.
- E2E: reload via CLI and SIGHUP.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Config changes take effect within seconds without restart.
- Invalid config does not replace last-known-good.
- Active jobs are not interrupted.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-c7xr.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- Partial writes/invalid config: keep last-known-good and warn.
- Debounce rapid edits to avoid thrash.
- Removing worker with active job -> mark draining; do not interrupt jobs.

## E2E Outline
- Modify workers.toml to add worker -> status updates without restart.
- Inject invalid config -> daemon keeps old config and logs error.
- Reload via SIGHUP and via `rch daemon reload`.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rchd/src/config.rs: reload/validate and reject invalid configs.
- rchd/src/workers.rs: reconcile add/update/remove (drain on remove).
- rchd/src/api.rs: reload endpoint returns status and error info.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-c7xr.sh: modify workers.toml and confirm status updates without restart.
- Exercise SIGHUP and CLI reload; verify active jobs remain running.

title: Feed multi-signal reliability debt into worker health/selection penalties
description:
Incorporate unresolved reliability debt into worker score/eligibility so degraded nodes are not repeatedly selected. Expand from process-only penalties to a unified multi-signal health model that combines process-triage debt, repo-convergence confidence, disk-pressure admission risk, and heartbeat/liveness evidence. Include quarantine/recovery hysteresis so recovered workers re-enter service safely without flapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Selection model aggregates multi-signal reliability debt (process, convergence, disk, heartbeat) into deterministic health states and penalties.
- Health states include at least healthy, degraded, quarantined, and probing-recovery with explicit transition rules.
- Penalties and quarantine windows are bounded and decay over time to avoid permanent exclusion from transient incidents.
- If all workers are unsafe/degraded, scheduler preserves fail-open local fallback with explicit reason-coded diagnostics.
- Unit/integration/E2E tests validate mixed-signal failure combinations, flapping resistance, and smooth reintegration after recovery, with structured decision logs.

title: Epic: Mutually Reinforcing Self-Healing RCH System
description:
# Epic: Mutually Reinforcing Self-Healing RCH System

## Vision
Create a robust, self-healing Remote Compilation Helper system where components automatically ensure each other's health, dramatically reducing "silent failures" where builds run locally without users realizing.

## Problem Statement
RCH currently has a "fail-open" design where:
1. If daemon isn't running → hook silently allows local execution
2. If hook isn't installed → daemon runs but all builds are local
3. Users often don't realize RCH isn't working until they manually check

This leads to frustration: "I thought my builds were being offloaded but they've been local the whole time!"

## Solution: Mutually Reinforcing Architecture

### The Core Insight
Each RCH component should verify and restore the others:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  MUTUALLY REINFORCING SYSTEM                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│    ┌─────────┐         auto-starts         ┌─────────┐      │
│    │  Hook   │ ─────────────────────────▶  │ Daemon  │      │
│    │ (rch)   │                             │ (rchd)  │      │
│    └─────────┘  ◀─────────────────────────  └─────────┘      │
│                     auto-installs hooks                      │
│                                                              │
│                          ▲    ▲                              │
│                          │    │                              │
│                     fixes│    │fixes                         │
│                          │    │                              │
│                       ┌──┴────┴──┐                           │
│                       │  Doctor  │                           │
│                       │ (--fix)  │                           │
│                       └──────────┘                           │
│                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Component Responsibilities

| Component | Primary Role | Self-Healing Role |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Hook** (rch) | Intercept builds, route to daemon | Auto-start daemon if unavailable |
| **Daemon** (rchd) | Manage workers, execute builds | Auto-install hook on startup |
| **Doctor** (rch doctor --fix) | Diagnose issues | Fix both hook and daemon |

### User Experience Goals

1. **Zero-config success**: Fresh RCH install "just works" after `rch daemon start`
2. **Self-recovery**: System recovers from daemon crashes automatically
3. **Clear feedback**: Users always know what's happening (logs, status)
4. **Opt-out available**: Power users can disable self-healing if desired

## Implementation Breakdown

### Phase 1: Core Self-Healing (bd-qsr3, bd-1emo)
- Hook auto-starts daemon when connection fails
- Daemon auto-installs hook on startup
- These two create the "mutual reinforcement"

### Phase 2: Doctor Integration (bd-3pam, bd-2juk)
- Doctor --fix actually fixes hooks (not just reports)
- Doctor --fix starts daemon if not running
- Provides manual repair path

### Phase 3: Configuration (bd-18e8)
- Config options to control self-healing
- CLI override flags
- Per-environment customization

### Phase 4: Testing (bd-xxxx - to be created)
- Comprehensive unit tests
- End-to-end test scripts
- Validation of all self-healing paths

## Success Metrics

1. **Reduced support burden**: Users don't ask "why are my builds local?"
2. **Faster recovery**: System self-heals within seconds of daemon crash
3. **Clear logging**: Every auto-recovery action is logged clearly
4. **No surprises**: Users understand what happened and why

## Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Infinite restart loop | Cooldown period (30s default) between auto-starts |
| Race conditions | Lockfile prevents concurrent daemon starts |
| Config confusion | Sensible defaults, clear documentation |
| Backwards compatibility | All self-healing enabled by default |

## Out of Scope
- Automatic worker recovery (separate epic)
- Network partition handling (complex distributed systems problem)
- Multi-user daemon sharing (security implications)

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All 5 implementation beads completed
- [ ] All unit tests passing
- [ ] E2E test script validates full self-healing cycle
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Config options documented
- [ ] Logging meets requirements

## Related Beads
- bd-qsr3: Hook Auto-Starts Daemon When Unavailable
- bd-1emo: Daemon Auto-Installs Claude Code Hooks on Startup
- bd-3pam: Doctor --fix Actually Fixes Hooks
- bd-2juk: Doctor --fix Auto-Starts Daemon
- bd-18e8: Add Configuration Options for Self-Healing Behavior

### E2E Test Script (scripts/test_config_doctor.sh)
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
LOG_FILE=${RCH_TEST_LOG:-/tmp/rch_doctor_test.log}

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }

log "Testing rch config doctor"

# Test 1: Doctor runs without error on valid config
log "Test 1: Doctor on valid config"
rch config doctor 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
if [ ${PIPESTATUS[0]} -eq 0 ]; then
  log "PASS: Doctor passes on valid config"
else
  log "WARN: Doctor found issues (may be expected)"
fi

# Test 2: Doctor detects invalid config
log "Test 2: Doctor detects invalid config"
mkdir -p /tmp/rch_test_config
echo 'invalid toml [[[' > /tmp/rch_test_config/config.toml
RCH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/rch_test_config rch config doctor 2>&1 | grep -qi "parse\|error" || {
  log "FAIL: Doctor didn't detect invalid TOML"
  exit 1
}
log "PASS: Doctor detected invalid config"

# Test 3: JSON output format
log "Test 3: JSON output format"
rch config doctor --json | jq -e '.checks' >/dev/null || {
  log "FAIL: JSON output missing .checks"
  exit 1
}
log "PASS: JSON output correct"

# Cleanup
rm -rf /tmp/rch_test_config

log "Config doctor tests complete"
```

### Logging Requirements
- Log each check started at DEBUG level
- Log check results at INFO level
- Log remediation suggestions at WARN level

title: Verify --json Flag Coverage for All CLI Commands
description:
## Overview

Audit all CLI commands to ensure `--json` flag produces proper structured output using the unified `ApiResponse<T>` envelope.

## Commands to Audit

### Core Commands
- [ ] `rch status` - verify JSON output uses ApiResponse<SystemOverview>
- [ ] `rch workers list` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch workers probe` - verify JSON output with ApiError on failure
- [ ] `rch workers benchmark` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch config show` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch diagnose` - verify JSON output

### Setup Commands
- [ ] `rch init` - add JSON output (currently interactive only, add --json for non-interactive)
- [ ] `rch doctor` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch hook install/test` - verify JSON output

### Agent Commands
- [ ] `rch agents list` - add/verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch agents status` - add/verify JSON output

### Fleet Commands
- [ ] `rch fleet deploy` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch fleet status` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch fleet rollback` - verify JSON output

### Other Commands
- [ ] `rch self-test` - add structured JSON output
- [ ] `rch speedscore` - verify JSON output
- [ ] `rch daemon status/logs` - verify JSON output

## Implementation Checklist

For EACH command:
1. Add `--json` flag if missing
2. Return `ApiResponse<CommandSpecificType>` envelope
3. On error return `ApiResponse::err(cmd, ApiError::from_code(...))`
4. Strip ANSI codes when --json is set
5. Set exit code: 0 for success, appropriate non-zero for failures

## Required Unit Tests

### Test File: `rch/src/commands/tests.rs`

Each command needs at minimum:

```rust
#[test]
fn test_status_json_output_structure() {
    // Verify output deserializes to ApiResponse<SystemOverview>
    // Verify api_version, timestamp, success fields present
}

#[test]
fn test_status_json_no_ansi_codes() {
    // Verify output contains no ANSI escape sequences
}

#[test]
fn test_status_json_error_format() {
    // Simulate error condition
    // Verify error uses ApiError with RCH-Exxx code
}
```

### Minimum Test Count: 16 tests

- `test_{command}_json_output_structure` - 8 commands x 1 = 8 tests
- `test_{command}_json_no_ansi_codes` - 4 core commands x 1 = 4 tests
- `test_{command}_json_error_format` - 4 commands x 1 = 4 tests

## E2E Test Script

### `scripts/e2e_json_flags.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# E2E Test: JSON Flag Coverage
# Tests that all commands produce valid JSON with --json flag

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
log_pass() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] PASS $*"; }
log_fail() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] FAIL $*"; exit 1; }

FAILED=0
PASSED=0
SKIPPED=0

test_json_output() {
    local cmd="$1"
    local name="$2"
    local expect_success="${3:-true}"

    log "Testing: $name"

    # Run command and capture output
    local output
    local exit_code=0
    output=$($cmd 2>&1) || exit_code=$?

    # Check if output is valid JSON
    if ! echo "$output" | jq . > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log_fail "$name: Output is not valid JSON"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    # Check envelope structure
    local has_api_version has_success has_timestamp
    has_api_version=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.api_version // empty')
    has_success=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.success // empty')
    has_timestamp=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.timestamp // empty')

    if [ -z "$has_api_version" ]; then
        log_fail "$name: Missing api_version field"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    if [ -z "$has_success" ]; then
        log_fail "$name: Missing success field"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    # Check for ANSI codes
    if echo "$output" | grep -qP '\x1b\['; then
        log_fail "$name: Contains ANSI escape codes"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    # Check exit code matches success field
    local json_success=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.success')
    if [ "$json_success" = "true" ] && [ "$exit_code" -ne 0 ]; then
        log_fail "$name: success=true but exit_code=$exit_code"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    if [ "$json_success" = "false" ] && [ "$exit_code" -eq 0 ]; then
        log_fail "$name: success=false but exit_code=0"
        ((FAILED++))
        return 1
    fi

    # If error, check error format
    if [ "$json_success" = "false" ]; then
        local error_code=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.error.code // empty')
        if [ -z "$error_code" ]; then
            log_fail "$name: Error response missing error.code"
            ((FAILED++))
            return 1
        fi
        if ! echo "$error_code" | grep -qP '^RCH-E[0-9]{3}$'; then
            log_fail "$name: Error code not in RCH-Exxx format"
            ((FAILED++))
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    log_pass "$name"
    ((PASSED++))
}

# Build fresh
log "Building rch..."
cargo build -p rch --release 2>&1 | tail -5

RCH="$PROJECT_ROOT/target/release/rch"

log "========================================"
log "Testing JSON output for all commands"
log "========================================"

# Core commands
test_json_output "$RCH status --json" "rch status --json"
test_json_output "$RCH workers list --json" "rch workers list --json" || true
test_json_output "$RCH config show --json" "rch config show --json" || true

# Setup commands
test_json_output "$RCH doctor --json" "rch doctor --json" || true
test_json_output "$RCH hook test --json" "rch hook test --json" || true

# Commands that may not have daemon running
test_json_output "$RCH daemon status --json" "rch daemon status --json" || true

log "========================================"
log "Summary: $PASSED passed, $FAILED failed, $SKIPPED skipped"
log "========================================"

if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
    exit 1
fi

log "All E2E JSON flag tests passed!"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All listed commands produce valid JSON with --json flag
- [ ] No ANSI codes in JSON output (verify with grep for escape sequences)
- [ ] Consistent ApiResponse envelope format across all commands
- [ ] Error responses use ApiError with RCH-Exxx codes
- [ ] Exit codes correct: 0 for success, non-zero for failure
- [ ] Exit codes align with `success` field in JSON
- [ ] Unit tests pass: 16 tests minimum
- [ ] E2E test script passes: `scripts/e2e_json_flags.sh`

title: EPIC: CLI Consistency and Usability Enhancements
description:
# CLI Consistency and Usability Enhancements

## Overview
RCH has 15+ main commands with 60+ subcommands. While individually well-documented, there are consistency issues that create friction for users learning the tool.

## Key Problems Identified

### 1. Inconsistent Flag Support
- `--verbose` exists on some commands but not others (missing on: workers list, self-test, queue)
- `--json` has no short form (-j) despite being commonly used
- `--format` has no short form (-f)

### 2. Missing Safety Features
- `rch daemon restart` has NO confirmation prompt despite potentially interrupting active builds
- `rch cancel` has no `--dry-run` to preview what would be cancelled
- `rch workers drain` takes effect immediately with no warning

### 3. Confusing Terminology
Commands use inconsistent terms for the same concept:
- `drain` vs `disable` vs `pause` - what's the difference?
- `job` vs `build` vs `compilation` - used interchangeably
- `worker` vs `remote` vs `node` - inconsistent naming

### 4. Missing Convenience Commands
- No `rch check` for quick yes/no health status
- No `--follow` on `rch queue` for streaming output
- No single command showing complete system health

## Key Files
- rch/src/main.rs - CLI definitions (lines 170-651)
- rch/src/commands.rs - Command implementations (10k+ lines)

## Design Principles
1. **Consistency**: Same flags should work the same way across all commands
2. **Safety**: Destructive/disruptive operations need confirmation
3. **Discoverability**: Related functionality should be grouped logically
4. **Efficiency**: Common operations should have short forms

## Success Criteria
- All commands support --verbose where it makes sense
- All destructive operations have confirmation prompts
- Terminology is unified and documented
- Short flags available for common options
close_reason: All CLI consistency criteria met: --verbose is global, -j/-F short forms exist, rch check command exists, confirmation prompts on destructive operations (daemon restart, workers drain, cancel --all). Terminology is documented in help text.

title: E2E: Integration Test Script for All Audit Fixes
description:
Create a comprehensive end-to-end test script that validates all 4 workstreams and verifies RCH performance requirements from AGENTS.md.

Script location: scripts/audit_e2e.sh (consistent with existing scripts/e2e_test.sh)
Alternatively: tests/audit_integration.rs (Rust integration test)

TEST PLAN:

1. BUILD VERIFICATION:
   - cargo check --all-targets (no compile errors)
   - cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings (no warnings)
   - cargo fmt --check (formatting correct)
   - cargo test --all (all unit tests pass)
   - Log: "BUILD: OK" or "BUILD: FAILED at step X"

2. PERFORMANCE BUDGET VERIFICATION (from AGENTS.md lines 250-258):
   - Hook decision for NON-compilation commands: must be <1ms, panic at 5ms
   - Hook decision for compilation commands: must be <5ms, panic at 10ms
   
   Test method:
   - Run classify_command() 100 times on known non-compilation commands (ls, cat, echo, git status)
   - Measure p50, p95, p99 latency
   - FAIL if p99 > 1ms for non-compilation
   
   - Run classify_command() 100 times on known compilation commands (cargo build, make, gcc)
   - Measure p50, p95, p99 latency  
   - FAIL if p99 > 5ms for compilation
   
   Log: "PERF: non-compilation p99={X}ms (<1ms required) {PASS|FAIL}"
   Log: "PERF: compilation p99={X}ms (<5ms required) {PASS|FAIL}"

3. WS1 VERIFICATION (Blocking I/O):
   - Run the hook with a timing history file present
   - Verify spawn_blocking is used (check tokio task metrics if available)
   - Log: timing of load/save operations

4. WS2 VERIFICATION (Allocations):
   - Run classify_command() on 1000 non-compilation commands
   - Measure elapsed time, verify <5ms average
   - Verify reason fields are Cow::Borrowed on reject path (if possible to introspect)
   - Log: "CLASSIFICATION: {N} commands in {T}ms, avg {T/N}ms"

5. WS3 VERIFICATION (Atomics):
   - Create a WorkerState, read all atomic fields concurrently from 10 threads
   - Verify no panics, all values are valid
   - Log: "ATOMIC ACCESS: {N} concurrent reads, 0 errors"

6. WS4 VERIFICATION (Multi-command):
   - Test split_shell_commands with edge cases (quoting, empty, long input)
   - Feed 20 representative multi-command strings through classify_command()
   - Verify expected classification for each
   - Test fail-open: feed malformed input, verify no panic
   - Log each: "MULTI-CMD: '{cmd}' → compilation={bool} (expected={bool}) {PASS|FAIL}"

7. FAIL-OPEN VERIFICATION:
   - Feed intentionally malformed input to the classifier
   - Verify it returns a valid result (not panic/error)
   - Log: "FAIL-OPEN: malformed input handled gracefully {PASS|FAIL}"

8. REGRESSION CHECK:
   - Run full cargo test suite
   - Compare test count before/after (should only increase)
   - Log: "REGRESSION: {passed}/{total} tests passed, {new} new tests added"

OUTPUT FORMAT:
  Each section logs [PASS] or [FAIL] with details.
  Include timestamps for each section.
  Final summary: "AUDIT E2E: X/8 sections passed"
  Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 otherwise.

LOGGING:
  Use tracing or simple println with timestamps.
  All output should be parseable for CI integration.
  Follow existing scripts/e2e_test.sh patterns where applicable.

title: Add TUI keyboard shortcuts for worker actions
description:
# Add Worker Action Keyboard Shortcuts

## Problem
Users must leave TUI to drain/enable workers or cancel builds. The TUI is read-only when it could support common actions.

## Proposed Shortcuts
When Workers panel is selected:
```
d     Drain selected worker (with confirmation)
e     Enable selected worker  
D     Drain ALL workers (with confirmation)
E     Enable ALL workers
r     Refresh worker status immediately
p     Probe selected worker
```

When Active Builds panel is selected:
```
k     Cancel selected build (SIGTERM, with confirmation)
K     Force kill selected build (SIGKILL)
c     Copy build command to clipboard
```

When Build History panel is selected:
```
c     Copy build details to clipboard
Enter View build logs (already works)
/     Filter builds (already works, but undocumented)
```

## Implementation Notes
1. Drain/enable should call daemon API via Unix socket
2. Cancel should send signal to remote process
3. Confirmations should use a modal dialog
4. Actions should show success/error feedback

## API Calls Needed
- POST /workers/{id}/drain
- POST /workers/{id}/enable
- POST /builds/{id}/cancel
- POST /builds/{id}/kill

These APIs should already exist in rchd; we just need to call them from TUI.

## Confirmation Dialog
For destructive actions, show centered modal:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Drain worker 'css'?             │
│                                 │
│ This will stop routing new      │
│ jobs to this worker.            │
│                                 │
│        [Y]es    [N]o            │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Files to Modify
- rch/src/tui/app.rs (event handling, API calls)
- rch/src/tui/state.rs (action state tracking)
- rch/src/tui/widgets.rs (confirmation dialog rendering, help text)

title: Epic: True End-to-End Integration Tests (No Mocks)
description:
# Epic: True End-to-End Integration Tests (No Mocks)

## Executive Summary

This epic establishes a comprehensive suite of **100% realistic end-to-end integration tests** for RCH (Remote Compilation Helper). Unlike the existing mock-based test suite, these tests will:

- Connect to **real remote workers** via actual SSH
- Execute **real cargo/compiler commands** on those workers
- Transfer **real project files** via rsync
- Retrieve **real build artifacts** back to the local machine
- Validate **output correctness** against local execution

## Merged Scope: Fleet & Worker Lifecycle Tests (formerly bd-guef)

This epic now also includes the fleet and worker lifecycle E2E tests that were previously in a separate epic. This consolidation reduces duplication and provides a single canonical, comprehensive E2E suite.

### Fleet & Worker Lifecycle Coverage

1. **Multi-Worker Scenarios (bd-2s8m)**: Load balancing, priority selection, cached project locality, fleet scaling, heterogeneous workers
2. **Worker Lifecycle**: Registration, health monitoring, removal, updates, disconnects
3. **Test Logging Standardization (bd-2zsu)**: Structured logging across all test files

## Background & Motivation

### Current Test Gap Analysis

The existing RCH test suite provides good coverage for:
- Command classification logic (e2e_hook.rs)
- Daemon lifecycle and API (e2e_daemon.rs)
- Worker connectivity patterns (e2e_worker.rs)
- Fleet operations (e2e_fleet.rs)

However, all tests use **mock infrastructure**:
- `RCH_MOCK_SSH=1` environment variable bypasses real SSH
- `WorkersFixture::mock_local()` creates fake workers
- No actual compilation happens on remote machines
- No real artifact transfer is validated

### Why This Matters

RCH is a **transparent compilation offloading system** for AI coding agents. The agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) have no awareness that their `cargo build` or `cargo test` commands execute remotely. This transparency requires **absolute correctness** in:

1. **Project synchronization** - Every file the build needs must arrive
2. **Command execution** - Exact same behavior as local execution
3. **Output capture** - Stdout/stderr must be byte-for-byte identical
4. **Exit codes** - Test failures (101), build errors (1) must propagate
5. **Artifact retrieval** - Compiled binaries must work locally

A bug in any of these areas breaks the illusion of local execution and causes agent confusion or failures.

## Test Categories

### Cargo/Rust Compilation (bd-12hi)
- cargo build, test, check, clippy, bench
- All CompilationKind variants

### SSH Infrastructure (bd-255k)
- Connection, authentication, command execution
- Output capture, timeout handling

### Project Sync (bd-1f2v)
- rsync transfer, excludes, incremental sync

### Artifact Transfer (bd-20zz)
- Binary retrieval, correctness verification

### Error Handling & Recovery (bd-23n3)
- Network failures, worker crashes, fail-open behavior
- Circuit breaker state transitions

### C/C++ Compilers (bd-v9pq)
- gcc, g++, clang, make, cmake, ninja

### Output Validation (bd-2ga8)
- Color preservation, ANSI codes, terminal semantics

### Performance & Timing (bd-1nhd)
- Hook classification <1ms, full pipeline <15% overhead

### Multi-Worker Scenarios (bd-2s8m)
- Load balancing, priority selection, heterogeneous workers
- Worker registration, health monitoring, lifecycle

### Test Logging Standardization (bd-2zsu)
- Structured JSON logging across all test files

## Success Criteria

- All CompilationKind variants tested with real workers
- Zero tolerance for output differences from local execution
- Exit codes must match exactly
- Tests pass reliably in CI with real infrastructure
- All tests produce structured, parseable logs
- Worker lifecycle scenarios pass in CI
- Multi-worker load balancing verified
- 100% structured logging compliance

title: Idea: Stable remote path per project when hash unchanged
description:
## Background
Remote path currently includes project hash and may churn; repeated builds with unchanged inputs should reuse the same remote path to improve cache hits and avoid redundant rsync dir creation.

## Goals
- Use a stable remote path for a project when its hash is unchanged.
- Keep isolation when hash changes (avoid mixing incompatible states).

## Design / Approach
- Maintain `project_id + hash` mapping but re-use existing remote dir if present.
- Add a small local cache file to remember last hash per project and worker (optional).
- Ensure cleanup routines respect stable paths.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- Adjust remote path computation to check for existing directory on worker.
- Add optional local cache metadata for speed.
- Update cleanup logic to avoid deleting active cache.

## Tests
- Unit: remote path selection logic.
- Integration: repeated build reuses remote dir.
- E2E: hash change triggers new remote dir.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated builds with unchanged inputs reuse remote path.
- Hash changes still isolate build state.

## Logging & E2E
- E2E script: scripts/e2e_bd-2df5.sh (one script per bead unless intentionally combined).
- Logging format: JSONL via TestLogger (tests/true_e2e/logging.rs) or scripts/test_lib.sh log_json.
- Required fields: ts, test, phase, worker, command, bytes_transferred, duration_ms, result, error (if any).
- Phases to log (as applicable): classify, select, sync_up, exec, sync_down, cleanup, summary.
- Include a final summary block with pass/fail counts and total elapsed time.

## Edge Cases & UX
- Stability is per-worker; do not reuse across workers.
- If remote dir existence check fails, fall back to normal path.
- Old hash dirs should be eligible for cleanup to prevent bloat.

## E2E Outline
- Same hash builds reuse same remote dir.
- Change key file -> new hash -> new remote dir.
- Cleanup keeps newest dir.

## Unit Tests (Detailed)
- rch/src/transfer.rs: remote path computation with hash reuse.
- cleanup logic ignores active hash dir.

## E2E Script Notes
- scripts/e2e_bd-2df5.sh: same hash -> reuse; different hash -> new dir.
close_reason: MERGED into bd-5a5k (Project Cache Affinity System). Stable remote paths are now part of the unified cache affinity feature.

title: Workstream: Canonical Worker Filesystem Topology (/data/projects + /dp)

This stream establishes idempotent bootstrap/enforcement, preflight checks, and migration safety so later dependency-convergence logic can rely on deterministic absolute/relative path semantics.

## Success Criteria
- Canonical path utilities and invariants are enforced across hook/daemon/worker boundaries.
- Workers failing topology invariants are automatically excluded from remote scheduling until repaired.
- Migration + rollback plan is validated on representative fleet states.
- Foundational path tests prove deterministic behavior and safety guardrails.

title: Create E2E test infrastructure with logging framework
description:
# Create E2E Test Infrastructure

## Overview
Before implementing individual features, we need a robust E2E test framework that all other tests can build upon. This provides consistent logging, terminal simulation, and validation utilities.

## Components to Create

### 1. Test Framework (scripts/lib/test_framework.sh)
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
# RCH E2E Test Framework

# Global test configuration
export RCH_TEST_MODE=1
export RCH_TEST_LOG=${RCH_TEST_LOG:-/tmp/rch_test_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log}
export RCH_TEST_VERBOSE=${RCH_TEST_VERBOSE:-0}

# Logging functions
log_info() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [INFO] $*" | tee -a "$RCH_TEST_LOG"; }
log_pass() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [PASS] $*" | tee -a "$RCH_TEST_LOG"; }
log_fail() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [FAIL] $*" | tee -a "$RCH_TEST_LOG"; }
log_skip() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [SKIP] $*" | tee -a "$RCH_TEST_LOG"; }
log_debug() { [ "$RCH_TEST_VERBOSE" = 1 ] && echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [DEBUG] $*" | tee -a "$RCH_TEST_LOG"; }

# Test assertion helpers
assert_eq() { [ "$1" = "$2" ] || { log_fail "Expected '$1' = '$2'"; return 1; }; }
assert_contains() { echo "$1" | grep -q "$2" || { log_fail "'$1' should contain '$2'"; return 1; }; }
assert_exit_code() { [ "$1" = "$2" ] || { log_fail "Expected exit $2, got $1"; return 1; }; }

# TUI testing helpers (using pseudo-terminal)
tui_send_keys() { ... }
tui_expect_output() { ... }
tui_screenshot() { ... }

# Cleanup helpers
setup_test_env() { ... }
teardown_test_env() { ... }
```

### 2. Test Runner (scripts/run_e2e_tests.sh)
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run all E2E tests with proper sequencing

source scripts/lib/test_framework.sh

TESTS=(
  "test_tui_icons.sh"
  "test_tui_help.sh"
  "test_verbose_flag.sh"
  "test_confirmations.sh"
  "test_error_codes.sh"
  "test_progress_indicators.sh"
  "test_config_doctor.sh"
)

PASSED=0
FAILED=0
SKIPPED=0

for test in "${TESTS[@]}"; do
  log_info "Running: $test"
  if scripts/e2e/"$test"; then
    ((PASSED++))
  else
    ((FAILED++))
  fi
done

log_info "Results: $PASSED passed, $FAILED failed, $SKIPPED skipped"
exit $FAILED
```

### 3. Log Analysis Tool (scripts/analyze_test_logs.sh)
Extract metrics from test logs for CI reporting.

## Files to Create
- scripts/lib/test_framework.sh
- scripts/run_e2e_tests.sh
- scripts/analyze_test_logs.sh
- scripts/e2e/.gitkeep (directory for individual tests)

## Integration with CI
Add to .github/workflows/ci.yml:
```yaml
- name: Run E2E Tests
  run: ./scripts/run_e2e_tests.sh
  env:
    RCH_TEST_VERBOSE: 1
```
close_reason: done

title: Implement progress rate limiting and terminal safety

Create progress infrastructure in rch-common/src/ui/progress/mod.rs for safe progress display:

- Terminal width tracking with resize handling

- Cursor visibility management (hide during progress, restore after)

Technical requirements:
- Use std::sync::atomic for rate limiting state
- Implement Drop trait for cleanup guarantees
- Register signal handler for SIGINT/SIGTERM
- Handle terminal resize (SIGWINCH) gracefully
