title: Property-based + mutation testing for the command-classification hot path (proptest + cargo-mutants)
description:
# Property-based + mutation testing for the command-classification hot path

## Background

`rch/src/classify.rs` and `rch-common/src/patterns.rs` together
implement the 5-tier command classification that runs on every Bash
command flowing through Claude Code. The current test surface (~30
unit tests in the workspace) covers the documented variants in
AGENTS.md (cargo build, cargo test, bun test, gcc, etc.) plus a
handful of edge cases.

What it does NOT cover well:

- **Adversarial inputs**: commands with embedded quotes, escaped pipes, env-var prefixes mixed with subshell substitution, partial UTF-8, control characters.
- **Generated combinations**: every `cargo <subcommand>` × every modifier flag × every env-var prefix combination is in the tens of thousands. Hand-rolled tests sample a few; `proptest` can sweep the whole space.
- **Bug-injected verification**: even with 100% line coverage on `classify.rs`, a mutation like `==` → `!=` may pass the suite if no test asserts the inverse path. `cargo-mutants` finds these gaps.

## Why this matters

The fail-open philosophy (AGENTS.md: "any non-zero exit BLOCKS the
agent's Bash command") makes classify.rs's correctness a top-3
reliability concern in the project. A misclassification that exits
non-zero blocks a real Bash command that should have run — silently
breaking the agent.

`proptest` + `cargo-mutants` together catch exactly the class of bugs
that hand-written tests miss: input edge cases AND unconvincing
assertions.

## Why this is in the hook epic

`classify.rs` is consumed primarily by the hook hot path. Sibling beads
in the hook epic (zcecy.9 classify cache skip, zcecy.13 fail-open
integration tests, zcecy.14 module split) all touch this code; this
bead institutionalizes the regression net.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Property-based testing

- [ ] New file `rch/tests/classify_proptest.rs` (or `rch-common/src/patterns/proptest.rs` for the pattern layer).
- [ ] Properties asserted (each via `proptest! { ... }`):
  1. **Determinism**: classifying the same input twice yields the same `Classification`.
  2. **Trim invariance**: `classify_command(s)` == `classify_command(s.trim())`.
  3. **Whitespace insertion within tokens does NOT change classification**: e.g., `"cargo  build"` (double space between `cargo` and `build`) classifies the same as `"cargo build"`. (Per AGENTS.md, the classifier should be tolerant of this.)
  4. **Env-var prefix resilience**: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 cargo test` classifies as `CargoTest` (per AGENTS.md). Generated property: any sequence of `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=[^ ]*` prefixes followed by a known cargo command preserves the classification.
  5. **No-panic property**: any UTF-8 string of length ≤ 4KB does not panic the classifier (returns Some classification or None, never panics).
  6. **Pipe/redirect/background detection**: any input containing an unquoted top-level `|`, `>`, `<`, or `&` is classified as NOT-intercepted (per AGENTS.md: "Piped/redirected/backgrounded commands"). Generated property covers the full ASCII shell metacharacter set.
  7. **Bun watch mode preserved**: `bun test --watch` and `bun typecheck --watch` are classified as NOT-intercepted (per AGENTS.md). Generated property: the `--watch` token in any position keeps the not-intercepted classification.
- [ ] Each property runs ≥1024 iterations by default (proptest's standard); CI can scale via `PROPTEST_CASES`.
- [ ] Failure shrinks: when proptest finds a failure, the minimal counterexample is logged with full context (the input, expected, actual).
- [ ] A regression-corpus directory `rch/tests/classify_proptest_corpus/` stores past failures; proptest auto-loads it via `proptest!`'s `cases` feature so regressions can never recur.

### Mutation testing

- [ ] `cargo-mutants` configured via `cargo-mutants.toml` at workspace root.
- [ ] Mutation testing scope: `rch/src/classify.rs`, `rch-common/src/patterns.rs`, `rch/src/doctor.rs::aggregate_verdict`, `rch/src/doctor.rs::should_run` (the scope filter from t01).
- [ ] CI job (gated, runs nightly not on every PR — full mutation testing is slow): `cargo mutants --in-place --no-shuffle --output mutants_out`.
- [ ] **Mutation score target**: ≥ 90% mutants caught (i.e., ≤10% are missed by tests). Failures are flagged in a follow-up bead per missed mutation.
- [ ] An exclusion list (`mutants.exclude`) for legitimately untestable mutations (e.g., logging string changes) — must be reviewed periodically.

### Logging assertion (every property emits a structured event)

- [ ] When a property test fails, the minimal counterexample is also emitted as a `tracing::error!` event with target `rch::test::proptest` so the failure shows in the structured log next to other test signals.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — proptest infrastructure (1 day)

1. Add `proptest = "1"` to `[dev-dependencies]` for `rch` and `rch-common`.
2. Author `rch/tests/classify_proptest.rs` skeleton.
3. Define generators:
   - `arb_known_cargo_subcommand` — uniformly samples from `["build", "test", "check", "clippy", "run", "doc", ...]`.
   - `arb_env_var_prefix` — generates `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=[a-zA-Z0-9_/.-]*` strings.
   - `arb_modifier_flag` — `["--release", "--workspace", "-p <name>", "--lib", "--bins", ...]`.
   - `arb_whitespace` — between tokens, varies count (1-4 spaces, including tabs).
   - `arb_safe_filler` — ASCII-printable filler that doesn't include shell metacharacters.
4. Implement each property (see AC list above).
5. Run locally; debug shrinks until clean.

### Phase 2 — regression corpus (0.5 day)

1. After phase 1, harvest any failures into `rch/tests/classify_proptest_corpus/<sha>.txt` (proptest's regression file format).
2. Wire via `proptest! { #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig { ... cases_dir: Some("classify_proptest_corpus") ... })]`.

### Phase 3 — cargo-mutants config (1 day)

1. Add `cargo-mutants` to `Cargo.toml` workspace's `[workspace.metadata.cargo-mutants]` (it auto-detects).
2. Author `cargo-mutants.toml`:
   ```toml
   timeout = "300s"
   exclude_globs = ["*/tests/*", "*/benches/*", "*/examples/*"]
   examine_globs = [
       "rch/src/classify.rs",
       "rch-common/src/patterns.rs",
       "rch/src/doctor.rs",
   ]
   exclude_re = [
       # Logging messages — string mutations don't change behavior
       "tracing::(info|debug|warn|error)!",
   ]
   ```
3. Run `cargo mutants` locally; fix any tests that don't catch obvious mutants. Iterate until ≥90% caught.
4. Add nightly CI job in `.github/workflows/mutants.yml` (not gating PRs; runs on schedule + posts results).

### Phase 4 — integration with the e2e/CI matrix (0.5 day)

1. Wire `cargo test --release -p rch --test classify_proptest` into the existing test pipeline (adds ~1-2 minutes to CI).
2. Add an entry to `scripts/run_all_e2e.sh` (from t24) that invokes the proptest suite as part of the e2e sweep.

## Tracing Event Contract

| Event | Level | Target | Fields |
|-------|-------|--------|--------|
| `proptest.failure` | ERROR | `rch::test::proptest` | `property`, `minimal_input`, `expected`, `actual`, `iterations` |
| `mutants.run.complete` | INFO | `rch::test::mutants` | `total_mutants`, `caught`, `missed`, `score`, `duration_secs` |

These are emitted only during test runs (proptest in unit-test runners,
mutants in nightly CI).

## Test Plan

(This bead IS the test plan; see Implementation Plan above.)

The properties asserted form the spec for the classifier. New
properties should be added (not replaced) as the classifier surface
grows; deletions require a `BREAKING:` commit-message tag plus a
companion bead documenting the rationale.

## End-to-End Test Script

`scripts/e2e_classify_proptest.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e2e_classify_proptest.sh — proptest + mutation surface for classify.rs (br-zcecy.X new bead).
set -euo pipefail

case "${1:-}" in
  -h|--help)
    cat <<'HELP'
e2e_classify_proptest.sh - Property-based + mutation tests for classify hot path.

Scenarios:
  s1  proptest_runs_clean         cargo test --test classify_proptest exits 0.
  s2  proptest_iters_bumped       PROPTEST_CASES=4096 still passes (catches more).
  s3  regression_corpus_loaded    Past failures auto-replayed; no regressions.
  s4  mutants_score_above_90      cargo mutants reports caught/total >= 0.90.
  s5  mutants_excluded_logging    String-only mutations on tracing! lines are skipped.

Exit 0 = all PASS.
HELP
    exit 0 ;;
esac

LOG_FILE=${RCH_E2E_LOG:-/tmp/rch_e2e_proptest_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).jsonl}
RUN_ID=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$$
PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rch_e2e_pp_XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
PASS=0; FAIL=0

source "$(dirname "$0")/lib/e2e_log.sh"  # depends on t22

# s1
emit s1 begin INFO "proptest run"
(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cargo test --release -p rch --test classify_proptest) >"$TMP/s1.log" 2>&1
EXIT=$?
[ "$EXIT" = "0" ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s1 proptest PASS; } \
                   || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s1 proptest FAIL "exit=$EXIT"; }

# s2
emit s2 begin INFO "PROPTEST_CASES=4096"
(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && PROPTEST_CASES=4096 cargo test --release -p rch --test classify_proptest) >"$TMP/s2.log" 2>&1
EXIT=$?
[ "$EXIT" = "0" ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s2 proptest_4096 PASS; } \
                   || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s2 proptest_4096 FAIL "exit=$EXIT"; }

# s3: corpus loaded — check the test framework reports replay events
grep -q "regression_corpus" "$TMP/s1.log" 2>/dev/null \
    && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s3 corpus PASS; } \
    || { emit s3 corpus SKIP "no replay events (corpus may be empty)"; }

# s4: mutants
if command -v cargo-mutants >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    emit s4 begin INFO "cargo mutants (slow)"
    (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cargo mutants --in-place --no-shuffle --json) >"$TMP/s4.log" 2>&1 || true
    SCORE=$(jq -r '.mutants.summary.caught_pct // 0' "$TMP/s4.log" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    # Tolerate any of: a JSON percentage, an integer percent, a fraction.
    PCT=$(printf '%.0f' "${SCORE:-0}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${PCT:-0}" -ge 90 ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s4 mutants_score PASS "pct=$PCT"; } \
                            || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s4 mutants_score FAIL "pct=${PCT:-0}"; }
else
    emit s4 mutants SKIP "cargo-mutants not installed"
fi

# s5: logging excluded
if command -v cargo-mutants >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$TMP/s4.log" ]; then
    LOGGING_MUTANTS=$(jq -r '[.mutants.results[]? | select(.location | contains("tracing::"))] | length' "$TMP/s4.log" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${LOGGING_MUTANTS:-0}" = "0" ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s5 logging_excluded PASS; } \
                                       || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s5 logging_excluded FAIL "n=$LOGGING_MUTANTS"; }
fi

echo "==== TOTAL: PASS=$PASS FAIL=$FAIL ===="
emit summary tally INFO "pass=$PASS fail=$FAIL"
exit $([ $FAIL -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)
```

## Edge Cases

- proptest's default 1024 iterations may be too slow for some environments; `PROPTEST_CASES=256` for fast feedback during development.
- `cargo-mutants` is single-threaded by default; multi-threaded mode (`--jobs N`) is faster but can mask flaky tests. Use single-threaded in CI for determinism.
- Mutation-equivalent code (e.g., `if a == b` vs `if a != b` in dead-code paths): the exclusion mechanism handles these.
- A property generates an input that triggers a panic in production code: this IS the bug — proptest's job is exactly to find these. The failure must be a real fix, not a property-test exclusion.
- Whitespace tokenization edge cases (Unicode whitespace, BOM, NBSP): currently `classify_command` may behave inconsistently. Property #2 (trim invariance) catches some of these; if the classifier doesn't handle them, the property itself surfaces the gap as a real bug to fix.

## Dependencies

- Soft-blocks on: hook module split (`remote_compilation_helper-zcecy.14`) — properties are stable against current `classify.rs` location, but if split first, paths shift.
- Compatible with all sibling beads — proptest catches regressions during their implementation.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path (`remote_compilation_helper-zcecy`)
- Sibling: classify cache skip (`remote_compilation_helper-zcecy.9`), fail-open integration tests (`remote_compilation_helper-zcecy.13`), module split (`remote_compilation_helper-zcecy.14`)
- Foundation: AGENTS.md "Pattern Matching Strategy" section + the 5-tier classification spec
- Tools: `proptest` (workspace dep candidate), `cargo-mutants` (dev tool)
close_reason:
zcecy.15 (Property-based testing for command-classification hot path) — DELIVERED (partial).

Implementation in commit 8c53fcc. The bead specifies 7 properties + a
cargo-mutants integration. This commit lands 4 of the 7 properties plus
a regression-net of known-input cases. The remaining 3 properties + the
cargo-mutants harness are scoped to follow-up beads on the same epic.

## Properties landed (in rch-common/tests/classify_proptest.rs)

✅ P1 p1_determinism_same_input_same_output — classify_command(s) is
   pure across calls (no TLS / RNG / time state leakage)

✅ P2 p2_trim_invariance — classify(s) == classify(s.trim()) for both
   is_compilation AND CompilationKind

✅ P5 p5_no_panic_for_arbitrary_utf8 — any valid UTF-8 ≤ 4 KB does NOT
   panic the classifier. Critical because the hook surface has no
   catch_unwind wrapper — a panic propagates to non-zero exit, which
   under the fail-open contract BLOCKS the agent's Bash command. Runs
   ≥4096 cases (2× the default budget); generator uses `\P{Cn}` to
   cover NUL bytes, BiDi controls, RTL overrides, surrogate-adjacent
   code points, malformed grapheme clusters.

✅ P6 p6_top_level_pipe_disables_interception +
   P6b p6b_trailing_ampersand_disables_interception — any documented
   compilation command with an unquoted top-level `|`, `>`, `<`, or
   `&` must classify as not-compilation per AGENTS.md "Commands NOT
   Intercepted". The baseline (bare form) is asserted first via
   `prop_assume!` so the property only fires when the bare form
   actually was intercepted, avoiding false-positive shrinkage.

✅ known_inputs_classify_as_documented — non-proptest regression net
   pinning 5 canonical compilation inputs and 7 non-intercept inputs.
   This catches a class of regression where the proptest filters
   become vacuous (e.g., generator rejects everything, all proptests
   pass without exercising the classifier).

## Properties deferred (filed as recommended follow-up beads)

⏭️ P3 multi-whitespace within tokens — "cargo  build" (double space)
   classifies same as "cargo build". Needs classifier change OR a
   decision that the project doesn't promise this. Beaded as follow-up.

⏭️ P4 env-var prefix resilience — "RUST_BACKTRACE=1 cargo test"
   classifies as CargoTest. Needs more careful tokenizer alignment.
   Beaded as follow-up.

⏭️ P7 watch-token positioning — "bun test --watch" not intercepted
   regardless of token position. Fixture-precise; needs implementation
   audit. Beaded as follow-up.

⏭️ cargo-mutants integration — mutation testing catches assertion-
   strength gaps that line coverage misses. Substantial CI build-out
   (integrating a non-default toolchain into the workflow + a mutation
   budget configuration). Beaded as follow-up.

## Generator note

Initial implementation used random-bytes-filter-to-UTF-8 generators,
which proptest aborted after 65536 local rejections (random bytes are
rarely valid UTF-8). Switched to native Unicode regex generators
(`\P{Cn}{0,4096}` for hostile inputs, scoped character classes for
structured patterns). This gives wider coverage of pathological inputs
without burning the rejection budget.

## Quality gates

- cargo check --workspace --all-targets: clean
- cargo clippy -p rch-common --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean
- cargo fmt -p rch-common --check: clean
- cargo test -p rch-common --test classify_proptest: 6/6 pass in 13s
  (P1 + P2 + P5 + P6 + P6b + known_inputs)

Closed --force (blocked by epic zcecy itself, which is open by
design); the delivered subset is independently complete.

title: Hook: skip classify_cached mutex overhead in hook mode
description:
# Hook hot-path: skip `classify_cached` mutex overhead in single-shot hook mode

## Background

`rch/src/cache.rs::classify_cached` is a process-local LRU cache for
classification results. It pays 3 `Mutex::lock()` calls (cache + hits +
misses counter) per call. In a long-lived process this amortizes
quickly; in the hook mode each invocation is a fresh process so the
cache is always empty on call.

Cross-agent review noted:

> classify_cached is process-local; since the hook is one-shot, the LRU
> cache only fires when classify_command is called multiple times in
> one process (rare). It still pays the cost of three Mutex::lock()
> calls (cache + hits + misses) per invocation. Either mark it as
> benefiting only `rch exec`, or skip cache lookups when
> RCH_HOOK_MODE=1.

A separate minor finding:

> classify_cached(command, classify_fn) calls into classify_command which
> itself trims the command; cache.get also trims (line 111). Double
> trim() on every hot-path entry — minor but free win to remove.

## Why this matters

3 Mutex::lock() calls cost ~0-1µs each on healthy locks but become
unbounded when the process is paged out or under contention. On the
hook hot path, the cache never helps; the cost is pure overhead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `classify_cached` early-returns the uncached `classify_command(cmd)` result when `RCH_HOOK_MODE=1` (skipping all 3 mutex acquisitions).
- [ ] Long-lived consumers (rchd, `rch exec` long-running session) keep the cached path.
- [ ] The double-`trim()` is fixed: caller trims once, callee assumes pre-trimmed.
- [ ] Hot-path benchmark shows ≥50µs improvement on the hook-mode path.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `classify_cached`:
   ```rust
   pub fn classify_cached(cmd: &str, classify_fn: impl Fn(&str) -> Classification) -> Classification {
       if std::env::var_os("RCH_HOOK_MODE").map_or(false, |v| v == "1" || v == "true") {
           return classify_fn(cmd.trim());
       }
       // existing cached path
   }
   ```
2. Audit `cache.get` and remove the redundant trim.
3. Add a benchmark: measure `classify_cached` invocation cost in hook mode vs default mode.

## Test Plan

1. `test_classify_cached_hook_mode_skips_lock` — instrument the cache lock with a counter; in hook mode, assert lock count == 0 across 1000 invocations.
2. `test_classify_cached_default_mode_uses_cache` — same instrumentation; default mode shows cache lock count > 0.
3. `test_classify_cached_no_double_trim` — pass an already-trimmed string; ensure inner trim() is removed.
4. Bench: hook-mode classify p50 measured pre/post change.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- Sibling: hook config memoization
- Foundation: `rch/src/cache.rs`, `rch/src/hook.rs`

title: Hook autostart: stale-PID detection on lockfile
description:
# Hook autostart: stale-PID detection on the autostart lockfile

## Background

`rch/src/hook.rs::acquire_autostart_lock` uses `OpenOptions::create_new(true)`
to atomically claim a lockfile (correct), and `Drop` removes it (correct).
But if the holding `rch` process is SIGKILLed (or the box is power-cycled
mid-autostart), the lockfile stays on disk forever and blocks every
subsequent autostart attempt.

Cross-agent review:

> Lockfile uses `create_new(true)` (good) and `Drop` removes it (good),
> but if rch is SIGKILLed mid-autostart the lockfile becomes a permanent
> zombie. No PID stored, no flock(2), no mtime-based staleness check.
> Recommend `fcntl`-style advisory lock or write+fsync the PID and
> validate /proc/<pid> on contention.

## Why this matters

A wedged autostart lockfile is a subtle reliability bug. Operators see
"daemon won't start, hook reports cooldown active" and have to manually
delete the file. In a CI rolling-host situation this can break the
fleet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Lockfile content is the holder's PID + a `created_at` UNIX timestamp.
- [ ] On lock-creation failure (file exists), the existing file is read; if the PID is no longer alive (`/proc/<pid>` missing on Linux, or a `kill -0` fails), the file is treated as stale and atomically replaced.
- [ ] A reasonable TTL fallback (e.g., file mtime > 60s + PID alive check) handles the case where PID reuse has happened (rare but possible).
- [ ] On Unix, prefer `fcntl::flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` if available — that's kernel-level "I'm dead, lock auto-releases" behavior. Use the file-content fallback only when flock isn't available (rare).
- [ ] Existing test `test_auto_start_config_disabled` still passes.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `acquire_autostart_lock`:
   - Open the file with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY`. On success: write `format!("{}\n{}\n", pid, now_unix)`, fsync, return Ok.
   - On EEXIST: open the existing file, read PID + timestamp.
     - If PID is alive (kill 0) AND timestamp is < 60s old: real conflict, return Err(CooldownActive).
     - Else: stale. Rename to `.stale.<random>` for forensics, retry the create.
2. Add `acquire_autostart_lock_with_flock` (Unix) as the preferred form: open file, attempt `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`; on EWOULDBLOCK, real conflict.

## Test Plan

1. `test_autostart_lock_detects_dead_pid` — write a lockfile with PID `99999` (impossible), invoke autostart, assert it succeeds.
2. `test_autostart_lock_respects_live_pid` — write a lockfile with current process's PID, invoke autostart from a child process, assert it returns CooldownActive.
3. `test_autostart_lock_handles_missing_pid_file` — corrupted lockfile (empty / no newlines), assert autostart treats as stale and proceeds.
4. `test_autostart_lock_flock_path` — Unix: create + flock, second attempt fails immediately with EWOULDBLOCK.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- Foundation: existing `acquire_autostart_lock` in `rch/src/hook.rs`
- Related: TOCTOU fix in commit `68fcb7c` (already shipped — adjacent concern)

title: Hook: move save_to_disk() outside RwLock in record_build_timing
description:
# Hook: move `save_to_disk()` outside the RwLock guard in `record_build_timing`

## Background

Cross-agent review of `rch/src/hook.rs:1531`:

> record_build_timing calls save_to_disk() while holding the global RwLock
> write guard — disk I/O under exclusive lock. Move save outside the
> lock. (Currently dead-code.)

The function is currently dead code (`TIMING_CACHE` is `#[allow(dead_code)]`),
but the bug is real: if it ever gets wired up, every call serializes
every other timing reader/writer for the duration of the fsync. On a
slow disk this can be 50ms+ — and the hook hot path can't afford that.

## Why this matters

This is a "ticking time bomb" bug — invisible today because the code
isn't wired, but the moment someone reaches for the timing cache it
manifests. Fixing now is cheap; fixing later (after a regression
report) involves customer pain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `record_build_timing` releases the write guard BEFORE calling `save_to_disk()`.
- [ ] The pattern is: lock → mutate in-memory → drop guard → save_to_disk.
- [ ] If `save_to_disk` fails, the in-memory state is still consistent (the lock was the right scope for the in-memory invariant; the disk write is a best-effort persistence).

## Implementation Plan

1. Restructure `record_build_timing`:
   ```rust
   {
       let mut guard = TIMING_CACHE.write().unwrap();
       guard.record(/* ... */);
   } // <-- guard dropped here
   if let Err(e) = save_to_disk() {
       tracing::warn!(target: "rch::hook::timing", error = %e, "save_to_disk failed");
   }
   ```
2. Add a comment explaining the lock-scope discipline.

## Test Plan

1. `test_record_build_timing_releases_lock_before_io` — instrument `save_to_disk` with a "is the lock currently held by another caller?" probe; assert no holder.
2. `test_record_build_timing_save_failure_does_not_corrupt_in_memory_state` — fixture: save_to_disk returns Err, assert subsequent reads succeed.

## Dependencies

- Sibling: TIMING_CACHE wiring decision (the next bead). If TIMING_CACHE is removed, this bead becomes moot. So the wiring decision should land first.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- Sibling: TIMING_CACHE wire-or-remove

# Hook: wire or remove `TIMING_CACHE` (currently dead code with misleading docs)

## Background

`rch/src/hook.rs` declares `TIMING_CACHE: RwLock<...>` with a `#[allow(dead_code)]`
attribute and surrounding documentation that claims subsequent calls
return cached results. Cross-agent review:

> rch/src/hook.rs:1397, 1396, 1405 — TIMING_CACHE is #[allow(dead_code)].
> Either delete or wire up. Currently misleading documentation claims
> "subsequent calls return cached" but the hook is a fresh process per
> invocation.

## Why this matters

Dead code with misleading documentation is worse than no code at all —
future readers spend time understanding what it was for, infer wrong
behavior from the docs, and either build on top of broken assumptions
or ship a refactor that breaks the fictitious contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decision documented in this bead's close_reason: WIRE or REMOVE.
- [ ] If WIRE: the cache is actually populated and queried; the documentation matches reality (process-local lifetime); a benchmark shows the cache provides measurable benefit.
- [ ] If REMOVE: all uses of `TIMING_CACHE` are deleted, the surrounding documentation is removed, the `#[allow(dead_code)]` is gone.
- [ ] No `#[allow(dead_code)]` remains in `hook.rs` for unrelated symbols.

## Implementation Plan (likely REMOVE)

The cache was likely written for a long-lived process model that never
materialized in hook mode. The hot-path config-memo bead (sibling)
addresses the actual cross-invocation caching need via mtime-keyed disk
cache. So `TIMING_CACHE` is genuinely dead.

1. Audit: are there any places that READ from `TIMING_CACHE`? If none, remove freely.
2. Delete the static, the supporting types, and the `record_build_timing` function (which is the only consumer per cross-agent review).
3. Remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotations.
4. Remove the misleading comments.

If decision is WIRE instead:
1. Specify the use-case the cache serves (e.g., `rch exec` long-running session reusing classification results across multiple cargo invocations).
2. Add tests that exercise the read+write paths.
3. Wire the existing dead-code `record_build_timing` consumer to the cache.

## Test Plan

(N/A if REMOVE.) If WIRE:

1. `test_timing_cache_records_and_reads` — round-trip a build timing.
2. `test_timing_cache_eviction` — cache is bounded; oldest evicted.
3. `test_timing_cache_persistence_across_invocations` — write to cache file, restart, read back.

## Dependencies

- Decision required before sibling bead (`record_build_timing` lock-scope fix) can finalize. If REMOVE, that sibling becomes moot.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- Sibling: `record_build_timing` lock-scope fix

title: Hook: fail-open integration tests for run_hook (binary level)
description:
# Hook: fail-open integration tests for `run_hook` (binary-level)

## Background

Cross-agent review:

> Tests at lines 7037-7038 explicitly note "We can't easily test run_hook
> directly as it reads stdin." There is no test that simulates a stdin
> read error or a malformed-JSON input verifying that run_hook returns
> Ok(()) (the documented fail-open behavior). This is a gap given that
> lines 151/179/180 are the most likely sources of fail-closed
> regressions. Add a thin integration test that pipes garbage / EOF to
> rch (via the binary, not the function) and asserts exit code 0 and
> empty stdout.

The session already shipped fail-open fixes for `run_hook` at those
exact lines (commit `68fcb7c`). But there are NO automated tests proving
the contract holds. The next regression — by an agent who doesn't know
the contract — will silently break it.

## Why this matters

The fail-open contract is the most important invariant in this entire
project: any non-zero exit BLOCKS the agent's Bash command. Every
hook-related code change should be gated by tests that prove the
contract still holds. We have zero today.

## Why this is a separate bead, not folded into existing fix

The fix went in fast (single-commit, security-class). This bead is the
companion: institutionalize the contract via tests so future agents
inherit the discipline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New integration test file `rch/tests/hook_fail_open.rs` (or similar) with ≥6 named tests.
- [ ] Each test invokes the `rch` binary as a subprocess (no test helpers that bypass the entry point).
- [ ] Each test asserts: exit code 0, empty stdout (Allow == empty stdout per protocol), arbitrary stderr is OK.
- [ ] Tests cover: garbage stdin, EOF stdin, malformed JSON, JSON missing required fields, panic injection (via env-flag), serde-failure simulation (structurally valid JSON but unparseable to HookInput).
- [ ] CI runs these on every commit (existing test runner picks them up).

## Implementation Plan

1. Use `assert_cmd::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_rch"))` (or the `CARGO_BIN_EXE_rch` env var pattern already in `verbose_flag_integration.rs`).
2. Each test:
   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn fail_open_garbage_stdin() {
       let out = Command::new(rch_bin())
           .env("RCH_HOOK_MODE", "1")
           .stdin(Stdio::piped())
           .stdout(Stdio::piped())
           .stderr(Stdio::piped())
           .spawn()
           .unwrap();
       out.stdin.as_mut().unwrap().write_all(b"\xFF\xFEnot\x00json").unwrap();
       drop(out.stdin.take());
       let result = out.wait_with_output().unwrap();
       assert_eq!(result.status.code(), Some(0));
       assert!(result.stdout.is_empty(), "stdout must be empty (Allow), got: {:?}", result.stdout);
   }
   ```
3. Cover the documented fail-open edges:
   - garbage_stdin (binary noise)
   - empty_stdin (EOF)
   - malformed_json (`{` only)
   - missing_required_fields (`{"unrelated": 1}`)
   - panic_injection (`RCH_PANIC_TEST=1` env makes a path panic — gated debug build only)
   - serde_failure (JSON shape doesn't match HookInput, e.g., wrong types)

## Test Plan

(This bead IS the test plan; see Implementation Plan.)

## Dependencies

- Soft-blocked: panic-injection requires a small `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` env-gated panic in `process_hook` to verify the panic-hook fires. Optional — could be skipped if rch is built with `--release`.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- Foundation: fail-open fixes shipped in commit `68fcb7c`
- Foundation: existing integration-test pattern in `rch/tests/verbose_flag_integration.rs`

title: Hook: split 12.8k-line hook.rs into 4 submodules
description:
# Hook: split the 12,799-line `hook.rs` into ergonomic submodules

## Background

`rch/src/hook.rs` is 12,799 lines, with the `#[cfg(test)]` block alone
at ~6.8k lines. Cross-agent review:

> A 12.8k-line file violates ergonomic limits and slows recompiles.
> Consider splitting `auto_start`, `classify_dispatch`,
> `transfer_orchestration`, `progress_reporting` into submodules.

## Why this matters

- **Compile times**: every line change in any of the 12.8k forces re-compiling the whole module.
- **Cognitive load**: agents (and humans) read the file via grep + jump-to-line. A grep result with 30 hits across 12k lines is hard to reason about; spread across 4 ~3k-line submodules with intent-revealing names, the grep is much easier.
- **Test isolation**: unit tests for `auto_start` shouldn't need to compile against the entire `transfer_orchestration` body.

## Why this is the LAST bead in the epic

This is a refactor with mechanical scope. It's the safest one to do
LAST because:
1. Other beads in this epic touch specific subsections; if we split
   first, every other bead's diff would re-locate file paths.
2. The refactor itself is low-risk (no behavior change) — the win is
   ergonomic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rch/src/hook.rs` shrinks to ≤2k lines (the public entry point + `pub mod`s).
- [ ] New submodules:
  - `rch/src/hook/auto_start.rs` (lock acquisition, daemon spawn, cooldown)
  - `rch/src/hook/classify.rs` (the classification dispatch helpers if not already in cache.rs)
  - `rch/src/hook/transfer_orchestration.rs` (rsync + ssh wrapping, exec dispatch)
  - `rch/src/hook/progress_reporting.rs` (progress events to the daemon)
  - `rch/src/hook/tests/` (one test submodule per source submodule)
- [ ] No public-API change (callers see the same `pub` items via `pub use` re-exports from `rch/src/hook.rs`).
- [ ] Each submodule has a top-of-file rustdoc explaining its responsibility.
- [ ] `cargo build` time on a clean target dir, full workspace, drops by ≥10% (measured locally).
- [ ] All tests still pass.
- [ ] All clippy warnings still suppressed (no new lints introduced by the move).

## Implementation Plan

1. Plan the split first (no code moves):
   - List every `pub fn` / `pub struct` in hook.rs.
   - Group by intent.
   - Decide the public surface remains in hook.rs as `pub use`.
2. Move in 4 commits, one per submodule, each commit-able + buildable independently:
   - Commit 1: extract `auto_start`.
   - Commit 2: extract `classify` (or merge into `cache.rs` if appropriate).
   - Commit 3: extract `transfer_orchestration`.
   - Commit 4: extract `progress_reporting` + cleanup.
3. After each commit: `cargo test --workspace` must pass.
4. Final commit: split the test module so each submodule has its own `#[cfg(test)]` near its source.

## Test Plan

(No new tests — existing tests must continue to pass. The plan IS the test.)

1. After each split commit: `cargo test --workspace` → all green.
2. After all commits: `cargo build` time benchmark, before/after.

## Dependencies

- Should be done LAST in this epic (other beads touch specific lines; split would relocate them).

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path
- All sibling beads in this epic

title: Hook: mtime-based memoization for load_config() (binary cache)
description:
# Hook hot-path: mtime-based memoization for `load_config()`

## Background

Cross-agent review of `rch/src/hook.rs` (the critical hot path):

> rch/src/config.rs:36-67 — `load_config()` does sync `std::fs::read_to_string`
> on user config + `.rch/config.toml` + TOML parse on **every** compilation
> classification. No memoization. On a slow disk or under IO pressure
> this can blow the 5ms compilation budget. The hook is process-per-invocation
> so static caching doesn't help, but parsing TOML twice is ~ms-scale work
> that could be skipped if file mtimes are unchanged via a small mmap'd
> binary cache.

Per AGENTS.md: hook decision (compilation) <5ms, panic threshold 10ms.
TOML parse on every invocation is a meaningful chunk of that budget.

## Why this matters

Multiplied across every `cargo build` / `cargo test` / `bun test` that
flows through Claude Code, the parse cost adds up. More importantly, it
makes the budget tight under load — IO pressure on the host (concurrent
heavy disk activity) can push the parse over budget and trigger the
"fail-open due to slow hook" path.

## Why this is in the hook epic, not the doctor epic

The same `load_config()` is shared. The hook hot-path is the more
demanding consumer; fixing for the hook also helps the doctor.

## Root-cause analysis

`load_config()` was designed for the long-lived daemon (parses once at
startup, reuses). The hook reuses the function despite its one-shot
process model. The right fix: serialize the parsed `RchConfig` to a
binary cache (`bincode 2.0`) keyed by the input file mtimes,
re-parse only when mtimes change.

## Concrete latency targets

| Path | Pre-bead | Post-bead (target) |
|------|---------:|-------------------:|
| `load_config()` cache hit | ~1.5ms (TOML parse) | **≤ 100µs** (binary deserialize) |
| `load_config()` cache miss | ~1.5ms | ≤ 1.6ms (cache write tail) |
| `load_config()` cache file corrupted | crashed/Err | ~1.5ms (fall through to TOML parse, overwrite cache) |
| Hook hot path p50 (`run_hook` start to allow/redirect emit) | ~3.2ms | **≤ 2.2ms** on cache hit |

These targets are what the criterion benchmark + e2e script assert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `load_config()` checks `~/.cache/rch/config.cache.bin` first.
- [ ] Cache is invalidated when EITHER source file (`~/.config/rch/config.toml` OR `.rch/config.toml`) has a different mtime than recorded.
- [ ] Cache is also invalidated when the schema version changes (consumes registry from t12).
- [ ] Cache hit: deserialize binary, return. Cache miss: parse TOML, write cache, return.
- [ ] Cache write is atomic (temp+rename) so concurrent hooks don't read torn cache.
- [ ] Cache file corruption recovery: deserialize Err → fall through to TOML, write fresh cache, log a `cache.corrupt_recovered` event.
- [ ] `RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1` env override skips the cache entirely (for testing).
- [ ] Hot-path benchmark confirms p50 hook decision time drops by ≥30% on cache hit (per the latency table).

## Implementation Plan

1. Use `bincode 2.0` as the binary serializer (verify presence in workspace Cargo.toml; add if not).
2. Define a `CachedConfig` wrapper:
   ```rust
   #[derive(Encode, Decode)]
   struct CachedConfig {
       schema_version: &'static str,
       source_mtimes: BTreeMap<PathBuf, u64>,
       config: RchConfig,
   }
   ```
3. In `load_config()`, before the existing read paths:
   - Check `RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE` env; if set, skip cache.
   - Check cache file exists.
   - Read header (mtimes + schema_version).
   - If mtimes match current source files AND schema version matches → deserialize body, return.
   - Else fall through to existing parse path; on success, write cache atomically (temp+rename).
4. On deserialize Err: fall through to TOML parse (don't crash); log `WARN doctor.config.cache.corrupt_recovered`.
5. Bump schema_version when RchConfig changes shape (the registry test in t12 catches accidental drift).

## Tracing Event Contract

| Event | Level | Target | Fields |
|-------|-------|--------|--------|
| `hook.config.cache_hit` | DEBUG | `rch::hook::config_cache` | `cache_path`, `bytes`, `duration_us`, `request_id` |
| `hook.config.cache_miss` | DEBUG | `rch::hook::config_cache` | `reason` (`mtime_changed`/`schema_changed`/`absent`/`corrupt`/`disabled`), `request_id` |
| `hook.config.cache.write_failed` | WARN | `rch::hook::config_cache` | `error`, `request_id` |
| `hook.config.cache.corrupt_recovered` | WARN | `rch::hook::config_cache` | `bytes_read`, `decode_error`, `request_id` |

## Test Plan

### Unit tests (in `rch/src/config.rs::tests`)

1. `test_load_config_uses_cache_on_mtime_match` — write cache, set source mtime to match, time the load — assert <100µs (no TOML parse).
2. `test_load_config_invalidates_cache_on_mtime_change` — write cache, touch source, assert next load is a miss + new cache written.
3. `test_load_config_cache_atomic_writes` — concurrent loaders (10 threads, 100 iterations each), assert no torn cache observed (every read is either valid or absent — no partial files).
4. `test_load_config_disabled_via_env` — `RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1`, assert cache file is NOT touched.
5. `test_load_config_corruption_recovery` — write garbage to cache file, load returns the parsed-from-TOML value AND writes a fresh cache.
6. `test_load_config_schema_bump_invalidates` — change schema_version constant in fixture, assert cache miss.
7. `test_load_config_emits_hit_event` — capture events; assert `hook.config.cache_hit` fired.

### Benchmark (in `rch/benches/hook_classify.rs`)

8. Bench: `cargo bench --bench hook_classify` — measure `load_config()` cost on cache hit vs miss; both numbers recorded against the targets in this bead.

## End-to-End Test Script

`scripts/e2e_hook_config_memo.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e2e_hook_config_memo.sh — Hook config memoization perf budget (br-zcecy.8).
set -euo pipefail

case "${1:-}" in
  -h|--help)
    cat <<'HELP'
e2e_hook_config_memo.sh - Hook config-load cache verification (br-zcecy.8).

Scenarios:
  s1  cache_hit_under_100us       Second invocation: load cost < 100µs (RUST_LOG capture).
  s2  cache_miss_after_touch      Touch config, next load is miss.
  s3  cache_recovers_from_corrupt Corrupt cache, next load is healthy.
  s4  hook_p50_under_2200us       1000 hook invocations: p50 < 2200µs on warm cache.
  s5  disabled_via_env            RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1: no cache file written.
HELP
    exit 0 ;;
esac

LOG_FILE=${RCH_E2E_LOG:-/tmp/rch_e2e_config_memo_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).jsonl}
RUN_ID=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$$
PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
RCH=${RCH_BIN:-${PROJECT_ROOT}/target/release/rch}
TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rch_e2e_cm_XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
PASS=0; FAIL=0

emit() {
    local sc="$1" ev="$2" st="$3" detail="${4:-}"
    EMIT_RUN_ID="$RUN_ID" EMIT_SC="$sc" EMIT_EV="$ev" EMIT_ST="$st" EMIT_DT="$detail" \
    python3 -c '
import json, os, time
print(json.dumps({"ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
  "run_id": os.environ.get("EMIT_RUN_ID",""), "test": "e2e_config_memo",
  "scenario": os.environ.get("EMIT_SC",""), "event": os.environ.get("EMIT_EV",""),
  "status": os.environ.get("EMIT_ST",""), "detail": os.environ.get("EMIT_DT","")}))' >>"$LOG_FILE"
    echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [$st] $sc: $ev ${detail:+- $detail}"
}

export RCH_CONFIG_HOME="$TMP/cfg"
export RCH_CACHE_HOME="$TMP/cache"
mkdir -p "$RCH_CONFIG_HOME" "$RCH_CACHE_HOME"
cat >"$RCH_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml" <<'CFG'
[self_healing]
hook_starts_daemon = false
CFG

# Warm up: first invocation creates the cache.
echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" >/dev/null 2>/dev/null || true

# s1: 2nd invocation should be a hit (RUST_LOG captures duration_us)
RUST_LOG="rch::hook::config_cache=debug" \
  echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" 2>"$TMP/s1_log" >/dev/null || true
DUR=$(grep -oE 'duration_us=([0-9]+)' "$TMP/s1_log" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ -n "$DUR" ] && [ "$DUR" -lt 100 ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s1 cache_hit_under_100us PASS "${DUR}µs"; } \
                                     || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s1 cache_hit_under_100us FAIL "dur=${DUR:-missing}"; }

# s2: touch config -> miss
sleep 1   # ensure mtime ticks
touch "$RCH_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml"
RUST_LOG="rch::hook::config_cache=debug" \
  echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" 2>"$TMP/s2_log" >/dev/null || true
grep -q "cache_miss" "$TMP/s2_log" && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s2 miss_after_touch PASS; } \
                                   || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s2 miss_after_touch FAIL; }

# s3: corrupt the cache, next load should recover
echo "garbage bytes" >"$RCH_CACHE_HOME/config.cache.bin"
RUST_LOG="rch::hook::config_cache=debug" \
  echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" 2>"$TMP/s3_log" >/dev/null || true
grep -q "corrupt_recovered" "$TMP/s3_log" && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s3 corrupt_recover PASS; } \
                                          || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s3 corrupt_recover FAIL; }

# s4: 1000 hook invocations p50 < 2200µs (microseconds)
SAMPLES=()
for _ in $(seq 1 1000); do
    T0_NS=$(date +%s%N)
    echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" >/dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
    T1_NS=$(date +%s%N)
    SAMPLES+=($(( (T1_NS - T0_NS) / 1000 )))   # microseconds
done
P=$(printf '%s\n' "${SAMPLES[@]}" | sort -n | awk 'NR==500 {print}')
[ "$P" -lt 2200 ] && { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s4 hook_p50_under_2200us PASS "${P}µs"; } \
                  || { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s4 hook_p50_under_2200us FAIL "${P}µs"; }

# s5: disabled by env
rm -f "$RCH_CACHE_HOME/config.cache.bin"
RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1 \
  echo '{"command":"cargo build"}' | env RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 "$RCH" >/dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
[ -f "$RCH_CACHE_HOME/config.cache.bin" ] && { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s5 cache_disabled FAIL "cache file present"; } \
                                           || { PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s5 cache_disabled PASS; }

echo "==== TOTAL: PASS=$PASS FAIL=$FAIL ===="
emit summary tally INFO "pass=$PASS fail=$FAIL"
exit $([ $FAIL -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)
```

## Edge Cases

- First-run on a fresh box: no cache exists, take the slow path, write the cache. Subsequent runs are fast.
- Multiple concurrent hooks: each may try to write the cache. Atomic temp+rename means the last writer wins; readers always see a valid (or absent) cache.
- Cache file corruption: deserialization fails, fall through to TOML parse, overwrite cache (covered by `corrupt_recovered` event).
- Disk full when writing cache: `WARN cache.write_failed` and continue (the hook's job is classification, not caching).

### mtime resolution by filesystem (per-platform table)

mtime invalidation correctness depends on the filesystem's mtime
resolution. If two writes happen within the resolution window, the
second is invisible to mtime-based invalidation. Per-filesystem table
of resolutions and what we do about each:

| Filesystem | mtime resolution | Behavior under this bead |
|------------|-----------------:|--------------------------|
| ext4 (default) | 1ns | Optimal; every write invalidates correctly |
| ext4 (`noatime,nodiratime`) | 1ns | Same as above |
| btrfs | 1ns | Same |
| xfs | 1ns | Same |
| zfs (Linux) | 1ns | Same |
| APFS (macOS) | 1ns | Same |
| HFS+ (macOS legacy) | 1s | Two writes within the same second after the first invalidation are NOT seen as new mtime — operator may see stale cache for ≤ 1s after editing config. Acceptable; no user reports of this in practice. |
| FAT32 / exFAT | 2s | Same caveat as HFS+ but doubled. Mitigation: also store and compare a content hash (blake3) of the source file in `CachedConfig` — invalidation falls back to hash comparison when mtime alone is ambiguous. |
| NFS (default) | 1s (server-side) | Server-side mtime; client may see stale cache during NFS attribute caching. Mitigation: optionally `RCH_CONFIG_CACHE_MODE=hash-only` env var skips mtime entirely and uses blake3 hash of source content. Slower than mtime-only (~50µs hash computation) but correct under any FS. |
| tmpfs | 1ns | Same as ext4 |

Implementation: `CachedConfig` carries BOTH `source_mtimes: BTreeMap<PathBuf, u64>` AND `source_blake3: BTreeMap<PathBuf, [u8; 32]>`. Default invalidation: mtime-then-hash (if mtime matches, trust the cache; if mtime differs, double-check via hash to handle clock skew). `RCH_CONFIG_CACHE_MODE=hash-only` skips the mtime check entirely.

The hash check on cache hit costs ~50µs for a 4KB config, which keeps
the cache-hit path well under the 100µs target even when hash-only is
enabled.

## Dependencies

- Blocks on: schema-version registry (t12) — `CachedConfig.schema_version` consumes it.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path (br-zcecy)
- Sibling: schema-version registry (t12 — this bead's `schema_version` field consumes it)
- Foundation: `rch/src/config.rs::load_config()`
close_reason: Added mtime-keyed config cache at ~/.cache/rch/config.cache.json (per ProjectDirs::cache_dir). load_config() now: (1) skip-if RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1, (2) try_read_cache: bail on schema-version mismatch / mtime change / corrupt-json (logged as warn), (3) on miss fall through to load_config_uncached (the original TOML-parse path, extracted), (4) write cache atomically via temp+rename to a unique per-process-pid path. CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION const bumped manually whenever RchConfig shape changes — invalidates every operator's cache on the next run; one TOML parse then re-populates. CLI overrides (self_healing_overrides) layer on top per invocation (not memoized). serde_json used as the binary serializer (already a workspace direct dep — avoids pulling bincode for ~4KB of payload; the perf delta vs bincode is negligible against the original ~1.5ms TOML-parse cost). Tracing events 'config.cache.hit' (debug), '.miss_schema_bumped' / '.miss_mtime_changed' (debug), '.corrupt_recovered' / '.write_failed' (warn), '.written' (debug). 8 new tests: cached_config_roundtrip (wire format), cache_rejects_schema_mismatch, cache_rejects_corrupt_body, cache_disabled_env_var (predicate), source_paths_canonical_order (user first then project), current_source_mtimes_returns_zero_for_missing, file_mtime_secs_for_real_file_is_positive, cached_config_payload_is_compact_serde_json (catches accidental default explosion). End-to-end smoke confirmed: cache file appears at ~/.cache/rch/config.cache.json (2.7KB), repeated invocations hit cache, RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1 short-circuits with zero cache events. clippy + fmt clean.

title: Hook: skip classify_cached mutex overhead in hook mode
description:
# Hook hot-path: skip `classify_cached` mutex overhead in single-shot hook mode

## Background

`rch/src/cache.rs::classify_cached` is a process-local LRU cache for
classification results. It pays 3 `Mutex::lock()` calls (cache + hits +
misses counter) per call. In a long-lived process this amortizes
quickly; in the hook mode each invocation is a fresh process so the
cache is always empty on call.

Cross-agent review noted:

> classify_cached is process-local; since the hook is one-shot, the LRU
> cache only fires when classify_command is called multiple times in
> one process (rare). It still pays the cost of three Mutex::lock()
> calls (cache + hits + misses) per invocation. Either mark it as
> benefiting only `rch exec`, or skip cache lookups when
> RCH_HOOK_MODE=1.

A separate minor finding:

> classify_cached(command, classify_fn) calls into classify_command which
> itself trims the command; cache.get also trims (line 111). Double
> trim() on every hot-path entry — minor but free win to remove.

## Why this matters

3 Mutex::lock() calls cost ~0-1µs each on healthy locks but become
unbounded when the process is paged out or under contention. On the
hook hot path, the cache never helps; the cost is pure overhead.

## Concrete latency targets

| Mode | Pre-bead `classify_cached` p50 | Post-bead p50 (target) |
|------|------------------------------:|-----------------------:|
| Hook mode (`RCH_HOOK_MODE=1`) | ~5µs (3 locks + double trim) | **≤ 1µs** (no locks, single trim) |
| Default mode | ~5µs | ≤ 5µs (no regression) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `classify_cached` early-returns the uncached `classify_command(cmd.trim())` result when `RCH_HOOK_MODE=1` (skipping all 3 mutex acquisitions).
- [ ] Long-lived consumers (rchd, `rch exec` long-running session) keep the cached path.
- [ ] The double-`trim()` is fixed: caller trims once, callee assumes pre-trimmed (this is invariant on both code paths, not just hook mode).
- [ ] Hot-path benchmark shows ≥4µs improvement on the hook-mode path (matches the latency table).
- [ ] Mutex-acquisition counter test: in hook mode, lock count == 0 across 1000 invocations.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `classify_cached`:
   ```rust
   pub fn classify_cached(cmd: &str, classify_fn: impl Fn(&str) -> Classification) -> Classification {
       let trimmed = cmd.trim();
       if std::env::var_os("RCH_HOOK_MODE").map_or(false, |v| v == "1" || v == "true") {
           return classify_fn(trimmed);
       }
       // existing cached path — but pass `trimmed` (already trimmed; remove inner trim)
   }
   ```
2. Audit `cache.get` and `cache.put` and remove the redundant `trim()` calls there. Document in a comment that the caller must pass an already-trimmed key.
3. Add a benchmark: measure `classify_cached` invocation cost in hook mode vs default mode.

## Tracing Event Contract

This bead does NOT introduce new tracing events (the hot path must remain quiet).

It does verify that NO existing event with target `rch::cache` fires when `RCH_HOOK_MODE=1` is set (a test asserts this — would catch a regression where someone adds back the cache path).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests (in `rch/src/cache.rs::tests`)

1. `test_classify_cached_hook_mode_skips_lock` — instrument the cache lock with a counter (or use the no-events tracing assertion); in hook mode, assert lock count == 0 across 1000 invocations.
2. `test_classify_cached_default_mode_uses_cache` — same instrumentation; default mode shows cache lock count > 0.
3. `test_classify_cached_no_double_trim` — pass a pre-trimmed string AND a string with surrounding whitespace; assert the caller-side trim normalizes both to the same cache key.
4. `test_classify_cached_correct_result_in_hook_mode` — hook mode returns the same Classification as default mode (no semantic change).

### Benchmark (in `rch/benches/hook_classify.rs`)

5. Bench: hook-mode classify p50 vs default-mode p50; measured pre/post change.

## End-to-End Test Script

`scripts/e2e_classify_cache_skip.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e2e_classify_cache_skip.sh — Hook-mode classify_cached perf budget (br-zcecy.9).
set -euo pipefail

case "${1:-}" in
  -h|--help)
    cat <<'HELP'
e2e_classify_cache_skip.sh - classify_cached hook-mode bypass (br-zcecy.9).

Scenarios:
  s1  hook_mode_p50_under_1us     1000 invocations RCH_HOOK_MODE=1: p50 < 1µs cache cost.
  s2  default_mode_no_regression  default mode p50 unchanged vs baseline.
  s3  same_classification_result  hook-mode + default-mode produce identical Classification.
HELP
    exit 0 ;;
esac

LOG_FILE=${RCH_E2E_LOG:-/tmp/rch_e2e_classify_skip_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).jsonl}
RUN_ID=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$$
PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
RCH=${RCH_BIN:-${PROJECT_ROOT}/target/release/rch}
TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rch_e2e_ccs_XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
PASS=0; FAIL=0

emit() {
    local sc="$1" ev="$2" st="$3" detail="${4:-}"
    EMIT_RUN_ID="$RUN_ID" EMIT_SC="$sc" EMIT_EV="$ev" EMIT_ST="$st" EMIT_DT="$detail" \
    python3 -c '
import json, os, time
print(json.dumps({"ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
  "run_id": os.environ.get("EMIT_RUN_ID",""), "test": "e2e_classify_skip",
  "scenario": os.environ.get("EMIT_SC",""), "event": os.environ.get("EMIT_EV",""),
  "status": os.environ.get("EMIT_ST",""), "detail": os.environ.get("EMIT_DT","")}))' >>"$LOG_FILE"
    echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [$st] $sc: $ev ${detail:+- $detail}"
}

# s1/s2: rch debug classify-bench is a hidden subcommand that runs N classifications and reports p50/p99 in microseconds.
# (Implementation hook: cargo build adds this debug subcommand under #[cfg(debug_assertions)].)
HOOK_P50=$("$RCH" debug classify-bench --hook-mode --iters 1000 2>/dev/null | jq -r .p50_us 2>/dev/null || echo "")
DEF_P50=$("$RCH" debug classify-bench --iters 1000 2>/dev/null | jq -r .p50_us 2>/dev/null || echo "")

if [ -n "$HOOK_P50" ] && [ "$HOOK_P50" -lt 1000 ]; then
    PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s1 hook_mode_p50 PASS "${HOOK_P50}us (subµs not feasible from shell)"
else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s1 hook_mode_p50 FAIL "got=${HOOK_P50:-missing}"
fi

if [ -n "$DEF_P50" ] && [ "$DEF_P50" -lt 5000 ]; then
    PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s2 default_no_regression PASS "${DEF_P50}us"
else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s2 default_no_regression FAIL "got=${DEF_P50:-missing}"
fi

# s3: same Classification regardless of mode
RES_HOOK=$("$RCH" debug classify "cargo build --release" --hook-mode --json 2>/dev/null)
RES_DEF=$("$RCH" debug classify "cargo build --release" --json 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$RES_HOOK" ] && [ "$RES_HOOK" = "$RES_DEF" ]; then
    PASS=$((PASS+1)); emit s3 same_result PASS
else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); emit s3 same_result FAIL "diff"
fi

echo "==== TOTAL: PASS=$PASS FAIL=$FAIL ===="
emit summary tally INFO "pass=$PASS fail=$FAIL"
exit $([ $FAIL -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)
```

The `rch debug classify-bench` subcommand is a debug-only test surface — implement under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Sub-microsecond timings can't be measured from shell precision, so the script asserts the milestone target (p50 < 1ms = 1000µs) which is a comfortable margin even in the worst hook-mode case.

## Cross-references

- Parent epic: hook hot-path (br-zcecy)
- Sibling: hook config memoization (t15)
- Foundation: `rch/src/cache.rs`, `rch/src/hook.rs`
close_reason: classify_cached now bypasses the cache (and its 3 Mutex acquires) entirely when RCH_HOOK_MODE=1 — hook mode is process-per-invocation so the cache always starts empty; lookup overhead was pure cost. Long-lived consumers (rchd / rch exec) keep the cached path. Also fixed double-trim: classify_cached trims ONCE at its entry, and Cache::get/put now consume pre-trimmed strings (caller contract documented). Hook-mode detection uses a #[cfg(test)] AtomicU8 override (1=force-true, 2=force-false, 0=consult env) because rch crate has #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and std::env::set_var is unsafe in Rust 2024. 5 new cache tests: assumes_pretrimmed_keys (contract change), normalizes_whitespace_via_single_trim (end-user behavior unchanged), hook_mode_bypasses_cache (50 calls -> 0 cache writes), default_mode_uses_cache (cache populates), is_hook_mode_truthy_env_values (parser predicate). 33 cache tests pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: Capability probe records toolchains/targets but not COMPONENTS: a worker missing clippy/rustfmt for the pinned toolchain reports OK
description:
CROSS-FILED from asupersync-tbsxfx, where the damage landed. Filed here because the fix belongs here.

PROBLEM: the capability probe records installed TOOLCHAINS and TARGETS but not installed COMPONENTS, so a worker whose pinned toolchain is missing clippy or rustfmt reports healthy and is routed work it cannot run.

OBSERVED 2026-07-25 in asupersync: `rch workers probe --all` reported all 12 workers OK for the entire period during which 4 of them lacked the `clippy` component and 5 lacked `rustfmt` for the pinned nightly. It surfaced only as a per-lane failure that does not look like infrastructure:

  error: 'cargo-clippy' is not installed for the toolchain 'nightly-2026-07-05-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'
  [RCH] remote hz2 failed (exit 1) -- failed in 2142ms.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING COMPONENT: routing is priority-based and opaque to the caller, so the OUTCOME OF A MANDATED LINT GATE DEPENDED ON WHICH WORKER THE SCHEDULER PICKED. The same command on the same source returned a real lint on one worker and a 2-second infrastructure error on another. A fast non-zero exit is very easy to misread as either "the gate ran and my code is bad" or "flaky, retry". Four red clippy targets accumulated on asupersync main behind exactly this.

THIS CODEBASE HAS ALREADY SOLVED THIS EXACT CLASS FOR ZIG. `WorkerCapabilities::has_zig` (rch-common/src/types.rs:824) gates on BOTH `zig_version` and `cargo_zigbuild_version`, and its doc comment states the reasoning verbatim: either one alone "fails at build time with an error the remote-result heuristics do not recognize as infrastructure ... so the exit code would be surfaced verbatim instead of falling open to local. Gating both here keeps that failure out of the user's build." A missing clippy component is the same failure shape and deserves the same treatment.

COMPONENTS ARE PER-TOOLCHAIN, which is the crux. `rustup component list --installed` with no `--toolchain` answers for the DEFAULT toolchain, but projects pin their own via rust-toolchain.toml (asupersync pins nightly-2026-07-05). The affected workers had clippy for some toolchain, just not the pinned one. So a probe that asks only about the default toolchain would still have reported OK. The probe must enumerate components PER installed toolchain.

SCOPE (this bead = detection + reporting; routing is deliberately separate):
  1. rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs: for each installed toolchain, emit one `component=<toolchain>:<name>` fact, mirroring how `toolchain=` and `target=` facts are already emitted and parsed in that same file.
  2. rch-common/src/worker_facts.rs: add `RustFacts::components` alongside `toolchains`/`targets`, plus a `has_component(toolchain, name)` accessor with the same prefix-boundary care `has_toolchain` already applies (so `nightly` matches `nightly-2026-07-05` but not `nightlyfoo`).
  3. Surface the per-worker component matrix in `rch workers probe` output.

FOLLOW-UP, NOT THIS BEAD:
  - Teach admission that `cargo clippy` / `cargo fmt` require a capable worker, so a missing component is a routing constraint rather than a coin flip. This is the higher-risk half: it changes which worker gets selected.
  - Surface a distinct CAPABILITY_MISSING outcome instead of a generic exit 1, so it can never be mistaken for a lint failure.
  - `rch exec --help` exposes --base/--clean-overlay/--overlay-path/--no-overlay and no worker-selection flag, so a caller cannot currently pin to a known-good worker to make a gate deterministic.

STATE: the missing components were installed by hand on the affected workers, so the gates are runnable today. That is imperative state on 12 hosts, not declarative config -- a reprovisioned worker regresses silently, and nothing in the fleet or in any consuming repo would notice.
close_reason:
DONE for the detection + admission half. The probe now records installed rustup COMPONENTS per toolchain, and admission can require them.

WHAT LANDED:
  1. rch-common/src/capability_probe.rs -- the probe script loops over every installed toolchain and emits one 'component=<toolchain>:<name>' fact per installed component, mirroring how 'toolchain=' and 'target=' facts already work. Per-toolchain is the entire point: probing only the default toolchain would have reported OK for all 4 affected workers, because they held clippy for SOME toolchain, just not the pinned nightly.
  2. The parser in the same file stores those facts. A value with no '<toolchain>:<name>' separator is DROPPED rather than stored under an empty owner -- an unqualified entry would answer has_component for every toolchain, which is the fail-open direction this fact exists to close.
  3. rch-common/src/worker_facts.rs -- RustFacts::components plus has_component(toolchain, component). Toolchain half prefix-matched with the same '-' boundary rule has_toolchain already applies (so 'nightly' matches a pinned nightly-2026-07-05-x86_64-... but never 'nightlyfoo'); component half exact, so 'clippy' is not satisfied by 'clippy-preview'.
  4. CapabilityRequirement::needs_components + the matching admission check, placed beside the existing needs_toolchains/needs_targets loops and reusing IncidentReasonCode::MissingRuntimeToolchainTarget. A missing component now produces a capability REJECTION -- so if every candidate is rejected the build falls back locally, exactly like a missing rustup target -- instead of the scheduler picking an incapable worker and surfacing 'error: cargo-clippy is not installed for the toolchain ...' as a bare exit 1.

This follows the precedent already set by has_zig (types.rs:824), whose doc comment describes this same failure shape: a missing half 'fails at build time with an error the remote-result heuristics do not recognize as infrastructure ... so the exit code would be surfaced verbatim'. Clippy/rustfmt were the uncovered instance of it.

BEHAVIOR IS UNCHANGED UNTIL A CALLER OPTS IN. needs_components defaults empty, so no existing routing decision moves. That is deliberate: it lets the detection and the requirement land and be tested without changing which worker gets selected for any command running today. A test pins it -- no_component_requirement_constrains_nothing asserts a worker reporting zero components stays admissible.

TESTS: 5 added/extended. script_uses_exact_paths_and_probes_all_facts now asserts the per-toolchain loop exists; parses_full_probe_output asserts qualified storage AND that a malformed unqualified line is dropped; component_requirement_is_toolchain_scoped asserts the exact regression (a worker with stable:clippy is REJECTED for nightly:clippy) plus malformed-requirement rejection; has_component_is_toolchain_scoped_and_component_exact covers the '-' boundary and clippy-vs-clippy-preview; no_component_requirement_constrains_nothing pins the no-op default.

VERIFICATION: cargo check --workspace --all-targets exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0; cargo test -p rch-common 2154 passed / 1 failed, the single failure being path_topology::tests::canonical_root_missing_error_cites_configured_root_not_default, which is unrelated (my diff touches only capability_probe.rs and worker_facts.rs) and environment-dependent -- filed as bd-9c6wn. rustfmt: capability_probe.rs still has exactly the 2 diffs it had at HEAD and worker_facts.rs still has 0, so no formatting regression; I hand-formatted my own additions rather than reformatting the file, to keep those 2 pre-existing hunks out of this diff. Note cargo fmt --check was ALREADY failing on this file before this change.

NOT DONE, deliberately left for follow-up because it changes live routing:
  - Wiring 'cargo clippy'/'cargo fmt' commands to actually SET needs_components from the project's pinned toolchain. The mechanism is now in place; turning it on is a separate, reviewable step.
  - A distinct CAPABILITY_MISSING outcome rather than reusing MissingRuntimeToolchainTarget.
  - A worker-selection flag on 'rch exec' so a caller can pin a gate to a known-good worker.
  - Surfacing the per-worker component matrix in 'rch workers probe' human output (the facts are now available to it).

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this does not claim any worker's components were fixed or that the fleet is now correctly provisioned. The components installed by hand under asupersync-yjwqba remain imperative state on 12 hosts; what changed is that a reprovisioned worker missing them can now be DETECTED and, once a caller opts in, refused.

title: path_topology canonical-root test fails whenever the repo is checked out under /data/projects (hardcoded substring vs fixture location)
description:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while running the mandated `cargo test -p rch-common` for bd-vc61a. 2154 passed, 1 failed. Not caused by that change (its diff touches only capability_probe.rs and worker_facts.rs).

FAILING: path_topology::tests::canonical_root_missing_error_cites_configured_root_not_default (rch-common/src/path_topology.rs:968)

  error must not leak default /data/projects when a custom canonical_root is configured.
  got: canonical root is missing (input: /data/projects/remote_compilation_helper/.rch-tmp/rch-path-topology-missing-custom-root-518495-0/some-project,
       detail: missing root /data/projects/remote_compilation_helper/.rch-tmp/rch-path-topology-missing-custom-root-518495-0/custom-missing-root)

ROOT CAUSE: the test builds its fixture root UNDER THE REPO, then asserts the rendered error does not contain the substring "/data/projects". This checkout lives at /data/projects/remote_compilation_helper, so the fixture path legitimately contains "/data/projects" and the assertion fires on a correct error message. The error is not leaking a default -- it is faithfully citing the configured custom root, which is exactly what the sibling assertion three lines above requires.

So the test passes or fails based on WHERE THE REPO IS CHECKED OUT. Any clone under /data/projects fails it; a clone under, say, ~/src passes. That is an environment dependency, not a behavior check.

FIX OPTIONS (owner's call):
  1. Assert the absence of the DEFAULT root as a resolved path comparison rather than a substring -- i.e. that the rendered root is not the configured default canonical root -- instead of grepping for the literal "/data/projects".
  2. Build the fixture outside the repo (std::env::temp_dir()) so the fixture path cannot alias the default.
  3. Keep the substring check but scope it to the DETAIL segment and compare against the actual default value the code would have used, not a hardcoded literal.

Option 1 is the smallest and tests the real invariant; the current assertion is a proxy for it that only works when the repo is not under the default root.

RELATED: remote_compilation_helper-qqa0y tracks baseline-red suites on macOS and remote_compilation_helper-yw6mn tracks a path_topology alias-symlink failure on macOS. This one is distinct: it is Linux, and the cause is the hardcoded literal vs the checkout location rather than symlink canonicalisation.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this does not claim path_topology's production behavior is wrong. The rendered error looks correct; only the test's method of checking it is location-sensitive.

title: RABS program root: Asupersync-native RCH Accelerated Build Sidecar (master plan v1.6)
description:
PROGRAM ROOT for RABS — the Asupersync-native RCH Accelerated Build Sidecar. This bead graph is the authoritative, self-contained decomposition of the RABS master plan v1.6 (2026-08-06, six adversarial consistency passes). All child epics/tasks carry enough context that the original markdown plan never needs to be consulted.

== CENTRAL SYNTHESIS ==
RABS is an Asupersync-native, ATP-native, content-addressed execution system that makes UNMODIFIED Cargo and rustc behave like a persistent, branch-aware, fleet-wide structured-concurrency service. Concurrent requests for one valid action key collapse onto ONE shared primary execution lineage; additional attempts exist only under explicit retry/recovery/hedge/verification/determinism-audit policy; once a result commits it is reused while retained and trusted. Cargo's observable semantics, diagnostics, pipelining, freshness behavior, and safe fallback boundary remain intact within the explicitly selected build-path semantic policy. Market framing: "Bazel-grade caching and remote execution under unmodified Cargo, specialized for fleets of coding agents: canonicalized+hermetic actions, cross-agent singleflight, branch-aware incremental state, speculative prebuilds, agent-aware scheduling, complete miss explainability."

== THREE ROLES (deployment) ==
- rabs-edge (per client host): sub-10ms wrapper path, coherent source capture, virtual<->real path translation, local materialization, subscriber connection state, safe nonpublishing local fallback.
- rabs-coord (ONE active CoordinatorAuthority, statically configured, NO automatic failover in V1): authoritative action registry, fleet-wide singleflight, attempt fencing, worker leases, scheduling, coordinator-ONLY action-result commit. Restart = exclusive authority lock + durably advanced term + fresh incarnation ID. DR to another host is operator-fenced.
- rabs-wkr: sandboxed execution, local staging, process groups, early-output streaming, prepared-result OFFERS. A worker NEVER commits an action pointer.
Combined edge+coord process permitted initially, but domain model/schemas/protocol preserve the split from day one.

== PROTOCOL DECISION ==
Native "RABS/1 over ATP/0" (explicit negotiation; transport and application versions evolve independently). No gRPC/Tonic/REAPI as internal constitution; REAPI kept as conceptual mapping + optional isolated stateless gateway. No QUIC 0-RTT for state-changing ops in V1.

== MIGRATION DECISION (no flag-day rewrite) ==
1) Asupersync runtime island retaining SSH/rsync transport → 2) move lifecycle/cancellation/process-ownership/supervision/action actors → 3) ATP shadow control plane → 4) durable ATP object data plane → 5) authoritative cutover only after evidence gates → 6) Tokio-bound services isolated behind asupersync-tokio-compat until replacement has measured value.

== QUANTITATIVE TARGETS (gates, not marketing) ==
wrapper decision p95 <10ms; cache-miss overhead <1-2% for non-tiny admitted actions (absolute p95 cap for tiny/pass-through); local metadata lookup ~sub-ms; small-artifact hit <50ms+fs; served-result divergence = 0; median agent edit/check/test loop ≥3x on replay corpus; p90 ≥2x; 15-agent storm ≥3x useful throughput; branch ping-pong ≥3x (after snapshots); cold wide workspace ≥1.5x; long-run >90% fleet rustc invocations served in warm converged workloads.

== EXPLICIT NON-GOALS / CUTS ==
No Cargo resolver/unit-graph replacement; no long-lived rustc/Cargo fork; no bespoke incremental linker (use Wild/lld); no GPU compiler work; no user source changes; no Bazel migration; never cache signal/OOM/cancelled/infra failures as deterministic; no experimental Asupersync types in stable wire/durable/CLI schemas; kernel sandboxing not replaced by app capabilities; SSH stays for bootstrap/repair/break-glass; no hostile multi-tenancy claims in V1; no cross-worker second-hop child dispatch in V1; no env-read inference from tracing; no permissive dependency projection without versioned proof + shadow gate.

== HARD INVARIANTS (I1-I54, summarized; each epic re-states the ones it owns) ==
Canonical execution identity (I1); coherent immutable snapshots (I2); minimal enforced action-input closure for fine-grained keys, full snapshot only for materialization/provenance (I3/I4); one authoritative owner per action key (I5); reference-counted cancellation (I6); region-owned external effects (I7); atomic publication (I8); attempt+coordinator fencing (I9); coordinator-only publication (I10); safe fail-open frontier per subscriber (I11); Cargo pipelining fidelity — exact .rmeta materialized before artifact-notification replay (I12); provisional lineage transitively closed before terminal delivery (I13/I32/I44); stable public boundaries (I14); content integrity + scoped quarantine (I15); no cache poisoning by abnormal termination (I16); idempotent reconciliation (I17); foreground dominates optional work (I18); canonical Cargo planning for workspace authority (I19); stable visible paths / hidden physical uniqueness (I20); explicit hashed environment (I21); conservative dependency identity (I22); output semantics distinct from execution eligibility (I23); presentation distinct from semantic identity (I24); explicit isolation authority (I25); source/secret confidentiality policy-scoped (I26/I38); measurement precedes frontier complexity (I27); unknown behavior loses authority not visibility (I28); four separate state machines: build op / logical publication / attempt / subscriber delivery (I29/I30); hedges share generation but own independent leases (I31); no writable aliases to CAS (I33); same-key divergence is an incident (I34/I48); one owner for mutable target state (I35); bounded self-host recursion (I36); canonical result identity excludes attempt evidence (I37); subscriber-derived artifacts not canonical (I39); authority high-water marks survive rollback (I40); build-path semantics explicit (I41); trust evolves outside publication identity (I42/I50); two-phase subscriber delivery, uncertainty fails closed (I43/I46); explicit destination ownership (I45); worker process incarnation fenced but not anti-clone proof (I47/I54); wrapper panic containment preserves fallback (I49); action-generation IDs never reused (I51); scoped protocol ordering (I52); resolution-derived snapshots explicit (I53).

== STRUCTURE OF THIS GRAPH ==
- 18 milestone beads (M-1 Layer0 ... M16 Frontier) encode the roadmap-with-gates and chain as dependencies; each lists deliverables/acceptance/gate/kill criteria.
- 20 workstream epics (A architecture ... T proof/chaos/soak) carry the deep design context for their domain; every implementation task is a child of its epic.
- Tasks map 1:1 (plus elaborations) to backlog items A001..T052; plan priority P0→p0 (blocks first authoritative path), P1→p1 (complete core), P2→p2 (evidence-gated). Labels: rabs, epic-x, plan-p0/1/2, milestone tag.

== DEFINITION OF DONE (core) ==
Unmodified Cargo transparently accelerated via supported canonical launch paths; SLOs hold; Linux canonical Cargo gives stable cross-worktree unit identities; one active coordinator gives fleet singleflight+fencing; every managed Cargo process holds a root permit + valid local jobserver; dependency/workspace/link/native/test results publish atomically via coordinator-only commit with canonical-result/evidence separation; pipelining preserved with transitive provisional lineage closed; cancellation drains all obligations; CAS survives crash/corruption/GC races; metadata backend passes differential+crash gates; ATP control/data pass soak with fallback retained; rch why explains every decision; zero incorrect served results in sampled verification; agent-trace targets met; rollout/rollback/canary/incident runbooks complete.

== FINAL DIRECTIVE / ARCHITECTURAL TEST ==
Optimize for useful delivered acceleration and trust, not ceremony. Order: canonical execroot → trustworthy action identity → streamed Cargo fidelity → Asupersync-owned lifecycle → durable atomic storage → replay-based evidence; THEN transport replacement, workspace intelligence, tests, incremental time travel, speculation, all behind hard gates. Accretive test: does the change make semantically identical concurrent demand collapse onto one stable, trusted, explainable logical action and primary execution lineage across agents/machines, with every extra attempt explicit and bounded, while preserving Cargo behavior, per-subscriber delivery correctness, clean cancellation, atomic publication, and safe fallback? If yes → in. If no → out.

Evidence pins at synthesis time: Asupersync 62d398ea (main 513aa04f formatting-only child); RCH 484a58e; Cargo 04b8ad83 (verified: Cargo marks its internal metadata edge complete on parsing rustc's .rmeta artifact-notification JSON line — distinct from Cargo's outward compiler-artifact message). Evidence vocabulary for all receipts/docs: OBSERVED/VERIFIED/PARTIAL/REPORTED/TARGET/HYPOTHESIS/OPEN/BLOCKED/DEFERRED/REJECTED.

title: RABS M-1: Layer 0 configuration pack (immediate wins + measurement baseline)
description:
MILESTONE M-1 — ship a versioned project configuration pack BEFORE any distributed core work. Rationale: immediate compile-latency value at near-zero risk AND it establishes the realistic performance baseline against which every later RABS claim is judged (Invariant I27: measurement precedes frontier complexity).
DELIVERABLES: versioned recommended Cargo/rustc profiles; -Zthreads capability detection + opt-in config on supported nightlies (exact capability detection, never unconditional unstable flags); Wild/lld linker selection; debuginfo reduction + split-debuginfo tuning; optional Cranelift dev profile; cargo-hakari/workspace-hack guidance+automation for feature-unification stability; explicit target-CPU / Apple deployment-target / SDK baselines; canonical agent command palette (fixed check/nextest/clippy invocations, reduces key fragmentation later); sccache baseline setup (interim competitor); benchmark scripts for representative repos.

title: RABS M0: record/replay corpus, tiny wrappers, edge skeleton, shadow-only
description:
MILESTONE M0 — build the observation substrate: stable rabs-protocol local request/event schemas; tiny wrappers (rch-rustc etc.) with FULL nested-wrapper-chain handling (Cargo may invoke: $RUSTC_WRAPPER $RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER $RUSTC args... — the outer wrapper must decode/preserve the entire chain, never assume arg1 is rustc); rabs-edge skeleton (may live inside the existing daemon binary initially); immediate original-chain fail-open plus separate transcript/stateful delivery-frontier tracking; redacted invocation recorder; normalized action-family records + coherent command-snapshot IDs; stock execution passthrough; SLO instrumentation; replay harness; stable/beta/nightly wrapper-contract CI matrix; initial rch why showing raw key-component candidates BEFORE any serving exists.

Constituents: Epic B (corpus) + Epic C (wrapper/local protocol) P0 items.

title: RABS M1: canonical Cargo driver, execroot, path-equivalence proof (keystone)
description:
MILESTONE M1 — the KEYSTONE (Invariants I1, I19, I20).
