EPIC M — Workspace action serving and pipelining (the M10 plane). Detect workspace rustc action classes via canonical Cargo; integrate canonical snapshots + observed-input recipes; conservative exact workspace dependency-artifact inputs + gated projection epochs; build the provenance/action DAG from artifact content identities (no reliance on unstable Cargo unit-graph APIs — actions reference dependency artifacts by content identity, artifacts reference producing actions, build observations establish order, provisional edges explicit, test actions reference binaries+data).
PROVISIONAL .rmeta LIFECYCLE (I13/I32/I44): provisional outputs are immutable verified objects pinned by (CoordinatorAuthority, ActionKey, ActionGeneration, AttemptId, ExecutionLeaseId, LogicalOutputId); visible only to authorized dependents + the awaiting edge/Cargo; Cargo-visible for one subscriber only after COMPLETE materialization at that subscriber's exact requested path; exactly ONE replayed rustc artifact-notification line per subscriber/logical metadata output (M005); marked provisional in provenance; never become stable because a sibling attempt succeeded; carry lineage records (producer action/generation/attempt, logical output ID, exact object ID); create a direct producer-commit obligation on the consumer and propagate the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE ancestor closure into every prepared descendant (A feeds B feeds C: C cannot commit until A and B resolve — direct-only checks insufficient, R64); descendants derived from unresolved lineage stay provisional even after their own process exits; terminal wrapper success + non-provisional final-output readiness WAIT for lineage closure (M020); GC only after all consumer/reconciliation obligations drain. ADOPTION: a different winning producer attempt satisfies lineage only when its committed result contains the SAME logical output object ID under compatible toolchain/event contract (explicit adoption edge); differing object -> every consuming descendant cancelled/refused (M017).
PRODUCER FAILURE (R39/R86): coordinator invalidates provisional lineage; dependent attempts cancelled/superseded; processes/tokens/streams/pins drain; the producer wrapper's nonzero exit naturally reports the original compiler failure to its Cargo; dependent publication blocked via the unresolved obligation; RABS does NOT claim it can make Cargo forget a replayed metadata notification — safety = prevent invalid commits + fail/cancel the live build coherently; journal provisional subscriber materializations and do ownership-safe cleanup (remove/replace a path only when current bytes still match the RABS-installed object AND the path belongs to that operation; else mark target dirty and require Cargo revalidation — never guess-delete user state, M019).
DEP-INFO (I39/R85): parse/normalize standard + binary dep-info, response files, exact extern artifacts, build-script generated sources, source-map/remap data, failed reads, dir enumerations, symlink resolutions, subprocess/PATH selection; dep-info is EVIDENCE not a security boundary (authoritative execution uses the closed view + abort-on-new-read); shared result stores CANONICAL dep-info; each edge derives subscriber-specific dep-info with exact Makefile escaping under a versioned derivation contract, installed privately, never masquerading as the canonical object; unprovable lossless rewriting bypasses the hit. Incremental serving stays DISABLED for shared classes until M13 gates pass (M018). RMETA PROJECTION EXPERIMENT (M012, before any reduced projection): corpus across internal repos; canonicalize first; record exact artifact received; compare conservative vs projected keys; classify interface vs implementation edits; measure byte-identical .rmeta frequency; inspect span/hash oversensitivity; shadow-execute every projected hit; proceed threshold + projection-epoch rollback.

title: RABS Epic N: build-script run cache
description:
EPIC N — Build-script run cache (Part VIII sec 34 + XIII sec 91). POLICY SPLIT: registry/git dependency build scripts = aggressive sandboxing + discovery, immutable source validated by checksum, native subcompile interception, determinism audit before broad sharing; workspace build scripts = audit-first, explicit project policy for git/clock/randomness/network/secrets, volatility preferred over optimistic caching, actionable rch why refusals.
REPLAY MUST PRESERVE exact ordered bytes + semantics for: cargo:rerun-if-changed / cargo::rerun-if-changed; cargo:rerun-if-env-changed; cargo:rustc-* directives; cargo:key=value metadata that becomes DEP_LINKS_* input for dependents; warnings/errors + exit status; the complete declared generated output tree. Exact stdout is accompanied by a STRUCTURED DIRECTIVE MANIFEST used for validation + downstream keys: path-valued rustc-link-search directives must resolve to declared generated outputs, immutable toolchain/native datasets, or explicitly captured host-bound inputs existing at the same canonical path for every consumer — else nonportable/volatile (R122); rustc-link-lib + implicit search semantics push selected native libraries, startup objects, plugins, default scripts, and negative search candidates into the downstream LINK closure; rustc-env/metadata/cfg/flag directives preserve exact bytes into downstream presented environment/invocation (RABS never guesses whether an arbitrary string is a path); replay validates every directive-referenced generated path is inside the installed post-run output tree BEFORE exposing stdout to Cargo (N014).
STATE SEMANTICS: a BuildScriptRun action models the PRE-RUN OUT_DIR + Cargo build-script output-cache state whenever observable (key input); a hit stages the complete post-state in a clean private directory and ATOMICALLY swaps it in, including deletions/tombstones — never merges into a stale OUT_DIR (R66); failed/cancelled runs NEVER publish partial OUT_DIR contents; for live-operation retry parity, either execute directly in the operation-owned Cargo destination or reproduce the exact observed failure post-state, else run locally (R101/N010/N013). INTERCEPTION MECHANISMS in preference order: (1) canonical Cargo-driver integration that intercepts the run without substituting path identity; (2) launcher shim at Cargo's expected path ONLY after compatibility proof (fingerprints, executable mtimes/identity, output-cache files, jobserver descriptors, DEP_LINKS_*, stable/beta/nightly); (3) no run-cache serving when neither preserves semantics. Detect vergen/built/time/git/network patterns (N006) -> volatility classification + denylist; networked generators use the captured-fetch split (fetch under network capability -> immutable objects -> offline generator keyed on captured content, N009).

title: RABS Epic O: test actions
description:
EPIC O — Test actions (Part XV). TestActionKey = H(test_binary_digest, exact_test_identity, runner_identity, arguments, presented_environment, sandbox_semantic_policy, positive+negative data inputs, virtual working directory, output_platform_contract, declared_side_effect_outputs) PLUS nextest/runner profile, retry policy, timeout/slow-timeout, fail-fast observability, setup-script/batch identity, injected runner config (O015). The test-binary digest conservatively invalidates every test in the binary; finer code-to-test projections are advisory research only.
ELIGIBILITY: closed data/process/network/time/randomness inputs; no unrepresented externally-visible side effects; no skipped fixture generation or shared-state initialization; reproducible sandbox/runner semantics; project policy permits. Process-per-test isolation does NOT imply semantic independence: suite ordering, once-per-suite initializers, shared DB/port/temp roots, global external state, setup/teardown effects force a TestBinaryBatch/suite action (whose key includes that state) or bypass (R69/O014). Cached per-test passes must never skip required suite initialization. NEXTEST INTEGRATION (shadow-first): enumerate tests, launch only policy-independent cases through a validated target-runner seam; setup scripts/archive state/once-per-run fixtures execute per the original profile and are represented as batch prerequisites, never skipped by per-test hits; per-test/batch actions capture stdout/stderr, exit status, duration, retry/flaky metadata, declared outputs, input closure; V1 serves stable PASSING results first; deterministic-failure serving is later opt-in with short TTL; retry-only passes classified FLAKY, never stable (R91); if the adapter cannot preserve nextest cwd/env/signal/retry/output semantics, tests stay uncached while compile actions still benefit (O011).
EVIDENCE RECORDS: ObservedStablePass / ObservedStableFailure / FlakyOutcome / TimingSensitive / NetworkSensitive / EnvironmentSensitive / SideEffecting / Quarantined. A cached pass is an execution-reuse fact, not correctness proof; release CI periodically bypasses caching (O013). AFFECTED-TEST SELECTION: provenance-DAG suggests tests affected by changed source/artifacts/data inputs — ADVISORY only, independent from result-cache correctness; CI periodically runs the fresh complete canonical suite to detect missing edges/cache masking (O007). DOCTESTS: agent inner loop defaults to nextest/profile excluding doctests where appropriate; doctest compile+run remain separate cacheable classes; CI runs canonical doctest coverage; generated doctest crate/source identity canonicalized + explainable. BENCHMARKS: BenchmarkCompile may reuse compile artifacts; BenchmarkRun is non-result-cacheable by default (timing is an observation of a machine/load) and remote-schedulable only on explicit hardware/pressure profile (O016/R92).

title: RABS Epic P: incremental snapshots and time travel
description:
EPIC P — Incremental snapshots and time travel (evidence-gated dev-profile feature; M13). Snapshot bundle: stable logical unit identity + canonical visible incremental path (/__rabs/incremental/UNIT — snapshot IDs only in hidden backing metadata); hidden snapshot manifest ID; toolchain/target/profile/projection identity; source/input recipe + compatible state point; incremental directory manifest; MATCHING output artifacts; trust/provenance + determinism status. Selection: exact state first -> nearest compatible git/source ancestor -> historical cost-benefit -> NO transfer when state size exceeds predicted compile saving -> no cross isolation/output-platform reuse without proof. Storage: FastCDC content-defined chunks (adjacent states highly self-similar) + zstd; bounded per-repo lineage retention; reachability/LRU GC.
SAFETY (R128): every restored snapshot materializes as a PRIVATE writable clone/copy per attempt; retained snapshot + CAS chunks stay immutable, never mounted writable by two rustc processes; capture only after the producing compiler and its output writers are quiescent; incremental manifest + matching ordinary outputs publish as ONE atomic auxiliary snapshot unit; cancellation/crash before commit leaves only disposable staging; sampled cold/exact rebuild verifies compatibility before a snapshot family gains portable authority. Until authoritative: shared serving disables incremental compilation for admitted classes or treats incremental state as private nonshareable — an incremental dir is never an implicit unkeyed input. KILL CRITERION: poor latency ROI or unacceptable storage/complexity on representative corpora -> keep exact artifact caching, defer state serving (R17/R18).

title: RABS Epic Q: speculation and agent intelligence
description: EPIC Q — Speculation and agent intelligence (Part XIV). SAVE-TIME SPECULATION: watcher detects stable edit boundary (debounce + editor write semantics) -> immutable snapshot of changed state -> likely action set from historical agent commands + provenance DAG -> nearest compatible incremental snapshot -> low-priority speculative submit -> brownout under pressure -> INSTANT promotion when the agent runs the matching command (same actor/key/generation; priority+deadline raised; transferred inputs + partial execution retained; brownout suspended while foreground interest exists; provenance records promotion) -> measure saved foreground latency vs wasted work. A speculative compile and a foreground compile with identical semantics MUST join the same ActionActor (Speculative is SubscriberKind/AttemptPurpose, never an action class). A subsequent edit demonstrates supersession, not false promotion. GIT-EVENT PREWARM: checkout/HEAD/pull/rebase/merge/worktree-create/lockfile/toolchain/CI-push -> fetch snapshot, locate nearest state, prewarm dependency + workspace critical path, seed likely workers, optional canonical test subset, stop instantly under foreground pressure. CI CANONICAL WRITER: every pushed commit may prebuild canonical profiles; CI-signed provenance gets stronger trust classification; developer pulls receive guaranteed-warm artifacts; trust tier is a publication/access policy, not a content-identity difference. FRAGMENTATION ANALYZER + RCH ADVISE (M15 content): quantify compiler-seconds lost to key fragmentation and recommend convergence; advise on crate-architecture rebuild tails with evidence/confidence/non-claims; no automatic mutation. Speculation optimizes expected saved foreground latency minus execution/transfer/storage cost; ROI dashboard gates default-on (Q010).

title: RABS Epic R: explainability and operations
description:
EPIC R — Explainability and operations (Parts XVII + XXIII). DECISION RECEIPT per scheduling/execution request: request identity; normalized invocation class; key breakdown digest; snapshot root + action closure; cache lookup decision; singleflight decision; subscriber state; worker candidate rows; selected worker + reasons; transfer plan; budget/priority; attempt authority; lifecycle events; provisional artifact events; output verification; publication decision; latency/resource metrics; fallback/refusal reasons; non-claims. EVENT TAXONOMY (stable, typed, causally linked): BuildIntentObserved, ActionKeyComputed, CacheLookupStarted, CacheHitValidated, CacheMiss, SubscriberJoined, WorkerCandidatesEvaluated, AttemptLeased, InputTransferStarted, SandboxReady, ProcessSpawned, MetadataReady, DiagnosticEmitted, ProcessExited, OutputVerified, PreparedResultOffered, ActionResultCommitted, SubscriberCompleted, CancellationRequested, DrainProgress, OperationReconciled, ObjectQuarantined.
RCH WHY queries (product pillar, required not polish): rch why action KEY | crate CRATE | miss REQUEST-OR-BUILD-ID | rebuild ARTIFACT | worker DECISION-ID | volatile ACTION | slow BUILD-ID. Miss explanation = structured diff between prior and current key breakdowns with the stable miss-cause taxonomy. OPERATOR CLI: rch rabs status/doctor/mode/replay/shadow-report/why/action show/operation show/object stat-verify-locate/quarantine list-inspect-release/gc plan-run-history/worker reconcile/cache fragmentation/advise/benchmark replay/protocol compatibility — all with bounded JSON/TOON output + stable reason codes. DOCTOR CHECKS: daemon reachability + fail-open latency; protocol compatibility; identity/cert binding; canonical execroot support; namespace/sandbox capabilities; toolchain consistency; target-CPU/profile drift; jobserver validity; disk/CAS health; DB/fs consistency; corruption sample; pressure freshness; path quality; stale operations/pins; GC headroom; wrapper-contract matrix status. METRICS: user-visible (intent-to-first-diagnostic/metadata-ready/completion/test-result; save-to-green), cache (hit rate, served-vs-executed, seconds saved, miss taxonomy, quarantines, materialization time, dedup), scheduler (queue delay, selection accuracy, jobserver utilization, PSI, fairness, speculation ROI, hedging value), transfer (bytes/dedup/time-to-first-useful/resume value/CPU-per-GiB/locality), reliability (drain latency, orphan prevention, leaks, restarts, reconciliation, corruption, divergence, denylist size). DASHBOARDS: fleet posture, latency distributions, cache effectiveness, top expensive crates, critical paths, transfer/CAS health, storage/GC/quarantine, speculation ROI, determinism status, fragmentation. TRACE/REPLAY: every incident convertible to normalized descriptor + event trace + conditions + receipts + manifests + cancellation/lease timeline + lab seed + minimized replay. ROLLOUT: feature modes off/record-only/shadow-key/shadow-execute/serve-dependencies/serve-selected-workspace/serve-all-eligible/remote-control-shadow/native-atp-control/native-atp-data/speculation-enabled/tests-enabled/incremental-snapshots-enabled/require-remote — independently controllable per repo/action-class/worker/trust-tier. CANARY: designated canary coordinator+workers; low-risk dependency actions first; automatic perf/correctness comparison vs current RCH; quarantine on cleanup/corruption/identity/divergence incidents; one-command rollback. INCIDENT CLASSES (each with detection, containment, runbook, evidence bundle, recovery, regression-test requirement): IncorrectResultDivergence, ObjectCorruption, PublicationFenceViolation, OrphanProcessOrResource, ProtocolCompatibilityFailure, WorkerIdentityMismatch, SecretExposure, StorageExhaustion, SchedulerPressureCollapse, CancellationHang, ReconciliationConflict, KeyInstabilityRegression, HitRateFragmentation. BACKUP/DR: CAS reconstructible from peers/cold/rebuild; periodic consistent metadata backups; ordinary index loss degrades to misses but authority/publication/generation/trust metadata is restored or explicitly reset/fenced before serving resumes; restore verifies object closure + schemas.

title: RABS Epic S: security and trust
description:
EPIC S — Security and trust (Part XVI). THREAT MODEL: agent-generated source/build scripts; proc macros + native tools; compromised/misconfigured workers; corrupted disks/stores; stale/replayed messages; malicious cache entries; accidental secret exposure; buggy wrapper/key logic; operator drift. V1 = ONE trusted administrative fleet (explicit non-claim of hostile multi-tenancy — S014), secret scoping still applies within it.
IDENTITY: durable cryptographic coordinator/worker identities (pubkey-derived peer ID, fingerprint, generation, rotation history, revocation, transport binding, trust scope); config labels are aliases, not proof; worker identity used for ATP authorization must bind to the authenticated transport identity (S002).
TRUST TIERS (evidence labels, not correctness assertions): UnverifiedCandidate / ShadowMatched / ReproducibleSameWorker / ReproducibleCrossWorker / CIPolicyApproved / ProjectReleaseEligible / Quarantined. Serving policy combines tier + isolation profile + output platform + action class + secret/privacy scope + project lane; tiers never alter content digests. Per-subscriber minimum evidence/isolation/privacy requirements; a committed result may exist yet be ineligible for a subscriber; verification appends evidence + new versioned ActionTrustEvaluationRecord; compromise/policy-change/divergence demotes or quarantines SERVING without rewriting publication (I42/S021/R99).
PROVENANCE RECEIPT per publication: key + epochs; descriptor digest; producing snapshot root + minimal closure; toolchain/platform contracts; sandbox policy; authenticated worker identity/generation; operation/generation/attempt/lease identity; termination record; observed-input closure result; output manifest; verification level; causal order; optional signature/MAC; redacted capability use; non-claims. Serve receipts separately name the CONSUMING snapshot.
POISONING PREVENTION: agents cannot write shared CAS/action entries; workers upload objects but never commit pointers; coordinator verifies closure + fencing; abnormal terminations never cached; schema/toolchain/platform mismatches fail closed; continuous sampled stock + cross-worker verification; narrowest-scope quarantine; release policy may require CIPolicyApproved or stronger. A cryptographically authenticated worker is still a semantic trust principal — digests prove transport/storage integrity, NOT that a compromised worker ran rustc honestly (R79); higher tiers can require two independent workers / stock differential / CI approval; divergence removes the worker from publication eligibility (S018).
SECRETS: exposed only via stable logical capability slots; never in plaintext breakdowns/logs/events/bundles; output-affecting secrets contribute trusted opaque HMAC(value/version/scope) generated OUTSIDE the untrusted action, or the action is noncacheable/nonshareable (R56); outputs in access-controlled namespaces, optional at-rest encryption; redacted from child diagnostics; cleaned at finalization. Source-transfer authorization enforced BEFORE upload; inventory/location queries access-controlled so restricted-object existence does not leak (S015/S019). SIGNING/NOTARIZATION (S016/R74): code signing, Apple notarization, package publication, timestamp-authority calls are separate credentialed actions; unsigned/ad-hoc intermediates cacheable by policy; signing keys never enter ordinary compiler workers or shared namespaces. RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION DEFENSES: per-peer/per-action limits on sessions, frames/sec, frame/extension sizes, queued bytes, in-flight requests, manifest depth/fanout, sparse ranges, diagnostics volume, output count/bytes, process count, memory/temp/disk quotas, retries/restarts; control/cancel capacity reserved independently. PRIVACY: logs/receipts avoid raw source, secrets, home/worktree paths, credentialed command lines, unbounded output, worker network details — store hashes/virtual paths/redacted labels/bounded excerpts; failure bundles need explicit retention+access policy. AUTHORITY HIGH-WATER (I40/S020/S024): peers durably persist highest accepted (credential_generation, term) lexicographically; restored DB/reused lower term cannot regain authority without cluster-root-signed operator-reset proof; worker boot-generation high-water + one active incarnation + clone-ambiguity fail-closed (incarnation fencing detects duplicates but does NOT prove legitimacy — hardware-bound enrollment or operator re-enrollment where it matters; I54/S022/S023/R106/R114). License/SBOM conformance gate (S017 with A016).

title: RABS Epic T: proof, fuzzing, chaos, and soak
description:
EPIC T — Proof, fuzzing, chaos, and soak (Part XXI). TRUST LADDER: Stage 0 observation only -> 1 shadow keys/lookups (always execute stock) -> 2 shadow result comparison (private candidate execution, byte/semantic compare, divergence corpus) -> 3 sampled serving (low-risk registry deps, high verification rate, instant quarantine on divergence) -> 4 broad dependency serving (+native subcompiles, eligible build scripts, cross-worker sampling) -> 5 workspace authoritative serving (only after canonical execroot + observed-input closure + long shadow evidence) -> 6 tests/incremental/speculation each independently gated.
TEST CLASSES: unit (codecs, key normalization, state transitions, scoring, path mapping, manifest/digest logic, failure classification); property (encode/decode round-trips, canonical serialization, key stability under irrelevant changes, key sensitivity to every semantic input, idempotency, monotonic fencing, manifest closure/reachability, GC never deletes pinned/reachable); metamorphic (equivalent worktrees -> identical keys/results; different chunking -> identical objects; resumed vs uninterrupted transfer identical; local vs remote equivalent; cache hit vs execution -> identical Cargo-observable stream; different schedules -> same committed result); differential (stock vs RABS; encoder impls; native ATP vs fallback; worker platforms within class); lab/deterministic (cancellation at every await; delay/loss/reorder/partition; restarts; lease expiry; duplicate/replayed messages; hedged races; provisional invalidation; stale health; pressure brownout); fuzz (ATP/RABS frames; manifests/recursive graphs; key canonicalization; path normalization/diagnostic rewriting; reconciliation sequences; corrupted journals/sparse ranges; CLI/local protocol); chaos/real-host (kill daemon mid-publish; kill worker mid-compile; fill disk; corrupt blob; restart NIC; suspend/resume; PSI/OOM; lose Tailscale; rotate identities during drain; independent version upgrades); soak (multi-day sessions; repeated reconnects; high object counts; millions of actor lifecycles; sustained storms; idle-then-burst; GC during active work).
NAMED CORE SCENARIOS (minimum): singleflight_many_subscribers; cancel_one_subscriber_shared_action_survives; cancel_last_subscriber_drains_everything; worker_dies_before_ack; worker_dies_after_metadata_ready; coordinator_dies_after_prepare_before_commit; stale_attempt_result_rejected; hedged_candidate_commit_and_late_divergence_quarantine; bulk_transfer_never_starves_cancel; corrupt_blob_quarantined_and_refetched; disk_full_never_exposes_partial_result; partition_resume_journal_no_duplicate_commit; speculation_browns_out_before_foreground; stale_worker_snapshot_fails_closed; cache_hit_stream_matches_stock_pipelining; virtual_execroot_cross_worktree_equivalence; proc_macro_untracked_input_invalidates_key; build_script_stdout_metadata_replays_exactly.
CORRECTNESS GATES before authoritative workspace serving: ~10^5-10^6 representative shadow actions with ZERO unexplained divergence; stable key equivalence across worktrees/machines in supported classes; complete observed-input coverage for target classes; no orphan process/slot/pin incidents in stress corpus; crash+reconciliation matrix passes; protocol canonical fixtures + N/N-1 compatibility; storage corruption/refetch proof; p95 overhead SLO compliance. Every production incident convertible to a minimized deterministic replay. High-risk subsystems (key schema, execroot, publication fencing, provisional lifecycle, identity binding, pins/GC, QUIC cutover, sandbox capabilities, incremental portability, test authority, snapshot-vs-closure, canonical driver, authority recovery, projections, jobserver accounting, platform matrix, metadata conformance, state machines, hedging conflicts, lineage adoption, no-writable-hardlinks, build-script state, licensing, resolution replay, process metadata closure, result/evidence identity, source confidentiality, content index, representation identity, runtime paths, dep-info derivation, wrapper signals, test semantics, path policy, delivery arbitration, trust evolution, plane grants, failure post-state, release profiles, publication/serving split, generation ABA, snapshot lineage, sequence domains, publication pins, waiter bounds, clone policy) each require a dedicated design review before implementation/cutover.

title: A001: create RABS domain crate skeleton with explicit edge/coord/worker roles
description: Create the RABS crate skeleton: rabs-protocol, rabs-action, rabs-key, rabs-cas, rabs-sandbox, rabs-scheduler, rabs-asupersync, plus explicit edge/coordinator/worker role modules (rabs-edge + rabs-coord may ship combined in one rabsd binary but authority, durable state, and protocol interfaces stay distinct; rabs-wkr is a specialized worker daemon, NOT a mode of atpd). WHY: the crate boundaries ARE the architecture — rabs-protocol must stay Asupersync-free and Tokio-free so wire/durable schemas cannot rot into implementation types (I14); rabs-action/key must run in plain deterministic tests and the Asupersync lab with no network/fs. ACCEPTANCE: workspace compiles; each crate has a doc header stating its dependency rules; rabs-action and rabs-key have zero fs/network/process effects.
close_reason: Implemented: 9 rabs crates (protocol/action/key/cas/sandbox/scheduler/asupersync/rabsd+edge,coord roles/wkr) as workspace members; dependency rules in each lib.rs doc header + manifest comments; rabs-action/key/protocol have zero deps and zero fs/network effects; cargo fmt+check+clippy green workspace-wide. Self-verified by re-execution (no independent verifier this session).

title: A002: dependency-direction CI forbidding Tokio/adapter deps in domain crates
description: Add dependency-direction CI that forbids domain crates (rabs-protocol, rabs-action, rabs-key, rabs-cas core) from depending on rabs-asupersync, Tokio, network servers, or daemon crates. WHY: compatibility islands must never contaminate the native action path (risk R24); an accidental Tokio edge into the domain crates would silently re-couple RABS to the runtime it is migrating away from. Implement as a cargo-deps graph check in CI that fails the build with the offending edge named. ACCEPTANCE: CI red on an intentionally introduced forbidden edge; green otherwise.
close_reason: Implemented dependency-direction CI as rabs-protocol/tests/dependency_direction.rs (runs in cargo test --workspace = CI): domain crates forbidden from tokio/asupersync/rabs-asupersync/daemon/network-server deps; pure crates (protocol/action/key/scheduler) restricted to an explicit allowlist; crate-existence guard prevents silent pass on renames; parser self-test. Verified with a PLANTED NEGATIVE (tokio inserted into rabs-key [dependencies] -> both checks fail with actionable messages; reverted). Green does not prove transitive-cone purity via renamed/re-exported crates — that extension lands with A008 boundary tests. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A003: pin exact Asupersync revision with ADR
description: Pin an exact Asupersync revision and record the pin plus rationale in an architecture decision record. Synthesis-time pin: 62d398ea17519d7e80cbdb32e062d70647cd58a4 (repo main was 513aa04f, a formatting-only child; behavioral claims stay pinned to the reviewed commit until CI revalidates a newer pin). WHY: Asupersync API churn leaking into RABS forces broad rewrites and schema instability (risk R8); all behavioral claims in the plan are evidence-pinned. ACCEPTANCE: ADR exists; Cargo pin exact; upgrade procedure documented (see A010 upgrade bot).
close_reason: Pinned asupersync as git dependency at the plan-reviewed revision 62d398ea (v0.3.10, rider license) in rabs-asupersync only; ADR 007 records context, the literal plan rule (behavioral claims stay pinned until CI revalidates), and the binding upgrade procedure (A010 report + A009 contract suite + ADR update + epoch discipline). Verified: pinned dep fetches and compiles (1m34s), clippy -D warnings, fmt, full workspace check green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A004: minimal rabs-profile Asupersync feature set + dependency inventory artifact
description: Define the minimal rabs-profile Asupersync feature set and generate a dependency/feature inventory artifact in CI. INCLUDE: production native runtime; process support; ATP object/journal/protocol support; native QUIC+TLS when transport enabled; tracing/metrics RABS needs; lab/test internals only in test builds. EXCLUDE unless explicitly needed: browser, Kafka, database, H3, WebTransport, mailbox, relay, broad compat features; io_uring only after measured benefit + compatibility validation. WHY: enabling the whole default surface indiscriminately bloats the critical binaries and widens the audit surface. ACCEPTANCE: CI emits a dependency+feature graph artifact proving exactly what entered the critical binaries.
close_reason: Minimal rabs-profile: asupersync dep now default-features=false + features=[proc-macros] exactly (drops experimental nightly-outcome-try Try impls; RABS uses explicit Outcome helpers). Conformance test pins the profile + rev, forbids browser/wasm/legacy/messaging-fabric/real-service-e2e/test-internals in runtime deps (comments exempt), and restricts test-internals to dev-dependencies. Proven with planted negative (feature widening -> red with actionable message -> restored). Compile verified without defaults (2m24s). CI cargo-tree inventory artifact joins A012 budget gates (shared plumbing, noted in test rustdoc). Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A005: key/protocol/database/object-manifest/sandbox schema version registries
description: Establish the five schema version registries: key, protocol, database, object-manifest, and sandbox. Every canonical serialization carries explicit schema identity; epoch changes create cold namespaces and never reinterpret old entries under new semantics. WHY: versioned-everything is the mechanism behind safe key-logic evolution (key_epoch/projection_epoch), N/N-1 protocol compatibility, transactional DB migrations, and manifest stability; without central registries these drift independently. ACCEPTANCE: registry files exist with initial v1 entries for each domain; CI validates that any schema struct change bumps the right registry entry.
close_reason: Implemented rabs-protocol::schema_registry: five domains (key/protocol/database/object-manifest/sandbox), 18 initial v1 entries (ATP/0 at v0), typed lookup with cross-domain rejection, epoch doctrine documented, FNV change-detector golden making registry edits deliberate. 5/5 unit tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt green. Struct-level bump enforcement extends via A002 CI as concrete schema types land (per bead text). Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A006: stable reason-code registry generation and validation
description: Add stable reason-code registry generation and validation. Families: KEY_* CACHE_* INPUT_* PATH_* TOOLCHAIN_* PLATFORM_* SANDBOX_* WORKER_* PRESSURE_* TRANSFER_* LEASE_* AUTHORITY_* CANCEL_* DELIVERY_* PUBLICATION_* EVIDENCE_* STORAGE_* VERIFY_* QUARANTINE_* FALLBACK_* PROTOCOL_* SPECULATION_* TEST_*. Codes are append-only within a protocol major version and documented in a registry consumed by DecisionReceipts, rch why, refusal messages, and operator CLI JSON. WHY: explainability is a product pillar; stable machine-readable reasons are what make refusals/fallbacks/misses diagnosable by agents. ACCEPTANCE: codegen or macro emits the registry; CI rejects removed/renamed codes.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::reason_codes: all 23 plan families (KEY_..TEST_) with prefix-unambiguity guarantee, 31 seed codes covering decisions the plan names (fallback frontiers, divergence quarantine, stale authority, negative-dep invalidation, break-even local, brownout, etc.), append-only doctrine + FNV change-detector golden, typed lookup. 12/12 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt green (via target-local; shared global target dir was lock-held by other agents' builds). Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A007: shared redaction library and data-classification policy
description: Create a shared redaction library and data-classification policy used by receipts, logs, key breakdowns, failure bundles, and telemetry. Rules: raw secrets never appear anywhere; source contents not logged by default; home/worktree paths become virtual paths or redacted labels; component hashes retained where raw values cannot be logged; bounded excerpts only. WHY: privacy/secret hygiene (I26/I38) must be a library, not a per-call-site discipline, or one forgotten call site leaks credentials into durable evidence. ACCEPTANCE: redaction unit tests including secret-bearing env, argv with credentials, and home-path diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::redaction: DataClass policy (Public/SecretSensitive/PathSensitive/SourceContent), broad secret-name classification (false positive = redacted line, false negative = credential leak), env/argv redaction incl. --flag=value and flag-then-value shapes, URL userinfo scrubbing, home->tilde path rewriting with boundary check, bounded excerpts with explicit marker, FNV correlation hash with explicit non-cryptographic non-claims. 19 lib tests incl. paired permitted cases (non-secret env/argv/URLs pass through unchanged). clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A008: boundary tests — no Asupersync types in public CLI/wire/persistence
description: Add architecture boundary tests ensuring public CLI JSON, wire formats, and persistence schemas contain no Asupersync implementation types (I14). Mechanism: compile-time assertions plus a schema-dump test that serializes every public/durable type and checks the type inventory against an allowlist owned by rabs-protocol. WHY: experimental Asupersync types in stable surfaces is an explicit non-goal; violations are almost impossible to unwind after data is durable. ACCEPTANCE: test fails when an Asupersync type is added to any public/durable struct.
close_reason: Implemented boundary tests (rabs-protocol/tests/boundary.rs): (1) structural foundation re-asserted — rabs-protocol has ZERO deps so Asupersync/Tokio types are unnameable in wire/durable/CLI schemas; (2) public-surface scan — rabsd/rabs-wkr may not declare any pub item mentioning asupersync, and the adapter may not re-export it (pub use), so downstream crates cannot reach Asupersync types through it; (3) HONEST BOUNDARY in rustdoc — source-text heuristic; exhaustive cargo-public-api/schema-dump verification joins the rabs CI job when concrete serializers exist. Planted negative proven: pub fn exposing asupersync::PlantedNever in rabsd turned the gate red with the convert-through-rabs-protocol message; removed, green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A009: consumer-driven adapter contract tests against pinned Asupersync
description: Add consumer-driven adapter tests against the pinned Asupersync revision: for every capability rabs-asupersync adapts (regions, Cx, process groups, supervision, ATP objects/journals, lab, observability, pressure), a contract test encodes the exact behavior RABS relies on. WHY: this converts implicit assumptions about Asupersync semantics into executable contracts, so a pin bump that changes behavior fails loudly in the adapter, not deep inside RABS (R8). ACCEPTANCE: contract suite green at the pin; intentionally perturbed adapter behavior fails.

title: A010: Asupersync upgrade bot/report for pin updates
description: Add an upgrade bot/report that diffs Asupersync public API and the feature graph before any pin update, producing a reviewable report of changed APIs/features that intersect the rabs-asupersync adapter surface. WHY: pin updates must be deliberate, evidence-based events; the report bounds review effort to what actually changed. ACCEPTANCE: report generated for a synthetic pin bump; CI blocks pin changes without an attached report.

title: A011: unsafe-boundary ledger for sandbox/process/network helpers
description: Create unsafe-boundary ledger entries for every sandbox/process/network privileged helper: the small audited privileged helper for mount namespaces/chroot, any seccomp/Landlock shims, and raw-socket/QUIC internals RABS touches. Each entry: what the boundary protects, protocol bounds, fuzz status, review date. WHY: helpers cross privilege boundaries; the plan requires their protocols to be bounded, path-safe, fuzzed where applicable, and ledgered so audits are tractable. ACCEPTANCE: ledger exists with entries for all initial helpers; CI check reminds when a helper changes without a ledger update.
close_reason: Created docs/rabs-unsafe-boundary-ledger.md: creation-gate provenance header (consumer=S010 release gate + reviewers; retirement condition), six-field entry contract (boundary/protocol-bounds/blast-radius/fuzz-status/review/deletion-condition), honest initial state = ZERO entries (no privileged code exists yet) + expected-entrants table (D003/D013/E005/E017). Currency enforced by rabs-sandbox/tests/unsafe_boundary_ledger.rs: ledger structure required; known helper locations without a ledger entry fail; all 9 rabs crates must keep unsafe_code=forbid (privileged code cannot hide in libraries). Planted negative proven (rabs-helpers/ dir -> red -> removed -> green; empty plant dir created+rmdir'd during verification, disclosed). Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A012: supply-chain/dependency budget gates per binary
description: Add supply-chain and dependency-budget gates for the edge, coordinator, and worker binaries: maximum dependency counts/classes, license compatibility checks, and build reproducibility notes per binary. WHY: wrappers and daemons have different budgets (tiny wrapper must stay tiny); unchecked dependency growth erodes startup latency, audit surface, and the license posture. ACCEPTANCE: CI budget check per binary with current baselines; failure on budget regression without explicit override.
close_reason: Implemented direct-dependency budget gates (rabs-protocol/tests/dependency_budget.rs): per-crate budgets with baseline rationale (protocol=0 by design, pure crates=1, adapters/daemons bounded); new-rabs-crate coverage guard (a member without a budget fails); license-posture gate (publish=false mandatory until A016 lands, risk R72). Planted negative proven: serde added to rabs-scheduler -> budget red with actionable message -> reverted. HONEST BOUNDARY in rustdoc: direct-dep budgets from textual scans; transitive-cone cargo-tree inventory needs CI plumbing (lands with the rabs CI job); A002 direction gate bounds what direct edges pull in meanwhile. All tests/clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A013: single-active coordinator authority acquisition + combined-role deployment contract
description: Define the single-active coordinator authority acquisition and combined-role deployment contract: on every start the coordinator takes an exclusive local authority lock, durably advances a cluster-wide monotonic term BEFORE issuing authority-bearing messages, carries a nondecreasing credential generation, and creates a fresh random incarnation ID. V1 has NO automatic cross-host failover; disaster recovery to another host is operator-fenced (revoke/rotate the fleet credential or prove the old authority stopped). CoordinatorAuthority{cluster_id, credential_generation, term, incarnation_id} is a structured fencing identity, NOT a consensus substitute — two simultaneously active leaders are out of contract. ACCEPTANCE: contract doc + type definitions + startup sequence tests (lock contention, term advance ordering, fresh incarnation).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::authority: CoordinatorAuthority/ClusterId/IncarnationId/OperatorResetGeneration types; PeerAuthorityHighWaterMark::evaluate with the full lexicographic decision table (stale generation always loses even with huge term; stale term; same-pair wrong-incarnation rejected as restored-DB/clone per R88; higher generation = new namespace PENDING credential-chain proof, never comparison alone; fresh operator-reset proof recovers fenced authority, stale/replayed reset does not); pure CoordinatorBoot model enforcing lock -> durable-term-advance -> fresh-incarnation -> issue ordering with typed errors (lock contention, issue-before-durable-advance, non-monotonic term, credential regression, repeated incarnation). Contract doc in rustdoc: no automatic failover, DR operator-fenced, fencing-not-consensus. 8 new tests (36 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A014: semantic ActionDescriptor vs non-key subscription/dispatch context split
description: Define the split between the semantic ActionDescriptor (immutable after final key computation; contains everything that can change output bytes or exit behavior) and non-key request/presentation context: ActionSubscriptionContext (snapshot root, edge, operation, subscriber, kind, presentation, compiler-event/pipelining contracts, path translation, ExecutionRequirements, minimum evidence tier, priority, deadline) and AttemptDispatchContext (attempt authority, purpose, selected worker, eligibility receipt, resource grant, sandbox implementation, object source plan — created only after scheduling, unique per attempt, never part of result identity). Compiler-event/pipelining contracts live in presentation context unless a versioned toolchain-specific proof shows a setting alters exit status or artifact bytes; ambiguous diagnostic/lint flags stay in the semantic invocation or force a presentation variant. ACCEPTANCE: types in rabs-protocol; doc table of what lives where; boundary tests that ExecutionRequirements fields provably cannot enter the key.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::descriptor: ActionDescriptor with EXACTLY the twelve semantic component digests + epochs + ActionClass (all 21 plan classes; Speculative/GitPrewarm etc. are deliberately NOT classes); key_input_components() destructures exhaustively so adding a field without deciding its key role is a compile error, and the component list drifting is a named test failure (key-epoch decision, F002). ActionSubscriptionContext (snapshot root, kind, presentation, path translation, ExecutionRequirements, priority, deadline) and AttemptDispatchContext (worker, sandbox impl, snapshot selection) carry NO channel into the descriptor — boundary test mutates every subscription/dispatch field incl. promotion and worker reselection and proves key inputs bit-identical; speculative and foreground subscriptions against one descriptor share one key. 3 new tests (57 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A015: platform/isolation authority matrix with explicit no-claims
description: Define the supported platform/isolation authority matrix with explicit no-claims. Matrix: Linux strict hermetic = dependency+workspace serving and cross-machine publication after gates; macOS VM/chroot strict = yes after platform proof within matching SDK/ABI class; macOS host-audit = selected immutable deps only, NO authoritative shared workspace, NO cross-machine; Windows initial = observation/limited classes, workspace deferred, no implied parity. Unsupported isolation/input-observation properties reduce authority explicitly — never optimistic parity labels (I25/I28). ACCEPTANCE: matrix doc + machine-readable table consumed by serving policy; tests that an unsupported profile yields reduced authority, not a false pass.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::authority_matrix: 6 isolation profiles x 3 serving scopes as a total const function with denial-default posture (I25/I28); every cell carries an explicit claim/no-claim boundary string; exact cell-by-cell plan-conformance test (stronger than a fingerprint — drift names the cell); reduced-profile tests prove host-audit/volatile/windows/dep-fast-path can never reach workspace authority. 23 lib tests, clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A016: fix license metadata (LicenseRef rider) + SBOM/release-notice alignment
description: Align RCH/RABS Cargo license metadata, license files, SBOMs, and release notices with the actual rider-bearing license. FINDING (verified at synthesis): both RCH and Asupersync carry "MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)" text, Asupersync metadata already uses LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider, but RCH workspace package metadata still advertises plain MIT — inconsistent with its own LICENSE file and a P0 release-metadata correction (risk R72). DO: switch Cargo metadata to the correct LicenseRef/license-file representation; keep SPDX/SBOM, crate metadata, installer notices, source archives, binary distributions, and website claims consistent; run dependency-license compatibility/attribution checks per release profile; never describe the project as ordinary OSI MIT; any future relicensing is an explicit owner decision, never an agent inference; ensure the REAPI gateway/compat islands impose no incompatible redistribution requirements. ACCEPTANCE: metadata/LICENSE mismatch gate green (S017).

title: A017: four separate state-machine domains (operation/publication/attempt/delivery)
description: Define BuildOperation, logical action publication, execution attempt, and subscriber delivery as four SEPARATE persistence/state-machine domains (I29/I30; risk R61). BuildOperation: Created->Snapshotting->CargoStarting->CargoRunning->CargoDraining->Completed (alt: Cancelled, FailedBeforeStart, FailedAfterObservableCommit, LocalFallbackCompleted, AbandonedClient, InternalFailure); owns requested->resolved snapshot lineage, sealed generation, root permit, wrapper connections, subscriptions. Logical publication slot: Absent->Executing(ActionGenerationId)->Committed(PublicationRecordId), with serving disposition as a separate versioned record. Attempt: Created->LeaseOffered->LeaseAccepted->AwaitingInputs->Materializing->Running(->MetadataReady events)->ProcessExited->{Harvest/Upload/Verify | HarvestCanonicalObservations | Draining}->PreparedResultOffered->{AcceptedAsWinner|RejectedAsDuplicate|RejectedAsStale|RejectedAsDivergent}->Draining->Finished. Subscriber delivery: the two-frontier transcript/stateful machine. A cache hit never re-commits; one action serves many operations; BuildOperationId never appears in the semantic key or as an actor singleton field. ACCEPTANCE: state-machine types + transition tables + property tests in rabs-action.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_action::state_machines: the four SEPARATE machines (I29/I30; R61). BuildOperation: full spine + exposure-split failure terminals (FailedBeforeStart only pre-run, FailedAfterObservableCommit only post) + fallback/cancel/abandon/internal terminals, terminals have no successors. PublicationSlot: Absent->Executing->Committed|Absent; Committed is immutable history — recommit/uncommit UNREPRESENTABLE (cache hit = no transition). Attempt: success + deterministic-failure pipelines both funneling through PreparedResultOffered (may_offer only there; abnormal outcomes drain directly; unverified states cannot offer); rejections (duplicate/stale/divergent) drain. SubscriberDelivery: transcript + stateful loops with fail-closed uncertainty states (uncertain cannot complete/re-emit/detach) + ExposureFrontiers::fallback_class encoding the three-band table (stateful dominates). 5 dense transition tests; denial-default everywhere. clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A018: canonical-result vs attempt-evidence vs publication schema split + divergence taxonomy
description: Split canonical result, attempt evidence, auxiliary incremental state, and publication record schemas, with the semantic/observable/evidence divergence taxonomy (I34/I37/I48; risks R80/R103/R115). CanonicalActionResultManifest holds ONLY replayable output/exit/observable facts (action key, descriptor digest, epochs, ResultKind, artifact_bundle_root derived deterministically from the single role-tagged logical_outputs map, canonical observations, normalized process outcome, semantic_result_digest, observable_result_digest — both computed over versioned projections excluding the digest fields themselves). AttemptEvidenceBundle holds authority, snapshot root, observed-input report, provisional lineage, isolation evidence, raw process/event evidence, provenance receipt, verification, timings, optional incremental snapshot ref. ActionPublicationRecord = immutable history (key, manifest id, winner generation/attempt/evidence, coordinator authority, committed causal sequence). Divergence taxonomy: semantic digest differs = action quarantine incident; semantic equal but observable differs = presentation/observability quarantine (replay disabled); evidence-only differences = normal append; equal declared digests but different canonical manifest bytes = serializer/projection-completeness incident. ACCEPTANCE: schemas in rabs-protocol + taxonomy unit tests.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::result_identity: TypedDigest (algorithm+domain+bytes; same bytes in different domains provably unequal, R121 — F034 owns the framing/computation); role-tagged LogicalOutput map; CanonicalActionResultManifest with validate() (deterministic failures: empty outputs + no bundle root; duplicate role+path rejected); AttemptEvidenceBundle SEPARATE from result identity; ActionPublicationRecord immutable history. Divergence taxonomy classify_same_key_candidate: IdempotentSameResult / SemanticDivergence / ObservableOnlyDivergence / ProjectionCompletenessIncident (equal digests + different manifest object never passes as evidence-only, R103). Test proves equivalent attempts with different evidence (worker/timing/incremental) classify idempotent (I37/R80/R115). 5 new tests (45 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Unblocks A020->A022 and the H011/H026/H029 designs.

title: A019: byte-preserving Unix path/argv/env wire types + escaped presentation
description: Define byte-preserving Unix path/argv/environment wire types and escaped presentation types (I38; risk R89). On Unix, argv elements, response-file names, env keys/values, paths, and symlink targets are canonical byte strings — never assumed UTF-8; lossy conversion is never a semantic key input. Human/JSON display uses escaped or loss-marked presentation forms without changing keyed bytes. Windows gets a separately versioned native path/environment encoding contract. ACCEPTANCE: round-trip fixtures with non-UTF8 argv/path/env/symlink bytes prove byte identity end-to-end (feeds T026).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::raw_bytes: RawBytes canonical byte strings (byte equality/ordering for canonical serialization) + RawPath/RawArg/RawEnvPair/RawSymlinkTarget carriers; deterministic INJECTIVE presentation escape (backslash doubling + \xNN; literal 'a\xe9' and byte 0xE9 render distinctly); Display = escaped form; as_utf8 only when actually valid. Tests: Latin-1 vs UTF-8 spellings stay distinct byte strings, injectivity on tricky pairs, byte ordering, env-pair preservation (root of the T026 fixture family). Windows contract explicitly separate. 29 lib tests + gates green; clippy/fmt ok (earlier 124 was transient lock contention, reran clean; 'unclosed table' in clippy log is asupersync's own malformed-manifest FIXTURE, exit 0). Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A020: immutable publication + append-only evidence + versioned trust-evaluation schemas
description: Define immutable publication, append-only evidence index, and versioned trust-evaluation schemas/policies (I42/I50; risk R99). ActionServingStateRecord: disposition (Eligible/EvidencePending/ExpiredNeedsRevalidation/Quarantined/ObjectsUnavailable/EvictedFromActiveIndex), reason codes, blocking quarantine IDs, policy epoch, monotonic state_revision, coordinator authority digest, ServingValidity (evaluated_at, max age, clock uncertainty, clock epoch — conservative expiry on rollback/uncertainty), revalidation flag. ActionTrustEvaluationRecord: evidence_set_digest (canonically sorted/deduped), policy digest, evaluated tier, isolation scope, privacy scope, serving restrictions. Evidence promotion/demotion never mutates canonical publication bytes; quarantine overrides every evaluation. ACCEPTANCE: schemas + transitions + replay-idempotency tests.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::serving: ActionServingDisposition (6 states incl. EvictedFromActiveIndex with H034 tombstone note); ServingValidity with CONSERVATIVE clock semantics (epoch discontinuity denies, rollback denies, age+uncertainty crossing the bound denies even when naive age passes); ActionServingStateRecord (monotonic state_revision — equal-revision replay refused; blocking quarantine IDs are the gate, never reason strings; may_serve_now composes disposition+quarantine+validity); TrustEvidenceTier ladder + ActionTrustEvaluationRecord referencing results by ID only (no field can mutate a publication — I50 type-level); evidence_set_digest_input canonical sort+dedup (insertion order/duplicates can never rename a set). 6 new tests (51 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Unblocks A022, F032/H033/H040/S021 designs.

title: A021: split tiny-wrapper vs daemon release profiles, benchmark-gated
description: Split tiny-wrapper and daemon/worker release profiles and gate them on startup/throughput corpus benchmarks (risk R100). Wrappers: optimize startup latency + footprint (opt-level z/s, strip, LTO chosen only after startup benchmarks) with panic containment NON-NEGOTIABLE (no abort-on-panic without a guard process — I49). Daemons/workers: sustained latency/throughput, hashing/scheduling/protocol/CAS/materialization performance, normally starting opt-level 3 with measured LTO/codegen-units/allocator; retain symbols/build IDs for crashpacks per release policy. RCH's current workspace-wide opt-level=z/panic=abort profile is an input to migrate, NOT to copy. ACCEPTANCE: package-specific profiles or separate release workspaces; benchmark evidence for each profile on startup, local-hit, cache-miss, transfer, hash, compile-storm traces.

title: A022: publication history separate from mutable serving/index disposition
description: Define immutable publication history separately from mutable serving/index/trust disposition in the domain model (I50). Quarantine, evidence expiry, retention eviction, and trust changes are versioned serving/index dispositions layered OVER committed history; changing them never rewrites canonical result identity; an eviction that forgets active lookup data retains a bounded generation/result tombstone until every stale-lease/conflict window closes. ACCEPTANCE: domain-model doc + rabs-action transition tests proving no serving-state transition can mutate a publication row.
close_reason: Implemented the I50 separation proof as rabs-action/tests/publication_serving_separation.rs, composing A017's PublicationSlotState with A020's serving records: (1) Committed has zero outgoing transitions — quarantine/expiry/eviction are only expressible against the serving layer; (2) cycling one serving record through ALL six dispositions (strictly-increasing revisions) leaves the governed publication identity bit-identical at every step; (3) eviction is a disposition, not deletion — the evicted record still names its publication (bounded-tombstone identity, H034/F031); (4) cross-publication serving updates refused (one action's quarantine cannot leak onto another's history). 2 integration tests + existing 5 lib green; clippy/fmt ok. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A023: RABS-owned causal-time/budget/peer/authority/sequence wire types
description: Define RABS-owned causal timestamp, deadline budget, duration, peer ID, authority, and sequence-domain wire types; forbid Asupersync type leakage (I14). Cross-host deadlines are encoded as relative budgets plus causal/wall-clock diagnostic metadata — never a foreign runtime's process-local Instant. ACCEPTANCE: types live in rabs-protocol; boundary test (A008) covers them; adapters in rabs-asupersync convert both ways with property-tested round trips.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::wire_time: DeadlineBudget (relative ms, saturating spend, exhaustion state — never a foreign Instant on the wire); CausalTimestamp (peer-scoped Lamport counter + wall-clock as DIAGNOSTIC-only field; cross-peer stamps causally incomparable by API; backward wall clock provably ignored); PeerId; SequenceDomain (the five I52 domains) + DomainSequence whose ordering API returns None across domains — a bulk gap is INEXPRESSIBLE as blocking a cancellation (R109) — and saturates instead of wrapping (ABA hazard). 4 new tests (40 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: A024: requested->resolved snapshot lineage + sealed generation binding in schemas
description: Make BuildOperation requested->resolved snapshot lineage and sealed action-generation binding explicit in all domain schemas (I53; risk R110). RequestedCommandSnapshot -> private resolution/fetch/lockfile overlay -> ResolvedExecutionSnapshot -> zero or more action-closure manifests. Every action subscription binds to exactly ONE sealed snapshot generation; no action observes mixed pre/post-resolution state; post-seal mutation of semantically relevant files forces a strictly newer sealed phase, coherent replanning, or downgrade to side-effecting whole-command/local. ACCEPTANCE: schema fields + rabs-action validation tests rejecting mixed-generation closures.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::snapshot_lineage (I53/R110): SnapshotLineage from_requested (phase 0) + seal() with strict phase monotonicity; ActionSnapshotBinding verifying BOTH phase existence and snapshot identity (stale/forged snapshots are a mismatch, never a pass); validate_closure rejects mixed-generation closures — the pre-resolution-Cargo.toml + post-resolution-Cargo.lock corruption is now a typed error, and empty closures are a caller bug rather than a silent pass. 3 new tests (54 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: B001: invocation-record schema (argv/env/cwd/tool/outcome/timing)
description: Define the invocation-record schema: argv (byte-preserving), normalized env digest, cwd mapping (real + virtual), tool identity (compiler/linker/build-script/native/Cargo/nextest), outcome (normalized exit/signal), and timing. This schema is the foundation of the entire measurement program — the corpus doubles as benchmark input, shadow-verification input, regression suite, key-stability study, scheduler training data, and launch evidence. Design for privacy from the start: input HASHES not source contents by default. ACCEPTANCE: schema versioned in the registry (A005); fixtures round-trip; redaction validated with the shared library (A007).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::invocation_record: ToolKind (10 contexts incl. rustdoc/nextest/whole-command), NormalizedOutcome preserving signal-vs-exit (Signaled(9) != Exited(137) is a test), InvocationRecord with capture() as the ONLY constructor — redaction applied at construction so unredacted argv/env are unrepresentable; raw-byte correlation digests (element-boundary-safe NUL separation; latin1 vs utf8 spellings correlate differently; explicitly correlation-grade until F034) + redacted presentation forms + tilde-redacted cwd. Registered rabs.invocation-record v1 in the A005 registry, exercising the deliberate-change flow (new entry -> golden red with fingerprint -> golden updated in same change). 5 new tests (62 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: B002: redacted invocation recorder in existing RCH wrapper/daemon path
description: Implement the redacted invocation recorder inside the existing RCH wrapper/daemon path (before any RABS daemons exist). Every intercepted invocation emits a record per B001 with normalized args and input hashes. WHY: real agent traces from the live RCH fleet are the highest-value corpus; recording must start as early as possible to accumulate stratified data. ACCEPTANCE: recorder runs in production RCH with negligible overhead (within existing hook SLO); records validate against schema; no source bytes or secrets in records.

title: B003: capture rustc/linker/build-script/native/Cargo/nextest contexts
description: Capture all relevant tool contexts in the recorder: rustc invocations (via wrapper), linker, build-script compile+run, native compilers (cc/c++/ar), Cargo whole-command context, and nextest runs. Each context tags its action-class candidate so later replay can stratify by class. ACCEPTANCE: corpus contains labeled records for every class from at least the RCH workspace itself plus one external repo.

title: B004: input/output digests only, no source contents by default
description: Store input and output digests without storing source contents by default. Content-address inputs/outputs so replay can verify identity without retaining bytes; retention of any actual content requires explicit policy (B007). WHY: privacy posture and corpus size both demand digest-only defaults. ACCEPTANCE: record inspection shows digests only; opt-in content retention gated by policy flag.
close_reason: Completed B004 on top of B001's digests-only schema: raw_content_fields() exhaustively destructures every InvocationRecord field (adding a field without classifying it is a COMPILE error) and the audit test asserts zero raw-content fields — the schema structurally cannot retain source bytes; ContentRetention policy type with DigestsOnly as the only unconditional mode and ExplicitIncidentRetention{incident_id} as the sole bytes path (expires with the incident per corpus policy sec 1/2). 2 new tests (76 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: B005: replay runner for stock and candidate RABS paths
description: Build the replay runner that can execute recorded invocations under stock and candidate RABS paths and compare: availability (would we have hit?), result metadata, outputs, diagnostics digests, timing. This is the engine of the trust ladder (Stage 1 shadow keys, Stage 2 shadow result comparison) and of every performance gate. ACCEPTANCE: replays a recorded session against stock path bit-faithfully; harness API supports plugging RABS candidate paths; produces the divergence corpus format.

title: B006: scenario labels (clean/no-op/leaf/root/branch/storm/CI/IDE)
description: Add scenario labels to records and replay selection: clean, no-op, leaf edit, root edit, branch switch, agent storm, CI, IDE. WHY: the quantitative targets are stratified (e.g. 15-agent storm >=3x, branch ping-pong >=3x); unlabeled corpora cannot prove them. ACCEPTANCE: labeler covers the benchmark scenario list; replay can filter by label.

title: B007: corpus retention, privacy, export, minimization policies
description: Create corpus retention, privacy, export, and minimization policies: how long records live, what may be exported off-host, anonymization/redaction rules, and how a failing trace is minimized into a shareable reproduction. ACCEPTANCE: written policy + enforcement hooks in the recorder/exporter; minimizer produces smallest reproducing action/input manifest (pairs with B011).
close_reason: Created docs/rabs-corpus-policy.md v1 with creation-gate provenance (consumers = B002 recorder / exporter / B011 minimizer implementations, which cannot close without conformance; defect class = credential/source leakage + unshareable dumps; retirement condition named). Fixes: content rules (records are B001 schema instances — no raw argv/env/source fields EXIST, additions are policy revisions; redacted paths; no hostnames/usernames), retention (180d rolling with incident/baseline/evidence pins; baselines indefinite; minimized repros die when their regression test lands; tooling sweep is the single sanctioned deletion path per AGENTS RULE 1), export (in-domain free; out-of-domain requires minimizer output + fresh redaction + operator sign-off; scanners advisory only), minimization contract (bisect/shrink/re-verify with reduction log + seeds), stratification tags as enums never free text (free text is a leak channel). Enforcement hooks are the consuming beads' acceptance criteria. Self-verified by review against B001/B004/A007 as implemented.

title: B008: benchmark report with p50/p90/p95 and full metric set
description: Implement the benchmark report: p50/p90/p95 whole-command and action-level metrics, first-diagnostic and first-metadata-ready latency, compiler/linker/test seconds executed vs saved, served-vs-executed ratio, hit rate + miss taxonomy, queue delay, transfer bytes/dedup/throughput, CPU+memory local/remote, storage growth, speculation cost/value, correctness/divergence result. One report format for every benchmark scenario. ACCEPTANCE: report generated from a replay run; stable machine-readable format consumed by CI gates (B013).

title: B009: sccache and current-RCH baselines captured
description: Capture sccache and current-RCH baselines on the benchmark scenarios (plus stock Cargo and Layer-0-only). WHY: comparative baselines are the honesty mechanism — RABS claims are relative to the strongest existing alternatives, and sccache serves as interim baseline and competitor during early measurement. ACCEPTANCE: baseline reports stored in replay/benchmark format for the representative repos.

title: B010: stratified automatic replay selection
description: Add automatic replay selection stratified by action class, duration, repo, and toolchain, so shadow/regression runs cover the distribution rather than whatever happened recently. ACCEPTANCE: selector produces stratified samples with documented coverage; used by the CI regression gate.

title: B011: divergence minimizer (smallest reproducing action/input manifest)
description: Add the divergence minimizer: given a diverging replay, extract the smallest reproducing action + input manifest (bisect inputs, shrink invocation) so incidents become tractable lab cases. ACCEPTANCE: demonstrated on a seeded synthetic divergence; output feeds the deterministic lab (Epic T).

title: B012: intent-to-green reconstruction from agent session timelines
description: Add intent-to-green reconstruction from agent session timelines: stitch invocation records into agent-visible loops (edit -> check -> test -> green) so the north-star metric (p50/p90/p95 intent-to-result over replayed real agent traces, including queueing/capture/key/lookup/transfer/execution/materialization/notification/cancellation/retries) is computable. ACCEPTANCE: intent-to-green computed for recorded RCH sessions; also feeds the likely-next-command model (Q002).

title: B013: CI regression gates against the corpus
description: Add CI regression gates against the corpus: PRs that regress wrapper SLO, p95 intent-to-result, hit rate, or divergence counts on the stratified replay sample fail. Performance gates are the enforcement of "targets are gates, not marketing": no default-on feature that violates SLOs, worsens p95 without compensation, bloats storage/transfer, degrades hit rate unexplainably, hurts cancellation/cleanup, or lacks rollback + receipt. ACCEPTANCE: gate wired into CI with baseline snapshots and override protocol.

title: B014: Layer 0 configuration pack (profiles, linkers, palette, hakari, sccache)
description: Layer 0 configuration pack (milestone M-1 core): versioned recommended Cargo/rustc profiles; -Zthreads detection + opt-in on supported nightlies (exact capability detection, never unconditional unstable flags); Wild/lld linker selection; debuginfo reduction (line-tables-only) + unpacked split-debuginfo profiles; optional Cranelift dev profile; cargo-hakari/workspace-hack setup for feature-unification stability; explicit target-CPU / Apple deployment-target / SDK baselines; canonical agent command palette (standard cargo check profile, standard nextest invocation, fixed features/target/lints, explicit doctest policy) — the palette directly reduces future key fragmentation; sccache baseline setup. Every knob independently enable/disable-able; no semantic regression in the intended lane. KILL: any knob that regresses representative p95, output equivalence, debugger behavior, or compatibility leaves the defaults.

title: B015: Layer 0 benchmark scripts + measured baseline storage
description: Layer 0 benchmark scripts + measured baseline storage: benchmark scripts for representative repos running the required scenario list; store the measured Layer-0 baseline in the replay/benchmark format so it becomes the reference point for all RABS claims. ACCEPTANCE: baseline artifacts exist for stock vs Layer-0 on at least the RCH workspace + one large external repo; wired into B008 report format.

title: C001: local wrapper protocol version handshake
description: Define the local wrapper protocol version handshake. Local UDS protocol version is distinct from ATP transport and RABS application versions; negotiate before any request; mismatch yields explicit downgrade or original-chain fallback, never silent assumption. ACCEPTANCE: handshake fixtures for match, forward-compatible, and refused cases; version registry entry (A005).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::local_protocol: LocalProtocolVersion + VersionRange (malformed min>max unconstructable) + negotiate() as a total const function — highest mutually supported version, or EXPLICIT Refused carrying both ranges so the reason is diagnosable from the receipt alone (never silent compatibility assumption; refusal pairs with PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED and fail-open to the original chain). Fixtures: match, forward-compatible N/N-1 both directions (upgraded edge/older wrapper and mirror), disjoint refusal, registry-version consistency with rabs.local-wrapper v1 (A005). 5 new tests (67 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: C002: bounded Unix-socket framing and event streaming
description: Implement bounded Unix-socket framing and event streaming for the wrapper<->edge protocol: length-bounded canonical frames; one request + ordered subscriber-delivery sequence domain; no large source content inline (object references only); decoders enforce size/count limits before allocation. ACCEPTANCE: framing fuzz target (feeds T003); frame-size boundary tests; streaming latency measured within wrapper SLO.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::framing: u32-LE length-prefixed frames with limits enforced from the 4 header bytes BEFORE any allocation (u32::MAX claim on a 5-byte buffer rejected immediately; claimed length never sizes a buffer); 1 MiB default max (bulk content rides object references per plan 182); complete-frames-only decode — every strict prefix incl. split headers is NeedMoreData, never partial delivery (the C023/C026 complete-frame counting substrate); encode-side oversize refusal; exact-boundary and back-to-back consumption tests. 6 new tests (73 lib total), clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: C003: peer-credential checks on the wrapper socket
description: Implement peer-credential checks on supported Unix platforms: SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid validation, socket ownership/mode validation, optional per-request capability token; TCP fallback is loopback-authenticated and disabled by default. WHY: the wrapper socket is the boundary between arbitrary local processes and a daemon that can schedule fleet work. ACCEPTANCE: unauthorized peer refused; tests for wrong-uid and wrong-mode sockets.

title: C004: wrapper connection timeout and circuit breaker
description: Implement wrapper connection timeout and circuit breaker: tiny bounded connect/decision timeout; on edge unavailability, run the original wrapper/tool chain immediately; circuit breaker prevents repeated per-command tax when the edge stays dead (risk R27: fail-open must not make every command pay). ACCEPTANCE: p95 added latency with dead edge is near-zero after breaker opens; breaker resets on edge recovery.

title: C005: silent/transcript/stateful-intent/stateful-commit delivery frontiers
description: Define the separate silent / transcript-exposed / stateful-commit-intent / stateful-commit delivery frontiers as wrapper-visible protocol state (I11/I43/I46). Stateful observable facts: atomically installing a Cargo-visible declared output at its live destination; replaying a rustc metadata/artifact notification after the named output is complete; returning a cached deterministic terminal failure; returning a completed cached terminal result. Ordinary diagnostics/stdout/stderr/progress are transcript-only unless a tool-specific contract makes an event state-advancing. ACCEPTANCE: frontier state machine in rabs-action with transition tests; protocol fields carry both frontiers per subscriber.
close_reason: Completed the frontier stack: A017 delivered the rabs-action state-machine half (SubscriberDeliveryState + ExposureFrontiers + fallback_class); C005 adds the wire carrier — rabs_protocol::local_protocol::SubscriberFrontierReport (both frontiers + STICKY uncertainty flags + last delivered seq) and FallbackPermission with the same dominance rule (stateful > transcript > clean; uncertainty counts as exposure, fail closed R97/R116). Cross-crate consistency test in rabs-action proves the wire report and the state machine agree on every certain combination and that each uncertainty flag maps exactly onto its certain band (no fourth band exists) — a wrapper deciding from the wire and an edge deciding from its machine can never disagree. All tests/clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: C006: pre-frontier-only fallback + labeled transcript recovery mode
description: Implement immediate original-command fallback ONLY before transcript exposure and before stateful commit intent, plus the explicitly configured LabeledTranscriptRecovery mode (detach subscription, run original chain with an unmistakable boundary marker) for post-transcript cases where exact fidelity is not required. After stateful commit intent: never uncoordinated fallback — reconnect/continue or fail coherently. WHY: silent restart after partial transcript duplicates/mixes output (R104); after stateful intent an independent local producer could mix incompatible state into Cargo's live build. ACCEPTANCE: scenario tests for all three frontier classes.

title: C007: stream stdout/stderr/JSON without whole-output buffering
description: Stream stdout/stderr/JSON without whole-output buffering: byte/line streaming with strict bounds and spill-to-object behavior for huge diagnostics (R36). Preserve line-delimited JSON framing and ordering for Cargo-consumed streams. ACCEPTANCE: memory stays bounded under adversarial 1GB-diagnostics test; ordering fixtures pass.

title: C008: preserve exact exit code and signal mapping
description: Preserve exact exit code and signal mapping through the wrapper: the terminal delivered item is the exact tool exit status; when the wrapped tool dies by signal, the wrapper restores default handling and re-signals itself with the same signal where the platform permits, rather than translating to 128+N (R94). ACCEPTANCE: exit/signal fixtures vs stock Cargo behavior including SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGSEGV children.

title: C009: stable/beta/nightly wrapper-contract CI fixture matrix
description: Add the stable/beta/nightly argv/env/JSON wrapper-contract CI matrix: fixtures pinning how each supported Cargo/rustc channel invokes wrappers (argv shapes, env, JSON diagnostics framing, artifact notifications). WHY: Cargo/rustc contract drift is a standing risk (R29); the matrix converts drift into red CI instead of production breakage. ACCEPTANCE: matrix runs in CI across three channels; recorded fixtures compared.

title: C010: wrapper overhead measurement, p95 <10ms gate
description: Measure wrapper startup and request overhead; gate p95 below 10ms before tool execution (the M0 acceptance SLO). Includes benchmark harness for wrapper cold start, UDS round trip, and decision path, wired into the corpus report (B008) and CI gate (B013). ACCEPTANCE: p95 <10ms demonstrated on target hardware; regression gate active.

title: C011: client disconnect = subscriber cancellation, shared work survives
description: Support client disconnect as subscriber cancellation without destroying shared work: UDS disconnect removes that subscriber's retained interest and closes its delivery obligation; the shared action survives while any retained interest remains (I6). A SIGKILLed wrapper is detected from UDS/PID liveness and loses only its own subscription. ACCEPTANCE: lab scenario cancel_one_subscriber_shared_action_survives passes at this layer.

title: C012: wrapper self-diagnostics and protocol compatibility output
description: Add wrapper self-diagnostics and protocol compatibility output: a wrapper diagnostic mode reporting protocol versions, edge reachability, breaker state, frontier state, and last refusal reasons in bounded JSON. ACCEPTANCE: rch rabs doctor consumes it; stable reason codes used.

title: C013: RUSTC_WRAPPER first-enable cold-rebuild warning/doctor check
description: Add RUSTC_WRAPPER first-enable cold-rebuild warning/doctor check: wrapper configuration changes Cargo fingerprints, so first enablement (or wrapper identity change) triggers a one-time rebuild; doctor detects and explains this instead of letting users interpret it as a regression. ACCEPTANCE: doctor check present; docs updated; fixture proves fingerprint change on enable.

title: C014: resumable request/subscriber tokens + edge-restart reconnect
