description: Implement resumable request/subscriber tokens and edge-restart reconnect sequencing: the wrapper holds a resumable token; on edge restart it reconnects and reports last fully accepted sequence + any possibly-in-flight frame; the edge reconciles both frontiers before resuming delivery. ACCEPTANCE: kill-edge-mid-stream fixtures resume without duplication or loss; uncertain cases fail coherently.

title: C015: wrapper-chain recursion detection + authenticated self-host bypass
description: Implement bounded wrapper-chain recursion detection and authenticated internal self-host bypass (I36/R70): detect RABS building/upgrading itself and wrapper re-entry loops; a signed/validated bypass marker executes the original chain without re-interception; arbitrary user env values cannot silently disable policy. ACCEPTANCE: recursion-depth detector fires in loop fixture; forged bypass marker rejected; RABS self-build completes.

title: C016: signal/parent-death/disconnect subscriber cancellation with exact mapping
description: Implement SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, parent-death, and UDS-disconnect subscriber cancellation with exact signal mapping: forward signals into that subscriber's cancellation state preserving signal-vs-exit classification; shared attempt cancelled only through reference-counted policy when no retained interest remains. ACCEPTANCE: signal-forwarding fixtures vs stock; parent-death (PDEATHSIG or platform equivalent) covered.

title: C017: per-subscriber bounded/spillable queues (slow-client isolation)
description: Isolate each subscriber behind a bounded/spillable queue so one slow client cannot stall shared action progress or other subscribers (R94 second half). Slow-subscriber isolation is per-subscriber backpressure with spill-to-disk, never backpressure on the canonical action stream. ACCEPTANCE: slow-subscriber test shows other subscribers and the action unaffected; memory bounded.

title: C018: uncoordinated-local-fallback telemetry + degraded storm benchmark
description: Add explicit uncoordinated-local-fallback telemetry and a degraded compile-storm benchmark (R87): when edge/coordinator are unavailable and wrappers fail open en masse, label the mode UncoordinatedLocalFallback, optionally engage a pre-existing host-local emergency limiter (without delaying the safety path), and measure workstation saturation in the storm benchmark. ACCEPTANCE: telemetry label present; degraded storm scenario in the benchmark suite.

title: C019: write-ahead stateful delivery intent + DeliveryUncertain fail-closed
description: Implement write-ahead stateful delivery intent, full-write acknowledgement, iterative sequence replay, reconnect resolution, and DeliveryUncertain fail-closed behavior (I43/R97): edge durably records stateful commit intent BEFORE the first visible rename/write or state-advancing event; wrapper acks only after complete exposure; crash in the uncertain interval forbids uncoordinated fallback and blind replay; delivery loops over many sequence items with ack after each; DeliveryComplete only after terminal item + all owned outputs. ACCEPTANCE: crash-at-every-delivery-boundary fixtures (feeds T031/T036).

title: C020: atomic materialization-rights revocation before local fallback
description: Revoke subscriber materialization rights atomically before local fallback and prove no late remote output enters the operation: fallback = detach subscription + revoke future materialization rights + discard private staging, THEN execute the original chain; a late-arriving remote result must be unable to write into the fallen-back operation's tree. ACCEPTANCE: race fixture with delayed remote output shows no write after revocation.

title: C021: transcript-only sequencing without fsync-per-line + labeled recovery
description: Implement transcript-only sequencing and the explicit labeled-recovery policy WITHOUT fsync-per-diagnostic-line (R104): TranscriptIntentRecorded means framed sequence assignment + retention in the reconnect window, not a metadata fsync per line; first fully acknowledged exposure sets TranscriptExposed; unacknowledged in-flight frames are conservatively TranscriptDeliveryUncertain. ACCEPTANCE: throughput benchmark shows no per-line durability cost; reconnect fixtures reconstruct uncertainty correctly.

title: C022: wrapper panic containment (unwind, nonprinting hook, no abort)
description: Add wrapper panic containment (I49/R105): panic=unwind for the wrapper; nonprinting pre-exposure panic hook recording internally without writing to Cargo; top-level unwind containment; before any exposure an internal panic executes the exact original wrapper/compiler chain; after exposure it fails per the applicable delivery frontier; abort-on-panic prohibited unless a separate minimal parent guard proves the same fallback; allocator abort/OOM mitigated via bounded allocation. ACCEPTANCE: injected-panic tests before/after exposure (feeds T037).

title: C023: transcript in-flight/uncertain sequencing + partial-write recovery
description: Implement transcript-intent/in-flight/uncertain sequencing and partial-write recovery (R116): the wrapper accepts only complete length-bounded frames; on reconnect reports last fully exposed sequence AND any frame whose write may have begun; if both wrapper and edge died, the Cargo command has failed and a later invocation starts a NEW BuildOperation rather than replaying an unknowable partial transcript. ACCEPTANCE: partial-frame crash fixtures resolve to the correct uncertainty state.

title: C024: re-signal wrapper on child signal termination, differential vs stock
description: Preserve Unix signal termination by re-signalling the wrapper where supported; test against stock Cargo: when the wrapped tool is signal-terminated, the wrapper restores default disposition and kills itself with the same signal so Cargo observes identical semantics. ACCEPTANCE: differential fixtures vs stock for SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL(child)/SIGSEGV.

title: C025: edge boot/incarnation/handoff fencing for live wrapper resumption
description: Define and fence edge boot/incarnation/handoff state for live wrapper resumption (R118): edge restart advances a durable boot generation + fresh incarnation; exactly one incarnation owns subscriber/materialization rights per boot generation EXCEPT during a bounded explicit handoff — successor presents a coordinator-authorized handoff token naming the predecessor/session set, both report delivery frontiers during reconciliation, predecessor is fenced before the successor becomes sole owner; arbitrary multi-incarnation overlap forbidden. ACCEPTANCE: EdgeIncarnationFenceRecord schema + overlap-rejection tests.

title: C026: complete-frame transcript ack/resume wire realization
description: Implement complete-frame transcript acknowledgement/resume with last-accepted and possibly-in-flight sequence reporting, without per-line fsync — the concrete wire realization of C021/C023 in the local protocol (SubscriberTranscriptIntent/Acknowledged/DeliveryUncertain messages mirrored locally). ACCEPTANCE: protocol fixtures across wrapper/edge versions and daemon-death points (the M0/T046 matrix).

title: D001: fixed workspace path + stable logical path-dependency repo IDs
description: Define the primary-workspace fixed path (/__rabs/workspace — safe because every sandbox is isolated) and stable logical IDs for additional path-dependency repositories (/__rabs/repos/LOGICAL-REPO-ID). Logical repo IDs derive from Cargo/package source identity or a project-configured stable UUID plus closure role — NEVER solely from a mutable git remote URL, local checkout path, branch, or current commit; collision/alias resolution is explicit in the repository-closure manifest. WHY: identical work in different worktrees must resolve to identical canonical paths or keys fragment (I1). ACCEPTANCE: ID derivation spec + tests covering renamed remotes, moved checkouts, and aliased repos.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_key::canonical_layout (D001; I1; plan sec 55; R1): WORKSPACE_ROOT fixed at /__rabs/workspace (safe under per-sandbox isolation); logical_repo_id derives /__rabs/repos/<id> from STABLE identity only — CargoSourceId (lockfile-resolved source id) or ConfiguredUuid, plus closure role, digested under rabs.logical-repo-id.v1. The acceptance's three mutations (renamed remote, moved checkout, advanced branch/commit) are UNREPRESENTABLE by construction: the derivation has no parameter for URL/path/branch/commit — tested via two agents with arbitrary local state producing byte-identical canonical paths. Distinctness: different sources fork, one source under two closure roles gets two IDs, and identity KIND participates (a UUID textually equal to a source id is a different identity — no cross-kind aliasing). Alias/collision resolution explicit per the bead: validate_closure_manifest returns typed DuplicateEntry/IdCollision naming the ID — never silent last-writer-wins. 4 tests (118 key lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Anchors I1 for the whole D-series path-normalization chain.

title: D002: canonical visible path layout + hidden backing-path policy
description: Define the canonical visible path layout and the hidden backing-path policy (I20): visible = /__rabs/{workspace, repos, registry/CHECKSUM, git/CHECKSUM, toolchain, cargo-home, out/UNIT, build/UNIT/out, incremental/UNIT, tmp, home} + /run/rabs-secrets/SLOT; hidden physical backing dirs MAY contain operation/action/attempt/snapshot IDs and random staging names because a mount namespace/chroot/VM hides them — but they must never leak into CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, OUT_DIR, TMPDIR, compiler args, generated source, dep-info, debuginfo, or any program-visible path (risk R42). ACCEPTANCE: layout spec doc + constants in rabs-sandbox; leak scanner (D012) enforces.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_sandbox::layout (D002; I1/I20; plan sec 55; R42): the canonical visible layout as pinned constants — the bead enumeration verbatim (/__rabs/{workspace,repos,registry,git,toolchain,cargo-home,out,build,incremental,tmp,home} + /run/rabs-secrets), asserted byte-for-byte by test with the exactly-two-namespaces rule. Hidden backing-path policy: PROGRAM_VISIBLE_SURFACES enumerates the R42 enforcement surfaces (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, OUT_DIR, TMPDIR, compiler args, generated source, dep-info, debuginfo, readback paths — coverage tested against the bead list); leaks_backing_path is the pure substring leak primitive the D012 scanner enforces with — proven to catch a physical staging root (with attempt IDs) embedded in env values, --remap-path-prefix flags, and JSON, while clean canonical values pass. is_visible_path is prefix-correct (/__rabs-evil and /__rabs/workspacex rejected). First real module in rabs-sandbox; 4 tests; clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. D012 (scanner over real surfaces) enforces the policy at runtime.

title: D003: Linux canonical Cargo-driver namespace + nested action-view materializer
description: Implement the Linux canonical Cargo-driver mount namespace and the nested per-action closed-view materializer: a canonical namespace per command (or compatible command group) in which the Cargo PROCESS itself runs; nested finer per-action mount views where a closed input view is required. Preferred stack: read-only snapshot/reflink/overlay lower layers; stable visible mounts; default-deny network namespace; pid/user/mount namespaces + controlled /proc; cgroup v2 envelope; seccomp/Landlock/bubblewrap per measured host support; deterministic hostname/locale/timezone; openat2-style path-escape defenses; small audited privileged helper only where unavoidable (ledgered per A011). WHY: I19 — Cargo creates path-sensitive unit identities BEFORE wrappers run; only canonical Cargo launch erases that divergence. ACCEPTANCE: canonical namespace boots Cargo on a fixture workspace; StrictHermeticLinux profile proves its documented boundary.

title: D004: mount immutable source snapshot read-only
description: Mount the immutable source snapshot read-only in the canonical namespace: the coherent command snapshot is materialized as an immutable lower layer; the build cannot mutate source; mutation attempts surface as errors, not silent divergence. ACCEPTANCE: write-to-source attempt fails inside sandbox; snapshot identity bound into provenance.

title: D005: canonical toolchain/sysroot/registry/git/output/temp mounts
description: Mount canonical toolchain, sysroot, registry, git-source, output, and temp roots at their stable visible paths. Toolchains are immutable ATP DatasetObjects mounted at /__rabs/toolchain — a stable path, never a digest-bearing program-visible path (digests would fragment keys and leak identity). ACCEPTANCE: rustc -vV and --print sysroot report canonical paths; registry/git sources resolve at checksum paths.

title: D006: stable logical OUT_DIR/incremental/temp/home/secret mappings
description: Implement stable logical OUT_DIR, incremental, temp, home, and secret-slot mappings: Cargo's exact requested OUT_DIR is authoritative and maps to hidden private backing storage; /__rabs/build/UNIT/out is valid ONLY when the canonical driver configured Cargo to produce that path before planning (a wrapper may not substitute a different OUT_DIR after Cargo selected unit hashes); TMPDIR=/__rabs/tmp per namespace; HOME=/__rabs/home; secrets at /run/rabs-secrets/SLOT. Logical unit IDs are stable across equivalent worktrees and exclude current source content unless Cargo's semantics require otherwise. ACCEPTANCE: OUT_DIR-embedding build script produces identical bytes across two worktrees.

title: D007: path-remap flag injection by toolchain capability
description: Implement path-remap flag injection by toolchain capability (--remap-path-prefix / trim-paths where supported). Remapping SUPPLEMENTS canonical execution — it is never a substitute, because remap flags cannot fix Cargo-side unit identity or runtime-visible paths. ACCEPTANCE: capability detection per toolchain; remap applied only where supported; differential fixtures show debuginfo paths remapped.

title: D008: virtual-to-real JSON diagnostic rewriting
description: Implement virtual-to-real JSON diagnostic rewriting: each edge maintains a subscriber-specific canonical-virtual-path -> requesting-worktree-path mapping applied to canonical structured compiler events, rendered diagnostics, and rch why output. Distinctions that must hold: the rustc artifact-notification path replayed to Cargo is the EXACT output path Cargo requested; Cargo's outward compiler-artifact message is a different Cargo-generated event and is never synthesized by RABS; a semantic result serves multiple subscribers only when translation is complete and safe, else presentation variant or bypass; raw stored provenance uses canonical paths + a redacted mapping receipt. ACCEPTANCE: rewriting fixtures across two worktrees; unsafe-translation bypass path covered.

title: D009: dep-info path rewriting/materialization for Cargo freshness
description: Implement dep-info path rewriting/materialization for Cargo: dep-info materialized for Cargo is rewritten coherently to the live Cargo path model and mtime/checksum policy; RABS never mutates immutable CAS inodes to adjust mtimes. ACCEPTANCE: cargo build after a served hit shows correct freshness (no spurious rebuild) across two worktrees.

title: D010: mtime choreography and repeated-hit tests
description: Implement mtime choreography and repeated-hit tests (risk R6): outputs become newer than relevant inputs from Cargo's perspective; a result bundle includes matching incremental snapshot where supported; repeated hits do not induce rebuild storms; atomic rename prevents partially materialized target trees; future/skewed source mtimes that cannot be represented coherently force validated checksum freshness or serving bypass rather than guessing. ACCEPTANCE: hit -> immediate rebuild test shows zero recompilation; skewed-mtime fixture bypasses correctly.

title: D011: cross-worktree descriptor/output equality test suite
description: Build the cross-worktree descriptor/output equality test suite: two (then N) worktrees of the same source run the same canonical command; compare normalized descriptors AND Cargo child argv, -C metadata values, output filenames, .rmeta bytes, dep-info, and selected binary sections. This is the M1 acceptance harness. ACCEPTANCE: suite green on fixture workspaces; any divergence produces a classified leak finding.

title: D012: path leak scanner for outputs and metadata
description: Build the path leak scanner for outputs and metadata: scan artifacts, metadata, compiler events, generated source, and dep-info for actual worktree roots, user homes, worker temp/CAS roots, hidden physical operation/action/attempt/snapshot paths, hostnames, usernames, actual target/build dirs, secret mount backing paths, and divergent Cargo metadata hashes. Distinguish debug-only from loadable/runtime-visible references; classify findings: admitted-canonical (BuildPathSemanticPolicy), presentation-only translated, remappable debug metadata, key-relevant semantic leakage, output-semantic path sensitivity, privacy/secret incident, or evidence Cargo was not actually launched canonically. Ambiguous loadable-data leakage loses portable authority -> path-preserving lane. ACCEPTANCE: scanner catches seeded leaks of every class.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_sandbox::leak_scanner (D012; I20; plan sec 58; R42; enforces the D002 policy with its leaks_backing_path primitive): scan_surface over the seven program surfaces (loadable artifacts, debug metadata, compiler events, generated source, dep-info, presentation transcripts, Cargo metadata hashes) against the hidden world (worktree roots, user homes, staging/CAS roots, host/user identities, secret BACKING paths). All seven finding classes per the bead, surface-sensitive: secret backing paths are ALWAYS PrivacySecretIncident; identities are privacy on loadable surfaces but remappable in debug metadata and presentation-only in transcripts (tested per surface); path leaks classify OutputSemanticPathSensitivity (loadable) / RemappableDebugMetadata / PresentationOnlyTranslated / KeyRelevantSemanticLeakage (dep-info, generated source, events); unverified canonical launch on the metadata-hash surface yields NonCanonicalLaunchEvidence independent of pattern matches. disposition() folds worst-first: Incident > PathPreservingLane (the D030 routing rule — ambiguous loadable/key-relevant leakage LOSES portable authority, never a canonical hit) > RemapThenShare > CanonicalAuthorityHolds — all four exercised, incident dominance over mixed findings tested. Acceptance: seeded leaks of every class caught (one fixture per class + clean-canonical negatives). During development the incident-dominance rule fired on a conflated fixture (username embedded in the worktree path) — the scanner was right; the fixture was made disjoint. 3 tests (12 sandbox lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: D013: macOS canonical process root via VM/chroot helper
description: Implement and prove a macOS canonical process root via a validated privileged chroot/sandbox helper with APFS-clone backing or a lightweight Virtualization.framework VM. APFS clones alone are NOT sufficient: they give efficient data copies but do not give many concurrent processes the same canonical visible absolute path (risk R47). ACCEPTANCE: two concurrent macOS actions observe identical canonical roots; helper is in the unsafe-boundary ledger; authority tier recorded per A015.

title: D014: platform-specific portability classes
description: Define platform-specific portability classes: which (platform, isolation profile, filesystem semantic class, SDK/ABI) combinations may share results, per the authority matrix. Unsupported properties reduce authority explicitly; no optimistic parity labels (I25/I28/R37). ACCEPTANCE: machine-readable class table consumed by serving policy + scheduler hard exclusions.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::portability (D014; I25/I28; plan sec 65; R37): may_share(producer PlatformFacts, consumer PlatformFacts, scope) -> Shareable | ExcludedHard{reason} — the machine-readable decision serving policy and the scheduler both consume (every ExcludedHard is a hard placement exclusion). Checks in order: (1) platform families NEVER share by analogy — cross-platform is a hard exclusion, no optimistic parity labels (tested Linux vs macOS with identical-looking facts); (2) the A005 authority matrix governs the producing profile per scope — ShadowOnly/NotAuthorized excludes carrying the matrix's own boundary text (tested: host-audit workspace serving surfaces the NO-authoritative-shared-workspace wording); (3) producer/consumer profile equality (strict consumer cannot take volatile output — tested); (4) D022 filesystem semantic class exact equality; (5) SDK/ABI class exact equality with UNKNOWN reducing authority explicitly (None excludes with a named reason, never silently passes — tested). Matching strict-Linux facts share cross-machine. 5 tests (112 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: D015: checksum-freshness opt-in and differential tests
description: Add the checksum-freshness opt-in and differential tests: where nightly Cargo supports checksum-based freshness, provide an opt-in profile, validate thoroughly, and design materialization to absorb stable checksum freshness later without changing CAS semantics. ACCEPTANCE: differential suite comparing mtime vs checksum freshness behavior on hits/rebuilds.

title: D016: symlink/xattr/permission policy tests
description: Add symlink/xattr/permission policy tests: object profiles define which metadata is retained (executable bits, symlink targets byte-preserved, xattrs/ACLs only via explicit profile); materialization verifies platform-critical metadata (code-signature-preserving xattrs, SDK attributes). ACCEPTANCE: fixtures for symlinked sources, executable outputs, xattr-carrying toolchains.

title: D017: canonical pseudo-files, hostname/locale/timezone setup
description: Add canonical pseudo-files and hostname/locale/timezone setup: deterministic hostname, fixed UTF-8 locale, TZ=UTC, approved pseudo-file and device allowlist, controlled /proc view. ACCEPTANCE: sandboxed probe program observes only canonical values; violations classified per effect class.

title: D018: coherent snapshot capture with mutation retry + path-dep closure
description: Implement coherent snapshot capture with mutation detection/retry and path-dependency closure (I2): resolve workspace, lockfile, .cargo configuration, toolchain files, and the path-dependency closure; include policy-relevant untracked files and symlink structure; exclude ephemeral locks and mutable build outputs; prefer filesystem snapshot/reflink primitives, else directory-generation watcher + at least two stable scans reading each file through an open descriptor, hashing bytes, verifying identity/size/metadata before and after; RETRY the entire capture on any watched mutation, directory-set change, inode replacement, symlink change, or metadata inconsistency; refuse authoritative snapshotting where a coherent boundary cannot be established; hide .git unless a canonical git-state object is declared; bind snapshot root + filesystem semantic class into provenance and every child action request. ACCEPTANCE: concurrent-mutation fuzz (E023/T018) forces retry, never a mixed snapshot.

title: D019: verify Cargo -C metadata/unit-hash/argv convergence across worktrees
description: Verify Cargo-generated -C metadata, unit hashes, output names, and child argv converge across worktrees under the canonical driver — the direct falsification test for risk R43 (Cargo running outside the canonical namespace produces path-sensitive unit identity divergence before any wrapper can help). ACCEPTANCE: automated comparison in the D011 suite across 2+ worktrees and 2+ machines in the same platform class.

title: D020: invariant test — no visible path contains action/attempt/snapshot IDs
description: Add the invariant test that no visible path contains an action, attempt, operation, or snapshot ID (I20/R42): sweep every program-visible surface (env, argv, mounted paths, outputs, dep-info, debuginfo) for hidden-identity patterns. ACCEPTANCE: test red when a seeded attempt-ID leaks into any visible path.
close_reason: Implemented rabs-sandbox/tests/visible_path_identity.rs (D020; I20; R42): the invariant tripwire over the D002 layout. Positive half: every program-visible surface the sandbox constructs (CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, OUT_DIR, TMPDIR, HOME, CARGO_HOME, argv out-dir/incremental, dep-info paths) plus every fixed visible root sweeps clean against hidden-identity patterns (attempt/operation/action/snapshot IDs) when unit segments are LOGICAL names. Acceptance red case: seeding an attempt ID as a unit name makes the sweep catch it on every unit-derived surface (>=2 catches asserted), with a companion assertion that any surface embedding the ID but escaping the sweep FAILS the test — sweep coverage cannot silently narrow; the suite also pins the D002 PROGRAM_VISIBLE_SURFACES list length as the coupling to the enforcement surface set. 2 tests (3 suites green in crate); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: D021: macOS VM/chroot and host-audit differential authority tests
description: Add macOS VM/chroot and host-audit differential authority tests: prove the macOS strict profile's claimed boundary and prove host-audit mode is correctly limited (selected immutable deps only; no authoritative shared workspace; no cross-machine publication). ACCEPTANCE: differential runs on both modes classify authority correctly; false-parity attempts fail.

title: D022: filesystem semantic classes defined and keyed
description: Define and key filesystem semantic classes (R71): case sensitivity, Unicode normalization, symlink and hardlink semantics, executable-bit/permission behavior, exposed xattr/ACL policy. Default: require class equality for actions that can observe namespace behavior; omission requires proof the action cannot distinguish. ACCEPTANCE: class detection per worker/filesystem; keyed into OutputPlatformContract by default; differential case/Unicode/symlink fixtures.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_key::filesystem_class (D022; plan sec 65; R71): FilesystemSemanticClass over the five observable dimensions (case sensitivity incl. preserving-vs-folding, Unicode normalization, symlink + hardlink semantics, permission/exec-bit behavior, xattr/ACL exposure) with keying_string() feeding the F008 filesystem_semantic_class slot. Acceptance: differential case/Unicode/symlink fixtures — every dimension changed in isolation forks the class (all six tested); keyed BY DEFAULT via ClassKeying::Keyed, and the ONLY omission arm requires a named registered proof that the action cannot observe namespace behavior (unproven omission unrepresentable; discriminant tags prevent a proof string colliding with a class string — tested). STRICT_LINUX_PRESENTED pinned as the fleet presentation contract: two workers with different backing stores presenting the same class key identically — presentation, not the host filesystem, is the sharing contract. 3 tests (121 key lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Honest boundary: per-worker runtime DETECTION probes land with the worker beads; this bead delivers the class definition + keying as the pure core.

title: D023: prohibit writable CAS hardlinks + inode-alias corruption tests
description: Prohibit writable CAS hardlinks and add inode-alias corruption tests (I33/R65): RABS never materializes a writable hardlink to an immutable CAS inode; mutable target/OUT_DIR/temp/incremental state uses private copies, CoW reflinks, or read-only binds; if a reflink implementation can mutate shared metadata/content it is unsupported and falls back to copy; mtime changes apply only to private materializations. ACCEPTANCE: alias-mutation test proves CAS digest never changes after materialization mutation attempts.

title: D024: exclusive/private mutable target-state leases + whole-command cloning
description: Implement exclusive/private mutable target-state leases and whole-command target cloning (I35/R67): no two unrelated Cargo operations concurrently mutate one target/build/incremental directory; whole-command hot worker state is exclusively leased (TargetStateLease) or cloned into a private operation root before mutation; fine-grained reuse flows only through immutable CAS objects. ACCEPTANCE: overlapping-operation test shows serialization or private cloning, never shared mutation.

title: D025: build-script OUT_DIR binding + pre/post-state replacement semantics
description: Bind build-script actions to Cargo-provided OUT_DIR plus pre-state/post-state replacement semantics: BuildScriptRun models the pre-run OUT_DIR/output-cache state when observable; replay installs the complete captured post-state including deletions into a clean private directory and atomically swaps — never merges into a stale OUT_DIR (R66). The Cargo-generated visible path is authoritative; RABS maps it to hidden backing storage. ACCEPTANCE: ghost-file and deletion fixtures show replay equals a clean run.

title: D026: canonical process-context capture (stat/umask/rlimits/CPU/FDs/argv0)
description: Capture or canonicalize stat/metadata, umask, rlimits, CPU-count/affinity, argv0/cwd, and inherited-FD semantics (R78): host introspection that can alter outputs (uname, CPUID, sysctl, /proc, loader config, pkg-config/SDK discovery, file metadata probes) is supplied from a canonical toolchain/platform view or captured as an explicit semantic input; unapproved inherited FDs closed before spawn; approved descriptors (local jobserver) capability-scoped and excluded from semantic identity only when proven output-neutral. ACCEPTANCE: system-context differential fixtures (T024).

title: D027: runtime-visible canonical-path portability scanner
description: Add the runtime-visible canonical-path portability scanner (R84): embedded canonical absolute paths are not automatically safe — runtime-visible strings are semantic, and code that later OPENS CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/OUT_DIR/another build-time path is RuntimePathSensitive unless the project packages the resource or guarantees the canonical runtime mount; classify and route to local-only where needed. ACCEPTANCE: fixture binary opening /__rabs/... at runtime is detected and classified.

title: D028: canonical dep-info + byte-correct subscriber derivation + bypass
description: Implement canonical dep-info storage plus byte-correct subscriber-specific derivation with bypass-on-unsafe-rewrite (I39/R85): the shared result stores CANONICAL dep-info; each edge derives a subscriber-specific dep-info file with exact Makefile escaping/path semantics under a versioned derivation contract, records the derivation + digest, installs it privately; derived real-path dep-info is never the canonical CAS object nor a semantic dependency artifact; unprovable lossless rewriting bypasses the hit. ACCEPTANCE: escaping edge cases (spaces, colons, non-UTF8) round-trip; bypass triggers on unsupported format.

title: D029: edge content-identity index, digest singleflight, rehash audit
description: Implement the edge content-identity index, digest singleflight, watcher-overflow detection, and periodic rehash audit (R83): full rehash of everything per command violates the miss SLO, so the edge maintains a durable per-filesystem index. Safe reuse sources strongest-first: RABS materialization receipt binding an immutable file to an object ID; real fs snapshot + proven stable file identity/version primitive; open-descriptor stat/version checks + no-overflow mutation journal; full rehash otherwise. Mtime/size alone are NEVER content authority; watcher overflow, rename ambiguity, coarse timestamps, network filesystems, index corruption, or audit mismatch force bounded rescan/rehash or reduced authority; sampled/full audits verify reused identities; snapshot manifests structurally share unchanged subtrees. ACCEPTANCE: overflow + memoization-miss fixtures (T027) force rehash; audit catches seeded stale entries.

title: D030: BuildPathSemanticPolicy + original-vs-canonical differentials + preserving lane
description: Implement BuildPathSemanticPolicy, original-vs-canonical differential fixtures, and the path-preserving lane (I41/R96): per-workspace-action policy = CanonicalPortablePath | PathOpaqueVerified | ProjectRelativeRemapped | SubscriberPathPreserving; default for a new family is shadow/audit; file!(), env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR), OUT_DIR-derived strings, panic locations, embedded source maps, runtime resource lookup, and path-asserting tests are the canonical hazards; unsafe/ambiguous remapping routes to the path-preserving/local lane rather than a canonical shared hit; the policy is part of descriptor + key breakdown. ACCEPTANCE: differential fixtures where original-path and canonical builds differ observably route to the preserving lane (T030).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_key::path_policy (D030; I41; plan sec 59; R96; T030): BuildPathSemanticPolicy (CanonicalPortablePath/PathOpaqueVerified/ProjectRelativeRemapped/SubscriberPathPreserving, wire-stable tags 1-4) + decide_lane routing + policy_component_digest for the keyed descriptor slot (four distinct digests under rabs.path-policy.v1 — two subscribers under different policies are different actions). T030 acceptance: an observable original-vs-canonical differential DEMOTES every shared policy to the preserving lane with shadow audit — never a canonical hit — and AMBIGUITY is treated exactly like a difference (both tested across all three shared policies). New families default to shadow/audit even with clean evidence (promotion is a policy decision, not an inference — tested); clean differentials serve the configured shared lane; explicitly-preserving families need no shadow. The plan's seven canonical path hazards (file!(), env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR), OUT_DIR strings, panic locations, source maps, runtime resource lookup, path-asserting tests) pinned verbatim as the differential runner's checklist. 5 tests (130 key lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Honest boundary: the differential RUNNER producing the evidence lands with B005/L-series; this bead delivers policy, routing, keying, and the hazard checklist.

title: D031: per-build destination reservations + disjoint-bundle concurrency
description: Implement per-build destination-path reservations and disjoint-bundle materialization concurrency (I45/R98): a per-operation destination arbiter reserves every declared output path before installation; disjoint bundles install concurrently; overlapping paths, parent-directory replacement, or undeclared writes serialize, bypass, or fail coherently; installation is atomic per owned file/subtree/bundle (a complete owned tree like one build script's OUT_DIR may swap atomically) — never by swapping an unrelated shared target root. ACCEPTANCE: two-bundle overlap fixture serializes; disjoint fixtures run concurrently (T031).

title: D032: requested->resolved snapshot lineage for Cargo resolution mutation
description: Implement requested->resolved execution snapshot lineage for Cargo fetch/resolution/lockfile mutation (I53/R110): Cargo resolution runs from RequestedCommandSnapshot against a private writable overlay; before the first resolution-dependent compile action the edge seals ResolvedExecutionSnapshot (derived lockfile/config/source-selection state); every fine-grained action names exactly one sealed generation; post-seal mutation forces reseal/replan or downgrade; lockfile replay to the worktree uses content preconditions and never retroactively changes snapshot identity of already-run actions. ACCEPTANCE: mutation-mid-command fixtures (T041) show reseal or coherent downgrade, never mixed state.

title: E001: sandbox profile schema by ActionClass (+ class/purpose separation)
description: Define the sandbox profile schema by ActionClass. Every action class (CargoWholeCommandBounded, RustcDependencyCompile, RustcWorkspaceCompile, RustdocCompile, Link, BuildScriptCompile, BuildScriptRun, NativeCompileC/Cxx, NativeArchive, BindgenGeneration, CodeGeneratorRun, NextestTestCase, TestBinaryBatch, DoctestCompile/Run, ClippyCompile, BenchmarkCompile/Run, ToolchainProbe, WorkerProbe) has a policy record: local-cache/remote-exec/deterministic-failure/speculation/hedge eligibility; required isolation + input-observation profile; declared/observed/negative input rules; output + side-effect declarations; exact presented-environment policy; network/secret policy; default budget + resource class; provisional-output allowance; verification/publication evidence requirements. NOTE: Speculative/GitPrewarm/CIRequired/DeterminismAudit/CacheVerification/AdministrativeRepair are NOT action classes (they would fragment identical work) — they are SubscriberKind/AttemptPurpose. ACCEPTANCE: schema + per-class records in the registry; identical speculative/foreground compiles produce the same key.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::class_policy (E001; plan sec 15/71; I23/I24 at policy level): ActionClassPolicy schema + CLASS_POLICY_REGISTRY with one record per ALL 21 action classes (totality test: exactly one record each; new class cannot ship without a policy decision). Record covers the bead list: local-cache/remote-exec/deterministic-failure/speculation/hedge eligibility, required IsolationProfile, NetworkPolicy (DenyAll/LoopbackOnly/AmbientVolatile), SecretPolicy (NonePresented/OpaqueDigestOnly via F006), provisional-output allowance, ResourceClass budget tier, min TrustEvidenceTier for publication. Class/purpose separation per acceptance: the registry is keyed by ActionClass ALONE — no SubscriberKind/purpose field is representable (destructure tripwire test), so identical speculative and foreground compiles consult one record and (per descriptor tests) share one key. Cross-cutting consistency tests: provisional outputs only on rustc compile classes (.rmeta pipelining concept); every remote-exec class requires StrictHermeticLinux and non-ambient network; BenchmarkRun fully volatile-local; BuildScriptRun never speculated, secrets opaque-only, cacheable under strict isolation. Defaults encode the plan; per-fleet overrides layer in D-series without schema change. 5 tests (95 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: E002: default-deny network namespace on Linux
description: Implement the default-deny network namespace on Linux: no network for sandboxed actions unless an explicit OpenNetwork capability applies (captured-fetch pattern). ACCEPTANCE: network attempt inside a hermetic action fails and is recorded as a NetworkSensitive observation.

title: E003: scrubbed/fixed environment builder (exact, hashed, never traced)
description: Implement the scrubbed/fixed environment builder: construct the COMPLETE minimal environment presented to each action (exact allowlist, canonical PATH, fixed locale/TZ/hostname/user/home where enforceable), hash every presented key/value AND relevant absences. Environment soundness never depends on discovering getenv calls (I21/R45 — env reads happen from process memory; tracers cannot see them). ACCEPTANCE: env mutation outside the allowlist provably cannot affect the sandbox; presented-env digest changes iff a semantic variable changes.

title: E004: cgroup v2 resource envelope setup
description: Implement cgroup v2 resource envelope setup per action attempt: CPU/memory/IO bounds from the resource envelope, and the cgroup doubles as the ultimate descendant-containment boundary for StrictHermeticLinux (with E029). ACCEPTANCE: envelope enforced in fixture; OOM inside the cgroup classified OomKilled (never a deterministic failure).

title: E005: filesystem read/write/exec observation prototype + overhead benchmark
description: Implement the filesystem read/write/exec observation prototype and benchmark its overhead: Linux candidates eBPF, fanotify, ptrace, seccomp-notify, Landlock + namespace enforcement in measured combinations. WHY: observation cost lands on the miss path, which carries the <1-2% overhead SLO — the mechanism must be chosen by measurement, not preference. ACCEPTANCE: overhead report per mechanism on representative compiles; chosen default documented with numbers.

title: E006: parse rustc dep-info into canonical input identities
description: Parse rustc dep-info into canonical input identities: map dep-info paths through the canonical layout to content identities; dep-info is EVIDENCE, not a security boundary (proc macros/build scripts read files dep-info never mentions). ACCEPTANCE: parser handles escaping edge cases; outputs canonical virtual paths + object IDs.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_key::dep_info (E006; plan sec 72; R12): parse_dep_info(content, virtualize, identify) -> DepInfoEvidence with canonical virtual paths + ObjectIds. Escaping edge cases per the rustc emitter proven in one acceptance fixture: backslash-space, backslash-hash, double-backslash, double-dollar, and trailing-backslash line continuation all round-trip; unescaped-space splitting is escape-aware. Phony per-source lines contribute nothing; cross-rule duplicates collapse; comment/blank lines skipped. Unmappable path (outside canonical layout) and unidentifiable path are typed HARD errors — silent drops impossible. The evidence-not-boundary rule is carried in the TYPE NAME (DepInfoEvidence, never Closure/Manifest — pinned by test) and rustdoc: proc macros/build scripts read files dep-info never mentions; entries feed observed-input cross-checks (E011), never completeness claims. Pure via caller-supplied virtualizer + identity lookup (A002). 4 tests (110 key lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: E007: binary-dependency dep-info integration
description: Integrate binary-dependency dep-info where available (rustc's binary dep-info emission): additional evidence for proc-macro/host-tool dependencies. ACCEPTANCE: binary dep-info merged into observed evidence when the toolchain supports it; absence handled gracefully.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_key::binary_dep_info (E007; plan sec 72; extends E006): merge_dep_info folds rustc's -Zbinary-dep-depinfo output into the E006 textual evidence. Acceptance both halves: (1) binary entries merge classified as BinaryArtifact evidence — the proc-macro dylib and rlib the textual stream never mentions surface (tested), deduplicated by path with the artifact class winning as the stronger fact; (2) absence is GRACEFUL: toolchains without the flag get a textual-only merge with an explicit NotEmitted support marker — no error, and no fabricated claim of binary coverage (tested). Artifact classification is a class-tag heuristic only (identity always content digests); parse errors in the binary stream propagate as hard errors per the E006 no-silent-drop rule (tested). 3 tests (137 key lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: E008: subprocess/tool invocation graph capture
description: Capture the subprocess/tool invocation graph: which executables an action spawned, how they were selected (PATH lookup order, misses = negative deps), and their content identities. ACCEPTANCE: nested tool fixture (build script spawning cc spawning as/ld) yields the full graph.

title: E009: network/git/hostname detection; clock/randomness per-profile classification
description: Detect network/git/hostname effects where enforceable and classify clock/randomness according to the isolation profile WITHOUT assuming syscall tracing is complete: clock_gettime may use vDSO; entropy arrives through several interfaces; FSEvents/inotify observe changes not reads. A strict profile must virtualize or deny those surfaces through a validated mechanism, else the action is classified ClockSensitive/RandomnessSensitive/etc. and loses shared authority (R46). ACCEPTANCE: probe programs using vDSO time and getrandom are correctly classified under each profile.

title: E010: positive/negative/environment/isolation-evidence schemas
description: Define the positive input, negative dependency, exact presented-environment, and isolation-evidence schemas: ActionInputManifest (positive only: virtual path + object identity, file type/exec bit/semantic metadata, symlink target + resolution chain, declared directories + enumeration results, approved generated/toolchain objects); NegativeDependencySet (failed opens, missing paths, directory listings/globs, PATH lookup misses + selected executable, missing symlink targets); PresentedEnvironment (sole owner of env presence/absence — never duplicated into the filesystem sets, F027); IsolationEvidenceRecord (what was ACTUALLY enforced — profiles record enforcement, not aspiration). ACCEPTANCE: schemas versioned; property tests that the three input categories are disjoint.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::input_evidence (E010; I3 input closure; F027 single-owner; plan sec 72; R12/R13): the four versioned schemas (INPUT_EVIDENCE_SCHEMA_VERSION=1). ActionInputManifest — positive ONLY: PositiveInput (virtual path, ObjectId, file type, exec bit, full symlink resolution chain), DirectoryEnumeration (declared dirs WITH observed listings), approved generated/toolchain objects. NegativeDependencySet — absences: FailedOpen, MissingPath, GlobResult (empty match set is a FACT distinct from never-globbed, tested), PathLookupMiss (probed-absent dirs; the selected executable lives positively in F006's PATH manifest), MissingSymlinkTarget. Disjointness proven structurally per acceptance: every positive row carries an ObjectId by construction while NO negative variant can (exhaustive match — absences have no bytes); env presence/absence is UNREPRESENTABLE in both filesystem sets (no env field exists; destructure tripwire forces the F027 decision on any addition; PresentedEnvironment in rabs-key F006 is sole owner). IsolationEvidenceRecord — enforcement not aspiration: per-control Enforced{mechanism}/NotEnforced{reason}; one unenforced control = not fully_enforced, loudly (tested). 5 tests (90 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Unblocks E006/E020 chains; fills the action_inputs/negative_dependencies descriptor slots' schema.

title: E011: first-run discovery and recipe persistence
description: Implement first-run discovery and recipe persistence: first-seen action families execute in nonserving discovery mode against the conservative broad read-only snapshot, capturing dep-info, successful+failed opens, enumerations, symlink resolution, subprocess/tool selection, network attempts, output writes; produce positive inputs, negative deps, volatility evidence, final descriptor; recompute the final key; store the ObservedInputRecipe by ActionFamilyKey + recipe epoch. Broad-snapshot discovery output is a CANDIDATE, not automatically authoritative. ACCEPTANCE: discovery of a proc-macro-using crate produces a complete recipe; recipe reload reconstructs the same final key on unchanged inputs.

title: E012: recipe reuse, validation, re-discovery on drift
description: Implement recipe reuse, validation, and re-discovery on drift: subsequent executions load the recipe, resolve/hash known positive+negative inputs from the new coherent snapshot, construct the final key directly, and look up; recipes are optimization hints, never trust anchors — a recipe cannot authorize serving without the final input-complete key + compatible trust evidence; observed drift (new read, changed enumeration) aborts and re-enters discovery (R38). ACCEPTANCE: drift fixture (new include file) triggers re-discovery, not a stale hit.

title: E013: volatility classification and reason codes
description: Implement volatility classification and reason codes: assign effect classes (Hermetic, HermeticWithCapabilities, ObservedStable, PathSensitive, HostIdentitySensitive, ClockSensitive, RandomnessSensitive, GitStateSensitive, NetworkSensitive, SecretSensitive, SideEffecting, Nondeterministic, Unclosable) with stable SANDBOX_*/INPUT_* reason codes so rch why can explain every refusal. ACCEPTANCE: classifier fixtures for each class; codes in the registry (A006).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::volatility (E013; plan sec 73; R14): the thirteen effect classes (Hermetic/HermeticWithCapabilities/ObservedStable/PathSensitive/HostIdentitySensitive/ClockSensitive/RandomnessSensitive/GitStateSensitive/NetworkSensitive/SecretSensitive/SideEffecting/Nondeterministic/Unclosable) with classify(ObservedEffects) and stable SANDBOX_*/INPUT_* reason codes so rch why can explain every refusal. Conservative rules with teeth: the WORST observed fact decides (clock+network -> NetworkSensitive, tested) and an observation GAP classifies Unclosable never Hermetic — absence of evidence is not evidence of hermeticity (tested; observation_complete defaults false so the zero value is Unclosable by construction). Acceptance: one fixture per class exercising all 13 arms; reason codes stable, family-prefixed, pairwise distinct; shareability restricted to exactly Hermetic/HermeticWithCapabilities/ObservedStable. 4 tests (107 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. title: E014: proc-macro untracked-file/env regression fixtures

title: F024: canonical descriptor byte-verification on every hit

StoredDescriptorEntry::commit is the ONLY constructor (bytes + independent digest + key can never be hand-assembled inconsistently); verify_hit checks (1) reloaded canonical descriptor bytes == committed bytes (storage/index corruption, torn writes), (2) independent descriptor digest recomputation under DOMAIN_DESCRIPTOR — its own domain, so a single SHA-256 collision cannot satisfy both hashes — plus deserialized-form re-serialization equality (writer/reader version drift), (3) action-key recomputation == index key (key-assembly bugs, index cross-links). Acceptance: corrupted-descriptor fixture (flipped byte) refuses with STORAGE_DESCRIPTOR_BYTES_MISMATCH; drift fixture refuses STORAGE_*; cross-linked-index fixture refuses KEY_RECOMPUTATION_MISMATCH; intact entries validate (CACHE_HIT_VALIDATED). title: G010: supervision policies and restart budgets
description: Configure supervision policies and restart budgets per the matrix: wrapper connection=stop; worker session=restart bounded-backoff (reconcile durable operations before admitting new authoritative work); ATP endpoint=restart/escalate (repeated failure degrades transport to fallback); action actor=stop or controlled retry via new fenced attempts; health collector=restart (stale evidence fails closed for remote-required); CAS writer=escalate on invariant violation (publication must not continue after storage corruption); compat HTTP/OTel island=restart/stop isolated; GC=restart with cadence/backoff; speculation=stop/restart optional. close_reason: Implemented rabs_asupersync::supervision (G010; Epic G matrix; R63): the nine-component supervision matrix as a total const policy function plus on_failure budget accounting. Matrix per the bead verbatim: WrapperConnection=Stop; WorkerSession=restart(5, 500ms base, ReconcileDurableOperations precondition, exhaustion Escalate); AtpEndpoint=restart(3, 250ms, exhaustion DegradeToFallbackTransport — repeated failure degrades transport); ActionActor=restart(2, NewFencedAttemptsOnly — never actor-replacement ambiguity); HealthCollector=restart(10; stale evidence already fails closed via I007); CasWriter=ESCALATE immediately (publication must not continue after storage corruption — tested: budget untouched, restart never an option); CompatIsland=restart isolated (local execution unaffected); GC=cadence-bounded restart; Speculation=optional. Restart-budget tests: restarts consume budget visibly (trace-visible counter), deterministic doubling backoff (250/500/1000 pinned), exhaustion behavior per component (degrade/escalate/stop all exercised); worker-session restarts carry the reconcile-before-authoritative-work precondition. 4 tests (13 crate lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. The live supervisor wires these policies over Asupersync supervision in the G-series runtime beads.

Publication can NEVER continue from an uncertain state: CrashConsequences structurally has no continue-publication arm (exhaustive destructure), and fail-open-locally is permitted ONLY when no exposure had begun — a crash after exposure forbids local fallback (the two-frontier rules govern; both directions tested). ACCEPTANCE: chunking determinism fixtures; parameter-version bump creates new manifests without invalidating old.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_cas::chunking (H004; plan sec 90; R95): FastCDC-style gear-hash CDC, pure and dependency-free (splitmix64 gear table derived from the profile seed). ChunkingProfile is VERSIONED (profile_version + min/mask/max + seed; PROFILE_V1 = 16K/64K/256K); every ChunkManifest records the version it was cut under, and the field exists for tooling identification only — reassembly needs just the spans, so old manifests are NEVER reinterpreted under new settings. Acceptance both halves: determinism fixtures (same bytes + profile = identical layout; min/max bounds hold; coverage tiles exactly) and the parameter-bump case — a v2 profile cuts a different layout while the v1 manifest remains exactly valid over the same object (chunking is storage; whole-object digest stays the correctness identity per H001, both validated). Dedup property pinned: a 64-byte insertion at offset 10000 in 1 MiB resynchronizes locally with the majority of chunk contents shared. Degenerate cases: empty object = empty manifest; tiny object = one chunk; torn coverage is a typed error. 4 tests (8 cas lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

Missing-diff correctness: empty receiver needs all 6 chunks; partial overlap returns exactly the gap (chunk 3 of the shared file + both chunks of the absent file); duplicate chunks across files count once. Acceptance both halves covered (subtree-sharing skip fixture + missing-diff correctness). 4 tests (12 cas lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Note: subtree digests are carried as data here; the H002 streaming hasher computes them when it lands.

A worker never sends a command asking another component to commit on its behalf; repeat offers idempotent; no in-place patching (correction = quarantine + recompute or new epoch). ACCEPTANCE: full protocol implementation + crash matrix (H015).

title: H017: reflink materialization backend

title: H020: storage-value model by action class and recomputation cost

title: H021: deterministic small-object packs and bounded member indexes

ACCEPTANCE: pack determinism fixtures; member access bounds enforced.

title: H022: mark/tombstone/grace/unlink GC + open-reader race tests
description: Implement mark/tombstone/grace/unlink GC with open-reader race tests (R58): mark -> tombstone -> grace period -> recheck liveness/pins -> unlink; never immediate deletion; final recheck defeats the race where a new read/materialization starts between mark and unlink. ACCEPTANCE: concurrent GC-vs-read stress finds no missing object referenced by a valid root.

Until then it runs as dogfood/differential. ACCEPTANCE: gate wired; differential mismatches block promotion.

title: H025: project namespace ACL / encryption-at-rest profile
description: Add project namespace ACL/encryption-at-rest profile for sensitive objects: source/object namespaces carry project/access classification; optional at-rest encryption per fleet policy; V1 is one administrative trust domain but scoping still applies within it. title: H026: same-key divergence quarantine (semantic/observable/evidence classes)
description: Implement same-key/different-semantic-result conflict quarantine, observable-only quarantine, and preservation of all candidate evidence (I34; risk R63): a second result with the same key but different canonical semantic-result digest quarantines the action, preserves BOTH candidates, disables serving, opens a determinism/key-soundness incident, and enumerates previously served consumers from provenance for escalation by trust/release tier; semantic-equal but observable-different gets narrower presentation/observability quarantine disabling ordinary replay; attempt-evidence differences append normally. ACCEPTANCE: all three divergence classes exercised (T019/T025).

title: H027: manifest path/type/case/symlink validation before storage+materialization
description: Validate manifest paths/types/case-equivalence/symlink containment before storage and materialization (R75): reject absolute member paths, dotdot, NULs, duplicates, platform-equivalent case/Unicode collisions, escaping symlinks, undeclared hardlinks, device/socket/FIFO nodes, and other special files unless an action class explicitly defines safe handling. ACCEPTANCE: malicious-manifest fuzz corpus fully rejected (T021).
close_reason: Implemented rabs_cas::manifest_validation (H027; plan sec 92; R75; T021) — first real module in rabs-cas. validate_manifest rejects, with typed per-rule violations: absolute member paths, dotdot components, NUL bytes, empty paths, exact duplicates, ASCII case-twin collisions AND Unicode NFC/NFD-twin collisions (the cafe-precomposed vs cafe-combining fixture fired RED against the first mark-stripping-only key and forced precomposed Latin folding — genuine red-to-green), symlink escapes (absolute targets and depth-counted ../ below the root; in-tree relative navigation admitted), hardlinks to undeclared targets, and device/socket/FIFO special nodes (no action class defines safe handling today — reject). Equivalence is CONSERVATIVE: paths that might collide on any platform collide here, because a manifest that materializes differently per host is not one object. T021 corpus test drives every hostile shape from the bead list plus a clean-manifest positive. 4 tests; clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Runs before storage AND before materialization by contract (callers wire both sites).

title: H028: transitive provisional-ancestor closure + adoption checks in commit
description: Implement transitive provisional-ancestor closure and exact-object adoption checks in the commit transaction (I32; risk R64): a prepared result stores a canonical sorted set of provisional ancestor references; commit verifies EVERY referenced producer action is committed and resolves to the EXACT consumed object (or an explicit compatible adoption edge from a different winning attempt containing the same logical output object ID); A->B->C chains require full transitive closure, not direct-only checks. ACCEPTANCE: T020 scenarios (including adoption and divergent-object refusal).

title: H029: canonical-result/evidence/publication separation + evidence append
description: Implement canonical-result/attempt-evidence/publication separation with compatible-evidence append behavior (I37; risk R80/R115): committed pointer names a canonical result manifest; worker identity, attempt IDs, timings, resources, trust observations, verification runs, provisional lineage, incremental snapshots are separately attached evidence that CANNOT create false result divergence; a new evidence bundle for the same canonical result appends idempotently. ACCEPTANCE: equivalent attempts with different evidence never diverge; append idempotency tests.

title: H030: storage representation IDs, multiple encodings without path ambiguity
description: Implement storage representation IDs supporting multiple verified encodings per logical object without path ambiguity (R81): StoredRepresentationId{logical, storage_profile, encoded_digest, encoded_size}; raw/zstd/packed representations coexist; concurrent writers with different profiles publish different representation records rather than racing one ambiguous pathname; representation selection never changes action keys. ACCEPTANCE: concurrent-encoding race tests (T029).

title: H031: acyclic manifest closure, depth/fanout, pack range-overlap validation
description: Add acyclic manifest-closure, depth/fan-out, and pack range-overlap validation (R95): tree/result manifests must be acyclic, depth/fanout/count bounded, closed under referenced object identity; pack member ranges checked for overlap/out-of-bounds. ACCEPTANCE: cycle/overlap fuzz corpus rejected before allocation-heavy traversal.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_cas::closure_validation (H031; plan sec 92; R95): validate_closure (acyclic + depth/fanout/node-count bounded + closed under referenced identity) and validate_pack_ranges (in-bounds, non-overlapping, non-empty, overflow-safe). Bounds are enforced AS COUNTERS during the single traversal — a hostile graph refuses before allocation-heavy expansion (depth checked before node lookup, fanout before descent, node cap before insertion). Corpus per the acceptance: self-cycle and chained two-node cycle reject with the offending identity; depth bombs, fan-out bombs, and dangling references (closure holes) reject by name; shared subtrees (diamond DAG) correctly ADMIT — a DAG is not a cycle; pack corpus covers overlap (order-independent: unsorted input caught after sort), out-of-bounds, offset+length u64 overflow (checked_add — cannot wrap into valid), and zero-length members. DEFAULT_BOUNDS 64 deep / 65536 wide / 1M nodes. 4 tests (19 cas lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: H032: commit ack gated on CAS + metadata durability profile
description: Gate commit acknowledgement on the explicit CAS-directory plus metadata-transaction durability profile: CAS objects/manifests satisfy their configured durability profile BEFORE the metadata transaction can commit; only after that transaction (including the publication pin) is durable does ActionResultCommitted go out. ACCEPTANCE: power-fail simulation shows no committed pointer to non-durable objects.

title: H033: append-only evidence index + versioned trust promotion/demotion
description: Implement append-only evidence indexing and versioned trust-evaluation promotion/demotion without mutating publication identity (I42; risk R99): evidence bundles attach via an index whose IDs are canonically sorted/deduped for evidence_set_digest; ActionTrustEvaluationRecords re-evaluate serving per latest nonrevoked policy; promotion/demotion/quarantine never rewrites canonical bytes. ACCEPTANCE: T032 scenarios (evidence promotion/demotion, policy change, post-publication compromise).

title: H034: result digests retained in eviction tombstones (divergence detection)

ACCEPTANCE: evict-then-recompute divergence fixture detected.

title: H035: equal-digests/different-manifest projection-completeness incidents
description: Detect equal-projection/different-canonical-manifest conflicts and quarantine as serializer/projection-completeness incidents (I48; risk R103): two candidates claiming identical semantic AND observable digests but different canonical manifest bytes/object IDs indicate a projection omission or serializer bug — never labeled ordinary evidence-only variation. ACCEPTANCE: T035 fixture opens the right incident class.

title: H036: publication reachability root/pin created atomically in commit
description: Create the action-publication reachability root/pin atomically in the publication transaction (risk R111): a crash cannot expose a committed pointer whose object closure is immediately collectible; the pin is coordinator-owned and workers can never release it (R127). ACCEPTANCE: T039/T049 publication-pin crash + release-attempt scenarios.

title: H037: authority/publication metadata-loss recovery vs explicit reset generation
description: Define authority/publication metadata-loss recovery versus explicit cluster credential/reset generation (risk R113): loss of ordinary object-location/index metadata degrades to misses + reindex; loss or rollback of coordinator authority, publication, generation-fence, trust, or subscriber-delivery metadata requires restore/reconciliation or an explicit new credential/operator-reset generation before serving resumes — NEVER treated as an ordinary cold cache. ACCEPTANCE: empty/rolled-back-DB startup refuses serving until reset proof (T039).

title: H038: full authoritative table set + constraints (generations/fences/pins/handoff)
description: Add the full authoritative table set with constraints: action generations + tombstones, immutable publications, mutable serving states, evidence index, trust evaluations, peer authority high-water, worker/edge incarnation fences, atomic publication pins, operations, edge subscribers, plus all object/pin/lease/quarantine tables (Epic H description lists all). Constraints: unique active ActionKey; only-active-authority writes; generation-ID non-reuse within cluster lineage; same-key/different-descriptor conflict quarantine; edge-handoff rows model at most one active + one named predecessor; deterministic failures are ResultKind publications (no second failure table). ACCEPTANCE: constraint tests; schema migration v1 recorded (R119).

title: H039: output-map role uniqueness + bundle-root derivation enforcement
description: Enforce canonical logical-output-map role uniqueness and deterministic artifact-bundle-root derivation; reject duplicate or contradictory specialized output indexes (risk R125): DB-level and decode-level checks that specialized indexes (dep-info, build-script metadata, provisional) are derived views consistent with the single role-tagged map. ACCEPTANCE: T047 rejection fixtures.

title: H040: revisioned authority-bound serving state, conservative TTL/clock epochs
description: Implement revisioned authority-bound serving-state records with conservative durable TTL/clock-epoch semantics and explicit blocking-quarantine references (risk R126): ServingValidity{evaluated_at, max_age, clock_uncertainty, coordinator_clock_epoch}; wall-clock rollback, epoch discontinuity, or uncertainty crossing the not-after bound expires serving CONSERVATIVELY; monotonic state_revision + authority digest make replay/idempotency explicit; serving rows name blocking quarantine IDs rather than treating reason strings as authority. ACCEPTANCE: T048 scenarios (TTL expiry, rollback, stale-revision replay, quarantine-reference recovery).

title: H041: authority-scoped pin leases, grace, fail-toward-retention
description: Implement authority-scoped pin leases with monotonic renewal/release, restart/partition grace, and fail-toward-retention reconciliation; forbid worker release of publication roots (risk R127): pin expiry never depends on a worker comparing wall clocks with coordinator timestamps; coordinator-issued lease IDs + renewal sequences + conservative validity; after restart/partition/clock uncertainty an unresolved pin stays protected through reconciliation + grace; release idempotent and authority-scoped. ACCEPTANCE: T049 scenarios (clock skew, restarts, contradictory leases, duplicate release, publication-root release attempts).

title: I001: coordinator-owned Cargo root-permit broker + local jobservers
description: Implement the coordinator-owned Cargo root-permit broker plus host/worker-local jobservers (risk R48): every managed Cargo process consumes a brokered CargoRootPermit backing Cargo's implicit token — a shared jobserver pipe alone cannot bound many independent Cargo invocations because each assumes its own implicit token. Starting ten Cargo processes requires ten root permits; no unaccounted implicit concurrency. ACCEPTANCE: broker + accounting; active Cargo count never exceeds granted roots under stress (T016).

title: I002: root permit before every Cargo process + valid jobserver injection
description: Acquire a root permit before every managed Cargo process and inject a valid local jobserver for its process tree: the edge (or worker for whole-command) obtains the permit, creates/joins a valid GNU make jobserver sized to remaining transferable capacity, and Cargo/rustc inherit valid descriptors/auth. The permit is held for the complete Cargo process lifetime and released exactly once (an obligation). ACCEPTANCE: permit lifecycle tests including crash-release; jobserver validity verified by nested make/cargo fixtures.

title: I003: strip local descriptors from remote requests; canonical capacity values
description: Strip invalid local descriptors from remote action requests: local jobserver descriptors/auth strings are execution capabilities replaced per host; worker-local descriptors never reference a client-host pipe (risk R7 — leaked descriptors cause hangs/oversubscription). Any child-visible logical capacity value (NUM_JOBS, normalized CARGO_MAKEFLAGS/MAKEFLAGS) is supplied canonically and enters the presented environment when it can affect behavior. ACCEPTANCE: remote request contains no local FDs; canonical capacity values keyed.

title: I004: worker-local jobserver bridge
description: Create the worker-local jobserver bridge: workers run their own jobserver trees sized from their execution resource grants; build scripts and native make/Ninja tools cooperate where supported. ACCEPTANCE: worker-side nested-make fixture respects worker capacity.

title: I005: action resource-envelope schema + estimator
description: Define the action resource-envelope schema: {cpu_threads, memory_bytes, memory_peak_class, disk_read/write_bytes, temp_space_bytes, network_in/out_bytes, linker_heaviness, lto_heaviness, process_count, expected_duration, uncertainty} — estimates from historical action-class/toolchain/crate observations, updated after completion. ACCEPTANCE: schema + estimator with update loop; estimates recorded in receipts.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::resource_envelope (I005; plan sec 84; R66): ResourceEnvelope with every bead field (cpu_threads, memory_bytes, memory_peak_class, disk_read/write_bytes, temp_space_bytes, network_in/out_bytes, linker_heaviness, lto_heaviness, process_count, expected_duration_ms, uncertainty_permille) — completeness pinned by exhaustive-destructure test. EnvelopeEstimator update loop: unobserved_prior() admits maximum uncertainty (1000 permille — confidence is EARNED, never asserted); first observation replaces the prior outright (the prior was ignorance, not data); subsequent observations fold via integer EMA (3/4 history + 1/4 observed — deterministic, no floats, no clocks); class fields take latest observation (modes, not averages); uncertainty decays 1000/(n+1) floored at 50 (never fully certain — the world changes). Tests: max-uncertainty prior, prior replacement + decay-to-floor, convergence toward a new heavier regime with no drift under stable observations, schema completeness. 4 tests (103 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Honest boundary: receipts RECORDING these estimates land with the provenance-receipt beads; this bead delivers schema + estimator as specified.

title: I006: worker pressure/eligibility snapshot pipeline
description: Collect CPU/memory/IO/disk/cache/toolchain/path snapshots per worker: WorkerPressureSnapshot{identity, boot generation, incarnation, captured_at_causal, valid_for, admin intent, eligibility, supported platforms, isolation profiles, queue, cpu, memory PSI, io PSI, disk, cache warmth, toolchain inventory digest, retrieval reliability, cancellation debt, path quality, confidence}. Pressure/queue/kernel/cache-warmth are execution eligibility, never key inputs; the coordinator timestamps receipt with its own monotonic clock and treats validity conservatively after reconnect. ACCEPTANCE: snapshot pipeline + staleness handling.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::pressure (I006; plan sec 84; R66/R127): WorkerPressureSnapshot with the bead's full field list (identity, boot generation, incarnation, causal capture seq, validity window, admin intent, eligibility, platforms, isolation profiles, queue, CPU, memory/IO PSI, disk, cache warmth, toolchain inventory digest, retrieval reliability, cancellation debt, path quality, confidence — completeness pinned by exhaustive destructure) + ReceivedSnapshot + judge_freshness. R127 clock discipline: staleness judged on the COORDINATOR's monotonic receipt stamp; the worker's causal value is an ordering aid never compared with coordinator time (no code path exists). Conservative reconnect handling per the acceptance: every snapshot received before a reconnect (older connection_epoch) is StaleByReconnect regardless of window — clock continuity across the gap is unprovable; a new-epoch snapshot is fresh again (tested). Window edge inclusive, one-past stale (tested). None of it reaches keys: the type has no descriptor linkage, and F008's boundary tests already prove eligibility has no digest channel. 3 tests (123 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Honest boundary: the live COLLECTION pipeline (PSI reads, disk stats) lands with worker runtime beads; this is the schema + staleness core.

title: I007: RCH health policy as pure candidate-receipt core
description: Adapt the Asupersync RCH health/admission model as the pure policy core for worker candidate receipts, extended with RABS action dimensions; output is a structured candidate receipt + final decision (deterministic, replayable). ACCEPTANCE: identical inputs give identical receipts; policy unit tests.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_scheduler::health_policy (I007; plan sec 84) — first real module in rabs-scheduler, honoring its zero-I/O/zero-clock charter. evaluate_candidate(snapshot, freshness, demands) -> CandidateReceipt: every rule consulted in FIXED order (snapshot-freshness, admin-intent, hard-eligibility, isolation-profile, platform-class, disk-envelope, then the soft scores queue-pressure/cpu-headroom/memory-psi/cache-warmth/retrieval-reliability — order pinned by test), each finding carrying its outcome, plus the final Admit{score}|Exclude{rule,reason}. Acceptance: identical inputs give identical receipts (pure — no clocks, randomness, or iteration-order dependence; tested byte-equal). RABS action dimensions extend the RCH health model: required isolation profile, platform class, and the I005 resource envelope (disk demand = temp + write bytes) each exclude by name. Stale evidence FAILS CLOSED at the first rule (the Epic G supervision law — tested for StaleByReconnect); draining/maintenance intent, failed probes, wrong profile, and insufficient disk all exclude with their rule named. Scores order candidates deterministically and each finding carries its exact contribution (queue-pressure delta -200 pinned). 3 tests; clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution.

title: I008: hard eligibility exclusions before scoring
description: Implement hard eligibility exclusions before scoring: incompatible platform/toolchain; stale/contradictory health evidence; insufficient disk/memory headroom; admin disabled/draining; active-project exclusion; unreliable artifact retrieval beyond policy; sandbox capability mismatch; trust/identity mismatch; transfer break-even failure under remote-required policy. Stale health fails CLOSED for remote-required work (R25). ACCEPTANCE: exclusion fixtures per rule with reason codes.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_scheduler::hard_exclusions (I008; plan sec 84; R25): check_hard_exclusions runs the nine hard rules in fixed order BEFORE scoring — an ineligible worker is not a lower-scored candidate, it is not a candidate. All nine per the bead with stable WORKER_EXCLUDED_* reason codes (distinctness tested): untrusted health evidence FIRST — stale (any Freshness != Fresh) OR contradictory fleet-record claims fail CLOSED for remote-required work (both fixtures tested, R25); incompatible platform; insufficient disk headroom vs the envelope demand; admin draining/maintenance; project exclusion list; retrieval reliability below the policy floor; sandbox capability mismatch (all-required-present check); identity mismatch (F029 fence verdict); transfer break-even failure under remote-required — with the 9b counter-fixture proving break-even is NOT an exclusion when remote is optional (local execution simply wins). One fixture per rule per the acceptance + the eligible-passes case. 3 tests (6 scheduler lib total); clippy/fmt green. Self-verified by re-execution. Composes with I007: exclusions gate, then evaluate_candidate scores survivors.

title: I009: predicted completion + transfer break-even scoring
description: Implement predicted completion and the transfer break-even score: expected_completion = predicted queue delay + missing-input transfer + toolchain materialization + predicted execution + output return + reliability risk penalty + pressure penalty. Break-even inputs: local queue/exec estimates, remote queue/exec, already-local object fraction, path throughput/RTT/loss, output size, toolchain availability, cancellation risk, uncertainty. Tiny actions with cold remote inputs usually run locally (R23); long/widely-shared actions justify moderate transfer cost. ACCEPTANCE: scoring golden fixtures; break-even decisions in receipts.

title: I010: weighted fairness and starvation limits
description: Implement weighted fairness and starvation limits: dimensions foreground-vs-optional, agent/user, repository/project, CI-vs-interactive, long-vs-short, cleanup-vs-new; weighted fair scheduling with deadline/critical-path overrides and hard starvation bounds; cleanup and cancellation control always retain reserved capacity. ACCEPTANCE: starvation-bound property tests under adversarial mixes (R22).

description: Implement foreground/optional/cleanup priority classes wired through admission, queues, and transfer priorities: foreground work dominates optional work (I18); cleanup is never starved. ACCEPTANCE: class-priority tests including cleanup under storm.

title: I012: SLO brownout integration for speculation
