ACCEPTANCE: speculation_browns_out_before_foreground scenario.

title: I013: advisory pool-sizing reports
description:
Add advisory pool-sizing reports using Asupersync's queueing-theoretic substrate for: concurrent compiler actions, hashing workers, CAS readers/writers, compression workers, linkers, native builds, test processes, transfer streams. ADVISORY only at this stage.
CREATION-GATE PROVENANCE (anti-ceremony): consumer = operators sizing pools AND the I017 managed-resizing opt-in gate, which requires this report's evidence trail before automatic resizing may be enabled; gate = I017 cannot ship without it; defect class = mis-sized pools observed as tail-latency/starvation in storm workloads; DELETION CONDITION = if I017 is killed or the frontier decision retires managed resizing, this reporting retires with it rather than living on as an unread dashboard.
ACCEPTANCE: reports generated with recommendations + confidence.

title: I014: fifteen-agent storm and pressure-collapse tests
description: Add fifteen-agent storm and pressure-collapse tests: multi-host storm benchmark (the M6 acceptance: >=2x at that stage, 3x final), plus pressure-collapse scenarios verifying no system-wide swap collapse and graceful admission refusal. ACCEPTANCE: benchmark automated; collapse scenarios produce bounded degradation with receipts.

title: I015: provenance-DAG critical-path estimator
description: Build the provenance-DAG critical-path estimator: prioritize actions by blocked dependents, historical downstream fan-out, remaining path duration, foreground urgency, metadata-ready potential, duration uncertainty, cache/prewarm status; a slow dependency blocking many crates outranks an independent leaf regardless of arrival order. ACCEPTANCE: estimator improves storm tail latency on replay corpus vs FIFO.

title: I016: safe hedging policy + CAS winner validation + divergence handling
description: Implement safe hedging policy, compare-and-set winner validation, and semantic/observable divergence handling: hedge only when critical-path + high predicted tail risk + acceptable duplicate cost + sufficiently independent workers + safe-to-duplicate + active publication fencing; hedges share the ActionGeneration but own independent leases (I31); first fully validated candidate wins compare-and-set; losers cancelled/drained; late divergent results quarantine (I34). ACCEPTANCE: hedged_candidate_commit_and_late_divergence_quarantine scenario.

title: I017: managed pool sizing behind opt-in + replay gate
description: Add managed pool sizing behind opt-in and a replay gate: automatic resizing requires stable observation windows, hysteresis, minimum evidence counts, replay validation, explicit operator opt-in, and rollback on tail-latency regression. ACCEPTANCE: gate enforced; rollback demonstrated on induced regression.

title: I018: single active coordinator action registry across edges
description: Implement the one active coordinator action registry shared by all edge hosts: fleet-wide DiscoveryActor and ActionActor registries keyed by family/action key; all edges submit final keys to the single coordinator (I5; R44). ACCEPTANCE: cross-edge identical demand joins one actor; per-subscriber latency/saved-work measured.

title: I019: root-permit implicit-token accounting stress tests
description: Add root-permit implicit-token accounting tests across many simultaneous Cargo processes: prove that C-capacity grants expose exactly C-1 transferable tokens + 1 implicit; no configuration relies on a contradictory very-high -j with hidden token limit without compatibility tests; exact -j/implicit-token/jobserver behavior tested across supported stable/beta/nightly Cargo/rustc. ACCEPTANCE: token-conservation property under storm (T016/T033).

title: I020: V1 same-worker child execution; second-hop dispatch disabled
description: Specify and benchmark V1 same-worker child execution; keep second-hop dispatch disabled: a remote Cargo process launches its child compiler/linker/build-script processes on the SAME worker under one worker-local jobserver and process tree; children may query local/shared CAS and join coordinator singleflight, but cross-worker child dispatch stays off until a separate design review + benchmark. ACCEPTANCE: nested-execution benchmark; dispatch-off enforcement test.

title: I021: C-1 transferable + 1 implicit token model; acyclic permit ordering
description: Model each Cargo grant as one implicit token plus C-1 transferable tokens and prove acyclic permit ordering: acquisition order = coordinator graph/root or action admission -> placement + bounded input-transfer reservation -> input materialization + temp/output disk reservation -> worker/edge execution admission + memory envelope -> local jobserver token immediately before spawn -> execution against pre-reserved output capacity; no code waits for an earlier-tier permit while holding a later-tier resource another action needs. ACCEPTANCE: ordering property tests; deadlock-freedom argument documented.

title: I022: hedge sibling-lease independence tests
description: Add hedge tests proving sibling execution leases remain independent within one action generation (R62): renewing/revoking/expiring one hedge lease never invalidates siblings; only coordinator generation supersession affects all. ACCEPTANCE: hedge lease-independence race tests.

description: Separate Cargo submission-frontier grants from selected-worker/local execution resource grants across all planes (R102): local-Cargo-with-remote-children = frontier grant bounding live graphs + submitted requests, worker CPU admitted separately; whole-command = worker-derived; coordinated local = edge pressure grant; uncoordinated fail-open = no stale fleet grant. A worker execution grant is never invented before worker selection merely because local Cargo holds a graph token. ACCEPTANCE: plane-specific accounting tests (T033).

description: Reorder input/disk/execution/jobserver acquisition so no compiler token is held during bulk transfer: root permits and jobserver grants acquire only AFTER input readiness and disk/output reservations; provisional-lineage waiters bounded. ACCEPTANCE: instrumented pipeline shows zero token-held-during-transfer occurrences.

title: I025: bounded provisional-lineage waiters + producer progress reserve
description: Bound provisional-lineage waiters and reserve producer progress capacity per Cargo root (R112): reserve at least one producer/progress slot per active Cargo root; bound the number and transitive depth of lineage-waiting wrappers; stop replaying additional provisional metadata when waiters would consume the root's progress reserve; prioritize unresolved producer attempts and their transfer/control traffic; measure pipelining benefit vs occupied-slot cost with fallback to full-result readiness for pathological graphs. ACCEPTANCE: waiter-saturation scenario keeps producers progressing (T041).

title: I026: sharded registries, bounded mailboxes, coordinator capacity gate
description: Shard coordinator action/discovery registries with bounded mailboxes, isolate critical queues, minimize serialized metadata sections, and gate on burst/storm/recovery capacity metrics (R130): shard by ActionKey; bounded per-actor mailboxes; authority/cancellation/lease queues isolated from telemetry/bulk planning; only generation-create/serving-mutate/publication-commit transactions serialize; slow subscribers/inventory scans/audits/dashboards outside actor critical sections; bounded overload -> explicit defer/refuse or pre-frontier fallback, never a second coordinator. Coordinator capacity is a RELEASE GATE: measure lookup/join/admission/publication latency, mailbox depth, commit latency, loop lag, CPU/memory, recovery scan under 15-agent replay + burst + long-lived sessions. ACCEPTANCE: T052 capacity scenarios green at gate thresholds.

title: J001: canonical ATP frame extension encoding (sorted, golden fixtures)
description: Replace/sort ATP extension maps for canonical frame encoding (Asupersync blocker 44.1; risk R10): ATP frame extensions must encode with deterministic canonical ordering (BTreeMap or explicit numeric sort); golden fixtures prove byte identity across runs and implementations. Noncanonical encoding breaks replay, signatures, and transcript hashing. ACCEPTANCE: byte-identical encodes for permuted insertion orders; fixture suite committed upstream or in the adapter.
close_reason: Implemented rabs_protocol::frame_extensions (J001; Asupersync blocker 44.1; R10 wire arm): the ONE canonical ATP extension encoding — entries sorted by numeric key strictly ascending before any byte is written (u64-LE count, u32-LE key, u64-LE length, raw value), so no map iteration order can reach the wire. Acceptance: all five non-identity permutations of the fixture set encode byte-identically; a COMMITTED golden fixture pins the exact bytes (count=3, keys 1<7<42) so any implementation change that moves a byte fails before it breaks replay/signatures/transcript hashing in the field. Duplicate keys are a typed error, never last-writer-wins. The decoder VERIFIES canonicality (strictly-ascending keys required — a hand-built unsorted block rejects, so two spellings of one frame cannot both decode), plus truncation/trailing-garbage/overflow rejection and the empty-set round trip. 4 tests (116 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. The negotiation state machine per acceptance: highest version inside both ranges per layer; transport and application refuse independently, each carrying BOTH sides' ranges so the operator sees exactly what to upgrade (tested at both layers). N/N-1 rolling-upgrade fixtures: N with N-1 agrees on the older concrete pair symmetrically (both sides derive the same answer); N with N gets current; N-2 refuses at the transport layer with ranges. 4 tests (127 protocol lib total); clippy/fmt green. description: Implement exactly-once logical MetadataReady, complete edge materialization, then rustc artifact-notification replay: worker emits MetadataReady per attempt/logical-output at most once; coordinator checks current attempt authority and forwards to subscribed edges; each edge fully materializes the exact requested path; the wrapper replays the artifact-notification line exactly once per subscriber/logical output. ACCEPTANCE: exactly-once property under retries/reconnects; Cargo starts dependents on time.

title: M006: dependent-action provisional obligation
description: Implement the dependent-action provisional obligation: a consumer of provisional metadata carries a DirectProducerCommit obligation plus the transitive lineage record (producer action/generation/attempt, logical output ID, exact object ID). ACCEPTANCE: obligation created on consumption; blocks descendant terminal paths until resolved.

title: M007: producer failure invalidation and dependent cancellation
description: Implement producer failure invalidation and dependent cancellation (R39): if the producer generation fails, is superseded without compatible adoption, or loses authority, the coordinator invalidates its provisional lineage; dependent attempts receive cancellation/supersession; processes/tokens/streams/pins drain; the producer wrapper's nonzero exit reports the original compiler failure to Cargo naturally; causal trace records which dependents started from the provisional output; already-emitted Cargo diagnostics are never fabricated or silently retracted (RABS cannot make Cargo forget a replayed notification — safety = block invalid commits + fail/cancel the live build coherently). ACCEPTANCE: producer-failure end-to-end scenarios (M016).

title: M008: no dependent commit before producer finalization
description: Prevent dependent result commit before producer finalization: the coordinator commit transaction refuses descendants whose provisional ancestors are not committed-with-exact-object (or adopted) — wiring M006 into H028. ACCEPTANCE: A->B->C transitive scenarios (T020).

title: M009: action DAG from artifact identities
description: Build action DAG edges from artifact identities: actions reference dependency artifacts by content identity; artifacts reference producing actions; live build observations establish invocation order and Cargo context; provisional edges explicit; test actions reference binaries + data inputs. No reliance on unstable Cargo unit-graph APIs. Uses: critical-path scheduling, rebuild explanation, affected-test selection, cache bisection, nearest incremental ancestor, speculation prediction, architecture advice, historical replay. ACCEPTANCE: DAG reconstructed for a fixture workspace; queries serve I015/O009.

title: M010: large stock differential shadow corpus (10^5-10^6 actions)
description: Run the large stock differential shadow corpus for workspace actions: 10^5-10^6 representative shadow actions with ZERO unexplained divergence required before broad workspace serving (M10 acceptance / trust ladder Stage 5). ACCEPTANCE: corpus run automated; divergence triage workflow; gate wired to serving flags.

title: M011: selected-repo sampled serving + quarantine switch
description: Add selected-repo sampled serving and quarantine switch: workspace serving starts on selected repos with sampling + one-command quarantine/rollback. ACCEPTANCE: sampling controls; quarantine switch cuts serving instantly.

title: M012: rmeta equality/skip-rate corpus experiment
description: Run the rmeta equality/skip-rate corpus experiment (Part XIII sec 94): across internal repos, canonicalize first; record the exact artifact each consumer receives; compare conservative exact keys vs candidate metadata projections; classify upstream edits interface-vs-implementation; measure byte-identical .rmeta frequency + downstream hit potential; inspect span/hash oversensitivity sources; shadow-execute every projected hit; define proceed threshold + projection-epoch rollback BEFORE enabling any reduced projection. ACCEPTANCE: experiment report with go/no-go recommendation.

title: M013: future public API hash adapter
description: Add the future public API hash adapter for workspace keys: consume rustc public_api_hash/RDR when usable upstream, entering through the projection framework with its own shadow gate (absorption point). ACCEPTANCE: adapter slot typed + inert until upstream lands.

title: M014: canonical Cargo-driver provenance required for workspace publication
description: Require canonical Cargo-driver provenance before workspace shared publication (I19/R43): a workspace result may publish for cross-worktree serving ONLY when Cargo's own planning ran in the canonical namespace (provenance proves it); noncanonical parents get the dependency/local lane at most. ACCEPTANCE: noncanonical-parent publication refused with reason code.

title: M015: full-snapshot vs minimal-closure hit-rate/invalidation benchmark
description: Add the full-snapshot-key versus minimal-closure-key hit-rate and invalidation benchmark (R41): quantify that minimal closures avoid whole-graph invalidation on one-file edits while full-snapshot keys would invalidate everything — the empirical justification of I3. ACCEPTANCE: benchmark report on representative repos; used in M10 acceptance.

title: M016: producer-failure-after-metadata-notification E2E tests
description: Add producer-failure-after-Cargo-metadata-notification end-to-end tests: the nastiest ordering — Cargo already consumed the metadata notification, dependents started, then the producer failed; verify dependents cannot publish, the build fails/cancels coherently, and target state is recovered ownership-safely. ACCEPTANCE: scenario suite green (with M019).

title: M017: transitive lineage verification + winning-attempt adoption
description: Propagate and transactionally verify transitive provisional lineage including different-winning-attempt adoption: every prepared descendant carries the complete transitive ancestor closure; commit verifies exact-object resolution; a different winning producer attempt satisfies lineage only when its committed result contains the SAME logical output object ID under compatible toolchain/event contract (explicit adoption edge); differing object cancels/refuses all consuming descendants. ACCEPTANCE: adoption + divergence scenarios (T020).

title: M018: shared incremental serving disabled until explicit + gated
description: Keep shared incremental serving disabled until every incremental input/output state is explicit and gated: admitted workspace classes run with incremental compilation disabled for shared serving, or treat incremental state as private nonshareable, until M13/Epic P gates pass — an incremental directory is never an implicit unkeyed input. ACCEPTANCE: enforcement test; serving flag coupling to the P-gates.

title: M019: provisional materialization journal + ownership-safe dirty-target recovery
description: Journal provisional subscriber materializations and implement ownership-safe invalidation/dirty-target recovery after lineage failure (R86): edge-local records for every output installed before lineage closure; on failure, remove/replace a path ONLY when current bytes/identity still match the RABS-installed object AND the path belongs to that operation; otherwise mark the target state dirty and require Cargo revalidation or a private target reset; Cargo fingerprint/output-cache cleanup follows stock differential fixtures; never guess-delete user state. ACCEPTANCE: dirty-target scenarios show no skipped invalid dependents on the next build.

title: M020: lineage-gated terminal success with early-metadata pipelining retained
description: Withhold descendant terminal success/final readiness until transitive provisional lineage closes, while retaining early-metadata pipelining (I44): a dependent wrapper may finish execution but not return terminal success until ancestors resolve; early metadata still unblocks dependents under the provisional journal; bounded waiters per I025. ACCEPTANCE: lineage-gated terminal-delivery tests.

title: N001: interception/shim contract proof across channels; else no run-cache
description: Prove canonical-Cargo interception and launcher-shim contracts across stable/beta/nightly; disable run-cache serving if neither preserves semantics: mechanism preference (1) canonical Cargo-driver integration intercepting the run without substituting path identity; (2) launcher shim at Cargo's expected path ONLY after proving executable identity, mtimes, Cargo fingerprints, output-cache behavior, and inherited jobserver descriptors remain correct; (3) no run-cache serving otherwise. The shim is evidence-gated, never assumed. ACCEPTANCE: feasibility matrix doc + fixtures per channel; serving flag coupled to the proof.

title: N002: exact stdout/stderr + directive capture
description: Capture exact stdout/stderr and Cargo directives for build-script runs: exact per-stream bytes, per-stream ordering, recorded cross-stream event sequence where observed (RABS does not invent an unknowable total order between independently piped streams); structured directive manifest alongside exact bytes. ACCEPTANCE: byte/order fixtures including interleaved writes.

title: N003: generated output manifest capture
description: Capture the generated output manifest: complete post-run OUT_DIR tree, deletions/tombstones, and Cargo output-cache files as an object manifest. ACCEPTANCE: manifest completeness fixtures including deletions.

title: N004: DEP_LINKS_* metadata reconstruction on replay
description: Reconstruct DEP_LINKS_* metadata semantics on replay: cargo:KEY=VALUE metadata becomes DEP_<LINKS>_* environment for dependent build scripts; replay must reproduce this exactly for downstream keys and execution. ACCEPTANCE: dependent-crate fixtures observe identical DEP_* values under replay vs stock.

title: N005: registry-aggressive / workspace-audit-first policy
description: Apply the registry-aggressive/workspace-audit-first policy split: registry/git dependency build scripts get aggressive sandboxing + discovery + interception + determinism audit before broad sharing; workspace build scripts are audit-first with explicit project policy for git/clock/randomness/network/secrets, volatility preferred over optimistic caching, actionable rch why refusals. ACCEPTANCE: policy routing tests.

title: N006: vergen/built/time/git/network pattern detection
description: Detect vergen/built/time/git/network patterns in build scripts: recognize common volatile generators (vergen, built, timestamp embedding, git describe, network fetch) and classify accordingly. ACCEPTANCE: detection fixtures for each pattern feed volatility classification.

title: N007: deterministic re-execution audits + denylist
description: Add deterministic re-execution audits and the denylist: sampled re-execution of cached build-script runs comparing outputs/directives; divergent scripts enter a shared-cache denylist with evidence retained. ACCEPTANCE: audit + denylist wiring; divergence quarantines.

title: N008: zero-divergence gate + cacheability report
description: Add the zero-divergence gate and cacheability report for build scripts: the M11 acceptance — zero divergence on the corpus and a report of what fraction of observed registry build scripts is safely cacheable (target >80%, subject to corpus). ACCEPTANCE: gate + report automated.

title: N009: captured-fetch action pattern for network generators
description: Add the explicit captured-fetch action pattern for network generators: (1) explicit fetch action under a network capability; (2) fetched bytes + response metadata captured as immutable objects; (3) build/generator runs offline against those objects; (4) keyed on captured content, never URL or wall-clock fetch. Non-separable cases are volatile/capability-specific and never enter the ordinary shared cache. ACCEPTANCE: networked-generator fixture converts to the split pattern.

title: N010: failed/cancelled runs never publish; live post-state parity policy
description: Verify failed/cancelled build-script state is never published as a shared cache hit and live-operation post-state follows the explicit parity/local policy (R101): failed/cancelled runs never publish partial OUT_DIR contents; for retry parity with stock Cargo, either execute in the operation-owned destination or reproduce the exact observed failure post-state, else run locally; shared staging cleaned only after live-operation semantics are resolved. ACCEPTANCE: failure/cancel fixtures + retry-parity fixtures (T034).

title: N011: ordered directive/stdout golden fixtures incl DEP_LINKS_*
description: Add exact ordered directive/stdout golden fixtures including DEP_LINKS_*: golden corpus for rerun-if-changed/-env-changed, rustc-link-search/-lib, rustc-env, cfg/flag directives, warnings, metadata, exit status — the byte-exact replay contract. ACCEPTANCE: goldens across stable/beta/nightly.

title: N012: pre-run OUT_DIR/output-cache in keys; atomic post-state replacement
description: Include pre-run OUT_DIR/Cargo output-cache state in eligible keys and atomically replace complete post-state with deletions (R66): pre-state digest (or proven-empty) is a key input when observable; replay stages the complete post-state in a clean private dir and atomically swaps, applying tombstones. ACCEPTANCE: stale-OUT_DIR ghost-file scenarios (T022) show replay == clean run.

title: N013: failure post-state preserved for live operation or local execution
description: Preserve failed/cancelled build-script live-operation post-state or execute locally; never publish it as a shared hit — the operational complement of N010 for the live Cargo operation's retry semantics: stock Cargo/build scripts may observe partial state on retry, so RABS preserves the exact failure post-state for the live operation (or executes locally) while never letting that partial state become a shared cache entry. ACCEPTANCE: retry-behavior differential vs stock.

title: N014: structured directive validation + path-valued/native-link closure
description: Parse and validate structured Cargo directives, close every path-valued/native-link dependency, and prove exact replay after output-tree installation (R122): path-valued rustc-link-search must resolve to declared generated outputs, immutable toolchain/native datasets, or explicitly captured host-bound inputs at the same canonical path for every consumer, else nonportable/volatile; rustc-link-lib + implicit search semantics push selected native libs, startup objects, plugins, default scripts, negative candidates into the downstream link closure; rustc-env/metadata/cfg preserve exact bytes downstream; replay validates every directive-referenced path is inside the installed post-run tree BEFORE exposing stdout to Cargo. ACCEPTANCE: T045 directive mutation/negative-lookup scenarios.

title: O001: nextest runner protocol definition
description: Define the nextest runner protocol: the target-runner/wrapper seam through which RABS intercepts test launches — enumeration, per-case launch, environment, cwd, signals, retries, output collection — versioned against supported nextest releases. ACCEPTANCE: protocol doc + adapter skeleton; version matrix started.

title: O002: per-test and batch keys (binary digest conservative invalidation)
description: Implement per-test and policy-selected batch keys: TestActionKey over test_binary_digest, exact test identity, runner identity, arguments, presented environment, sandbox policy, positive+negative data inputs, virtual cwd, output platform, declared side-effect outputs; the binary digest conservatively invalidates all tests in that binary (finer code-to-test projections are advisory research only); batch keys include the shared state that motivated batching. ACCEPTANCE: key fixtures; binary-change invalidates all cases.

title: O003: test input/side-effect observation (fixtures/env/subprocess/net/time)
description: Capture fixture/config positive and negative inputs, exact environment, subprocesses, network/time/randomness, and declared side effects for tests: fixtures/snapshots/goldens, failed opens + dir listings, env/config files, dynamically loaded libraries, subprocess selection, network/clock/entropy access, declared output/state dirs. ACCEPTANCE: observation fixtures per category.

title: O004: stable-pass cache for admitted tests
description: Cache stable passing results for admitted tests: V1 serves stable PASSES first; a cached pass never suppresses required migrations, fixture generation, or setup side effects. ACCEPTANCE: repeated-loop latency savings measured; setup-protection fixtures.

title: O005: deterministic-failure and flaky classifications
description: Implement deterministic-failure and flaky classifications for tests: evidence records ObservedStablePass/ObservedStableFailure/FlakyOutcome/TimingSensitive/NetworkSensitive/EnvironmentSensitive/SideEffecting/Quarantined; deterministic test-failure serving is a later opt-in with short TTL after presentation and retry semantics are proven. ACCEPTANCE: classification fixtures; flaky detection on seeded flaky tests.

title: O006: preserve nextest output/timing/retry semantics
description: Preserve nextest output/timing/retry semantics: stdout/stderr, exit status, duration reporting, retry/flaky metadata identical to stock nextest across supported versions. ACCEPTANCE: differential fixtures vs stock nextest.

title: O007: periodic full-suite verification
description: Add periodic full-suite verification: CI periodically runs a fresh COMPLETE canonical suite (and selected high-risk/release lanes always do) to detect missing dependency edges and cache masking. ACCEPTANCE: scheduled full runs wired; discrepancy alerts.

title: O008: zero-incorrect-pass gate
description: Add the zero-incorrect-pass gate: the M12 hard gate — no cached pass may ever be wrong; any incorrect pass is an IncorrectResultDivergence incident with quarantine. ACCEPTANCE: gate wired to serving; incident path tested with a seeded wrong pass.

title: O009: affected-test advisory graph
description: Build the affected-test advisory graph: provenance-DAG-based suggestion of tests affected by changed source/artifacts/data inputs — ADVISORY selection only, independent of result-cache correctness. ACCEPTANCE: suggestions computed for fixture edits; precision/recall measured against full runs.

title: O010: doctest compile/run action support
description: Add doctest compile/run action support: DoctestCompile and DoctestRun as separate cacheable classes; agent inner loop may exclude doctests by profile; CI runs canonical doctest coverage; generated doctest crate/source identity canonicalized + explainable. ACCEPTANCE: doctest class fixtures; identity canonicalization tests.

title: O011: nextest interception semantics proof before serving
description: Prove nextest target-runner/interception cwd, env, signal, retry, and output semantics before serving: shadow-first integration; if the adapter cannot preserve semantics, test execution remains UNCACHED while compile actions still benefit. ACCEPTANCE: semantics-proof matrix per nextest version; serving flag coupled.

title: O012: side-effecting/setup/fixture-generation ineligibility fixtures
description: Add side-effecting/setup/fixture-generation ineligibility fixtures: tests that mutate databases, write shared state, generate fixtures, or depend on external services are detected and denied caching with clear reasons. ACCEPTANCE: fixture corpus covering each pattern.

title: O013: mandatory periodic uncached full-suite for release lanes
description: Add the mandatory periodic uncached full-suite policy for release lanes: release CI bypasses test-result caching by policy at defined cadence — a cached pass is an execution-reuse fact, not correctness proof. ACCEPTANCE: policy enforcement + audit trail.

title: O014: suite-order/shared-state coupling detection -> batch or bypass
description: Detect suite-order/setup/shared-state coupling and force batch/suite actions or bypass (R69): once-per-suite initializers, ordering dependence, shared DB/port/temp roots, global external state, setup/teardown side effects -> TestBinaryBatch (key includes that state) or bypass; cached per-test passes never skip required suite initialization. ACCEPTANCE: order/setup mutation fixtures route to batch/bypass.

title: O015: setup scripts/runner profile/retry policy keyed; retry-pass = flaky
description: Key nextest setup scripts, runner profile, retry/timeout/fail-fast policy; classify retry-only passes as flaky (R91): setup scripts/archive state/once-per-run fixtures represented as batch prerequisites never skipped by per-test hits; the runner profile and retry/timeout/fail-fast policy are key inputs; a test passing only after retry is flaky, never a stable authoritative pass. ACCEPTANCE: retry-pass fixture classified flaky; profile change invalidates.

title: O016: benchmark-run non-cacheability + hardware/load scoping
description: Enforce the non-result-cacheable benchmark-run policy with matching hardware/load evidence (R92): BenchmarkRun results are observations of a machine/load — never served from cache; remote scheduling only on explicit hardware/pressure profiles; a benchmark harness declared as a functional deterministic test uses TestBinaryBatch instead. ACCEPTANCE: bench-run cache attempts refused; hardware-profile scheduling fixtures.

title: P001: incremental snapshot compatibility contract
description: Define the incremental snapshot compatibility contract: toolchain, target, profile, projection identity, output-platform class, isolation class — a snapshot is selectable only within its proven compatibility class; no cross-class reuse without proof. ACCEPTANCE: contract schema + class-mismatch refusal tests.

title: P002: atomic output+state capture after quiescence
description: Capture output artifacts and matching incremental state atomically: the incremental directory manifest and the MATCHING ordinary outputs publish as one auxiliary snapshot unit; capture only after the producing compiler and output writers are quiescent; crash/cancel before commit leaves only disposable staging. ACCEPTANCE: atomicity + quiescence tests (T050).

title: P003: FastCDC/zstd snapshot manifest
description: Implement the FastCDC/zstd snapshot manifest: content-defined chunking (adjacent incremental states are highly self-similar) + zstd; chunk parameters versioned. ACCEPTANCE: dedup ratio measured on sequential-edit corpus.

title: P004: git/source-state ancestry index
description: Build the git/source-state ancestry index for incremental snapshots: map every retained snapshot to its producing git commit/source-state identity so nearest-compatible-ancestor queries (P005) are cheap graph walks rather than content scans. Must handle: branchy histories (ping-pong A<->B is the headline workload); worktrees on divergent commits; dirty-tree states between commits (snapshot keyed to source-state identity, not just commit); rebases/amends that orphan states; and bounded index growth alongside P008 retention. WHY: the >=3x branch ping-pong target depends on finding the nearest usable state in milliseconds; without an ancestry index every branch switch degrades to a scan or a cold rebuild. ACCEPTANCE: ancestry queries return correct nearest candidates on a branchy fixture repo including dirty-tree and rebase cases; index size bounded under retention policy.

title: P005: nearest compatible ancestor selection
description: Implement nearest compatible ancestor selection: exact state first; nearest compatible git/source ancestor; historical cost-benefit estimate; never across incompatible classes. ACCEPTANCE: selection fixtures across branches.

title: P006: transfer-vs-rebuild ROI estimation
description: Estimate transfer-versus-rebuild ROI: no snapshot transfer when state size exceeds predicted compile saving; model uses historical costs. ACCEPTANCE: ROI decisions in receipts; negative-ROI fixture skips transfer.

title: P007: branch/worktree prewarm
description: Implement branch/worktree prewarm: on branch switch/worktree creation, prewarm the nearest compatible snapshot + critical-path artifacts (couples to Q007 git events). ACCEPTANCE: branch ping-pong benchmark shows the >=3x target trajectory.

title: P008: per-repo snapshot retention and GC
description: Implement per-repo snapshot retention and GC: bounded per-repo lineage budgets; reachability/LRU eviction; delayed deletion. ACCEPTANCE: retention bounds enforced; GC never breaks selectable lineage invariants.

title: P009: branch ping-pong benchmark + portability differential
description: Run the branch ping-pong benchmark and portability differential: the M13 acceptance benchmark (>=3x on target workloads) plus cross-worker/cross-class portability differentials. ACCEPTANCE: benchmark + differential automated.

title: P010: kill-switch — disable serving if ROI/storage gates fail
description: Disable serving if target ROI/storage gates fail (kill criterion): if corpora show poor latency ROI or unacceptable storage/complexity, retain exact artifact caching and DEFER incremental state serving. ACCEPTANCE: kill-switch wiring + decision record template.

title: P011: private writable clones, quiescent capture, crash cleanup
description: Materialize immutable snapshots as per-attempt private writable clones with quiescent atomic capture and crash/cancel cleanup (R128): the retained snapshot and CAS chunks stay immutable and are never mounted writable by two rustc processes; sampled cold/exact rebuild verifies compatibility before a family gains portable authority. ACCEPTANCE: concurrent-restore + mid-capture crash scenarios (T050).

title: Q001: filesystem edit watcher with stable write debounce
description: Implement the filesystem edit watcher with stable write debounce: detect a stable-enough edit boundary using debounce and editor write semantics (rename-into-place, atomic saves) before snapshotting for speculation. ACCEPTANCE: editor-pattern fixtures (vim/vscode-style saves) produce clean boundaries.

title: Q002: likely-next-command model from session corpus
description: Build the likely-next-command model from the session corpus: predict the agent's next build/test command from historical command sequences + provenance DAG (uses B012 intent reconstruction). ACCEPTANCE: prediction precision measured on held-out sessions.

title: Q003: immutable speculative source snapshots
description: Generate immutable speculative source snapshots: seal a coherent snapshot of the edited state for speculative actions; speculative snapshots may be abandoned when edits continue (an explicit user command still gets its own coherent snapshot before authoritative serving/execution). ACCEPTANCE: abandonment + supersession fixtures.

title: Q004: low-priority speculative action submission (same actors)
description: Submit low-priority speculative actions: speculative subscriptions (SubscriberKind::Speculative) join/create the SAME action actors as foreground work — identical semantics must collapse (E001 guarantee). ACCEPTANCE: speculative+foreground join fixture; no duplicate execution.

title: Q005: promotion to foreground without restart
description: Implement promotion to foreground without restarting: same actor/key/generation; priority+deadline promoted; transferred inputs and partial execution retained; brownout suspended while foreground interest exists; provenance records the promotion; a subsequent edit demonstrates supersession rather than false promotion. ACCEPTANCE: promotion + supersession scenarios.

title: Q006: SLO brownout + pressure cancellation for speculation
description: Integrate SLO brownout and pressure cancellation for speculation: soft threshold stops new speculation; hard threshold cancels low-value speculative work and drains; cleanup/integrity work unaffected (I012 wiring). ACCEPTANCE: speculation_browns_out_before_foreground at the agent-intelligence layer.

title: Q007: git checkout/HEAD/worktree prewarm events
description: Implement git checkout/HEAD/worktree prewarm events: branch checkout, HEAD change, pull/rebase/merge, worktree creation, lockfile update, toolchain change, CI push -> fetch snapshot, locate nearest state, prewarm dependency + workspace critical path, seed likely workers, optional canonical test subset, stop instantly under foreground pressure. ACCEPTANCE: event handlers + prewarm receipts.

title: Q008: CI canonical prewarm/trust tier
description: Implement the CI canonical prewarm/trust tier: every pushed commit may prebuild canonical profiles; CI-signed provenance gets CIPolicyApproved trust; developer pulls receive guaranteed-warm artifacts; local agent results remain useful but may need more verification for release use; trust tier is publication/access policy, never content identity. ACCEPTANCE: CI writer pipeline + trust-tier assignment.

title: Q009: speculation ROI dashboard
description: Build the speculation ROI dashboard: saved foreground latency vs wasted execution/transfer/storage cost; promoted/cancelled/wasted/saved accounting from provenance. ACCEPTANCE: dashboard fed by real speculation runs.

title: Q010: default-on speculation gated on positive p95 value
description: Gate default-on speculation behavior on positive p95 value: speculation ships default-off until the ROI dashboard proves positive net saved foreground latency and improved foreground p95 without pressure regressions. ACCEPTANCE: gate wiring + decision record.

title: Q011: key-fragmentation analyzer
description: Build the key-fragmentation analyzer: quantify compiler-seconds lost to dependency-version spread, feature drift, lockfile inconsistency, toolchain drift, RUSTFLAGS/profile divergence, target-CPU drift, path-policy drift, command-palette drift, build-script volatility, platform fragmentation, duplicate snapshots; output costed convergence recommendations. ACCEPTANCE: analyzer report on fleet corpus with quantified costs.

title: Q012: rch advise evidence reports
description: Build rch advise evidence reports: crate-architecture recommendations (split rebuild-tail crates, reduce feature coupling, interface crates, isolate proc macros/build scripts, align versions, reduce generated churn, link bottlenecks, dominating tests, profile/linker/toolchain configs) each with evidence, expected saved latency, confidence, and non-claims; NO automatic source/config mutation. ACCEPTANCE: advise output on fixture repo with attributable evidence.

title: R001: stable decision-receipt persistence
description: Implement stable decision-receipt persistence: every scheduling/execution request produces a durable DecisionReceipt (request identity, invocation class, key-breakdown digest, snapshot root + closure, cache lookup decision, singleflight decision, subscriber state, worker candidate rows, selected worker + reasons, transfer plan, budget/priority, attempt authority, lifecycle events, provisional events, verification, publication decision, latency/resources, fallback/refusal reasons, non-claims). ACCEPTANCE: receipts persisted + queryable; schema versioned; redaction verified.

title: R002: rch why miss/rebuild/worker/volatile/slow
description: Implement rch why miss/rebuild/worker/volatile/slow: rch why action KEY | crate | miss REQUEST-OR-BUILD-ID | rebuild ARTIFACT | worker DECISION-ID | volatile ACTION | slow BUILD-ID — miss explanation is the structured breakdown diff with the stable taxonomy; explainability is a product PILLAR, required before broad serving (M0 initial version shows raw components; full version by M4). ACCEPTANCE: each query answers on fixture data with stable reason codes.

title: R003: action/operation/object inspection commands
description: Implement action/operation/object inspection commands: rch rabs action show KEY, operation show ID, object stat/verify/locate ID — bounded JSON/TOON output with stable reason codes. ACCEPTANCE: commands on live fixture daemon; schema-stable output.

title: R004: CAS doctor/verify/locate/quarantine commands
description: Implement CAS doctor, verify, locate, and quarantine commands: rch rabs quarantine list/inspect/release (release requires verified repair receipt), object verification, location listing. ACCEPTANCE: quarantine lifecycle drivable from CLI with evidence.

title: R005: GC plan/run/history commands
description: Implement rch rabs gc plan|run|history operator commands over the H014 GC engine: `gc plan` produces a dry-run receipt (what would be reclaimed, why, per policy layer — committed-result LRU, toolchain retention, branch/commit pins, incremental budgets, provisional/staging expiry, quarantine retention); `gc run` executes with active-build protection and emits the actual reclaim receipt; `gc history` lists prior runs with planned-vs-actual deltas. All output bounded JSON/TOON with stable STORAGE_*/QUARANTINE_* reason codes. WHY: GC is the single most dangerous background subsystem (risk R26 — deleting a needed object breaks hits and running actions); operators need to preview, audit, and correlate every reclaim decision, and the plan requires planned AND actual reclaim receipts as first-class evidence. ACCEPTANCE: plan/actual parity visible on fixture data; history retained; refusal paths (disk-pressure emergency mode, active-pin conflicts) produce typed reasons.

title: R006: worker reconcile + stale-operation doctor
description: Implement worker reconcile and stale-operation doctor: rch rabs worker reconcile W triggers session reconciliation; doctor finds stale operations/pins and proposes safe resolution. ACCEPTANCE: seeded stale state found + resolved.

title: R007: fleet/cache/latency dashboards
description: Implement fleet/cache/latency dashboards: fleet posture + worker pressure; user-visible latency distributions; cache effectiveness + miss causes; top expensive/repeated crates; action critical paths; transfer/CAS health; storage/GC/quarantine; determinism/verification status. ACCEPTANCE: dashboards fed by live metrics on fixture fleet.

title: R008: incident bundle generation + runbooks (13 incident classes)
description: Implement incident bundle generation and runbook links: each incident class (IncorrectResultDivergence, ObjectCorruption, PublicationFenceViolation, OrphanProcessOrResource, ProtocolCompatibilityFailure, WorkerIdentityMismatch, SecretExposure, StorageExhaustion, SchedulerPressureCollapse, CancellationHang, ReconciliationConflict, KeyInstabilityRegression, HitRateFragmentation) has detection signal, automatic containment, operator command/runbook, evidence bundle, recovery path, regression-test requirement. ACCEPTANCE: bundle generation per class; runbooks written.

title: R009: schema/protocol compatibility doctor
description: Add the schema/protocol compatibility doctor: verifies local/ATP/RABS protocol versions, schema epochs, N/N-1 compatibility, and wrapper-contract matrix status across the fleet. ACCEPTANCE: doctor flags a seeded version skew with remediation.

title: R010: fragmentation dashboard + convergence recommendations
description: Implement the fragmentation dashboard and convergence recommendations: fleet convergence view over Q011 analyzer output with costed recommendations. ACCEPTANCE: dashboard renders analyzer results; recommendations actionable.

title: R011: action DAG browser + critical-path report
description: Implement the action DAG browser and critical-path report: navigate the provenance DAG, inspect critical paths and rebuild tails. ACCEPTANCE: browser over fixture DAG; critical-path report matches I015 estimates.

title: R012: operator rollback + canary orchestration + feature modes
description: Add operator rollback and canary orchestration: canary coordinator/workers designation; low-risk dependency actions routed first; automatic perf/correctness comparison vs current RCH path; promotion on canary success; quarantine on cleanup/corruption/identity/divergence incidents; ONE-COMMAND rollback to the prior path; feature modes (off/record-only/shadow-key/shadow-execute/serve-dependencies/serve-selected-workspace/serve-all-eligible/remote-control-shadow/native-atp-control/native-atp-data/speculation-enabled/tests-enabled/incremental-snapshots-enabled/require-remote) independently controllable per repo/action-class/worker/trust-tier. ACCEPTANCE: canary flow + rollback rehearsed end-to-end.

title: S001: durable coordinator/worker identity store + rotation

description: Separate signing/notarization/publication credentials and effects from ordinary compilation/link caching (R74): code signing, Apple notarization, package publication, timestamp-authority calls are separate credentialed actions; unsigned/ad-hoc intermediates cacheable by policy; credentialed signatures keyed/scoped to exact signing identity + captured response where reproducible, else noncacheable side-effecting release steps; private signing keys never enter ordinary compiler workers or shared cache namespaces. ACCEPTANCE: malicious-worker simulation caught by verification; eligibility revoked (T032).

title: S019: namespace ACLs + pre-upload local-only/secret path policy

title: T012: automated failing-trace minimization
description: Add automated failing-trace minimization: every failing lab/chaos/differential/soak trace is automatically reduced to the smallest reproducing case — bisect the input manifest, shrink the invocation, drop uninvolved actions/messages, and re-verify the failure reproduces deterministically at each step (built on the B011 divergence minimizer and the T053 structured logs that carry seeds and causal IDs). WHY: the verification program produces enormous traces (multi-day soaks, 15-agent storms); un-minimized failures are practically undebuggable and stall the zero-divergence gates; the plan requires every production incident to be convertible into a minimized replay case. ACCEPTANCE: demonstrated on seeded failures from at least three suite classes (lab scenario, chaos kill, differential divergence); minimized cases run in seconds and are archived alongside the incident bundle.

title: T054: flagship 15-agent demo as automated E2E acceptance script
description: Automate the flagship fifteen-agent demonstration (plan section 205) as a scripted end-to-end acceptance run with full structured logging: (1) start fifteen agents across several edge hosts and separate worktrees; (2) launch Cargo through canonical driver namespaces; (3) show coherent snapshots but minimal per-action input closures; (4) run overlapping check/test/clippy workloads; (5) show ONE coordinator-owned action actor per identical key across hosts; (6) show .rmeta fully materialized and its rustc artifact event replayed before bulk outputs; (7) show worker placement using cache locality, root permits, and pressure receipts; (8) show one agent cancelling without killing shared work; (9) disconnect the coordinator BEFORE observable commit and demonstrate safe nonpublishing local fallback; (10) repeat AFTER observable commit and demonstrate coherent failure/reconnect rather than mixed execution; (11) switch branches and restore nearest state (after the M13 gate); (12) let the watcher seal a quiescent edited snapshot, start optional speculation, invoke the matching command to promote that same action actor, then edit again to demonstrate supersession rather than false promotion; (13) use rch why to show a negative-dependency, exact-artifact, or environment miss; (14) use rch advise to identify the rebuild tail. Each step asserts its expected observable state from the structured logs (T053 standard). WHY: this is the integration proof that the headline capabilities compose — an asserting cross-subsystem E2E test, not a scripted showcase; any demo/dogfood use is a side effect of it passing.
